sfd7c333979.title: Auditable Human-Agent Teams for Autonomous X-ray Experimentation
sfd7c333979.description: arXiv:2611.12933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contribution
sfd7c333979.summary: Researchers demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices using coding-agent infrastructure with human oversight and auditable transcripts.
sfd7c333979.why: Shows agentic systems operating real scientific instruments over sustained periods, with audit trails for reconstructing decisions.

s6d6fb689fb.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
s6d6fb689fb.description: arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual
s6d6fb689fb.summary: EarthRecord is a benchmark testing multimodal agents on raw four-decade satellite archives from 56 sites for land-change analysis.
s6d6fb689fb.why: Existing benchmarks skip raw multi-sensor data, so this tests whether agents can handle the messier inputs real Earth observation work requires.

s541a6d0474.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
s541a6d0474.description: arXiv:2611.12935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro
s541a6d0474.summary: TopicScope trains sparse autoencoder-based classifiers that label the topic of each token during generation, allowing topic changes mid-response.
s541a6d0474.why: Offers a generation-time monitoring approach beyond the two or three harmful-content classes current activation monitors handle.

s43dfb67f4b.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
s43dfb67f4b.description: arXiv:2611.12936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-t
s43dfb67f4b.summary: LandslideFM is a unified foundation model proposed for landslide detection, combining visual perception tasks with contextual scene interpretation.

s20e1f6f9d2.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
s20e1f6f9d2.description: arXiv:2611.12938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout. Adding a graph image yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, driven by strong precision improvements on low-complexity questions (+4.65 F1). Mixed-effects and regression analyses show that these multimodal gains do not depend strongly on model scale, but are highly sensitive to graph layout: image-only settings sharply
s20e1f6f9d2.summary: A controlled study over 1,500 questions finds adding graph visualizations to prompts yields an average 1.85 F1 gain for knowledge graph question answering in vision-language models.
s20e1f6f9d2.why: Gives practical evidence on when adding graph images to prompts helps or hurts, relevant to multimodal retrieval pipeline design.

s4070047534.title: Reinforcement Learning based control of Cancer Chemotherapy treatments
s4070047534.description: arXiv:2611.12940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement Learning has achieved tremendous success in recent years. Extending its scope from the traditional complex games such as Atari, Go, Pokeman, and Chess, reinforcement learning has caught researchers' attention on modelling real-life scenarios. Personalized medicine and the dynamic treatment regimen are two such preliminary research fields; researchers are focusing their mindsets currently. Estimating the optimal dynamic treatment regimens from the observational real clinical data is being popularized among the researchers, widening its scope towards more advanced versions of reinforcement learning algorithms. This research is about a research study that focused on reinforcement learning techniques that have been approached in the
s4070047534.summary: A paper surveys reinforcement learning for dynamic treatment regimens and personalized cancer chemotherapy control from clinical data.

scc15aefa9a.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
scc15aefa9a.description: arXiv:2611.12941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. We propose the competence circuit, summarized as IKC + KC + C, that decomposes an agent's real-world impact into three pathways: intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Using the canonical fast-takeoff debate as a stress test, we formalize the conditions for intelligence-mediated fast takeoff as a conjunction jointly sufficient for fast catastrophic supremacy, showing that most rely on rapid knowledge acquisition or control attainment rather than intelligence alone. We operationalize epistemic intelligence as hypothesis-selection efficiency and validate this framework via stochastic simulation on NK fitnes
scc15aefa9a.summary: The paper proposes a competence circuit framework for AI agent governance, decomposing real-world impact into discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control.
scc15aefa9a.why: Offers a conceptual governance framing that shifts focus from limiting intelligence to controlling agent actions and knowledge boundaries.

s61855ac1e7.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
s61855ac1e7.description: arXiv:2611.12942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict from a labelled context in a single forward pass. A recent benchmark reported that they decisively outperform tree ensembles for customer churn, but it compared them with untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and scored only ranking metrics, while a retention campaign is judged in money. We re-evaluate TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast and TabICL v2 against Optuna-tuned GBDTs on five public telecom churn datasets over 10 seeded splits. We separate three questions: whether a model ranks churners well, whether that ranking earns more expected maximum profit (EMP), and whether its probabilities can drive a threshold policy. With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparison
s61855ac1e7.summary: Researchers re-evaluate tabular foundation models against Optuna-tuned gradient boosting for telecom churn, scoring models on profit and calibration as well as ranking.
s61855ac1e7.why: Challenges claims that tabular foundation models beat tuned tree ensembles when judged by business value and calibration rather than ranking alone.

s30a60a7a11.title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
s30a60a7a11.description: arXiv:2611.12950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Black-box LLM fingerprinting aims to determine whether a target model was derived from a source model when only the output responses to input queries are observable. One way to reveal this relationship is to perturb each query and observe the resulting responses of both models, yielding two corresponding sets of response variations. These sets provide two complementary sources of information: the relations among response changes within each set, and the correspondence of response changes between the two sets. Existing approaches, however, have not fully exploited both. We introduce \textbf{SetPrint}, a training-free method that jointly captures both within-set relations and between-set correspondence. SetPrint expresses each response change r
s30a60a7a11.summary: SetPrint proposes a black-box method to determine whether a target LLM was derived from a source model by comparing response changes under query perturbations.
s30a60a7a11.why: Provides a way to verify model lineage using only API outputs, relevant to provenance and licensing checks.

sf2bc00eafe.title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
sf2bc00eafe.description: arXiv:2611.12953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprises increasingly use large language model agents to execute standard operating procedures (SOPs): long, branching, tool-intensive workflows. Yet there is little controlled evidence for choosing among competing agentic architectures. Holding the model, tasks, and tools fixed and varying only the architecture, we compare four designs (a function-calling single agent, a skill-augmented agent, centralized multi-agent orchestration, and a triage swarm; eight arms) across 13 enterprise SOPs, and introduce a skill-definition quality rubric to build matched high and low-quality skill corpora. Three takeaways emerge. (1)~\textbf{There is no universal best architecture; the right choice is SOP-dependent.} On a given SOP, task success ranges fro
sf2bc00eafe.summary: A controlled evaluation compares four agent architectures across 13 enterprise SOPs, holding model and tools fixed to measure cost and success trade-offs.
sf2bc00eafe.why: Gives controlled evidence on how architecture choice affects cost and success for enterprise agent workflows.

sbe31652c9b.title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
sbe31652c9b.description: arXiv:2611.12954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. However, extending WSP to physical problems remains challenging, particularly in achieving both solution accuracy and physical consistency. In this paper, we propose Physics2Weight (PtW), a framework that extends WSP to solving partial differential equations by directly generating neural network weights and editing architectures based on governing equations and initial and boundary conditions. PtW introduces physics-constrained prompting and physics-guided architecture editing, combined with iterative weight refinement from WSP, to improve solution accuracy and physic
sbe31652c9b.summary: Physics2Weight uses LLMs to directly generate neural network weights and architectures for solving partial differential equations from governing equations.

s5d52a51230.title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
s5d52a51230.description: arXiv:2611.12958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. We argue that overcoming this paradox requires embedding \emph{learnability
s5d52a51230.summary: The paper argues existing self-driving labs disconnect language models from physical grounding and proposes embodied science agents for learnable experimental design.

sa97fd66b9b.title: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes
sa97fd66b9b.description: arXiv:2611.12959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. Online partial coverage increases shadow-route share over no monitoring by .701 [.574,.826] and .575 [.412,.737], while task accuracy remains .905/.913 and signed frozen message contribution remains .592/.563. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuff
sa97fd66b9b.summary: An arXiv paper reports that monitoring one communication channel changes how learned agents route messages, while task accuracy stays high in a sender-receiver game.
sa97fd66b9b.why: Shows that observing a visible channel does not fully control agent communication, relevant to designing monitoring for multi-agent systems.

sbd26e36ced.title: IIT Patna at "ICPR 2026 TVRID Competition on Privacy-Preserving Person Re-Identification from Top-View RGB-Depth Camera"
sbd26e36ced.description: arXiv:2611.12960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Privacy-aware person re-identification (Re-ID) from top-view cameras replaces frontal appearance with anthropometric shape, while depth sensing further reduces color-based identity cues. The ICPR 2026 TVRID competition evaluates this setting using 86 identities captured by four synchronized Intel RealSense D455 cameras with RGB and Depth streams across flat, ascent, descent, and oblique viewpoints. Performance is measured using mAP and CMC@1 across within-camera in/out, ascent-descent, and flat-oblique scenarios. The competition had 147 registered participants and 33 final submissions. Three teams from IIT Patna participated: 'abhinavkumar03' and 'sjkdgfhl_' ranked 5th and 7th among 31 ranked participants, and 'vivek katuri' reached 77.67% CM
sbd26e36ced.summary: IIT Patna describes its entry to the ICPR 2026 TVRID competition on privacy-preserving person re-identification using top-view RGB-depth cameras.

s842888daa2.title: RBLA+: Efficient Rank-Specific LoRA Adapter Extraction for Federated Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous Clients
s842888daa2.description: arXiv:2611.12961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) reduces communication and computational overhead by training and exchanging compact trainable LoRA factors. Clients may use different LoRA ranks to meet adapter communication budgets and accommodate different local adaptation needs. The server must process these differences during aggregation and construct adapters at each client's rank for local training. We distinguish pre-aggregation alignment, which handles factor dimensions and scaling conventions before aggregation and rank-specific LoRA adapter extraction, which constructs client-sized pairs from the aggregated global model. Two common approaches to rank-specific extraction are direct rank truncation and Singular Value Decomposition
s842888daa2.summary: RBLA+ is a method for rank-specific LoRA adapter extraction in federated fine-tuning where clients use different LoRA ranks.
s842888daa2.why: Addresses server-side aggregation when clients have heterogeneous adapter ranks, a practical issue in federated LLM fine-tuning.

s40518b4096.title: BuySideFlow: A Point-in-Time Benchmark for LLM Agents in Investment Research
s40518b4096.description: arXiv:2611.12966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate SQL and SQL--Python workflows for investment research, but ensuring point-in-time (PIT) validity remains challenging. Agents must enforce disclosure cutoffs and select the appropriate historical states and record versions throughout data retrieval and financial analysis. We introduce \textsc{BuySideFlow}, a benchmark of 408 practitioner-derived Chinese-language tasks spanning equities, funds, fixed income, and macroeconomics over a fixed snapshot from a licensed production financial database. We provide executable references and a taxonomy of temporal errors, pairing result checks with expert audits of executed workflows. We evaluate nine agent configurations on all tasks, with result accuracy ranging
s40518b4096.summary: BuySideFlow is a benchmark of 408 Chinese-language investment research tasks testing whether LLM agents respect point-in-time data validity.
s40518b4096.why: Highlights that agents doing financial analysis must correctly enforce disclosure cutoffs, a hard data-leakage risk for production pipelines.

s81dde059ee.title: TrustMod-SM: A Multi-Axis Benchmark for Evaluating Trustworthiness of LLMs in Social Media Content Moderation
s81dde059ee.description: arXiv:2611.12970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong potential for social media content moderation, but their trustworthiness beyond overall accuracy remains underexplored. We introduce TrustMod-SM, a benchmark of roughly 29,000 instances across eight datasets, to evaluate LLM moderators on five dimensions: trustfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and context integrity. Evaluating 16 open-weight models (0.5B-284B parameters, spanning text-only and vision-language architectures) and one closed frontier model, we find persistent trustworthiness gaps. Higher detection accuracy often coincides with greater demographic disparity, and models frequently comply with concealment or exaggeration prompts, assign high confidence to wrong predictions, rarely escal
s81dde059ee.summary: TrustMod-SM is a benchmark of about 29,000 instances testing LLM content moderators on trustfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and context integrity.
s81dde059ee.why: Shows persistent trustworthiness gaps in LLM moderators beyond accuracy, informing evaluation before deploying them in moderation systems.

s2b631cac55.title: ZeroPoint: Lightweight Energy-Based Decision Model
s2b631cac55.description: arXiv:2611.12992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) assign a scalar energy to every joint value of the observed and predicted variables. In decision models, the prediction is chosen from a finite list of options provided with each input. Inference then reduces to comparing the energies of the options, and training lowers the energy of the correct option relative to the others. A complete decision must also account for the possibility that no option is acceptable. However, the energies learned by a standard EBM define only relative compatibility: adding the same input-dependent quantity to all energies leaves the predictions, the Gibbs distribution, and the usual training losses unchanged. The model therefore has no learned reference level against which to decide whet
s2b631cac55.summary: ZeroPoint is a lightweight energy-based decision model that adds a way to express that no option is acceptable.

s7197c98c31.title: Seeing Is Not Believing: Counterfactual Lesion Erasure Teaches a Small Medical Vision-Language Agent to Report Only What the Image Shows
s7197c98c31.description: arXiv:2611.13006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) often report a finding because the question names it; standard benchmarks miss this. From public segmentation datasets we build counterfactual views without manual annotation: the lesion erased by inpainting, a same-shape control edit elsewhere, and unedited lesion-free images. The evidence sensitivity gap (ESG) is the rate of absent-or-refer answers after erasure minus the rate after the control edit; it is zero for a model that ignores the image or reacts to both edits alike. MedScope-4B (Qwen3.5-4B, LoRA, image tools) was trained on label-derived trajectories, selected by a pre-registered rule and tested once against nine frontier and six open VLMs; four pre-registered checks then probed the mechanism.
s7197c98c31.summary: MedScope-4B is a small medical vision-language model trained with counterfactual lesion-erasure views to report only findings visible in the image.
s7197c98c31.why: Targets a known failure where medical VLMs report findings because the question names them, relevant to clinical AI reliability.

s18a9da27de.title: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
s18a9da27de.description: arXiv:2611.13015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts th
s18a9da27de.summary: Ask2Decide is a benchmark of 43 planning tasks testing whether LLM agents ask humans for decision-relevant missing information.
s18a9da27de.why: Tests a gap in agent behavior: acting on incomplete requests rather than seeking clarification, relevant to agent deployment design.

s3921e24143.title: Multi-Future Drafting: Mixture Block Drafters for Tree-Verified Speculative Decoding
s3921e24143.description: arXiv:2611.13017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Block drafters such as DFlash draft a block of future tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees such as DDTree verify the prefixes ranked highest by the product of the drafter's per-position distributions. Under tree verification, the expected number of accepted tokens is the probability mass the tree covers. We show that a product misallocates it: when the continuation can follow several futures, it splices them into chimeras, prefixes stitched together from different futures that the target never produces, and gives them as much budget as the futures themselves. Barring ties, no product-ranked tree can hold two futures that disagree in $m$ positions without $2^{m-1}-1$ chimeras, however well the drafter is trained, and in practice chimera
s3921e24143.summary: The paper proposes mixture block drafters for tree-verified speculative decoding, arguing product-based drafting misallocates verification budget across futures.
s3921e24143.why: Offers a potential way to improve accepted tokens per verification step in speculative decoding for faster LLM inference.

se3529a8465.title: ChipOmni: A General-Purpose AI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
se3529a8465.description: arXiv:2611.13020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electronic design automation (EDA) workflows remain highly fragmented, requiring engineers to coordinate heterogeneous representations, specialised software tools, and iterative verification across multiple design stages. Although large language models have brought more general reasoning and code-generation capabilities to EDA, many existing approaches remain focused on isolated tasks and struggle to plan, verify, and repair designs autonomously within executable engineering environments. Here we introduce ChipOmni, a knowledge-enhanced, context-evolving AI agent framework for EDA. ChipOmni integrates multimodal understanding, dynamic planning, multi-agent collaboration, and verification-driven tool interaction into a unified autonomous syste
se3529a8465.summary: ChipOmni is a knowledge-enhanced general-purpose AI agent aimed at planning, verifying, and repairing electronic design automation workflows.
se3529a8465.why: Shows agents extending into chip design toolchains, relevant to engineering teams automating EDA workflows.

sf4c275ca21.title: Understanding-First AI Engineering: Purposes, Reference Architecture, and Architectural Patterns for Human Understanding
sf4c275ca21.description: arXiv:2611.13022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems can produce reliable results without developing human understanding. However, human understanding remains valuable for shaping subsequent AI-supported work, forming preferences, governing collective choices and satisfying curiosity, even when human participation is unnecessary for correcting errors. We propose understanding-first AI engineering, which treats purpose-specific human understanding as a first-class design principle guiding requirements, design and operation. The purposes of understanding are organised into four complementary rationales: reflective agency, effective action, collective governance and epistemic value. A reference architecture connects production, verification, use, and learning and exploration through sha
sf4c275ca21.summary: The paper proposes understanding-first AI engineering, treating purpose-specific human understanding as a first-class design principle with a reference architecture.
sf4c275ca21.why: Offers architectural patterns for keeping humans understanding AI-supported work, relevant to system design and governance.

s3efc27ecba.title: GRAP: Gender Rubric-Aware Probing for Analyzing Gender Bias in LLMs
s3efc27ecba.description: arXiv:2611.13024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLMs increasingly mediate everyday interactions, subtle gender biases in open-ended responses pose growing societal risks. Existing probing methods have two key limitations: they rely on fixed-format tasks, such as pronoun resolution or occupation association, that alignment-tuned models can easily handle; and they compare raw group-level rubric scores, ignoring per-dimension variance and obscuring which bias dimensions reliably distinguish gender groups. We introduce GRAP (Gender Rubric-Aware Probing), a framework that uses a lightweight logistic probe to identify the most discriminative bias dimensions from responses scored across 10 rubric dimensions, operating task-agnostically on open-ended instruction following.
s3efc27ecba.summary: GRAP is a gender rubric-aware probing framework that uses logistic models to find which rubric dimensions reliably distinguish gender groups in LLM responses.
s3efc27ecba.why: Offers a more rigorous method for measuring gender bias in open-ended LLM outputs than fixed-format probes.

s7fd5e0603f.title: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
s7fd5e0603f.description: arXiv:2611.13030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have demonstrated strong generalization in robotic manipulation, yet processing dense visual tokens often incurs high inference latency. Visual token pruning offers a practical way to reduce this cost, but identifying a compact set of tokens that preserves reliable action generation remains challenging. Existing methods largely rely on static or immediate heuristic cues to estimate token importance. We introduce APS-VLA, a framework that learns visual token selection from robot demonstrations while keeping the pretrained VLA backbone frozen. A lightweight Decision Influence Estimator scores tokens conditioned on current visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioception. Its training com
s7fd5e0603f.summary: APS-VLA is a framework that learns visual token pruning from robot demonstrations to reduce inference latency in vision-language-action models.
s7fd5e0603f.why: Targets high inference latency in robotic VLA policies, a practical bottleneck for deploying them on real hardware.

s7d5d4ac444.title: Trust, but verify, audit and attribute: a human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced research results
s7d5d4ac444.description: arXiv:2611.13042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems now produce research results in bulk: in October 2026 a single laboratory released more than 700 AI-generated mathematics manuscripts, only part of them with machine-checked proofs. Such volumes will be checked mostly by AI agents that call specialised software. A passing check certifies only the artefact that was checked. For proofs translated into the proof assistant Lean, it has been shown that this artefact may state something other than the author's text, and that deciding whether a translation is faithful is undecidable in general. The human researcher therefore stays in the loop, and human and AI contributions must be recorded. We propose a domain-independent, human-in-the-loop framework for checkin
s7d5d4ac444.summary: The paper proposes a human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced research results, focusing on auditing and attributing Lean proof translations.
s7d5d4ac444.why: Addresses verification of AI-generated proofs, where a passing check may not confirm the author's original statement.

s5909ef816c.title: Elicitation of the parameters of a multi-criteria sorting model
s5909ef816c.description: arXiv:2611.13062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiple-criteria decision aiding (MCDA) proposes models and methods for different types of decision problems such as choice, ranking or sorting. Such models involve various parameters that must be elicited. In the elicitation process, all necessary information has to be taken from the decision-maker. For this, several direct and indirect elicitation methods are suggested in the literature. In this work, we concentrate on direct elicitation: we aim at providing a rigorous elicitation procedure for the parameters of the Non-Compensatory Sorting model (NCS), which has been characterized by an axiomatic analysis. A basic version of the NCS model is considered, i.e., a model with two categories and no vetoes. The parameters are the set of suffici
s5909ef816c.summary: The paper presents a rigorous procedure for directly eliciting parameters of the Non-Compensatory Sorting model in multi-criteria decision aiding.

s27306145fb.title: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
s27306145fb.description: arXiv:2611.13113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the absence of extrinsic rewards or task supervision, human behavior is guided by intrinsic motivation---neural signals that drive curiosity, creativity, play, and other essential facets of intelligence. Intrinsic motivation plays an important developmental role in building robust world models that enable generalization and adaptation. Yet existing studies leave open how a broad range of intrinsic motivations interacts with world-model representation learning to support downstream control. This limits our understanding of which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable models. To address these gaps, we integrate 24 intrinsic objectives, including established methods and explicit variants spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency
s27306145fb.summary: Researchers study how intrinsic motivations such as curiosity and play shape world-model representation learning to support downstream control.
s27306145fb.why: Clarifies which intrinsic reward signals yield robust world models, which may inform exploration design in agent training.

s34d6266c33.title: Activation-Guided Graph Retrieval for Cognitive Memory Reconstruction in Language Model Systems
s34d6266c33.description: arXiv:2611.13127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented language model systems generally select context by query-conditioned relevance. We argue that long-lived AI systems require a second operator: activation-conditioned memory availability. We specify an architecture in which request and goal cues seed an authorized memory graph, activation and fan attenuation allocate a bounded traversal frontier, retrieved entities recursively emit cues, and a typed evidence graph is reconstructed before generation. The specification yields five architectural consequences about candidate selection, traversal control, graph regularization, evidence reconstruction, and reinforcement. We derive implementation-level cost estimates and define ablations, failure conditions, and a reproducible eva
s34d6266c33.summary: Authors propose an architecture for language model memory retrieval based on activation-conditioned availability, using a bounded traversal of an authorized memory graph before generation.
s34d6266c33.why: Offers a design alternative to query-relevance-only retrieval for long-lived AI systems, though the text is a specification without reported results.

sd9850902f8.title: Agreeing on the Answer but Not the Reason: Measurement Limits of LLM Reasoning Failure Taxonomies
sd9850902f8.description: arXiv:2611.13140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Failure taxonomies for LLM reasoning are increasingly reported as measurements: papers state what fraction of a model's errors fall into named categories, then compare those fractions across models. We show that for one such category the reported fraction is largely a property of the measurement procedure. We defined Compositional Collapse (a model notices a required sub-part of a problem, then drops or misapplies it) and measured it across twelve models and eleven languages on a public multilingual math benchmark (2,316 graded records). First, 50.1% of failures carry evidence for more than one category, so the reported plurality depends on the order in which the classifier tests them: reversing two tests moves it in eleven of twelve models,
sd9850902f8.summary: Study finds that the reported share of LLM reasoning errors in a 'Compositional Collapse' category largely depends on the measurement procedure, across twelve models and eleven languages.
sd9850902f8.why: Suggests failure-taxonomy comparisons across LLM papers may reflect measurement choices rather than model differences, so treat such fractions cautiously.

sd5072bbe36.title: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
sd5072bbe36.description: arXiv:2611.13144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective teaching requires reasoning about the learner as well as the task, a capacity that Theory of Mind describes as inferring another agent's latent state from its behavior. We ask whether a stronger LLM teaches a fixed student better when it applies this principle. The student is an LLM agent acting through a harness that fixes its tools, context, and action budget, so a procedure that helps one model can exhaust the budget of another. We introduce Student-Aware Teaching (SAT). The teacher builds a learner model that pairs an empirical profile with hypotheses about the student's limitations, tests these hypotheses with diagnostic probes, and writes reusable skills for the diagnosed failures. A skill enters the library only after it rais
sd5072bbe36.summary: Introduces Student-Aware Teaching, where a stronger LLM builds a learner model of a fixed LLM agent to teach it skills within a constrained harness.
sd5072bbe36.why: Points to teacher-side adaptation for agents with fixed tool and action-budget limits, relevant to agent skill transfer design.

s4970cc7763.title: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
s4970cc7763.description: arXiv:2611.13161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective search and rescue (SAR) operations require autonomous systems capable of coordinating multiple heterogeneous agents, adapting to dynamic hazards, and aligning with human mission intent. Existing language-guided reinforcement learning (RL) methods primarily focus on single-agent instruction following and lack mechanisms for team-level coordination in complex, partially observable environments. This paper presents a Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios. Human instructions are interpreted by a large
s4970cc7763.summary: Proposes a language-grounded hierarchical reinforcement learning framework to coordinate multiple heterogeneous robots in simulated search and rescue operations.

s703d720342.title: AI Alignment Is Neither Solvable nor Sufficient
s703d720342.description: arXiv:2611.13167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humans and AI systems increasingly act within the same social and economic environments. Alignment, the goal of ensuring that AI systems act in accordance with human values, is widely regarded as a central challenge for ensuring that AI benefits society while avoiding harm. We argue that this endeavor is misguided. First, alignment is not well defined, as it presumes a sufficiently stable and identifiable set of human intentions or values. Second, where a concrete notion of alignment can be specified, it is not solvable. Third, where alignment appears solvable, solving it would not necessarily mitigate the negative consequences of AI. A key reason is that alignment is typically framed as a property of individual AI systems, while the resultin
s703d720342.summary: Position paper argues that AI alignment is ill-defined, unsolvable in concrete forms, and insufficient as a goal for ensuring AI benefits society.
s703d720342.why: Challenges the premise of alignment as a central engineering target, which may affect how safety goals are framed in product and policy work.

s8958081307.title: From Process Models to Composable Agentic Workflows: Combining BPMN, Agents and Enterprise Knowledge
s8958081307.description: arXiv:2611.13196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based agents can reason, use tools and collaborate. However, coordinating increasingly complex agentic applications becomes difficult to understand, monitor and improve. Decisions distributed across prompts, tool calls and application logic make workflows implicit. We introduce **Recursive Capability Composition**, enabling agents to execute business processes and expose them as reusable Agentic Tools. This paper presents a BPMN-based approach to Agentic Workflows, combining explicit orchestration with autonomous reasoning. SemTalk BPMN models are transformed into executable workflows using a LangGraph/Pregel runtime. Agentic Tasks introduce LLM reasoning at selected activities, while conventional BPMN controls process flows, deterministi
s8958081307.summary: Presents Recursive Capability Composition, a BPMN-based approach that lets agents execute business processes and expose them as reusable Agentic Tools.
s8958081307.why: Combines explicit process orchestration with autonomous agent reasoning, a pattern relevant to enterprise workflow monitoring and maintainability.

sec11ae4c31.title: Counting Under Disagreement: Dollar-Weighted Measurement, Selective Machine Labelling and Budgeted Human Review from Disagreeing AI Readers of Administrative Text
sec11ae4c31.description: arXiv:2611.13215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study AI-assisted measurement when one text label applies to many administrative records, the target is a monetary total, and the human readings that anchor the machines disagree. The testbed is 121,070 grant-purpose texts from US tax filings (799,675 records, \$126.4B), labelled by a rule-based classifier and three language models, with a designed sample of 651 texts read independently by three people under one codebook. We state exact conditions for a fixed-predictor difference estimator and for a cross-fitted predictor whose folds are assigned to the whole frame before sampling, under Poisson sampling, and assess the implemented fixed-size procedures by simulation: 8 predictors whose own totals span \$11.2-15.0B agree to within \$0.4B o
sec11ae4c31.summary: Paper examines dollar-weighted measurement of administrative text labels using disagreeing AI readers, selective machine labelling, and budgeted human review, tested on US tax-filing grant purposes.
sec11ae4c31.why: Gives statistical methods for estimating monetary totals when AI labelers and human readers disagree, useful for large-scale document measurement pipelines.

s58dbe3f793.title: Reliability of Claude Code as an Agentic AI Grading System for Handwritten University Exams
s58dbe3f793.description: arXiv:2611.13217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study examines the reliability of Claude Code, an agentic deployment of the Claude Opus 4.6 large language model, as a grading system for handwritten university exams. Four research questions addressed agreement with expert human grading on total scores (RQ1), agreement across five question types from multiple choice to evaluative judgement (RQ2), consistency across two independent grading sessions one week apart (RQ3), and the accuracy of AI-generated feedback (RQ4). Claude Code graded the 20-mark mid-term papers of 60 consenting students in a Saudi computer graphics course in a single agentic session, guided by three rubric files. Reliability was estimated on disjoint samples: 20 papers for RQ1, RQ2 and RQ4, and 15 papers for RQ3. Anal
s58dbe3f793.summary: Study evaluates Claude Code, an agentic deployment of Claude Opus 4.6, as a grader for 60 students' handwritten university mid-term exams against expert human grading.
s58dbe3f793.why: Provides evidence on agreement, consistency, and feedback accuracy for AI grading in education, a concrete reliability benchmark for similar deployments.

s55ee63f867.title: W-ISA: Transactional Execution of Weight-Space Intervention Programs
s55ee63f867.description: arXiv:2611.13232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present W-ISA, a software instruction set and transactional runtime for executing weight-space intervention programs on pretrained language models. Shape-checked instructions express parameter updates, projections, ablations, and rank-one transformations. The runtime applies these programs within request-scoped execution contexts and restores saved parameters after completion or interruption. Activation-based match-action rules connect measured model states to intervention selection. We evaluate restoration and replay on SmolLM-135M-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, and compare materialized rank-one updates with equivalent PyTorch hooks on the latter. In 45 timed requests, both intervention implementations produce identical greedy sequen
s55ee63f867.summary: Introduces W-ISA, a software instruction set and transactional runtime for applying and restoring weight-space interventions on pretrained language models.
s55ee63f867.why: Offers transactional, restorable parameter edits for model runtimes, relevant to teams running request-scoped model modifications.

s749af7c7da.title: Decisions by Discrimination: Differential Evidence for Medical Reasoning
s749af7c7da.description: arXiv:2611.13233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly studied for clinical decision support, and medical question answering provides a testbed for evaluating this capability. In particular, medical multiple-choice questions (MCQs) reflect a core challenge in clinical decision-making: plausible options often share overlapping evidence, while only a few decisive factors distinguish the correct option from incorrect ones. However, existing retrieval-based and reasoning-oriented methods mainly focus on supplying broadly relevant knowledge or eliciting reasoning paths, rather than identifying the compact differential evidence that separates confusing alternatives. In this work, we present a retrieval-grounded differential evidence framework for medical MC
s749af7c7da.summary: Proposes a differential-evidence approach to medical multiple-choice reasoning that focuses on features distinguishing correct options from plausible incorrect ones.

sac832a5de6.title: NCP: Verifier-Guided Optimization of Weight-Space Control Policies
sac832a5de6.description: arXiv:2611.13236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the Neural Control Plane (NCP), a closed-loop system that observes language-model execution, synthesizes candidate weight-space intervention rules, evaluates them, and maintains a versioned table of admitted policies. NCP separates a pretrained model's inference data plane from the control policy that selects temporary parameter interventions. W-ISA supplies transactional execution and parameter restoration; NCP supplies telemetry, candidate synthesis, admission criteria, priorities, and rule lifetime management. The optimization state consists of active rules and an archive of evaluated candidates, while base-model parameters are restored after each request. In a local SmolLM-135M-Instruct experiment, NCP generated three candidate
sac832a5de6.summary: Presents the Neural Control Plane, a closed-loop system that synthesizes, evaluates, and versions weight-space intervention policies for a language model's execution.
sac832a5de6.why: Separates control policy from the inference data plane, a architectural pattern relevant to managing runtime model behavior at scale.

see5c244e19.title: ExpertCrowd-SWE: Measuring Frontier Coding Agents on Expert-Authored Engineering Tasks in Unfamiliar Codebases
see5c244e19.description: arXiv:2611.13246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ExpertCrowd-SWE (EC-SWE) is a benchmark of 100 expert-authored, multi-file software engineering tasks for evaluating autonomous coding agents in large, unfamiliar codebases. Each task is a change request written by a practising engineer against a pinned commit of a real repository, paired with a sealed reference solution and a task-specific grader whose weighted, mostly executable criteria award partial credit; must-pass blockers and pass/fail gates encode what a maintainer would refuse to merge. The tasks span 87 open-source projects and 11 languages. The median ticket is 148 words, while the median reference solution changes 471 lines. Every task image is calibrated before release so that the reference solution scores 1.0 and both the untou
see5c244e19.summary: Introduces ExpertCrowd-SWE, a benchmark of 100 expert-written multi-file engineering tasks across 87 open-source projects for evaluating coding agents in unfamiliar codebases.
see5c244e19.why: Offers a more realistic benchmark for coding agents on maintainer-style change requests, useful for evaluating agent tooling choices.

s6a904438c6.title: Dependable Long-Horizon LLM Agents: A Trajectory-Centered Empirical Study of Where Errors Enter and Which Controls Reach Them
s6a904438c6.description: arXiv:2611.13254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an LLM agent fails part-way through a long task, the usual analysis records a symptom: a failure-mode label, or the agent and step judged responsible. It does not say where the error entered, which state carried it to the symptom, whether anything in the trajectory contradicted it, or which control could have caught it. We define an episode record that ties a candidate fault to its origin, propagation, detection, response and consequence, located by operational phase and state domain, and that names the control families whose observation and reach cover it. We turned the record into a written annotation protocol and applied it to 95 failed runs of six multi-agent systems from the public Who&When and MAD corpora, reading each trajectory i
s6a904438c6.summary: Empirical study proposes an episode record that traces where errors enter, propagate, and are detected in long-horizon LLM agent trajectories, and which controls could catch them.
s6a904438c6.why: Gives engineers a framework for diagnosing root causes of multi-step agent failures rather than only labeling symptoms.

s7dc37bfaaa.title: Towards Scalable Network-Based Interventions for HIV Treatment and Prevention via R2C-Agent
s7dc37bfaaa.description: arXiv:2611.13312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) remains a pressing public health challenge worldwide. Targeting limited HIV prevention and treatment resources effectively with network-based algorithms is a long-standing problem with a rich history at AAMAS and other computational venues. However, optimizing targeted biomedical interventions for minimizing spread of HIV often requires observability of the contact network of HIV transmission risk behavior among individuals, which is prohibitively expensive to collect at scale. Peer referral networks, i.e., networks collected through a recursive peer referral process, are an alternative network class often used to study HIV in hidden populations that can be collected digitally at scale, but they deviate from
s7dc37bfaaa.summary: Introduces R2C-Agent, an approach for network-based HIV intervention targeting using peer referral networks in place of expensive full contact-network observation.

s7ebed4a663.title: F3-AGI v4.0: Bioenergetically-Gated Active Inference, Metaplastic Preconditioning, and Residual Program Synthesis for Sample-Efficient Abstract Reasoning
s7ebed4a663.description: arXiv:2611.13325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Few-shot abstract reasoning on ARC-AGI requires inducing algorithmic transformations from 2 to 5 demonstration pairs without task-specific pretraining. Because few-shot demonstrations under-constrain the hypothesis space, program synthesis suffers from the Rashomon effect (predictive multiplicity): heuristic search finds spurious programs with low training error that fail on test inputs, while unconstrained library growth degrades latency. We introduce F3-AGI v4.0, a CPU-native neuro-symbolic and active inference architecture comprising three mechanisms: (1) F3-Metabolic-Optim, combining mistake-gated plasticity, Fisher-EMA preconditioning, and virtual ATP gating; (2) Adaptive Complexity-Guided Program Synthesis (AACR) with a Cycle-3 Residual
s7ebed4a663.summary: F3-AGI v4.0 is a CPU-native neuro-symbolic and active inference architecture for few-shot abstract reasoning on ARC-AGI, aiming to reduce spurious programs.
s7ebed4a663.why: It targets sample-efficient program synthesis without pretraining, a problem relevant to engineers building reasoning systems under limited demonstrations.

s60af3987b6.title: Agent-Guided Discovery of Exchange-Correlation Functionals with Physics-based Validation
s60af3987b6.description: arXiv:2611.13329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate, compact exchange--correlation functionals are central to predictive density functional theory. Symbolic search and language-model agents can propose new functional forms, but it remains unclear whether their gains survive self-consistency and external evaluation, whether the new terms carry physical content, whether agents outperform evolutionary search, and how language-model backbones compare. We connect frontier LLM agents to a GPU evaluator through the Model Context Protocol, with training-only fitting, persistent memory, and self-consistent and external evaluation. Opus-5.5 agents passed the screening gate with about 40-fold fewer tokens than Codex (GPT-6-Astra) agents and found a candidate with lower validation and held-out er
s60af3987b6.summary: Researchers connect frontier LLM agents to a GPU evaluator via Model Context Protocol to discover exchange-correlation functionals, validated with physics-based checks.
s60af3987b6.why: It shows LLM agents proposing scientific models with validation against external evaluation, a pattern useful for building agentic discovery pipelines.

s555c7b027b.title: Do AI Agents need Preventive Care? An Epidemiologic Cohort Design for Agentic AI
s555c7b027b.description: arXiv:2611.13333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI agents increasingly perform tasks autonomously across sectors, including healthcare and biomedical research, understanding how their behaviors develop and influence outcomes over time becomes increasingly important. Existing evaluations largely focus on model capabilities and performance on predefined tasks. Here, we propose an epidemiologic cohort design for studying agentic AI, drawing on principles established in human population studies. The framework treats individual agents as members of a cohort, their underlying model as genetic makeup, accumulated work as their time scale, and naturally occurring behaviors as exposures that may influence subsequent outcomes. By following agents longitudinally, this approach enables investigatio
s555c7b027b.summary: A paper proposes an epidemiologic cohort design for studying agentic AI, treating individual agents as members of a cohort to track behavior over time.
s555c7b027b.why: It suggests longitudinal monitoring of deployed agents, which may matter for teams evaluating agent behavior beyond fixed benchmarks.

s00283657fe.title: Disentangling Multimodal Rotary Positional Embedding in Vision-Language Models
s00283657fe.description: arXiv:2611.13334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models widely adopt Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding (MRoPE), an extension of Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) that incorporates temporal, height, and width axes to encode the spatial structure of visual tokens. However, MRoPE also assigns height and width coordinates to text tokens that lack inherent spatial structure, introducing spatial positional effects into text-vision attention. Existing MRoPE variants explore different frequency allocations and coordinate layouts, with their designs suggesting different intuitions about these cross-modal effects: they may provide useful spatial references for associating language with visual regions, or introduce unnecessary positional preferences that hinder text-vision interactio
s00283657fe.summary: A paper examines Multimodal Rotary Position Embedding in vision-language models, finding that assigning height and width coordinates to text tokens introduces spatial effects.
s00283657fe.why: It highlights a positional-encoding issue in VLMs that could affect text-vision attention in models engineers build or fine-tune.

sa3171b4b89.title: Veritas: A Verifier Generation Harness for Agent Tasks
sa3171b4b89.description: arXiv:2611.13336v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effectiveness of a self-improving system relies heavily on the quality of its verifier, which judges the outcome of each improvement round. However, the verifiers of most tasks are written by hand, which is expensive and does not scale to tasks that come without one. We propose Veritas, a harness that generates verifiers automatically. Unlike general-purpose agent harnesses, Veritas adds three mechanisms for verifier generation: an evidence header stating what the verifier will observe, a library of domain rules that tasks leave unstated, and authoring principles, partly refined by a self-improvement loop. We evaluate on six benchmarks: four scored by execution, whose official verifiers we first certify, and two that compare pairs of resp
sa3171b4b89.summary: Veritas is a harness that automatically generates verifiers for agent tasks, using evidence headers, domain-rule libraries, and related mechanisms.
sa3171b4b89.why: Automatically generated verifiers could reduce the manual cost of evaluating self-improving agent systems.

sf7cfe52357.title: Multi-Stage Phase-Aware Self-Supervised Reconstruction for Multi-Echo Gradient-Echo MRI
sf7cfe52357.description: arXiv:2611.13352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: To develop a phase-aware self-supervised framework for accelerated high-resolution multi-echo gradient-echo (mGRE) MRI that preserves anatomical detail and complex echo information for quantitative mapping. Methods: We developed multi-stage phase-aware self-supervised reconstruction (MSPR-GRE), integrating progressive k-space expansion with phase estimation and refinement. Sequential unrolled networks reconstruct complex multi-echo images and update echo-dependent phase priors. A relaxation-informed temporal subspace is used for acquisitions with at least four echoes, while shorter echo trains are reconstructed in the image domain. Training uses held-out acquired k-space samples without fully sampled targets. Evaluation included 9.4
sf7cfe52357.summary: Researchers present MSPR-GRE, a multi-stage phase-aware self-supervised reconstruction method for accelerated multi-echo gradient-echo MRI.

sdaf4dd6995.title: A Technique to Model Product Information and User Reviews (MPIUR)
sdaf4dd6995.description: arXiv:2611.13361v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern e-commerce platforms naturally provide three complementary modalities: textual item descriptions, item images, and user reviews. However, existing multimodal recommendation methods often omit reviews or do not integrate all three modalities within a unified framework. In this paper, we propose MPIUR, a multimodal graph-based recommendation model that encodes reviews in heterogeneous graphs, aligns image and text representations, and adapts collaborative--semantic alignment to item interaction density. Experiments on the Amazon Reviews 2023 Musical Instruments and Baby categories show that MPIUR achieves the best global nDCG@10 and Recall@10 among the evaluated methods on both datasets. It also obtains the best nDCG@10 and Recall@10 on
sdaf4dd6995.summary: MPIUR is a multimodal graph-based recommendation model that combines product descriptions, images, and user reviews within a unified framework.
sdaf4dd6995.why: It offers a unified approach to integrating text, image and review signals in e-commerce recommendations, relevant to recommender system builders.

s654e4d0d98.title: No finite rulebook can certify every safe program: an impossibility theorem for gatekeeping AI agents
s654e4d0d98.description: arXiv:2611.13367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An AI assistant writes small programs, and a gatekeeper must decide, from the code alone, whether each one may run. Suppose the rules are fixed: never perform a forbidden action, never let the output depend on a secret, always answer eventually. Can two rulebooks, one listing what is allowed and one listing what is not, both be complete, if every rule must be backed by evidence that a machine can check in finite time? We prove that they cannot. Checkable evidence can only establish what a finite record settles, and ``never'' and ``eventually'' are never settled by a finite record. For prohibitions the failure is one-sided: every violation can be caught by watching, but no safe program can be cleared for good. For confidentiality and responsiv
s654e4d0d98.summary: A paper argues that no finite rulebook can certify every safe program, proving an impossibility result for gatekeeping AI agents' generated code.
s654e4d0d98.why: It implies static rule-based gatekeeping of agent-generated code cannot be fully complete, so guardrails need layered design beyond fixed rules.

sf719d44769.title: Online-Adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps for Neuro-symbolic Financial Forecasting
sf719d44769.description: arXiv:2611.13388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a neuro-symbolic framework that pairs online-adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (FCMs) with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for financial forecasting. Financial markets exhibit regime shifts and nonlinear dynamics. Existing models often trade off one of these key properties: these models capture temporal patterns but hide causal drivers, or they recover causal graphs that cannot adapt post-training. We close this gap with two frameworks. Framework I constructs an FCM from live dual-source price series and macroeconomic indicators, and adapts its edges online through an error-driven Hebbian rule. We introduce the Asymmetric Additive Residual Fusion method to seamlessly combine the FCM and LSTM predictions under Framework I. Framew
sf719d44769.summary: A neuro-symbolic framework pairs online-adaptive Fuzzy Cognitive Maps with LSTM networks for financial forecasting across regime shifts.

s65031a1a53.title: Living constitutions: Participatory alignment for sovereign foundation models
s65031a1a53.description: arXiv:2611.13402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Constitutional AI, a plain-text "constitution" encodes values and gets incorporated into a model via post-training. However, the procedure for creating such a constitution poses significant challenges: who contributes, who decides which norms are included, and to what extent must the process be participatory or democratic? These challenges can be paralyzing. Yet, we argue that taking action is essential: without a deliberate constitution, sovereign models would risk misalignment or default to norms set by frontier model providers. We propose treating the development of a constitution as an evolving, participatory process akin to citizen science, iteratively drafted, tested, and refined. We therefore formulate five desirable principles: ite
s65031a1a53.summary: The paper proposes participatory processes for creating constitutions for sovereign foundation models used in Constitutional AI post-training.
s65031a1a53.why: It raises governance questions for teams deciding which values and norms their own fine-tuned models should encode.

s9d5773919c.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
s9d5773919c.description: arXiv:2611.13410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-bit quantization reduces the inference cost of LLM agents but can compromise task success. Examining failed rollouts, we find that quantized agents overlook task requirements or environmental conditions, producing environment transitions that diverge from successful full-precision references. Correcting these behavioral divergences remains difficult: offline data may miss the student's failure contexts, while its own rollouts may provide few correct responses in those contexts. We introduce SteerDistill, a quantization-aware distillation method in which a full-precision teacher guides the student to revise failed responses and iteratively refines its guidance using feedback from student execution. This closed-loop teacher steering produce
s9d5773919c.summary: SteerDistill is a quantization-aware distillation method that uses closed-loop teacher steering to recover task success in low-bit quantized LLM agents.
s9d5773919c.why: It addresses accuracy loss when quantizing agents to cut inference cost, directly relevant to teams deploying cheaper agent models.

s97ab6cd013.title: SafeRoute-MAS: Coverage-Aware and Risk-Calibrated Message Routing for Multi-Agent Scientific Reasoning
s97ab6cd013.description: arXiv:2611.13454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce SafeRoute-MAS, a coverage-aware, risk-calibrated procedure that keeps all specialist messages or removes one using only pre-integration information. On a sealed cache of 5,328 committees, its source-compatible operating point gains +1.80 percentage points (95% CI [+1.13, +2.52]) while removing 12.76% of message tokens. We also run 4,580 controlled integrations over a stratified 458-committee sample on a public gpt-oss-120b endpoint. The sample estimate is -0.09 points; design weighting to the original workload gives +0.94 points (95% CI [-1.31, +3.50]) and 18.72% acted-input reduction. A weighted token-matched comparison likewise does not establish a selector advantage (+1.68 points, CI [-1.27, +5.10]). Only 13 of 88 cached non-n
s97ab6cd013.summary: SafeRoute-MAS is a coverage-aware, risk-calibrated procedure that keeps or removes specialist messages in multi-agent scientific reasoning, reporting token savings.
s97ab6cd013.why: It reports a token reduction in multi-agent message passing, which could lower costs for multi-agent systems.

s7d4a8da4bf.title: When Reasoning looks like Hidden Understanding: How Chain-of-Thought Fosters Anthropomorphism, Perceptions of Epistemic Superiority, and Cognitive Deference
s7d4a8da4bf.description: arXiv:2611.13456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI-based products permeate society, specifically systems using generative models, a belief system is emerging about what these products are and what they can and cannot do. One common belief concerns the perception of the form of language as evidence of 'understanding' language. As these generative models reproduce linguistic patterns rather than understand meaning, interpreting these patterns as evidence of understanding is a misattribution. This misconception is extended by the notion that generative models can 'explain their reasoning.' Anecdotally, these misconceptions which mistake the form of language for its meaning are driving cognitive deference to AI systems in a way that displaces human agency. Such mistakes involve attributions
s7d4a8da4bf.summary: A paper studies how chain-of-thought reasoning displays foster anthropomorphism, perceived epistemic superiority, and cognitive deference among users.
s7d4a8da4bf.why: It suggests that exposing reasoning traces in products can shape user trust in ways product teams should account for.

s332ba74db4.title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
s332ba74db4.description: arXiv:2611.13487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing Chinese educational corpora often suffer from fragmented coverage and a lack of systematic organization. In this paper, we propose WoW (\textbf{Wo}rld Kno\textbf{w}ledge), a large-scale dataset designed for the full-cycle training of foundation models. The construction of this dataset is driven by an Educational Knowledge Graph, which serves as a taxonomic backbone for the systematic collection and completion of missing educational modules across all levels. Compared to previous versions, this iteration provides enhanced systematicity, superior quality, and a larger scale, while incorporating multimodal signals and supporting every stage of model development. Experiments demonstrate that WoW significantly improves model performance a
s332ba74db4.summary: WoW is a large-scale Chinese world knowledge corpus built around an Educational Knowledge Graph for full-lifecycle foundation model training.

s4b7749e23d.title: Nepali-English Code-Mixed Speech Recognition: Data Preparation and Adaptation of a Speech Foundation Model
s4b7749e23d.description: arXiv:2611.13512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nepali speakers regularly mix English words into conversation, but multilingual speech recognisers often struggle with language switches and the writing script used for English words. We study how to adapt SraVaani, a 449M-parameter hybrid TDT-CTC model, using a 172.8-hour corpus covering six Nepali speech domains. Its pretrained tokenizer does not support digits and several common symbols. Rather than replace it or discard these recordings, we generate Nepali and English readings for numbers and use zero-shot ASR output to select a plausible form. Full fine-tuning reduces test word error rate (WER) from 48.6% to 17.1%; a 12-epoch run reaches 16.3%, compared with 16.4% for fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo. Freezing the encoder increases WER
s4b7749e23d.summary: Researchers adapt the 449M-parameter SraVaani hybrid speech model on 172.8 hours of Nepali speech, extending its tokenizer for digits and symbols for code-mixed English.
s4b7749e23d.why: It offers a practical recipe for adapting speech foundation models to code-switched, low-resource languages.

sdcbae86e00.title: Agent Benchmarks Stop Ranking Before They Run Out of Tasks
sdcbae86e00.description: arXiv:2611.13541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-science and ML-engineering agents are evaluated on benchmarks such as MLE-bench, ALE-Bench, SWE-fficiency and AlgoTune, whose tasks yield a quantity (a Kaggle metric, contest score or speedup). When one stops separating the best models, the usual remedy is a harder version. Re-scoring released runs of eight benchmarks, including SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench for breadth, we find much of this saturation lies in the measurement, not the tasks. Most agent benchmarks reduce a run to one pass/fail bit, which fails in two ways. It is too coarse: neighbouring top-ten agents on SWE-bench Verified differ by less than its tests' errors, and correcting them reorders neighbours no more than deleting a random sixth of each agent's passes. It
sdcbae86e00.summary: Researchers re-scored released runs of eight agent benchmarks and argue saturation stems from pass/fail measurement rather than the tasks themselves.
sdcbae86e00.why: Suggests teams should use richer scoring than a single pass/fail bit when judging agent benchmarks, so rankings stay informative longer.

s817a122912.title: Darmok: Championship Cryptic Crossword Solving via Constraint Tightening and Resilient Orchestration
s817a122912.description: arXiv:2611.13557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Darmok, the first automated system to reach superhuman performance on British cryptic crosswords. Unlike American-style crosswords, cryptic clues disguise an unmarked definition and compositional wordplay beneath a misleading surface reading, sparse grids leave nearly half of each word's letters unchecked, and tournament rules rank a grid with even a single wrong or blank square behind all error-free solutions regardless of speed. Competing alongside an elite human field at the 55th Times Crossword Championship in London, Darmok solved all seven championship puzzles error-free and finished faster than every human competitor in every round. It solved the Final puzzle in 6m 52s, a full 3m 13s ahead of the human champion. Today's fron
s817a122912.summary: Darmok, an automated system, reportedly reached superhuman performance on British cryptic crosswords and competed at the 55th Times Crossword Championship in London.
s817a122912.why: Shows an automated system handling ambiguous, compositional language puzzles at expert human level, though the text offers little on engineering details.

s0d7f29e3cd.title: Benchmarking Vendor-Guided Optimizations on Edge NPUs: From NPU Only to End-to-End Performance. Extended technical report
s0d7f29e3cd.description: arXiv:2611.13563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Edge NPU performance depends not only on hardware capabilities, but also on model transformation and the overall deployment pipeline. We propose a benchmarking methodology that separates these effects by comparing three configurations: Baseline, Vendor Guided NPU Only (VG-NPU), and Vendor Guided End-to-End (VG-E2E), where VG-NPU preserves common model I/O and host-side processing while VG-E2E follows the vendor-native deployment pipeline. We apply this methodology to four edge NPUs and three vision workloads. VG-NPU improves both accuracy and Runtime-call latency in 10 of 12 NPU--workload combinations, whereas VG-E2E reduces System-level latency in all combinations but improves accuracy in only four. Moreover, NPU-level performance rankings d
s0d7f29e3cd.summary: Researchers propose a benchmarking method comparing baseline, vendor-guided NPU-only, and vendor-guided end-to-end configurations across four edge NPUs and three vision workloads.
s0d7f29e3cd.why: Shows edge NPU performance depends on the full deployment pipeline, not just hardware, so benchmarks should measure end-to-end results.

s925194cc50.title: Transformers Provably Learn Graph Search: Training Dynamics and the Exponential Power of Depth
s925194cc50.description: arXiv:2611.13594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress on complex reasoning tasks, yet the mechanisms by which they acquire reasoning capabilities and the efficiency of their reasoning remain poorly understood. In this paper, we investigate the path-finding problem over directed graphs, a symbolic abstraction of multi-step reasoning. We first characterize the architectural requirements for this task, proving that one-layer transformers require $\Omega(N^2)$ size on dense graphs to implement the key DFS child-selection primitive. While a two-layer transformer implements full DFS with $O(N\log(N))$ size. Thus, a second layer is necessary and sufficient for near-linear DFS reasoning. We then extend this expressivity analysis to deeper mo
s925194cc50.summary: Paper proves theoretical architectural requirements for transformers on graph path-finding and analyzes training dynamics and the benefit of depth.
s925194cc50.why: Provides theoretical grounding on how depth affects transformer reasoning efficiency, though its practical implications for engineers remain indirect.

sbf5584c7f2.title: Towards Reliable VLM Judges: State-Conditional Invariance and Presentation-Aware Diagnostics
sbf5584c7f2.description: arXiv:2611.13596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for multimodal and embodied tasks, yet aggregate accuracy or consistency alone does not reveal whether a judge changes its verdict for the right reason. We propose State-Conditional Invariance (SCI), a reliability principle requiring a judge to remain stable under semantics-preserving changes in presentation while responding to causal interventions that change the task outcome. We instantiate SCI in GridWM-Judge, a simulator-grounded diagnostic benchmark built from deterministic MiniGrid trajectories with aligned Full, evidence-removal, and counterfactual variants, plus presentation and representation probes. Across five diagnostic tasks, GridWM-Judge tests local percepti
sbf5584c7f2.summary: Introduces State-Conditional Invariance and GridWM-Judge, a diagnostic benchmark testing whether vision-language model judges change verdicts for the right reasons.
sbf5584c7f2.why: Offers a way to test whether VLM-based evaluators are reliable, relevant for teams using models as automated judges.

sfc66a0be23.title: Earth Embeddings in Environmental Remote Sensing
sfc66a0be23.description: arXiv:2611.13612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Earth observations from satellite platforms have profoundly transformed research and applications across numerous domains. However, uneven observation coverage and frequent data gaps continue to limit their ability to capture Earth's surface dynamics. Moreover, processing multi-modal Earth observations requires substantial computational resources and sophisticated data harmonization frameworks, which may not be readily accessible to many remote sensing practitioners. Earth embeddings have emerged as promising solutions to these challenges. As general-purpose representations converted from multi-source Earth observations, Earth embeddings can support a wide range of downstream tasks with no requirement of task-specific feature design and prepr
sfc66a0be23.summary: A paper reviews Earth embeddings as a way to make multi-modal satellite observations more accessible for environmental remote sensing practitioners.
sfc66a0be23.why: Suggests pretrained embeddings could lower compute and harmonization barriers for geospatial data work, though the text gives limited specifics.

s8aa2adf327.title: Megrez: A Knowledge-Guided Agent for Formal Mathematics over MK Set Theory
s8aa2adf327.description: arXiv:2611.13613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose coding agents equipped with proof-assistant tools have shown strong performance on standalone competition problems, yet cumulative textbook formalization inside a low-resource mathematical library still faces three obstacles: aligning textbook concepts with library declarations, keeping long-horizon search synchronized with live proof states, and integrating locally verified proofs reliably into a growing codebase. We present Megrez, a knowledge-guided formalization agent for Rocq libraries built on Morse--Kelley (MK) set theory. Megrez coordinates a general coding agent through three mechanisms: (1) a source-rebuildable knowledge graph merging formal declarations, compiler references, and curated metadata to support retrieval
s8aa2adf327.summary: Megrez is a knowledge-guided coding agent for formalizing textbook mathematics in Rocq libraries built on Morse-Kelley set theory.
s8aa2adf327.why: Illustrates how domain knowledge can make coding agents more reliable when building and extending large verified codebases.

s0248e8342c.title: DrugCoding: A Scientific Programming Agent for Drug Discovery
s0248e8342c.description: arXiv:2611.13651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Drug discovery involves multiple interconnected research stages, including molecular design, property prediction, and virtual screening. These processes are characterized by complex workflows, interdependent computational tasks, and diverse specialized tools, placing substantial demands on the coordination of scientific models and computational resources. However, existing large language model (LLM)-based scientific agents still face challenges in autonomous planning of complex tasks, adaptive selection of specialized models, and reliable execution of multi-stage scientific computations, limiting their effectiveness in automating complex drug discovery workflows. To address these challenges, we propose DrugCoding, a scientific programming age
s0248e8342c.summary: DrugCoding is a scientific programming agent designed to plan drug discovery workflows, select specialized models, and execute computational tasks.
