s0248e8342c.why: Shows agent designs for coordinating multiple specialized scientific tools, a pattern relevant to complex domain pipelines.

sb199698e39.title: Benchmarking LLM Next-Step Recommendations with Knowledge Space Theory
sb199698e39.description: arXiv:2611.13667v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Selecting an LLM for next-step recommendation requires benchmarks that reflect the intended educational task and domain. We present a benchmarking method that uses Knowledge Space Theory (KST) as a formal evaluation reference. Given a task catalogue and an existing prerequisite relation, the method derives admissible knowledge states and the complete set of immediate next steps for each state. Recommendations generated by a model under a specified prompt are compared with these reference sets. A sample evaluation study uses 2,400 responses from six models across four mathematics domains, four prompt conditions, and two catalogue orders. Exact-set accuracy was 61.3% with descriptions only, 62.8% when models were asked to reconstruct prerequisi
sb199698e39.summary: Proposes a benchmark using Knowledge Space Theory as a formal reference to evaluate LLM next-step recommendations, with a sample study of 2,400 responses.
sb199698e39.why: Offers a formal, domain-grounded method for choosing LLMs in educational recommendation tasks rather than relying on generic benchmarks.

scc7b11ab42.title: A computational framework for understanding embodied plans
scc7b11ab42.description: arXiv:2611.13669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning about people's plans and goals based on their actions is fundamental to human social interaction and essential for cooperative, embodied artificial intelligence. Formalizing this capacity in naturalistic, embodied settings has been a longstanding challenge. Here, we present GenEA, a novel agent representation capable of reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans. At the heart of GenEA lies a multilevel state-space that couples the coarse biomechanics of an articulated body and its interactions with nearby objects by extending the task-and-motion planning framework from robotics with simulation-based intuitive physics. By embedding this state-space in a generative model, GenEA yields a joint probability distribution over
scc7b11ab42.summary: Introduces GenEA, an agent representation for reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans using a multilevel state-space.
scc7b11ab42.why: Relevant to embodied AI teams working on inferring human plans, though the practical deployment path is not described.

s7f4c5d8e8d.title: Topological Dynamics Under Non-Stationary Supervision: Persistent Homology of Neural Network Weight Evolution
s7f4c5d8e8d.description: arXiv:2611.13701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how the persistent topology of neuron- weight point clouds evolves under stable and non-stationary supervision. An identical multilayer perceptron is trained on Fashion-MNIST with correct labels, a fixed random permutation of the training-label vector, or a fresh permutation every epoch. Five paired seeds share initialisation and minibatch order, yielding 15 models trained for 100 epochs. Raw and row-normalised incoming weight clouds are analysed with H0 and H1 Vietoris Rips persistence at 22 checkpoints. Correct-label models reach 89.39% mean true-label test accuracy; fixed-random models fit 67.94% of their assigned training targets without generalising to the original task. Correct-label models have descriptively greater time
s7f4c5d8e8d.summary: Study tracks persistent homology of neuron-weight point clouds in an MLP trained on Fashion-MNIST under correct, fixed, and per-epoch permuted labels.

s67622406a1.title: SeqFold: Timestamp-Addressable Compressed States for User Action Sequence Backbones
s67622406a1.description: arXiv:2611.13704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing sequential user modeling methods mainly focus on improving the backbone encoder or learning task-specific user representations for a single prediction objective. We instead study how to export the multi-layer user states of a frozen long-history backbone as compact, timestamp-addressable representations for downstream training backfill and serving. In this setting, the user state at a given timestamp summarizes the user's actions before that time, so downstream systems need only the state aligned to each target timestamp rather than the full hidden-state timeline. To this end, we present \texttt{SeqFold}, a compressed-state interface that combines learned multi-channel fusion, channel-specific temporal decay, and Lookup-Free Quantiza
s67622406a1.summary: SeqFold proposes exporting multi-layer user states from a frozen long-history backbone as compact, timestamp-addressable representations for downstream systems.
s67622406a1.why: Offers a serving-oriented approach to reuse long user-action histories without re-running the full backbone for each prediction target.

sbe598c7556.title: Agentic AI Meets Formal Verification in the Era of Agentic Hardware Development
sbe598c7556.description: arXiv:2611.13705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI agents become increasingly capable of generating and optimizing hardware circuits, ensuring the correctness of AI-generated designs becomes more important. Meanwhile, advances in AI lower the barriers to developing and applying formal methods, creating new opportunities to automate and improve hardware verification. This invited paper presents an overview of the methodologies and applications of hardware formal methods in the AI era. First, we examine how agentic AI advances hardware formal methods across three levels: specification, proof construction, and reasoning engines. Second, we discuss how formal methods support reliable AI-driven hardware development through RTL generation, debugging, and correctness-preserving optimization. W
sbe598c7556.summary: Invited paper surveys how agentic AI can advance hardware formal verification across specification, proof, and related stages of circuit design.
sbe598c7556.why: Highlights growing need to verify AI-generated hardware designs, a concern for teams adopting agentic chip development.

s6f21f818dd.title: AutoManifold: Agentic Design of Data Visualisation Algorithms via Manifold Embedding
s6f21f818dd.description: arXiv:2611.13710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Manifold embedding for data visualisation is dominated by a small set of hand-designed state-of-the-art (SOTA) algorithms. Their design targets are fixed at development time, resulting in inflexible algorithmic behaviour that cannot be readily steered towards user-specified structural priorities. Hand-designing new embedding algorithms to address user priority requires highly specialised expertise and is time consuming. To address autonomous algorithm design tailored to user preference, we introduce an agentic algorithm generation pipeline AutoManifold. It composes new manifold embedding algorithms from a constrained vocabulary of affinity, cost, and optimisation primitives, supported by multi-agent large-language-model (LLM) orchestration. A
s6f21f818dd.summary: AutoManifold is an agentic pipeline that automatically generates manifold embedding algorithms tailored to user-specified structural priorities for data visualisation.
s6f21f818dd.why: Shows agents automating algorithm design for visualization, though the text offers limited detail on performance or availability.

sd9f43b94a1.title: Broad-Persistent Advising in Interactive Reinforcement Learning via Latent State Encoding
sd9f43b94a1.description: arXiv:2611.13712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep Interactive Reinforcement Learning (Deep IntRL) accelerates reinforcement learning training by incorporating external advice. However, conventional Deep IntRL uses each piece of advice only in the current step and discards it after a single interaction. Persistent Advising and Broad-Persistent Advising (BPA) extend this process by storing advice in persistent memory and reusing it in similar states through state generalisation based on K-means clustering. This research proposes Encoder BPA, which employs a latent encoder to retrieve and reuse advice. In this framework, a trained encoder is used to map a state sequence into a latent representation at every time step. Advice can be retrieved through latent comparison, together with a top-(
sd9f43b94a1.summary: Proposes Encoder BPA, which uses a latent encoder to retrieve and reuse stored external advice in interactive reinforcement learning.
sd9f43b94a1.why: Offers a refinement for speeding reinforcement learning with human advice, but its relevance outside research settings is limited.

sa2c06c3017.title: Toward Autonomous RTL and Synthesis Optimization: Benchmarking and Self-Improving Agents
sa2c06c3017.description: arXiv:2611.13713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and autonomous agents are creating new opportunities for hardware design optimization. This paper examines three connected directions toward autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization: (1) Realistic benchmarking. We discuss reference-based and open-ended RTL optimization benchmarks that evaluate optimization opportunities under realistic EDA workflows. (2) Tool-grounded RTL optimization. We present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework that automates critical-path analysis, RTL rewriting, and implementation-level evaluation, while continuously improving through reusable optimization skills. Evaluated on 20 real-world RTL designs, Dr.~RTL achieves average WNS/TNS improvements of 21\%/17\% with a 6\% ar
sa2c06c3017.summary: Researchers discuss benchmarks for autonomous RTL and synthesis optimization and present Dr. RTL, a multi-agent framework for critical-path analysis and RTL rewriting.
sa2c06c3017.why: Shows LLM agents being applied to hardware design workflows, with benchmarks for evaluating RTL optimization under realistic EDA flows.

s6449663e12.title: Integrating Action Prefix Prediction and Alignment Across Modalities for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
s6449663e12.description: arXiv:2611.13782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning representations from multimodal observations is difficult in reinforcement learning with limited interaction data. Multimodal Joint Predictive Representation combines multimodal latent prediction with contrastive learning across modalities, but its recursive rollout depends on earlier predictions and its pairwise alignment focuses on correspondence between modalities. We propose Improved Predictive Representation, which combines prediction from action prefixes with alignment at the observed anchor based on Contrastive Multimodal learning. At each horizon, it predicts future representations directly from the observed anchor and the corresponding sequence of actions. We evaluate two crop configurations: IPR-S with a minimum retained cr
s6449663e12.summary: Researchers propose Improved Predictive Representation, combining action-prefix prediction with anchor-based multimodal contrastive alignment for reinforcement learning.

scbf32c0366.title: Ceci n'est pas une pipe -- Toward a Symbolic Solver for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus Using Evolutionary Computation
scbf32c0366.description: arXiv:2611.13831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) is a benchmark designed to assess the capability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems to generalize starting from a few samples, a task humans excel at. The ARC-AGI contests held since 2020 have been the focus of intense competition, with participants proposing approaches ranging from traditional symbolic AI to Transformer architectures. Despite a long history of successes, evolutionary algorithms (EAs) were notably absent from the approaches appearing in the main contest. As score-and-search program synthesis approaches, EAs suffer from issues related to choosing the proper representation in the Domain-Specific Language applied to the problem (for example, pixel-level or object-level), and distin
scbf32c0366.summary: Researchers explore an evolutionary-computation symbolic solver for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus, an area largely absent from ARC-AGI contest entries.

sb3c538648c.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
sb3c538648c.description: arXiv:2611.13850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot's physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track
sb3c538648c.summary: Researchers present URDF2Ontology, an LLM-assisted neurosymbolic framework that converts raw URDF robot files into grounded OWL ontologies for task reasoning.
sb3c538648c.why: Offers a way to add formal semantic context to robot descriptions, which could ease symbolic task allocation in robotics systems.

s4752feadf9.title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
s4752feadf9.description: arXiv:2611.13914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To
s4752feadf9.summary: Researchers propose using LLMs to turn counterfactual edits for recommender systems into coherent human-readable narratives instead of long low-level edit lists.

s1927375398.title: Beyond Proxy Metrics: MLLMs as Human Surrogates for Explainable AI Evaluation
s1927375398.description: arXiv:2611.13926v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has expanded into a broad and impactful research area, but the fundamental question of how best to evaluate explanation techniques has proven frustratingly elusive. Methodologies typically revolve around either proxy metrics which tell us little about the utility of an explanation, or human evaluation which---while generally considered the gold standard---is expensive, difficult to scale, and challenging to reproduce. In this paper, we investigate if Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can act as surrogate human participants to automate the evaluation of XAI. To do this, we first propose a ``purpose-grounded'' evaluation framework with metrics applicable to both MLLMs and human users alike. Then, we offer some concep
s1927375398.summary: Researchers investigate whether multimodal LLMs can act as surrogate human participants for evaluating explainable AI techniques.
s1927375398.why: Could offer a cheaper, more reproducible alternative to human studies for evaluating explanation methods, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sa5ae3cddbb.title: TreeAgent: Structure-Aware Memory Agent for Processing Long Hierarchical Data
sa5ae3cddbb.description: arXiv:2611.13946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Practical Web applications increasingly require agents to interpret long conversations or documents. For inputs exceeding the context windows of large language models (LLMs), memory agents process segments sequentially and retain past information in bounded memory. However, they typically divide inputs into flat token segments without preserving structure or hierarchy, causing three limitations for structured data such as API responses or HTML documents. First, fixed-length segmentation can split fields of the same record, breaking their relationships. Second, segments lack hierarchical information, obscuring their structural context and positions. Third, successive memory updates may discard details of earlier sibling records needed for reas
sa5ae3cddbb.summary: Researchers introduce TreeAgent, a structure-aware memory agent that segments long hierarchical data like API responses and HTML while preserving record structure.
sa5ae3cddbb.why: Addresses fixed-length chunking breaking related fields in structured inputs, relevant to agents processing long API or web documents.

s7b6925d8ed.title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries
s7b6925d8ed.description: arXiv:2611.13975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, the nature of expert specialization remains controversial. Reports of domain-associated expert preferences contrast with analyses attributing routing primarily to token identity or syntactic patterns. To clarify these differing accounts, we look beyond expert-level routing to investigate the neuron-level organization of domain-specialized computation using Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling (RAMP), a measure developed for this analysis. Using mixed-domain calibration data, we identify domain-specialized neuron sets with 58-74% overlap across multi-source samples of the same domain, compared with 15-24% across domains. To understand how this organization evolves during training, we trace neuron importance thr
s7b6925d8ed.summary: Researchers use Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling to study neuron-level organization of domain specialization in Mixture-of-Experts language models.
s7b6925d8ed.why: Clarifies whether MoE expert specialization reflects domains or token patterns, informing how engineers interpret and debug MoE models.

s22c74d91a0.title: Personalized Memory Rubrics: Learning What to Remember per User via Rubric-Guided Credit Assignment
s22c74d91a0.description: arXiv:2611.14017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon personalized agents maintain an evolving memory by continuously deciding what to add, modify, or discard. However, learning an optimal update policy remains challenging. Conventional training relies solely on terminal question-answering accuracy, yielding a coarse feedback signal that treats all intermediate updates identically. Furthermore, update utility is inherently user-specific, as identical memory actions may yield opposite effects across different user personas. Existing methods fail to address this heterogeneity, relying on globally shared evaluation standards with at most a single scalar intermediate reward. To address these challenges, we propose \textbf{Personalized Memory Rubrics} (\textbf{PMR}), a framework that tra
s22c74d91a0.summary: Researchers propose Personalized Memory Rubrics, using rubric-guided credit assignment to learn per-user memory update policies for long-horizon personalized agents.
s22c74d91a0.why: Targets the problem of coarse terminal-only feedback in training agent memory updates, relevant to building personalized assistants.

see0ce55992.title: Hx2Dx: From Anamnesis to Diagnosis - A Multimodal Arena for Conversational Clinical Reasoning in LLMs
see0ce55992.description: arXiv:2611.14122v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve expert-level diagnostic accuracy in static evaluations, where the model receives a curated vignette or case report that already condenses the diagnostically relevant findings. Such evaluations measure inference over already selected evidence; the evaluations do not account for the inquiry used to obtain it. In clinical practice, however, diagnosis is an iterative process of inquiry. Clinicians take the patient's history, or anamnesis (Hx), through targeted questioning, examine the patient, and request and interpret tests, progressively narrowing the differential until they reach a final diagnosis (Dx). We introduce Hx2Dx ARENA, an interactive benchmark of 1'000 clinical cases from the New England Journal o
see0ce55992.summary: Researchers introduce Hx2Dx, a multimodal arena that evaluates LLMs on conversational clinical reasoning, where diagnosis requires iterative history-taking rather than curated vignettes.
see0ce55992.why: Highlights that static diagnostic benchmarks miss the inquiry process, a gap relevant to evaluating LLMs in clinical settings.

s0bd64d4e0b.title: BARS: Budget-Aware Sequential Sampling with Refusal for Majority Identification under Unknown Distributions
s0bd64d4e0b.description: arXiv:2611.14171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeated sampling with majority selection is an effective means of enforcing self-consistency in large language models. Recently, a variant has also been introduced that terminates early to save costs when the output distribution is favorable. But it still cannot yield a correct confidence estimate from the answer distribution. For this issue, we formalize this as majority identification under an unknown distribution with a budget and a target error rate, and propose BARS, a sequential rule certifying the top-two gap and returning an early stop, a budgeted majority vote, or a refusal when feasibility cannot be established. A refusal is a statement about the rule and its budget, not a claim that a question is unanswerable, and it tells practit
s0bd64d4e0b.summary: Researchers propose BARS, a budget-aware sequential sampling rule with refusal for majority identification in LLM repeated sampling under unknown output distributions.
s0bd64d4e0b.why: Offers a statistically certified early-stopping method for self-consistency sampling, which could reduce LLM inference costs.

s0f508bc7c4.title: Cross-Border Fulfillment Center Selection via Doubly Robust Estimation and Linear Programming
s0f508bc7c4.description: arXiv:2611.14174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the cross-border (XB) fulfillment center (FC) Selection Model: a multi-stage optimization framework combining forecasting, doubly robust estimation, and linear programming to select optimal source FCs. For each source-destination shipping arc, the objective is to choose a subset of source-country FCs that minimize delivery time and cost while maximizing profit and shipped units under a fixed domestic network. We evaluate the model on three production-scale international shipping corridors for a large e-commerce company using 12 months of shipment data, employing both aggregate offline replay and shipment-level counterfactual nearest-neighbor matching. Across all shipping corridors, the XB FC Selection Model achieves 8.5-51.1% red
s0f508bc7c4.summary: Researchers present a cross-border fulfillment center selection model combining forecasting, doubly robust estimation, and linear programming, evaluated on e-commerce shipping corridors.

s760a620198.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming
s760a620198.description: arXiv:2611.14183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal-difference critics regress onto a bootstrapped target and usually need a target network. Lifted Bellman Linear Programming (LBLP) instead expresses the in-sample optimal values of offline RL as the solution to a linear program over the dataset. Its neural solver ALBUM relaxes the constraints into hinge penalties with fixed coefficients, and its guarantees are conditions on coefficients chosen in advance. We solve the same program with the method of multipliers: the coefficients become multipliers learned by dual ascent, with one penalty parameter $\rho$. In the convex case the fixed points are the KKT pairs of LBLP, and at every stationary point the applied constraint weights balance the objective exactly. The critic can serve a Gaus
s760a620198.summary: Researchers propose solving the Lifted Bellman Linear Programming problem with the method of multipliers, learning coefficients via dual ascent for offline RL.

s3567100223.title: Joint Quantization and Dynamic Partitioning for Context-Aware Edge Vision Transformers
s3567100223.description: arXiv:2611.14196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying vision transformer models across connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) requires joint management of computation and Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication. Static split-inference methods use fixed partition points and cannot adapt to time-varying link bandwidth, processing load, and concurrent multi-stream traffic. This paper proposes an edge orchestration framework that jointly selects model partition points, per-layer quantization bitwidths, and execution placement across heterogeneous vehicular compute nodes. The joint partitioning and mixed-precision allocation problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Linear Program (MILP) that minimizes compute and communication energy subject to end-to-end latency and task-quality constraint
s3567100223.summary: Researchers propose an edge orchestration framework that jointly selects vision transformer partition points, quantization bitwidths, and placement across connected vehicles.
s3567100223.why: Addresses running vision transformers on vehicles under varying bandwidth and load, relevant to edge deployment engineering.

s37bfbe069a.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
s37bfbe069a.description: arXiv:2611.14209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: During extended wakefulness, mammalian neocortical networks experience localized periods of transient neuronal silence termed off-states. Here, we examine how analogous spatiotemporally concentrated disruptions affect sequential reasoning in autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). Evaluating 250 paired derivations on the GSM8K benchmark across two 8B models (Qwen3-8B and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct), we contrast clustered bursts of attention head masking against budget-matched diffuse i.i.d. dropout. Concentrated bursts induce substantial reasoning degradation: at onset parameter $\mathcal{B}=0.10$ (scheduling $\sim 5.7\%$ of vulnerable head-token volume), Qwen3-8B accuracy drops from $91.2\%$ under diffuse noise to $78.8\%$ under burst dropou
s37bfbe069a.summary: Researchers find that concentrated bursts of attention head masking degrade multi-step reasoning in 8B LLMs more than budget-matched diffuse dropout on GSM8K.
s37bfbe069a.why: Suggests that how attention faults are distributed matters for reasoning robustness, relevant to reliability testing of deployed LLMs.

se53b9c7c62.title: Personalized Affective Perception via Continual Learning in Human-Agent Negotiation
se53b9c7c62.description: arXiv:2611.14247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-interested intelligent agents that negotiate with humans should interpret nonverbal expressions and adapt their behavior accordingly. However, generic facial-affect models degrade across individuals and contexts, creating a generalization gap. We introduce an affect-adaptive negotiation strategy that incorporates Continual Learning with Imagination for Facial Expression Recognition (CLIFER) to personalize valence-arousal perception in real time. Differential feedback converts changes in valence-arousal direction and intensity into adjustments of the agent's target utility. An asynchronous architecture updates CLIFER in the background during live interaction. In a counterbalanced within-subject study in which 66 participants negotiated wi
se53b9c7c62.summary: Researchers propose an affect-adaptive negotiation strategy using continual learning (CLIFER) to personalize facial valence-arousal perception in real time during human-agent negotiation.
se53b9c7c62.why: Generic facial-affect models degrade across individuals, so continual personalization may matter for agents interacting with humans in varied contexts.

s67e1d3f3c6.title: A Cross-Scenario Survey and Analysis of Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents
s67e1d3f3c6.description: arXiv:2611.14256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work shows that multimodal agents increasingly self-improve without recurring human annotation. However, each self-improvement mechanism is designed and evaluated within a single scenario, leaving its preconditions unverified under cross-scenario transfer. This survey investigates the structural source of asymmetric mechanism transfer across four scenarios: multimodal reasoning, multimodal generation, GUI and Web navigation, and embodied manipulation. We first formalize the self-evolving multimodal agent by four criteria and a differentia of self-reference, and adopt the three-stage self-evolving loop of experience generation, feedback acquisition, and update consolidation as our analytical framework to position the scenarios along cei
s67e1d3f3c6.summary: A survey examines how self-improvement mechanisms for multimodal agents transfer, or fail to transfer, across four scenarios including reasoning, generation, GUI navigation, and embodied manipulation.
s67e1d3f3c6.why: Self-improvement methods validated in one scenario may not carry over to others, which affects how teams adopt them.

s526c715ee2.title: Recurrent Modular Structure in Spiking Neural Network Reinforcement Learning
s526c715ee2.description: arXiv:2611.14262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Biological neural circuits are both modular and recurrent, with dense communities sparsely linked to one another. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) for reinforcement learning are usually feed-forward, and it is unclear how to obtain functional modules in a recurrent SNN or what they buy. In this work, we introduce a class of spiking networks, called Community Recurrent SNNs (CoRe SNNs): recurrent networks partitioned into communities with fixed roles. A controller community receives the stimulus, each action has its own community, and latent communities carry internal state. Spiking activity is then a walk between communities, and the action is the community the walk reaches. All learning is local and three-factor, and the recurrent communities
s526c715ee2.summary: Researchers introduce Community Recurrent SNNs, recurrent spiking networks partitioned into fixed-role communities, for reinforcement learning.

sf6be5bac9a.title: LM-SimBench: A Unified Framework, Dataset, and Benchmark for Large Language Model Training Simulation
sf6be5bac9a.description: arXiv:2611.14285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating candidate parallelization strategies through distributed training runs makes strategy selection prohibitively expensive at scale. Performance simulation offers a lower cost alternative, yet controlled comparisons among existing simulators remain difficult because they differ in the training stages they model and the workloads on which they are evaluated. We introduce LM-SimBench, a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for evaluating LLM training simulators. The framework decomposes simulation into functional stages from model compilation to schedule level aggregation, connecting execution representations and cost estimators to measurable evaluation targets. Following this framework, we profile 23 model settings from
sf6be5bac9a.summary: Researchers introduce LM-SimBench, a unified framework, profiling dataset, and benchmark for evaluating LLM training simulators used to compare parallelization strategies.
sf6be5bac9a.why: Simulators can cheaply rank parallelization strategies before costly distributed runs, so controlled benchmarks help teams choose tools.

s13ac1f5091.title: Multimodal Abstention That Preserves Acquired Correct Answers
s13ac1f5091.description: arXiv:2611.14311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adding abstention to a task-adapted multimodal model can discard correct answers, including capabilities acquired during adaptation. We formulate abstention repair as maximizing correct abstention on unanswerable questions under a budget on newly lost correct answers. We propose ReFrain (Regression-Free Abstention), which combines a linear probe on first-token logits, threshold calibration on held-out image clusters, and a deterministic veto that replaces rejected outputs with the displayed "none of the above" option while preserving all other responses. "Regression-free" denotes zero loss on the calibration set at the zero-budget target. All abstention methods in our main comparison start from the same answering-SFT checkpoint; we separately
s13ac1f5091.summary: Researchers propose ReFrain, a method that adds abstention to task-adapted multimodal models while limiting newly lost correct answers.
s13ac1f5091.why: Adding abstention to fine-tuned models can silently discard capabilities, so regression-controlled methods matter when deploying them.

sd8b62352da.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
sd8b62352da.description: arXiv:2611.14320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: External memory enables LLM agents to improve from experience by distilling trajectories of past tasks into concise lessons for new tasks. However, memory can also lead to memory-induced degradation, where an agent fails on tasks it would solve without memory, often because it follows a lesson that is incorrect, or misapplies or misreads a valid one. This is because lessons are inferred from trajectories labeled only with task success or failure, yet are typically provided without the trajectories they came from, leaving the agent no way to check them. To address this, we introduce WikiTrace, an evidence-linked memory system designed to let agents check each lesson against its original trajectory. Specifically, motivated by the finding that a
sd8b62352da.summary: Researchers propose evidence-linked memory for LLM agents so lessons are checked against their source trajectories, reducing memory-induced performance degradation.
sd8b62352da.why: Agents that follow incorrect or misread lessons can fail tasks they would otherwise solve, so verifiable memory affects reliability.

sa951875c3b.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
sa951875c3b.description: arXiv:2611.14326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly operate in long-horizon, verifier-rich environments, but current self-improvement mechanisms often write episode-derived lessons directly into memory, making local success an unreliable signal for reusable and safe knowledge. This paper addresses the core question of when an experience-derived behavioral update should be admitted into persistent agent state. We propose Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution (FGSE), a verifier-grounded framework that represents each candidate lesson as a structured hypothesis with an explicit precondition, behavior change, expected effect, and verifier. FGSE applies the hypothesis only in a temporary state, tests it on target-transfer, falsification, and archived-regression probes, and then
sa951875c3b.summary: Researchers propose Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution, which treats agent lessons as hypotheses and admits them into persistent state only after verification.
sa951875c3b.why: Writing unverified episode lessons into agent memory can store unreliable knowledge, so gating updates may improve agent safety.

s8f711999a0.title: CLADE: Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
s8f711999a0.description: arXiv:2611.14355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented systems often retrieve passages that are accurate and relevant but state the answer at a coarser level of granularity than the question requires. For example, a question may ask which specific disease a drug treats (familial hyperlipidemia), while the retrieved passage mentions the broader disease family (hyperlipidemia). Prior work on context sufficiency treats such coarse passages simply as insufficient. We argue that they form a distinct case, which we call resolvable insufficiency: text alone cannot settle the fine-grained answer, but the broader category it mentions maps to a short list of candidate answers in a domain ontology. When language models read these coarse, family-only passages, they exhibit a phenomenon we
s8f711999a0.summary: The CLADE paper addresses retrieval-augmented QA where retrieved passages are accurate but more coarse-grained than the question, proposing category-level answering from such evidence.
s8f711999a0.why: RAG systems may wrongly treat coarse but correct passages as insufficient, which affects answer quality and abstention behavior.

s218878fcb4.title: Cognitive Mapping of Learning by Thinking Mechanisms in Large Language Models
s218878fcb4.description: arXiv:2611.14382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly exhibit capabilities that resemble human Learning by Thinking (LbT), the acquisition of new insight through internal processes such as explanation and reasoning, without new external input. A systematic account of the cognitive mechanisms behind these capabilities, and of their limits, remains underdeveloped. This paper proposes a Cognitive LbT Framework that maps four mechanisms (Reflective Reasoning, Synthetic Memory Formation, Internal Simulation, and Conceptual Self-Organization) onto computational processes in LLMs. Drawing on representative methods, including chain-of-thought prompting, self-consistency, self-reflection, Tree-of-Thoughts search, Self-Instruct, and self-taught reasoning, the anal
s218878fcb4.summary: Researchers propose a Cognitive Learning-by-Thinking framework mapping four internal mechanisms in LLMs onto computational processes.

s63d1654f56.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
s63d1654f56.description: arXiv:2611.14413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget. On Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B with simulated round-to-nearest weight quantization (8, 6, 4 and 3 bits, fp16 reference), read from the logits of the letters A to D on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU and HellaSwag (300 items each), 6 bits lose no accuracy against fp16 (they score +1.8 (+1.0 to +2.5) and +0.9 (+0.3 to +1.5) points higher, which we do not explain), and 8 bits change it by -0.7 (-1.1 to -0.3) and -0.4 (-0.7 to -0.2) points. At 4 bits the answer-slot skew rises from 0.1
s63d1654f56.summary: A study compares spending a fixed inference budget on weight quantization precision versus averaging over answer-option reorderings in small Qwen3 local models.
s63d1654f56.why: Engineers running small local models can use these results to decide between memory savings and reducing option-order sensitivity.

s53ed6f0743.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
s53ed6f0743.description: arXiv:2611.14418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local decoding usually fixes one weight precision for the whole generation. We study a different allocation: store 8-bit weights, decode with their top 4 bits, and redo a step at 8 bits only when the low-precision output distribution looks uncertain (entropy above a threshold or a small top-two margin). Quantization is simulated, the model is Qwen3-0.6B, and the benchmark is GSM8K. Cost is counted in weight bytes read per token. On 36724 replayed steps the entropy of the low pass ranks argmax flips with AUC 0.93. At a 15% escalation budget it catches 78% of flips and the margin gate 94%, against the 15% expected for a random gate of equal rate (a computed expectation, not a run). In 150 live problems all-high scores 64.0% and all-low 55.3% (M
s53ed6f0743.summary: Researchers propose decoding with top 4 bits of 8-bit weights and re-running uncertain steps at 8 bits, using simulated quantization on Qwen3-0.6B and GSM8K.
s53ed6f0743.why: Escalating precision only on uncertain steps could cut weight bytes read per token for local inference, a cost-relevant tradeoff.

s872cf8e087.title: Evaluating LLM-Generated World Models for Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning
s872cf8e087.description: arXiv:2611.14419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formal world models can support planning, verification, and safety reasoning, but constructing them from open-ended natural-language situations is difficult, particularly in multi-agent settings where several formalizations may be plausible. We study whether five LLMs can generate such world models as partially observable stochastic games and whether mechanical validity is sufficient to establish that the resulting model faithfully represents the intended decision problem. We introduce a benchmark of 44 scenarios spanning game, situational, and cultural settings and evaluate generated world models along three dimensions: mechanical validity, reference-relative structural agreement, and semantic criteria. Across three empirical tracks, we anal
s872cf8e087.summary: Researchers evaluate whether five LLMs can generate formal partially observable stochastic game world models from natural-language scenarios, using a 44-scenario benchmark.
s872cf8e087.why: Mechanically valid generated models may still misrepresent the intended decision problem, which matters for verification workflows.

s59baae1735.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
s59baae1735.description: arXiv:2611.14487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, Re-Search tracks how a model's idea evolves as it asks questions and receives binary oracle feedback, isolating ideation from execution. Across six recent LLMs, nearly all progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, which large
s59baae1735.summary: Re-Search introduces a two-player Twenty Questions-style game in which models must rediscover a paper's core idea, built from 200 ICML 2026 papers.
s59baae1735.why: The benchmark exposes how LLMs search the research-idea space step by step, which shows where ideation progress stalls.

sd8eb7a8e98.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
sd8eb7a8e98.description: arXiv:2611.14492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it. Only this last stage depends on
sd8eb7a8e98.summary: ReTrace converts a natural-language SOP and logged agent runs into a reusable workflow where code, not an LLM, selects each next step.
sd8eb7a8e98.why: Code-driven step selection could reduce latency and cost for repetitive business process automation with agents.

s7c93d9f0e5.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
s7c93d9f0e5.description: arXiv:2611.14493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the
s7c93d9f0e5.summary: A three-phase study compares three evaluation frameworks for enterprise LLM analytics agents, covering harness stability, failure detection, and discovery.
s7c93d9f0e5.why: Evaluation method choice affects whether teams reliably catch failures in multi-tool enterprise agent workflows.

saba4cacb34.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
saba4cacb34.description: arXiv:2611.14514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the uni
saba4cacb34.summary: Researchers propose Contrastive Discovery, which has LLM agents test a question against mutually exclusive competing explanations rather than a hypothesis against its negation.
saba4cacb34.why: It offers engineers a way to design discovery agents that identify which alternative evidence supports, not just that a claim is unlikely.

sd52182a33e.title: Data augmentation using generative networks to identify dementia
sd52182a33e.description: arXiv:2004.05989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data limitation is one of the most common issues in training machine learning classifiers for medical applications. Due to ethical concerns and data privacy, the number of people that can be recruited to such experiments is generally smaller than the number of participants contributing to non-healthcare datasets. Recent research showed that generative models can be used as an effective approach for data augmentation, which can ultimately help to train more robust classifiers sparse data domains. A number of studies proved that this data augmentation technique works for image and audio data sets. In this paper, we investigate the application of a similar approach to different types of speech and audio-based features extracted from interactio
sd52182a33e.summary: A 2020 arXiv paper explores using generative models for data augmentation to train more robust dementia classifiers on small medical datasets.

s93a0dba59f.title: Causal Time Series Modeling of Supraglacial Lake Evolution in Greenland under Distribution Shift
s93a0dba59f.description: arXiv:2510.15265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Causal modeling offers a principled foundation for uncovering stable, invariant relationships in time-series data, thereby improving robustness and generalization under distribution shifts. Yet its potential is underutilized in spatiotemporal Earth observation, where models often depend on purely correlational features that fail to transfer across heterogeneous domains. We propose RIC-TSC, a regionally-informed causal time-series classification framework that embeds lag-aware causal discovery directly into sequence modeling, enabling both predictive accuracy and scientific interpretability. Using multi-modal satellite and reanalysis data-including Sentinel-1 microwave backscatter, Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 optical reflectance, and CARRA mete
s93a0dba59f.summary: Researchers present RIC-TSC, a causal time-series classification framework for modeling Greenland supraglacial lake evolution under distribution shift.

s0ba9bbf87e.title: Textual Response-Aware Guidance for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
s0ba9bbf87e.description: arXiv:2610.40309v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong zero-shot generalization but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Existing adversarial fine-tuning methods often use pre-trained model guidance to preserve image--text alignment while improving robustness. Our analysis of visual representation drift reveals complementary limitations of two representative forms of guidance. Matching visual features constrains all directions equally, providing broad coverage without semantic emphasis. Matching prediction distributions prioritizes semantically relevant directions, but remains limited by the candidate texts and prediction probabilities. These limitations can hinder preservation of pre-trained image--text relationships and degrade zero-shot perfo
s0ba9bbf87e.summary: Researchers propose textual response-aware guidance to improve zero-shot adversarial robustness of vision-language models during adversarial fine-tuning.
s0ba9bbf87e.why: Adversarial robustness for VLMs matters for deployments relying on zero-shot generalization, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sb9b63e2762.title: AFNO: Universal Certifiably-Arbitrage-Free Operator Learning Framework for European Call-Price Surfaces
sb9b63e2762.description: arXiv:2611.12899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural operators (NOs) have been introduced as deep learning-powered solutions to the computational bottleneck of solving families of problems. Once trained, an NO can rapidly output approximate solutions, avoiding the need to rerun classical solvers. However, standard NO architectures cannot guarantee static no-arbitrage when predicting European call-price surfaces from market or model features and, as we verify experimentally, can yield negative PnL in downstream trading tasks. We introduce a certifiably arbitrage-free (AF) and universal encoder-decoder NO framework, continuously mapping inputs from a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) $\mathcal{H}$ over any fixed subset of $[0,\infty)^2$ to a convex combination of arbitrage-free Eur
sb9b63e2762.summary: Researchers introduce AFNO, a neural operator framework that certifiably guarantees static no-arbitrage when predicting European call-price surfaces.
sb9b63e2762.why: Standard neural operators can produce negative PnL in trading tasks, so guaranteed arbitrage-free outputs matter for quantitative finance systems.

sb353a5fa61.title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
sb353a5fa61.description: arXiv:2611.12901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes. With this goal, we present StepRefine, a plug-and-pl
sb353a5fa61.summary: Researchers propose Step-Aware Decoding, which flags anomalous denoising steps via entropy spikes to reduce hallucinations in multimodal diffusion language models.
sb353a5fa61.why: It suggests a training-free decoding fix for hallucinations in diffusion-based multimodal models, relevant to teams deploying them.

s547056184a.title: SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer
s547056184a.description: arXiv:2611.12903v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Context compression is now routine for language models with long inputs, but a compressed context is useful only if it keeps the evidence for the answer. Existing checks compare the reader model's answer or its most likely words, and thus miss a frequent failure, silent evidence loss: key evidence is removed while the answer stays the same, leaving the answer unsupported and risky for other models that reuse the context. To address this challenge, we propose SELD (Silent Evidence Loss Detector), which needs no training and no labels. Its principle is that when evidence is lost, a reader model's preferences among the answers it leaves unsaid shift even if its answer does not, so comparing these preferences before and after compression reveal
s547056184a.summary: Researchers introduce SELD, a training-free, label-free detector for silent evidence loss, where context compression removes key evidence while answers stay unchanged.
s547056184a.why: Compressed contexts can silently drop evidence that downstream models rely on, a risk for pipelines that reuse compressed context.

sa0f36bc474.title: Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation
sa0f36bc474.description: arXiv:2611.12904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. In principle, these clinician edits represent a scalable source of supervision for model training. In practice, not all edits represent actionable feedback: for instance, on data drawn from real-world deployment of an AI clinical documentation product, our review suggests that over 45% of edited outputs contain user-added information that is not directly supported by the inputs to the model. Naively fine-tuning on such edits risks teaching the model to hallucinate. In this paper, we develop a method to address this challenge. Given that real clinician edits on deployed documentation too
sa0f36bc474.summary: A paper argues that clinician edits to LLM clinical documentation can supply training signal, but many edits add unsupported information and need filtering.
sa0f36bc474.why: Over 45% of edits in the reported deployment data add unsupported content, so raw edit logs need filtering before training.

sed74ed5328.title: Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models
sed74ed5328.description: arXiv:2611.12906v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work presents a new benchmark that aims to address the limitations of current methods for evaluating LLMs in Brazilian Portuguese. We introduced Brasilidade, an assessment methodology comprised of standardized tasks distributed across four different domains, and we are making available the tasks from its first domain, which address nuances of the language, grammar, and variations of Brazilian Portuguese. The results show that model size, by itself, does not determine performance; several medium-sized models outperformed larger models in the protocols evaluated. Specific models for Portuguese, in general, did not perform above average, despite their targeted training. Different task levels revealed significant nuances: while some tasks
sed74ed5328.summary: Researchers release Brasilidade, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on Brazilian Portuguese language nuances, starting with its first domain of tasks.
sed74ed5328.why: It finds model size alone does not determine performance, so teams serving Portuguese users should benchmark locally rather than assume scale wins.

s03ea85f94d.title: M\"obius Interaction Filtering: Order-Selective Spectral Regularization for Multimodal Humor Detection
s03ea85f94d.description: arXiv:2611.12913v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal humor detection requires interpreting language, vocal delivery, and visual behavior jointly. Expressive fusion must also regulate how interactions of different orders enter the final judgment. We propose M\"obius Interaction Filtering (MoIF), which learns a modality-subset prediction function and imposes order-selective spectral regularization through its aggregation structure. Private temporal encoders and balanced reciprocal interaction construct supervised unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal predictors. Their uniform aggregate is exactly a M\"obius-domain filter with a geometrically decreasing interaction-order response. This formulation retains higher-order representations while regulating their contribution to prediction. Contro
s03ea85f94d.summary: Researchers propose Möbius Interaction Filtering, an order-selective spectral regularization method for multimodal humor detection across language, audio, and visual inputs.

s47943b509f.title: Token Importance-Aware Semantic Communication Enabled Robust Video Transmission
s47943b509f.description: arXiv:2611.12928v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video applications are increasingly prevalent, yet their high data volume and temporal dependency make robust wireless transmission challenging under limited communication resources. To address this issue, we propose a token importance-aware semantic communication (Ti-SemCom) framework for bandwidth-efficient video transmission. Specifically, object and motion information is jointly extracted to identify communication-relevant regions, which are hierarchically associated with semantic tokens according to their importance. The transmitted tokens are then dynamically selected based on both token importance and the available bandwidth, prioritizing more informative video content under resource constraints. At the receiver, untransmitted region
s47943b509f.summary: Researchers propose Ti-SemCom, a token importance-aware semantic communication framework for bandwidth-efficient and robust wireless video transmission.
s47943b509f.why: Prioritizing communication-relevant tokens could help video streaming over constrained wireless links, though the text gives few performance details.

s6d39fa1244.title: When Proofs Are Abundant, What Is a Paper For?
s6d39fa1244.description: arXiv:2611.12943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI systems now produce formally verified proofs of celebrated open problems, and the cost of obtaining a correct proof is falling toward zero. If correctness becomes cheap, what is left for a research paper to communicate? I argue that a paper is not exhausted by a verified statement. It is a narrative exposed to the criticism of a community, made of an intension (the author's choice of problem and perspective), a scientific chain of thought (the reasoning steps leading to the result), and the arguments supporting each step. Most published mathematics is judged on these two elements rather than on correctness alone, and machine-generated formal scripts convey neither. Borrowing from logic and type theory, I formalise the first as a Derivati
s6d39fa1244.summary: An essay argues that as AI makes formally verified proofs cheap, a research paper's value lies in its narrative, problem choice, reasoning, and community critique.
s6d39fa1244.why: As verified results get cheap, teams evaluating AI-generated research should weigh reasoning and justification, not just correctness.

s42536bc696.title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
s42536bc696.description: arXiv:2611.12955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Time-series classifiers deployed in risk-sensitive domains must be (1) accurate, (2) interpretable, and (3) able to abstain when evidence is weak. Existing methods do not deliver all 3 at once, and the obstacle is structural, rather than logistical. Meaningful temporal patterns cannot be defined without knowing segment boundaries, yet meaningful boundaries cannot be placed without knowing which patterns to expect. Existing approaches break this circularity by using fixed windows or expert-annotated vocabularies, thereby sacrificing at least one of the 3 properties. We introduce ConceptTime, which closes the loop through a single self-supervised signal. A frozen probabilistic forecaster predicts a distribution over the next observation at ev
s42536bc696.summary: Researchers propose predictive surprise as a self-grounding concept bottleneck for interpretable time-series classification that can abstain when evidence is weak.
s42536bc696.why: Interpretable, abstaining time-series classifiers matter for risk-sensitive deployments, though the text gives few implementation details.

s1fbf3ed871.title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation
s1fbf3ed871.description: arXiv:2611.12956v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) reduces the computational cost of attention through token-level selection. However, its indexer still scores the entire causal prefix for each query, making indexing a dominant source of latency in long-context inference. Notably, the indexer alone can account for more than 50% of total prefill GPU time at long context lengths. To address this bottleneck, we propose ADIndex, an Adaptive and Distillation-driven Indexing method for token-level sparse attention. ADIndex integrates three key components: (i) a layer-wise calibration strategy that adaptively accommodates cross-query retrieval overlap, motivated by our observation of pronounced inter-layer heterogeneity; (ii) a group-level distillation scheme that l
s1fbf3ed871.summary: Researchers propose ADIndex, a layer-adaptive sparse attention indexing method using group-level distillation to cut indexer latency in DeepSeek Sparse Attention.
s1fbf3ed871.why: The indexer can take over 50% of prefill GPU time at long context lengths, so cutting it directly targets long-context inference cost.

se0cdf5275f.title: Trajectory-Regularized Distribution Distillation for One-Step Generation
se0cdf5275f.description: arXiv:2611.12978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distilling flow matching models for one-step generation generally follows two paradigms. Trajectory alignment supervises the student with the teacher's probability flow ODE, but its performance degrades under very small sampling budgets. Distribution matching directly optimizes the generated distribution, but estimating its reverse Kullback-Leibler gradient typically requires a separate network to track the evolving student score. We propose trajectory-regularized distribution distillation (TRD), which combines distribution-level and trajectory-level supervision through a momentum-mixture policy predicted in a single student forward pass. This policy serves simultaneously as a one-step generator, an estimator of the student's marginal veloc
se0cdf5275f.summary: Researchers propose trajectory-regularized distribution distillation (TRD), combining distribution and trajectory supervision to distill flow matching models into one-step generators.
se0cdf5275f.why: It targets a known tradeoff in one-step distillation, where trajectory methods degrade at small sampling budgets, relevant to faster generative inference.

s6bfc54e288.title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
s6bfc54e288.description: arXiv:2611.12980v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs cont
s6bfc54e288.summary: MADSNet, a multi-scale axial-attentive dense spiking network, is proposed to reconstruct images from spike camera streams with improved fidelity over shallow SNN methods.
s6bfc54e288.why: It suggests spiking networks may narrow the fidelity gap with ANNs for efficient high-speed vision on low-power hardware.

s5f3628a82c.title: ICLayout-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Custom Circuit Layout Design
s5f3628a82c.description: arXiv:2611.12982v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are being explored for circuit design, but their ability to produce high-quality custom layouts has not been extensively evaluated. ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark in which agents use electronic design automation (EDA) tools to construct and optimize GDSII layouts from transistor-level circuit netlists. These layouts are evaluated using physical verification, parasitic extraction, and post-layout simulation. Layouts that pass the physical and functional checks are scored on electrical performance and area. The benchmark includes 165 tasks across 13 process design kits (PDKs), covering technology nodes from 3 nm to 180 nm. The tasks span analog, mixed-signal, and digital circuits in open-source and commercial
s5f3628a82c.summary: ICLayout-Bench is a benchmark evaluating LLM agents that use EDA tools to build and optimize GDSII custom circuit layouts from netlists.
s5f3628a82c.why: It offers a measured baseline for whether LLM agents can handle physical chip layout work beyond schematic-level tasks.

sd816aab4fd.title: Third Eye: Beyond Immediate Gains in Recursive Self-Improvement
sd816aab4fd.description: arXiv:2611.12988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Does a useful self-update remain useful after the model updates again? Third Eye separates immediate performance from the outcome of a further native update. We evaluate five 3-8B backbones on math and code: 64 fresh runs, three candidates per run, and three continuations per candidate. Selection and final scoring use disjoint items. In the balanced Qwen3-4B/Llama-3.2-3B comparison, immediate-selected utility is near zero, but continuation reduces it by 1.78 percentage points (simultaneous 95% interval [0.68, 2.88]). Candidate-averaged immediate utility is already negative: selection partly accounts for the apparently neutral first step. Continuation also lowers utility for SmolLM3-3B and Llama-3.1-8B; Qwen3-8B remains inconclusive. Target
sd816aab4fd.summary: Third Eye tests whether a self-update that helps immediately still helps after further native model updates, across five 3-8B backbones on math and code.
sd816aab4fd.why: It finds immediate gains from self-improvement can be misleading, which matters for anyone deploying self-updating models.

se9f54f8b3a.title: Specializing Meta Multi-Objectivization as Baseline for Software Engineering Optimization
se9f54f8b3a.description: arXiv:2611.12991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given the discrete nature of many software engineering (SE) optimization problems, trapping at local optima remains a crucial issue in the optimizer designs. Meta Multi-Objectivization (MMO) is an optimization model for overcoming local optima by introducing an extra, auxiliary objective. Yet, MMO is originally designed only for configuration tuning, leaving its suitability for other SE problems in doubt, particularly regarding the choice of the auxiliary objective. In this paper, we study the possibility and resolution for specializing MMO as a general baseline across a range of SE optimization problems, making it a fundamental counterpart for future SE optimizers that seek to mitigate the issue of local optima. We do so by providing both
se9f54f8b3a.summary: The paper studies specializing Meta Multi-Objectivization, an auxiliary-objective method for escaping local optima, as a baseline for software engineering optimization problems.
se9f54f8b3a.why: It may help engineers tune search-based SE optimizers, though the summary gives limited detail on results.

s1b65d3f577.title: TIB: Sample-wise Tempered Information Bottleneck for Multimodal Attribution beyond Alignment Assumption
s1b65d3f577.description: arXiv:2611.12997v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Existing multimodal attribution methods typically rely on paired modalities as proxy supervision, implicitly assuming that image-text pairs are semantically aligned. Information bottleneck (IB)-based attribution methods follow this general paradigm and instantiate it through a global sufficiency-compression objective. In realistic multimodal datasets, however, this assumption is frequently violated due to partial semantic misalignment and unreliable cross-modal correspondences. Through theoretical analysis, we show that, under such misalignment, information-bottleneck-based attribution objectives e
s1b65d3f577.summary: TIB proposes a sample-wise tempered information bottleneck for multimodal attribution that does not assume image-text pairs are always semantically aligned.
s1b65d3f577.why: Better attribution on misaligned multimodal data could improve model interpretability for vision-language systems.

sc1f5bc0719.title: PhysMoE: Fast Spatial Grounding with Single-Token Coordinate Representation in Modality-Decoupled VLMs
sc1f5bc0719.description: arXiv:2611.13000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are backbones for robotic planning and manipulation. However, for coordinate prediction in grounding tasks, existing architectures suffer from two distinct bottlenecks: discrete tokenization disrupts spatial continuity with high decoding latency, while standard point regression fails on multi-contact affordances and irregularly shaped targets. To resolve these challenges, we propose PhysMoE, introducing three core contributions: (1) sharing lower layers for multimodal context while routing upper layers to specialized spatial (pixel) and linguistic (text) experts by physical modality, eliminating gradient interference; (2) encoding each coordinate as a single token by reusing the visual encoder's learne
sc1f5bc0719.summary: PhysMoE proposes single-token coordinate representation and modality-decoupled routing in embodied vision-language models to speed up spatial grounding for robotics.
sc1f5bc0719.why: Lower decoding latency for coordinate prediction could matter for real-time robotic planning and manipulation.

s015de7d9fe.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
s015de7d9fe.description: arXiv:2611.13005v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Synthesizing programs from execution traces is a fundamental challenge in algorithmic interpretability and the reverse engineering of complex systems. We bring a rough-path-theoretic perspective to program induction, treating execution traces as high-dimensional rough paths and encoding them with the path signature transform, a tool from stochastic analysis whose expectation provably characterizes the distribution of traces a program induces. On three program-induction domains, Karel, List, and RASP, our log-signature trace encoder outperforms LSTM, Transformer, and Fourier baselines in almost every setting, with its largest margins when training data is scarce. We further observe that the trace-to-program pipeline is naturally contractive:
s015de7d9fe.summary: The paper uses path signatures from rough-path theory to encode execution traces, improving trace-to-program induction on Karel, List, and RASP domains.
s015de7d9fe.why: It offers a new encoding approach for inferring programs from execution behavior, relevant to reverse engineering research.

s6e5bbec41a.title: Just AI Governance and the Forbidden-Boundary Principle
s6e5bbec41a.description: arXiv:2611.13007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly shapes consequential decisions, yet predictive accuracy is not a sufficient justification for delegated authority. This conceptual study develops an integrated framework for assessing just AI across normative, data, model, and governance layers. Drawing on plural theories of justice, sociotechnical fairness research, and publicly available governance standards, it maps six justice requirements to observable evidence, decision rights, and remedies. It proposes a two-stage evaluation rule: exclude uses that fail independently justified minimum rights constraints, then compare eligible alternatives across multiple performance and governance criteria. As an explicitly limited normative analogy, Genesis
s6e5bbec41a.summary: A conceptual study proposes a framework for assessing whether AI decisions are justified across normative, data, model, and governance layers, with a forbidden-boundary evaluation rule.
s6e5bbec41a.why: It offers a structured governance checklist for deciding when AI should hold delegated authority, though it is conceptual and untested.

sff9bcde1f5.title: An Open Implementation Flow for the Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 that Runs in the Browser, Checked Byte for Byte Against ISE
sff9bcde1f5.description: arXiv:2611.13008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The author describes an open implementation flow, from HDL to a programmable bitstream, for the Xilinx Spartan-3E (XC3S100E to XC3S1200E) and Spartan-6 (XC6SLX16, XC6SLX45), devices that only the discontinued ISE 14.7 supports. The flow runs unchanged in a web browser or in Node.js: Yosys and nextpnr compiled to WebAssembly, with nextpnr's Himbaechel framework given Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 architectures generated from Silinx's own device descriptions, bit database and timing model, and Silinx's own bitstream writer. The bit database was built by black-box observation of ISE's documented XDL and bitgen tools, using codeword-batched experiments; the router is given only switches whose bits were measured, and the writer refuses a feature it h
sff9bcde1f5.summary: An open HDL-to-bitstream flow for Xilinx Spartan-3E and Spartan-6 runs in a browser via Yosys and nextpnr compiled to WebAssembly, checked against ISE.
sff9bcde1f5.why: Open toolchains for legacy FPGAs reduce dependence on discontinued vendor software for hardware projects.

s3deda12018.title: Compile-Gated Lean Proof Refactoring with Enterprise Agent Practices: A Model per Step under a US\$3 Cap, Followed by Programmatic Rewrite Rules
s3deda12018.description: arXiv:2611.13011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Our closed-track entry (Arena username Vexorium-Agent) scored 86.31 points on the final board (L = 77.07, H = 81.86, Z = 100) over the 60 final problems, against 33.33 for the reference proofs, 8th at the deadline (top: 92.57), for US\$166.33 at list prices with every call counted (per problem: mean US\$2.772, at most US\$2.874; US\$3 cap). Three practices carry the entry. First, each paid stage runs the model that measured best per dollar for it among the 9 we tested in our own harness: GPT-6.1 Sol the early sessions, GPT-6.1 Terra the later ones and the tail at 70% of Sol's cost per turn, and Gemini 4 Argon the review and repair; Sol also runs the style rewrite. Second, what our development and research runs learned ships as compiler-chec
s3deda12018.summary: A closed-track Lean proof refactoring entry reports a score of 86.31 on 60 problems at about US$166 total, using a model-per-step approach under a per-problem cost cap.
s3deda12018.why: It gives a concrete cost-per-task example for routing different models across agent pipeline stages.

s7c1fdbc6ea.title: Repository-Context-Guided Image Understanding for Agentic Software Development
s7c1fdbc6ea.description: arXiv:2611.13026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents increasingly receive UI screenshots as part of bug reports, yet degraded image quality - caused by low resolution, compression artifacts, or small rendered text - can prevent them from identifying the relevant UI elements and source files. Vision-language models become less reliable as image quality deteriorates, while OCR-assisted approaches may propagate recognition errors from degraded inputs. Both approaches are limited when the visual evidence required for localization is no longer clearly observable in the query screenshot. We propose augmenting coding agents with repository-rendered reference images: crisp screenshots generated from the same codebase that the agent is tasked with modifying. These references provide read
s7c1fdbc6ea.summary: A method uses repository context to help coding agents localize relevant UI elements and source files from degraded bug-report screenshots.
s7c1fdbc6ea.why: Coding agents often receive low-quality screenshots, so grounding localization in repo context could improve bug triage.

sc97463a0a3.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
sc97463a0a3.description: arXiv:2611.13028v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshot
sc97463a0a3.summary: GTAGym is an environment and framework for evaluating and reinforcement learning agents on GTA V tasks, with a 103-task benchmark derived from main-story missions.
sc97463a0a3.why: It provides a verifiable testbed for agent perception and control in complex 3D environments.

sd782ee3a90.title: Code-Grounded Agentic Explanations for Static Analysis Vulnerability Findings
sd782ee3a90.description: arXiv:2611.13041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools surface vulnerabilities early and their verdicts are rule-based and auditable. Yet developers routinely dismiss findings they cannot interpret. Large language models can supply the missing explanation, but designs that also hand the model the detection give up the auditability that makes static analysis defensible. We keep detection with the analyser and give the model only the explaining. A preliminary user study with 20 participants and a workshop with 19 practitioners yielded five requirements.
