Guided by these we redesigned SAFE, an open-source IntelliJ IDEA plugin that explains findings from any analyser reporting in the Static Analysis Results Interchange Format. It tiers explanations by
sd782ee3a90.summary: The paper proposes keeping static analysis detection with the analyzer while using an LLM only to explain SAST vulnerability findings, based on a 20-participant study.
sd782ee3a90.why: Separating detection from LLM explanation keeps findings auditable while addressing developers dismissing unexplained alerts.

scd8e4fdbf5.title: Beyond the Document: Compiled Context and Governed Agents for Any Work Product
scd8e4fdbf5.description: arXiv:2611.13055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A document preserves the visible result of professional work but often discards the research, calculations, assumptions, evidence, and authorization boundaries behind it. We study a different unit of delivery: a Portable Agent Format (PAF) package that carries a work product together with compiled context, evidence, provenance, and rules for subsequent interaction. To test whether this context remains useful beyond the process that produced it, we evaluate four new packages, created after the hosted and offline readers were fixed: an investment proposal, fund research, financial-statement analysis, and an engineering incident review. Two packages were produced by specialized agents and two through a general-purpose assistant's packaging ski
scd8e4fdbf5.summary: The paper proposes Portable Agent Format packages that carry work products with compiled context, evidence, provenance, and rules for later agent interaction.
scd8e4fdbf5.why: Packaging provenance and authorization rules with deliverables could matter for governed agent workflows, though evidence presented is limited here.

se59034b806.title: Continuous-Time Set-Transformers for Asynchronous WiFi-IMU Indoor Localization
se59034b806.description: arXiv:2611.13057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Indoor localization commonly combines WiFi received signal strength indicator (RSSI) fingerprints with inertial measurements. However, these sensor streams are sampled asynchronously at different rates; therefore, observations rarely align in time and may be missing or stale. Most existing methods resample the data onto a shared clock and process each modality using a separate branch. We instead present a continuous-time transformer that represents observations as an unordered set of timestamped tokens. Each token encodes its measurement, modality, and elapsed time since acquisition. A single attention block jointly fuses information across modalities and time, avoiding both resampling and modality-specific branches while remaining invarian
se59034b806.summary: A continuous-time set-transformer represents asynchronous WiFi RSSI and IMU measurements as timestamped tokens for indoor localization without resampling.
se59034b806.why: Handling asynchronous, missing sensor streams directly could improve indoor localization accuracy in practice.

s3379b1c779.title: The Indic Token Tax in 2026: Measuring Tokenizer. Disparity and Its Cost for the Languages of India
s3379b1c779.description: arXiv:2611.13058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Commercial language model APIs bill per token, so a tokenizer that needs more tokens for the same content in one language makes that language more expensive, slower, and able to fit less text in a fixed context window. We measure this disparity for nine public tokenizers, including those of GPT-4, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5, DeepSeek-V3, Mistral-Nemo and four Sarvam models, on all 25 languages of India available in FLORES-200 (2,009 professionally translated sentences aligned with English) and on 13,732 human-translated Hinglish-English social media pairs from PHINC. On GPT-4o's tokenizer the same content needs between 1.57 times (Hindi) and 5.01 times (Odia) the tokens of English, and 13.7 times for Santali in Ol Chiki script; GPT-4's tokenizer needs
s3379b1c779.summary: A study measures tokenizer disparity across nine public tokenizers, including GPT-4o and Sarvam models, for all 25 Indian languages in FLORES-200 and Hinglish text.
s3379b1c779.why: Tokenizers that need more tokens for some languages raise per-token API costs, latency, and effective context length for those users.

s89d16a6d7d.title: A Multi-Word Tokenizer for 204 Languages That Needs Fewer Tokens Than GPT-4o's, Including on English
s89d16a6d7d.description: arXiv:2611.13059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Languages of India need 1.6 to 14 times as many tokens as English on GPT-4o's tokenizer for the same content, which makes them more expensive and slower to serve. We train tokenizers from scratch on human-written text in about 200 languages. Havon v3 is a byte-level BPE tokenizer with 262,144 tokens and a pre-tokenizer that keeps combining marks with their letters and chunks scripts written without spaces. On FLORES-200 devtest it needs fewer tokens than GPT-4o's o200k_base on all 25 languages of India (median 0.74 of GPT-4o's count) and on 172 of 204 languages, but 7% more on English. Havon v4 adds a second, multi-word training stage (SuperBPE) to v3. At exactly GPT-4o's vocabulary size of 200,019 tokens, v4 needs 6.1% fewer tokens than GP
s89d16a6d7d.summary: Researchers present Havon v3, a 262,144-token byte-level BPE tokenizer trained on about 200 languages, which reports fewer tokens than GPT-4o's o200k_base on all 25 Indian languages tested.
s89d16a6d7d.why: Lower token counts for non-English languages could cut serving cost and latency for multilingual applications, though results are from a benchmark.

sd2dafd82a8.title: One Temperature to Rule Them All?
sd2dafd82a8.description: arXiv:2611.13077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inference-time sampling is a central mechanism for improving large language models, with temperature controlling the tradeoff between reliability and diversity. While recent work suggests that varying temperature across samples can improve multi-sample inference, simple fixed-temperature schemes remain the standard in practice. We investigate this discrepancy in the canonical pass@K setting, asking when temperature diversity is useful, and when a single tuned temperature suffices. To this end, we analyze per-question success probabilities across multiple models and datasets, tracking how they vary with sampling temperature. We identify several consistent properties of these profiles, including that harder questions are less likely to share
sd2dafd82a8.summary: The paper analyzes when varying sampling temperature across samples helps pass@K inference and when a single tuned fixed temperature is sufficient.
sd2dafd82a8.why: It helps teams decide whether to add per-sample temperature schemes or keep a single tuned temperature for multi-sample inference.

sc3c1773245.title: ASPIRE: An Agentic System-Identification Platform for Iterative Reasoning and Exploration
sc3c1773245.description: arXiv:2611.13114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: System identification requires expert decisions on the identification method, incorporation of prior physical knowledge, and model validation. We propose ASPIRE, a framework for nonlinear system identification in which a large language model agent selects and executes the identification method. ASPIRE constructs closed-form, nonlinear static or dynamic models from measured data, optionally supplemented by a system description, the intended use of the model, and physical requirements expressed formally or in natural language. Each model includes its parameters, an estimation record, an interpretation of its terms, and an error evaluated on test data inaccessible to the agent. Formal physical requirements are verified independently. ASPIRE op
sc3c1773245.summary: ASPIRE is a framework where an LLM agent selects and executes methods to build nonlinear system-identification models from measured data.
sc3c1773245.why: It shows an agentic workflow applied to engineering modeling tasks that traditionally need expert judgment.

sfec7ec029e.title: Just Image Transformers with Late-Stage Pixel Refinement
sfec7ec029e.description: arXiv:2611.13120v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent work on latent-free diffusion transformers has demonstrated the feasibility of training image generators without a latent VAE. This avoids compression artifacts from the VAE and simplifies the training pipeline. In particular, JiT showed that even a standard transformer can be trained to generate images when the model is trained to predict the final image ($x$-prediction). Even though JiT unlocks training efficiency comparable to latent models, it still suffers from reduced image quality likely arising from modeling the image as a collection of large patches. In this work, we revisit JiT and show that adding simple convolutional pixel-pathway layers in a post-training phase significantly improves generation quality. Moreover, we show
sfec7ec029e.summary: The paper proposes adding late-stage pixel refinement to latent-free Just Image Transformers (JiT) to improve image quality over pure x-prediction.
sfec7ec029e.why: It addresses a known quality gap in latent-free diffusion training, which could simplify image generator pipelines.

sb43a9c4dee.title: Which Successes Make Good References? Action-Sequence Alignment for Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation
sb43a9c4dee.description: arXiv:2611.13135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) reduces train-inference distribution mismatch by supervising a student on its own trajectories. For multi-turn tool-use agents, conditioning the teacher on a validated same-task successful trajectory as a reference can provide useful hindsight, but different successes may reach incompatible interaction states and offer misleading supervision. We cast successful-reference selection as a free-target optimal transport problem, which reduces to assigning each failed trajectory its most compatible successful reference. Because latent state paths are hidden, we use action-sequence alignment as an observable proxy for compatibility and instantiate it with longest common subsequence (LCS), which identifies a shared orde
sb43a9c4dee.summary: The paper proposes selecting successful reference trajectories via free-target optimal transport to improve on-policy distillation for multi-turn tool-use agents.
sb43a9c4dee.why: Better teacher references may improve training of tool-using agents by avoiding misleading supervision from incompatible successes.

s72f0a4e9a8.title: DOBB: Dynamic Oriented Bounding Boxes for Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance under State Uncertainty and Heterogeneous Dynamics
s72f0a4e9a8.description: arXiv:2611.13142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning-based decentralized collision avoidance must remain reliable under state-estimation uncertainty and heterogeneous agent dynamics. Existing methods typically address these factors through training-domain variation or by exposing uncertainty and capability estimates to the policy at runtime. However, both leave the policy to infer how these quantities should alter the physical separation required for safe interaction, which can couple collision-avoidance behavior to relationships learned from the training distribution. We introduce the Dynamic Oriented Bounding Box (DOBB), an online geometric representation that maps the current state estimate, uncertainty, and agent-specific response characteristics into a dynamic, direction-depende
s72f0a4e9a8.summary: DOBB introduces dynamic oriented bounding boxes to make learning-based multi-agent collision avoidance robust to state uncertainty and heterogeneous dynamics.
s72f0a4e9a8.why: Encoding uncertainty and agent capability into the safety geometry may make decentralized robot policies more reliable outside training conditions.

s2583c092e5.title: Autonomous Optimization of Numerical Algorithms by an AI Agent: Application to Atomistic Simulation
s2583c092e5.description: arXiv:2611.13143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents built on large language models, run in automated improvement loops, can discover more efficient algorithms. We present AIOA, a framework that brings this approach to the numerical algorithms of atomistic simulation: an agent improves an algorithm against a pre-specified metric in a loop guarded by verifiers it cannot alter. Applied to ASE, a widely used atomistic simulation library, AIOA targets two facets of an algorithm: its implementation, rewritten to run faster with unchanged results, and the method itself, redesigned to converge with fewer force evaluations. Agents made six kernels 22-24 times faster on average in Python with NumPy and SciPy. On unseen problems, optimizers from the best configuration needed 3.1-3.4 times
s2583c092e5.summary: AIOA uses an LLM coding agent in an improvement loop, guarded by verifiers, to optimize numerical algorithms in the ASE atomistic simulation library.
s2583c092e5.why: It demonstrates agent-driven code optimization with verifiers that the agent cannot alter, a pattern applicable to scientific software.

sc315050692.title: Everything in its right place: attention is a radio head
sc315050692.description: arXiv:2611.13146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Attention, the core of language models, is a digital calculation over tokens: an exponential selects them, a division normalizes and a positional code sets the order. We show that attention can instead emerge from the synchronization of a receiver with its context tokens. Each past token is an oscillator whose state carries its content and whose frequency drifts with its age. The present token selects them by content, aligning an antenna with its query, and by position, setting the frequency of a receiver with its dial. Solving Kuramoto's problem for this receiver yields an attention layer in closed form with two phases: above a critical coupling set by the context, the receiver locks and its weights normalize; below it, it stays silent and
sc315050692.summary: The paper proposes that attention can emerge from synchronization of oscillators, reframing it as a Kuramoto-style process rather than a digital calculation.
sc315050692.why: It is a theoretical reframing of attention with limited immediate engineering impact beyond conceptual interest.

sd97648b01f.title: How Much of Your VLA Is kNN
sd97648b01f.description: arXiv:2611.13160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models now exceed 95% success on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, yet it remains unclear how much of this performance requires generalization beyond the training demonstrations. In this work, we show that retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks achieves a success rate of 91.7 % on LIBERO without policy training. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations, retrieval shows the smallest drop of all evaluated policies. Across nine publicly available VLAs, fine-tuning mostly makes the vision-language backbone a better retrieval key, and the actions of the VLAs remain close to the demonstrations. In addition, we introduce Local Action Consistency (LAC), an offline metric that measures whether nearby obse
sd97648b01f.summary: The paper shows retrieving nearby demonstrations and reusing their action chunks reaches 91.7% success on LIBERO without policy training, and analyzes nine VLAs.
sd97648b01f.why: It suggests high VLA benchmark scores may rely heavily on memorized demonstrations rather than generalization, which affects how teams evaluate robot policies.

s47b69533bd.title: AgentScript-Eval: Benchmarking LLMs and Agents for Code Generation in an Enterprise DSL
s47b69533bd.description: arXiv:2611.13183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Domain-specific languages (DSLs) are widely used in enterprise software, giving a compact interface to complex tasks, from data access to infrastructure automation. Platforms increasingly extend them to agents, where a developer declares the topics, permitted actions, and guardrails of an agent rather than writing general-purpose code. Large language models (LLMs) write general-purpose code well, but that ability has been measured almost entirely on languages abundant in public pretraining data, and enterprise DSLs are neither abundant nor public. We introduce AgentScript-Eval, an execution-graded benchmark of 100 real tasks for AgentScript, the declarative DSL that Salesforce uses in Agentforce to build conversational agents. Tasks span au
s47b69533bd.summary: AgentScript-Eval is a benchmark evaluating LLMs and agents on generating code in an enterprise domain-specific language for declaring agent behavior.
s47b69533bd.why: Enterprise DSLs are underrepresented in pretraining data, so this benchmark helps teams gauge LLM reliability for internal platform code.

s06c0788af4.title: Multimodal Road Closure Mapping via Cross-Modal Graph Attention
s06c0788af4.description: arXiv:2611.13192v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate and timely identification of road closures is critical for large-scale navigation and logistics systems, yet remains challenging due to the need to jointly reason over visual evidence, spatial context, and road network topology. Existing approaches either rely on manual map updates or focus on detecting closure-related objects without resolving which road segment is affected. In this work, we introduce a unified multimodal and multitask framework that jointly performs road closure classification (no, partial, complete) and road segment association within a single learning architecture. Our model integrates graph-structured map data, satellite imagery augmented with projected street-level detections, and street-view images using mod
s06c0788af4.summary: The paper introduces a multimodal, multitask framework that classifies road closures and identifies affected road segments using cross-modal graph attention.
s06c0788af4.why: Automated closure detection could reduce manual map updates for navigation and logistics systems.

sa7ebca7b73.title: Structured Kernel Surrogate Models for Multimodal Attribution
sa7ebca7b73.description: arXiv:2611.13198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of cross-sample modality attribution, which involves measuring how one modality in one sample affects the learning outcome in other multimodal samples. This problem is crucial in a multimodal system because a data modality (such as a text description) may be redundant for one sample (a self-explanatory image), but the same data modality would otherwise be uniquely informative for another sample, or informative when combined with other modalities. Prior work focuses on influence estimation at the level of one sample, and it remains an open question how one should capture the interactions across both samples and modalities. To capture scenarios like the above, we propose structured kernel surrogate models, which are surro
sa7ebca7b73.summary: The paper proposes structured kernel surrogate models for cross-sample modality attribution, measuring how one modality in a sample affects learning on other samples.
sa7ebca7b73.why: Attribution across samples could help diagnose which data modalities matter in multimodal training pipelines.

s180ed424e5.title: XAI-Driven Confidence Estimation for OOD-Resilient Runtime Prediction
s180ed424e5.description: arXiv:2611.13199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning-based resource management (RM) models degrade under out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs at runtime, yet existing approaches in the literature rely on a single global error margin that is overly conservative and fails to distinguish reliablepredictions from catastrophic failures. We propose Lightweight Runtime EXplainability (LEX), the first post-hoc XAI framework for input-specific runtime confidence estimation in ML-based RM. LEX clusters the embeddings of the training input space using a Gaussian Mixture Model and associates per-cluster prediction error bounds to input samples, enabling fine-grained runtime confidence signals without retraining. Evaluated on a state-of-the-art LSTM-based IPS forecasting model on Intel Alder
s180ed424e5.summary: LEX is a post-hoc explainability framework that estimates input-specific runtime confidence for ML resource management models under out-of-distribution inputs.
s180ed424e5.why: Per-input confidence could let runtime resource managers avoid catastrophic failures that a single global error margin misses.

s05a355378b.title: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood
s05a355378b.description: arXiv:2611.13213v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Children's earliest years are a period of intense social learning, during which meaning is built through gaze, gesture, and physical contact. Yet, this critical aspect of social interaction remains under-evaluated in multimodal video understanding, as existing benchmarks prioritize the conversation-driven interactions of adults. We address this gap with \bench ($\textbf{N}$aturalistic $\textbf{E}$arly-childhood $\textbf{S}$ocial in$\textbf{T}$eractions), the first child-centric benchmark for nonverbal social reasoning. \bench comprises \totalvids manually annotated clips ($\sim$12s) curated for diversity across naturalistic settings, cultural contexts, and developmental stages. Beyond a lack of data, targeted model improvement in this domai
s05a355378b.summary: The paper introduces a child-centric video benchmark for evaluating nonverbal social reasoning in early childhood interactions.
s05a355378b.why: Existing multimodal benchmarks focus on adult conversation, so this highlights a gap in evaluating nonverbal social understanding.

s8a2197d07a.title: Wrong the Same Way: Cross-Prompt Sharing Both Suppresses and Amplifies Reward Hacking in RLVR
s8a2197d07a.description: arXiv:2611.13218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two accounts of how reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) interacts with an imperfect verifier coexist: in one, reward hacking is inherited from the base model; in the other, RL amplifies it. We study both in a controlled environment small enough to compute the entire response distribution exactly. We vary the universality of a leak, or the fraction of prompts that accept the same wrong response, and the verifier's static false-positive rate. At its KL-regularized optimum, RLVR acts as a filter that reweights the accepted set without altering its composition, so the hack rate is inherited exactly. Taking that as a null model, a known decomposition writes the drift from it as a sum over prompts of covariances between reward a
s8a2197d07a.summary: Researchers study how RL with verifiable rewards interacts with imperfect verifiers, testing whether reward hacking is inherited from base models or amplified by RL.
s8a2197d07a.why: Clarifies when imperfect reward verifiers lead to reward hacking, which matters for anyone training models with verifiable rewards.

s028ccf691b.title: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement across Seven Open Reasoning Models
s028ccf691b.description: arXiv:2611.13223v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reasoning models write a reasoning trace at every turn of a multi-turn tool session, and later turns read this history. Across 94k ShareGPT conversations, 73 percent of user interactions span multiple turns. Upstream providers bind each trace to its issuer, so a request forwarded across issuers arrives with its history deleted, and the task cost of this stripping remains unmeasured. To the best of our knowledge, this paper presents the first direct, blind, multi-seed measurement of full reasoning-history deletion in multi-turn tool calling, through three rendering conditions, seven open-weight reasoning models, three seeds, 794 tasks, and the official checker. The same deletion spans -4.4 to +51.3 points with both ends excluding zero, and f
s028ccf691b.summary: Researchers measure how deleting reasoning history in multi-turn tool calling affects task performance across seven open reasoning models.
s028ccf691b.why: Shows that dropping reasoning traces when routing requests across providers may degrade multi-turn tool use, relevant to system design.

sab069fbac4.title: STAR: Semantic-Criticality Tiered Allocation of Radio Resources via Zero-Shot Learning
sab069fbac4.description: arXiv:2611.13238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In remote inference, edge devices transmit high-resolution images over wireless links to a receiver, where an artificial intelligence (AI) model answers task-specific questions about these images to enable reliable decisions. These answers are often determined by a small set of task-causal pixels, such as those of text, whose corruption changes the answer, so these pixels must be delivered with high fidelity. Conventional transmission protects every pixel equally, so it either consumes many resource elements (REs) or corrupts these regions at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). To overcome these limitations, in this paper, a zero-shot, domain-agnostic framework, termed semantic-criticality tiered allocation of resources (STAR), is proposed. In
sab069fbac4.summary: STAR proposes allocating wireless radio resources by semantic criticality, protecting task-critical image pixels with higher fidelity in remote AI inference.
sab069fbac4.why: Offers a way to cut bandwidth use in edge-to-cloud vision systems by protecting only the pixels that affect answers.

s23fdec7c4b.title: Curie's Jarvis: Autonomous Robotic Chemistry Experiments from Printed Protocols
s23fdec7c4b.description: arXiv:2611.13251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A person running a bench experiment works from a printed instruction sheet, tells identical containers apart by the labels written on them, and looks at the bench again before each step. Lab automation usually works the other way around: the procedure is written as a script, and containers stand at fixed positions or carry fiducial markers. We present Curie's Jarvis, a system that lets a robot arm carry out a chemistry experiment on a bench set up for people. It reads the steps from a photo of the printed sheet, finds containers on an ordinary bench with no fixed positions or markers, tells identical-looking containers apart by reading their labels in four camera views, locates its target again before every step, and sets how each step is c
s23fdec7c4b.summary: Curie's Jarvis is a robot arm system that reads chemistry steps from a printed sheet and carries out experiments on a bench built for humans.
s23fdec7c4b.why: Shows lab automation that works from human-oriented materials rather than fixed scripts and fiducial markers.

s5f6e045aa5.title: Adaptive Residual Quantization for Memory-Efficient Temporal Action Segmentation
s5f6e045aa5.description: arXiv:2611.13262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Temporal action segmentation (TAS) is commonly trained on large banks of pre-extracted frame features, but storing and replaying those features becomes a practical bottleneck for long-form video, especially in incremental TAS where past-task data must remain available to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Recent TAS replay and condensation methods reduce this burden, but they rely on dense frame-wise annotations and allocate storage through fixed segment-level structures, limiting their flexibility for long procedural videos whose frame complexity varies substantially over time. We introduce Adaptive Residual-Quantized Variational AutoEncoder (ARQ-VAE), a compact and label-free memory representation for TAS features that learns a discrete re
s5f6e045aa5.summary: Researchers propose adaptive residual quantization to reduce storage of frame features for memory-efficient temporal action segmentation in long videos.
s5f6e045aa5.why: Addresses storage bottlenecks in replay-based incremental video training, relevant to teams handling large video feature banks.

se87bf005cd.title: Off-policy Learning with Excursion Policies
se87bf005cd.description: arXiv:2611.13275v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Off-policy reinforcement learning (RL) tries to learn the value of a target policy while data comes from a different behavior policy. This often requires trading off bias for variance or stability. One way to trade these off is to linearly interpolate between the behavior and target policies, but this represents only one point in a broader space of interpolation mechanisms. We introduce excursion policies--a structured alternative where the agent follows the target policy for a multi-step "excursion" before reverting to the behavior policy. We derive dynamic programming results for these policies, establishing the theoretical basis for their use in RL. We further develop provably sound off-policy temporal-difference (TD) algorithms for excu
se87bf005cd.summary: Researchers introduce excursion policies, which follow the target policy for multi-step stretches before reverting to the behavior policy in off-policy RL.
se87bf005cd.why: Offers an alternative to linear interpolation for trading bias against variance in off-policy learning.

sf528898dd8.title: MRFoundry: Knowledge-guided agent loops for end-to-end MRI research
sf528898dd8.description: arXiv:2611.13289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents can write code, use scientific software, and revise computational workflows, opening new possibilities for MRI research. Effective assistance requires connecting acquisition physics, data conventions, specialized tools, and scientific validation. We present MRFoundry, an open-source, extensible package that connects MRI knowledge to agent actions and output checks. Project-local memory preserves decisions and evidence, while reviewed contributions allow researchers to improve shared guidance. Researcher-supervised examples demonstrate skill-guided sequence auditing and acquired-data reconstruction, connecting tool use, output checks, and documented decisions. Alongside MRFoundry, we introduce MRI Agent Bench to compare agents with
sf528898dd8.summary: MRFoundry is an open-source package that connects MRI domain knowledge to AI agent actions, with project memory and output checks.
sf528898dd8.why: Provides a reference pattern for grounding research agents in domain knowledge and validation checks.

s54a9efd3b8.title: Train High, Ship Low: Efficient LoRA Synchronization for Distributed On-Policy Post-Training
s54a9efd3b8.description: arXiv:2611.13306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transmitting LoRA adapters to rollout workers can bottleneck distributed on-policy post-training over bandwidth-constrained networks. Lowering the training rank may limit the capacity a workload needs, while adaptive optimizer updates are difficult to compress. Rollout workers can instead reconstruct updates from gradients by maintaining replicated optimizer states. We introduce HiLo, a compressor-agnostic framework that replaces parameter transmission with compressed gradient dissemination and local optimizer replay. By applying the same decoded gradients, the learner and workers maintain consistent policy states at the same version under reproducible execution. We further develop Spar, a budget-aware gradient compressor that combines spec
s54a9efd3b8.summary: HiLo replaces LoRA adapter transmission with compressed gradient dissemination and local optimizer replay for distributed on-policy post-training.
s54a9efd3b8.why: Could reduce bandwidth bottlenecks when syncing adapters to rollout workers in distributed RL post-training.

sf1f493aee5.title: PegasusAI Studio: Legible Cyberinfrastructure and Accountable AI Agents for Scientific Workflows
sf1f493aee5.description: arXiv:2611.13309v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI coding agents can now construct scientific workflows, but operating them on shared cyberinfrastructure (CI) raises problems that code generation does not solve. Agents need current knowledge of the workflow system and its execution sites and access to the runtime state of distributed executions, while facilities need to attribute every agent action to a user and bound it by that user's privileges. We present PegasusAI Studio, an AI-assisted science gateway built on the Pegasus and HTCondor stack. Studio makes CI legible to agents by projecting one facility-curated knowledge base into the native configuration of several coding agents, by introspecting workflow interfaces and execution sites, and by grounding diagnosis in workflow and sche
sf1f493aee5.summary: PegasusAI Studio is an AI-assisted science gateway that lets agents run scientific workflows on shared infrastructure with per-user attribution and privilege limits.
sf1f493aee5.why: Shows how agents operating on shared compute can be attributed to users and bounded by their privileges.

sae658b55be.title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
sae658b55be.description: arXiv:2611.13331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-tuning large-scale foundation models across resource-constrained, distributed clients presents significant computational and communication challenges. While merging Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with Federated Learning (FL) enables rank-based flexibility, the interdependence of the adaptation matrices ($\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$) often complicates optimization. In this work, we theoretically demonstrate that LoRA fine-tuning with Gaussian initialization and a frozen $\mathbf{A}$ matrix acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, where batch gradients are subject to a random, rank-dependent perturbation. Motivated by this insight, we propose freezing and periodically resampling $\mathbf{A}$ matrices at the client level. This
sae658b55be.summary: Researchers show theoretically that LoRA with Gaussian initialization and frozen A acts as stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, and propose rank-aware learning rates for federated LoRA.
sae658b55be.why: Offers theory and a learning-rate method for federated fine-tuning on resource-constrained clients.

s49ee4f8d95.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
s49ee4f8d95.description: arXiv:2611.13348v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Protein engineering requires navigating rugged fitness landscapes, where small sequence changes can produce large functional differences, but experimental screening can only sample a small fraction of sequence space. Thus, a central challenge is to efficiently traverse the large combinatorial space of mutations in silico. We introduce ProTEUS, a mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution. Pretrained on deep mutational scanning assays, ProTEUS learns a joint representation of sequence, evolutionary, and structural information using MutationFormer, a mutation-biased attention architecture. Variants are represented as states in this joint latent space, and mutations define actions whose functional consequences are predicte
s49ee4f8d95.summary: ProTEUS is a mutation-resolved world model pretrained on deep mutational scanning data for in silico closed-loop protein evolution.

s81db90f258.title: When Are Predictions Enough? An Evaluation Protocol for Frozen Expert Composition
s81db90f258.description: arXiv:2611.13356v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Practitioners often combine independently trained models while keeping their weights frozen. These experts are commonly combined through their final predictions, although their internal features may retain useful information that those predictions omit. We ask when combining features improves on combining predictions, and how to make that comparison fair. We introduce a reusable evaluation protocol, apply it to 21 frozen deepfake detectors from DF40 (Yan et al., 2024), and audit how evaluation choices change the conclusions. The protocol uses strong prediction baselines, compares simple and larger feature combiners, varies architecture and training data separately, and reports results by held-out generator with train/test overlap controls.
s81db90f258.summary: Researchers propose an evaluation protocol for combining frozen deepfake detectors, comparing feature combination with prediction combination across 21 DF40 detectors.
s81db90f258.why: Shows how evaluation choices can change conclusions about whether combining features beats combining predictions.

sd6c31b0a32.title: Enforcing Axioms for AI Alignment under Loss-Based Rules
sd6c31b0a32.description: arXiv:2611.13369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many alignment methods, most notably reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), train reward models by minimizing a loss on pairwise comparisons of model responses. Inspired by principle-guided methods such as Constitutional AI, we treat each principle as a voter that compares responses according to that principle, for example, preferring the more helpful or less toxic response. We represent these voters as linear directions in a fixed embedding space, a simplifying assumption motivated by the Linear Representation Hypothesis. In this linear social choice model, Ge et al. (2024) showed that an optimal linear reward model can violate Pareto optimality (PO): From the principles-as-voters lens, this means a response A can be less helpf
sd6c31b0a32.summary: Researchers treat alignment principles as voters over pairwise response comparisons and study enforcing axioms under loss-based reward model training.
sd6c31b0a32.why: Connects principle-guided alignment with reward model training objectives, relevant to alignment method design.

s7936e5709c.title: The AI Era's Lines of Code? A Case Study on What an Engineer's Token Spend Measures
s7936e5709c.description: arXiv:2611.13396v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Organizations use engineers' token spend to monitor AI adoption, set budgets, and measure productivity, but the metric's relationship with engineering output is unclear. We link five weeks of token usage in coding agents to the commits of 404 engineers at JetBrains, and analyze a company survey of 412 employees. We find that token spend varied mostly between engineers, and which engineers spent the most stayed largely the same over the five weeks. Among weeks with similar commit counts, the 90th percentile of spend was 39 to 240 times the 10th. Within an engineer, doubling spend was associated with about 10% more commits. Available work metrics explained 38% of the variation in spend between engineers and 13% of the week-to-week variation w
s7936e5709c.summary: A JetBrains case study links five weeks of coding agent token spend to commits of 404 engineers, finding spend varies mostly between engineers.
s7936e5709c.why: Suggests token spend is a weak proxy for engineering output, a caution for leaders using it as a productivity metric.

s10765b98dd.title: The Dose Makes the Poison: Exposure-Aware Evaluation of Generative Drug Design
s10765b98dd.description: arXiv:2611.13398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative models are increasingly used to propose molecules for drug discovery. They can produce far more candidates than can be experimentally tested, making computational selection essential. Most selection methods rely on predicted molecular properties, such as potency and toxicity, but overlook how these properties translate into drug exposure at a given dose. As a result, molecules that appear promising on paper may require impractical doses or raise safety concerns. We investigate this gap by using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) simulations to re-evaluate molecules selected from three PARP1-targeted generative pipelines. Of 60 shortlisted molecules, seven fail to achieve sufficient target exposure, while 28% of the rema
s10765b98dd.summary: Researchers propose exposure-aware evaluation of generative drug design, using physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling to assess candidate molecules at practical doses.
s10765b98dd.why: Argues that selecting molecules by predicted properties alone overlooks whether they are practical at real doses.

s4c5f07b26f.title: Stinging the Swarm: Extracting Attacker Intelligence from a Twin-Controller OT Honeypot
s4c5f07b26f.description: arXiv:2611.13406v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous language-model agents can drive industrial controllers over fieldbus protocols, probing a plant at machine speed and in coordinated swarms. We present Talos, an inline gate that judges every agent request to a controller in milliseconds and routes agents it flags as hostile to a device-faithful decoy -- a mirror twin of the real plant -- where their attack continues harmlessly and is read for intelligence. We evaluate the full pipeline (detect -> quarantine -> mirror -> extract) against 2,400 autonomous attacker agents, 600 in each of four tiers that escalate the attacker's effort to stay hidden, from no concealment to an explicit non-disclosure rule and a trained cover story. No write reached the real plant in any tier: the gate
s4c5f07b26f.summary: Researchers present Talos, an inline gate that flags hostile LLM agent requests to industrial controllers and diverts them to a mirror-twin decoy to extract attacker intelligence.
s4c5f07b26f.why: OT and ICS operators facing autonomous agent attacks on fieldbus protocols get a concrete detect-quarantine-decoy design to study.

s203c8c072e.title: Bursts That Outlast Themselves: Persistent Degradation in Prefix-Cached Agent Serving
s203c8c072e.description: arXiv:2611.13412v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents drive inference engines with closed-loop sessions whose context grows every turn, and serving them economically depends on prefix caching: a hit costs an incremental prefill of about a thousand tokens, a miss recomputes a 10--40K-token context. We show that this makes prefix-cached agent serving metastable. With an identical base workload, a few minutes of extra arrivals leaves a vLLM server in a degraded regime--a ~10% hit ratio, about half the throughput, and a backlog that grows for the remaining 70 minutes--while its no-burst twin stays healthy (9 of 12 pairs; none in the reverse direction). The regime appears at loads the cache-warm server sustains, is absent without prefix caching, and also appears with Qwen3-32B on SWE-ben
s203c8c072e.summary: A paper shows that bursts of traffic can push a prefix-cached vLLM agent-serving system into a degraded regime with low cache hit ratio and halved throughput that persists after the burst.
s203c8c072e.why: Engineers running multi-turn LLM agents on prefix caching may see sustained performance collapse after transient load spikes.

s8c081fbae1.title: Placing LLM Lookup Tables by Per-Layer Prefetch Deadlines
s8c081fbae1.description: arXiv:2611.13413v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: DeepSeek-V4.1's 203 GB of Engram n-gram tables sit in host DRAM today, taking 190 of the 223 GiB a 4-GPU serving process uses. Row indices depend only on input tokens, so reads can start with each step and overlap earlier layers. V4.1's two Engram layers have windows that differ by 30x (0.3 vs. 9.3 ms). We show that this deadline, together with session reuse and contention on a shared device, decides which tier each table can use and which layers need cache, and we give a model that predicts the resulting slowdown from measured read times. Agent and chat traffic reuse rows within sessions, and static hot sets transfer poorly. We build SlackTier, a table tier for SGLang that issues all lookups at step start. It reads the short-window layer f
s8c081fbae1.summary: A paper proposes placing DeepSeek-V4.1's 203 GB of Engram n-gram lookup tables across memory tiers based on per-layer prefetch deadlines, and models the resulting slowdown.
s8c081fbae1.why: Serving teams sizing host memory and GPU cache for large lookup-table models can use the deadline-based placement model.

s2ced68674c.title: Free Lunch Uncertainty: Sequence-Level R\'enyi Entropy from Particle Decoding for Adaptive LLM Reasoning
s2ced68674c.description: arXiv:2611.13414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantifying uncertainty over an entire LLM completion is critical for selective prediction and adaptive compute. Zero-cost signals such as mean token entropy and log-probability are local to tokens or to one completion, and self-consistency needs many extra completions. We show that Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) decoding for power sampling already estimates the normalizing constant of the power distribution, which gives the sequence-level R'enyi entropy (SRE) of the model's completion distribution at zero marginal cost, with a guarantee at every particle budget. A R'enyi chain rule extends this readout to a family of stepwise entropies of any order. We prove that orders above one are tied to the most likely token of each step, which explains
s2ced68674c.summary: Researchers show that sequence-level Rényi entropy can be estimated at zero extra cost from Sequential Monte Carlo decoding used for power sampling, for adaptive LLM reasoning.
s2ced68674c.why: It offers a free uncertainty signal for selective prediction and adaptive compute without the cost of multiple sampled completions.

s344b696db4.title: You Don't Need Feature Learning to Do In-Context Learning
s344b696db4.description: arXiv:2611.13431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How should we understand memorization vs. generalization in in-context learning (ICL) tasks, and when does one happen vs. the other? To investigate, we study how rotation-invariant kernel machines learn the ICL linear regression task proposed by Raventos et al. (2023). By decomposing the task in the kernel eigenbasis, we obtain a spectral picture of learning in this ICL setting. This picture reveals that as sample size grows, kernel machines learn successively-higher-degree components of the memorizing solution, which depend upon successively-higher-degree statistics of the training task set. The generalizing solution is approximately a low-degree truncation of the memorizing solution, and so the model first generalizes, then degrades into
s344b696db4.summary: A theoretical paper studies how rotation-invariant kernel machines learn the in-context linear regression task, using a spectral view of memorization versus generalization.

s3cc08dcc95.title: Inherited Weights: Measuring the Tokenization Premium and the Sovereignty Cost of Language Models for the Global South
s3cc08dcc95.description: arXiv:2611.13441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most language models deployed outside the United States and China are fine-tuned descendants of a small number of pretrained families. We argue that fine-tuning leaves the decisive properties of a model inherited from its base: vocabulary, knowledge, cultural alignment, memorized data and license. We contribute (i) an updated, reproducible measurement of the tokenization premium across 31 languages and 7 tokenizers released in 2023-2024, on 27 articles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, with explicit correction for unknown-token collapse. Premiums reach 10x for Amharic in older tokenizers and remain at 6.8x in the newest commercial one; Indigenous South American languages pay between 1.6x and 2.7x under global tokenizers. A vocab
s3cc08dcc95.summary: A paper measures a tokenization premium across 31 languages and 7 tokenizers and argues that fine-tuned models inherit vocabulary, knowledge, and license from a few base families, affecting sovereignty.
s3cc08dcc95.why: Teams building models or products for non-US and non-China markets should weigh inherited tokenizer costs and base-model licensing.

s6b61db8712.title: ForeSpark: Joint Draft and Verification Budget Scheduling for Parallel Speculative Decoding
s6b61db8712.description: arXiv:2611.13442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parallel drafters accelerate LLM decoding by proposing a whole block of draft tokens in a single forward pass, making them attractive for LLM serving. Recent systems optimize goodput (i.e., accepted tokens per second) because rejected drafts steal compute from other requests. However, these systems control only how many tokens are verified, so every request still drafts a full block. At high serving load, we find that drafting consumes up to 40% of step time, of which a majority is discarded because it is never verified. Yet, draft-length control from autoregressive drafters does not carry over, because a parallel drafter commits to its length before its single pass. Moreover, draft and verification lengths are coupled across the batch, so
s6b61db8712.summary: ForeSpark proposes jointly scheduling draft and verification budgets for parallel speculative decoding, reporting that drafting can consume up to 40% of step time under high load.
s6b61db8712.why: Inference-serving engineers can reduce wasted drafting compute at high load by adapting draft length per request.

seb351c272e.title: Leveraging Psychophysical Attentional Distribution for Gaze-Augmented Reward Modeling
seb351c272e.description: arXiv:2611.13477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrating human feedback into language models has gained increasing attention as a means to align model outputs with human preferences, with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) serving as a prominent framework for preference-based alignment. Recent studies have incorporated eye-tracking (ET) data as an additional supervisory signal for reward model training, grounding reward learning in human reading behavior. Building on this approach, we extend prior fixation-centric models by leveraging established findings from cognitive psychology on human letter recognition. Specifically, we model visual attention as a spatially graded distribution centered on the current gaze location and incorporate this representation into reward mo
seb351c272e.summary: Researchers propose a gaze-augmented reward model for RLHF that uses psychophysical attentional distribution from eye-tracking data as a supervisory signal.

s7554eaeab4.title: Sharp Sample Complexity of KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning
s7554eaeab4.description: arXiv:2611.13480v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: KL-regularized reinforcement learning, the objective behind maximum-entropy RL and RL from human feedback, is variational inference in the graphical model of "control as inference": the regularized optimal policy is a posterior over trajectories, and the suboptimality of a policy is $\beta$ times a KL divergence between path measures. However, it is not known how many samples it takes to learn this posterior, even with a generative model. Earlier $1/\epsilon$ guarantees scale with $H^5$ in the effective horizon $H$, and no lower bound for MDPs depends on the temperature $\beta$. In this work, we show that for a discounted MDP with $K$ state-action pairs, the plug-in estimator finds a policy that is $\epsilon$-optimal from every initial stat
s7554eaeab4.summary: A paper studies the sample complexity of KL-regularized reinforcement learning, improving prior guarantees that scaled with the effective horizon to the fifth power.

s8ee85a0ad5.title: Reasoning-Aware Relational Representation Learning for Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation
s8ee85a0ad5.description: arXiv:2611.13496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-Vocabulary Scene Graph Generation (OV-SGG) requires models to recognize visual relationships beyond the training vocabulary, yet existing methods often rely on dataset-specific object--predicate co-occurrence patterns. Under long-tailed distributions and noisy object localization, such reliance leads to biased, entangled relation representations, limiting both rare-relation recognition and generalization to unseen predicates. To address these challenges, we propose RaRe, a reasoning-aware relational representation learning framework that transforms MLLM-generated chain-of-thought (CoT) rationales into structured relation embeddings. Rather than using CoT only as an intermediate reasoning trace for final prediction, RaRe directly optimi
s8ee85a0ad5.summary: Researchers introduce RaRe, a reasoning-aware relational representation learning framework for open-vocabulary scene graph generation to handle long-tailed relations.

s07ef33281d.title: Dark Matters: VAE-Aware HDR Encoding for SDR-to-HDR Video Reconstruction
s07ef33281d.description: arXiv:2611.13504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: SDR-to-HDR reconstruction is an ill-posed problem in which clipped highlights, crushed shadows, and quantization artifacts must be recovered while preserving the original content. Latent diffusion models provide powerful generative priors for restoring missing detail, but their effectiveness is constrained by how HDR signals pass through the pretrained VAE. We find that common log-like encodings suppress low-luminance chromatic differences before generation, producing a dark-side collapse in the frozen-VAE latent. We introduce EquivFlow, a compact, invertible exposure-equivariant encoding that maps exposure changes to additive shifts while retaining a scale-independent chromatic component, without modifying the VAE. Encoding-level tests acr
s07ef33281d.summary: Researchers introduce EquivFlow, an encoding for SDR-to-HDR video reconstruction that addresses dark-side collapse in the frozen VAE latent of latent diffusion models.
s07ef33281d.why: Teams using latent diffusion for video restoration may gain better HDR reconstruction by changing how signals pass through the VAE.

sbd483352e8.title: Developing an Operational Model for an Internet of Data Based Trusted Data Space for Vocational Education
sbd483352e8.description: arXiv:2611.13520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data circulation in vocational education has long been constrained by unclear ownership, a lack of trust, and insufficient incentives. The Internet of Data provides a new underlying technology for enabling trusted cross-domain data circulation. Building on an Internet of Data based trusted data space for vocational education, this paper develops a multi-stakeholder operational model encompassing a value network, a product portfolio, revenue allocation, and governance rules. Emphasizing data sovereignty protection and incentive compatibility, the model provides a reference for the sustainable operation of regional vocational education data ecosystems.
sbd483352e8.summary: A paper develops a multi-stakeholder operational model for a trusted Internet of Data based data space for vocational education, covering value network, revenue allocation, and governance.

s5e58811dbf.title: Massive Activations Confound Sparse Autoencoders
s5e58811dbf.description: arXiv:2611.13548v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are commonly evaluated by variance explained and ablation damage. We show how massive activations undermine both evaluations, and propose a correction. Massive activations cause up to 99.9% of activation variance to lie along the first principal component (PC1). Because the PC1 component has no unique sparse decomposition, each SAE run rebuilds it from a different set of features. These features dominate importance rankings: an average of 47 of the 50 most important features are unmatched in a separate run, compared with about 27 of a random 50. A dictionary can also report 99.96% of variance explained while leaving 33% of the variance outside PC1 unexplained. We bypass PC1 by training the SAE on activations with
s5e58811dbf.summary: A paper shows that massive activations can make up to 99.9% of activation variance lie along the first principal component, undermining common sparse autoencoder evaluations, and proposes a correction.
s5e58811dbf.why: Interpretability researchers relying on variance explained or ablation damage to judge SAEs may draw misleading conclusions without this correction.

s05d198b7bb.title: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
s05d198b7bb.description: arXiv:2611.13560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: RLVR trains language models to reason by rewarding correct final answers. A widely used algorithm, group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), gives every token of a solution the same credit, so dense process rewards have been proposed to credit intermediate steps, for example with a Monte-Carlo reward that scores each step by sampling continuations from it. Comparing such a reward with GRPO per training update, or vetting it with a gradient test on a single batch, leaves out what it costs: in our setting, the continuations alone take 91% of all generated tokens. We introduce a matched-compute protocol that gives every training intervention the same budget, measured in generated tokens and training GPU-hours, and tests it in preregistered st
s05d198b7bb.summary: A study questions whether dense Monte-Carlo process rewards are worth their cost in GRPO, finding continuations alone take 91% of total training compute in their setting.
s05d198b7bb.why: Teams training reasoning models with RLVR should account for the large compute overhead of dense process rewards before adopting them.

scadacec90a.title: A Concept-Based Interpretable Framework for Clinical Text-based Prediction via Token-Concept Attention without Concept Supervision
scadacec90a.description: arXiv:2611.13564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Objective: Concept-based interpretation has emerged as a promising approach for explaining blackbox models using human-understandable, high-level concepts. However, most existing methods require annotated concept labels to train the model to identify concepts in the input, and obtaining such annotations in clinical text is often expensive. This study aims to enable concept-based interpretation for language models without concept supervision on clinical prediction tasks. Methods: We propose a novel framework that enables concept-based interpretation without concept supervision through a tailored cross-attention bottleneck. Clinical text and the text descriptions of medical concepts are first tokenized and embedded by a pretrained language mo
scadacec90a.summary: Researchers propose a concept-based interpretable framework for clinical text prediction using token-concept attention, without requiring annotated concept labels.

s2ee90c02a3.title: Metamorphic testing of learned AC optimal power flow surrogates reveals representation dependence
s2ee90c02a3.description: arXiv:2611.13566v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating a learned AC optimal power flow (AC-OPF) surrogate on one grid serialization cannot show whether its accuracy depends on that encoding. We test this dependence with thirteen metamorphic relations, each specifying when a transformation is valid and how to compare its outputs. Our audit covers 17 model and pipeline configurations: two released trained checkpoints and 15 random-weight architecture or mechanism controls. Every configuration violates at least six relations, even at reporting tolerances ten times tighter or looser. For GridSFM-Open v1.1, source inspection and intermediate-tensor interventions point to an indexing bug and three noncanonical or numerically unstable preprocessing choices; a repaired checkpoint remains unt
s2ee90c02a3.summary: Researchers applied thirteen metamorphic relations to learned AC optimal power flow surrogates and found every tested configuration violates at least six relations.
s2ee90c02a3.why: Shows that surrogate accuracy for grid models can depend on how the grid data is serialized, so single-encoding evaluations may overstate reliability.

s50eba93b06.title: Market-Conditioned JEPA: Learning from Unpredictable Market Shocks
s50eba93b06.description: arXiv:2611.13572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Much of the variation in financial time series is driven by market-wide shocks that cannot be predicted from an asset's own history. Per-asset self-supervised learning treats this variation as irreducible noise. Under a latent factor model, we show that conditioning prediction on the realized market factor makes the asset's market exposure necessary for optimal prediction, while reducing the noise against which the asset-specific component is learned. Building on this insight, we introduce Market-Conditioned JEPA (MC-JEPA), a joint-embedding predictive architecture for financial time series. During training, we construct a leave-one-out market condition for each asset from the future target embeddings of other assets and incorporate it thro
s50eba93b06.summary: Researchers propose Market-Conditioned JEPA, a self-supervised model that conditions asset prediction on the realized market factor instead of treating market-wide shocks as noise.
s50eba93b06.why: Offers a modeling approach for financial time series that separates market-wide shocks from asset-specific signals, relevant to quant and ML teams.

s00d813f9f3.title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
s00d813f9f3.description: arXiv:2611.13576v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly positioned as world simulators, it is essential to evaluate whether their videos conform to physical commonsense. However, existing benchmarks rely on annotators who rate each video with a single score based on intuition, yielding ratings that are subjective and do not tell which physical principle is violated. We introduce PhyRubric, a rubric-grounded diagnostic framework for evaluating physical commonsense in T2V generation. For each caption, PhyRubric constructs a caption-specific rubric before any video is seen, decomposing the caption into semantic and physical items, and derives scores from item-level verdicts grounded in timestamped evidence. We instantiate this framework as PhyRubric-Be
s00d813f9f3.summary: PhyRubric is a rubric-based diagnostic framework that scores text-to-video outputs on physical commonsense by checking caption-specific principles.
s00d813f9f3.why: Gives teams a more diagnostic way to evaluate video generation for physical plausibility than single subjective ratings.

s3a1f8ba10f.title: Synapse-Control: Making Agent Experience Actionable with Lightweight Runtime Control
s3a1f8ba10f.description: arXiv:2611.13615v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model agents reuse execution experience to improve reliability on complex tool-based tasks. Systems such as Sentry call large models to generate failure diagnoses before retrieving advice, adding inference cost to experience reuse. We present Synapse-Control, an agent runtime whose lightweight control plane selects advice and determines when to send it to the task-executing model. Rules shortlist relevant advice, and a lightweight 1.7B classifier fine-tuned on teacher-labeled state-suggestion pairs scores those candidates instead of generating a diagnosis. Micro-contracts encode reusable interface checks, such as required arguments or valid options, without prescribing complete task programs. A Prompt Value Table records earl
s3a1f8ba10f.summary: Synapse-Control is an agent runtime whose lightweight control plane selects experience-based advice and decides when to send it, using a 1.7B classifier instead of large-model diagnoses.
s3a1f8ba10f.why: Suggests a lower-cost way to reuse agent execution experience without adding large-model inference overhead to every retrieval step.

seab9fc0f84.title: MOAI: Module-Optimizing Architecture for non-interactive secure transformer Inference
seab9fc0f84.description: arXiv:2611.13641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Privacy concerns have been raised in Large Language Models (LLM) inference when models are deployed in Cloud Service Providers (CSP). Homomorphic encryption (HE) offers a promising solution by enabling secure inference directly over encrypted inputs. However, the high computational overhead of HE remains a major bottleneck. To address this challenge, we propose MOAI, an efficient HE-based, non-interactive framework for secure transformer inference. MOAI gains significant efficiency improvement from: (1) a novel evaluation flow that combines column and diagonal packing with consistent strategies across all layers, eliminating expensive format conversions. (2) rotation-free algorithms for Softmax and LayerNorm that significantly reduce the nu
seab9fc0f84.summary: MOAI is a homomorphic-encryption framework for non-interactive secure transformer inference, aiming to reduce HE's computational overhead for LLM inference in cloud settings.
seab9fc0f84.why: Addresses privacy for cloud-hosted LLM inference, though the text provides limited detail on measured performance gains.

s41572b1ed7.title: Bootstrapped On-Policy Distillation
s41572b1ed7.description: arXiv:2611.13680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves language models by distilling teacher predictions on student-generated trajectories, while on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) removes the need for an external teacher by using a reference-conditioned copy of the model as the teacher. Despite its great early improvements, we find that OPSD does not remain consistently effective under continued training and can eventually suffer substantial performance degradation. We study this training behavior and link the degradation to a growing mismatch between the evolving reference-free student and the frozen privileged teacher. In the early stage of OPSD, the privileged teacher remains closely aligned with the student and provides useful guidance for improving th
s41572b1ed7.summary: Researchers find on-policy self-distillation degrades under continued training due to a growing mismatch between the evolving student and its reference-conditioned teacher, and study this behavior.
s41572b1ed7.why: Warns teams using self-distillation for LLM training that gains may reverse with longer training runs.

sf9dc12b18f.title: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
sf9dc12b18f.description: arXiv:2611.13685v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate how human egocentric videos can benefit robot policy learning without action supervision. Building on a pretrained VLM, we propose Shared Prediction on Action and Representation (SPAR), an MoT architecture in which future visual state prediction can provide independent and complementary learning signals alongside action prediction. We find that representations learned from egocentric videos improve downstream performance on out-of-distribution robot tasks, with further gains as video data scales. We also study the effects of objective choices and data curation, providing insights into how to leverage action-free videos for scalable robot learning.
sf9dc12b18f.summary: Ego Guidance proposes SPAR, a model that uses action-free human egocentric videos alongside action prediction to improve robot policy learning on out-of-distribution tasks.
sf9dc12b18f.why: Suggests unlabeled human video can improve robot policies, reducing dependence on costly action-labeled robot data.

sca14ffd310.title: AURA: Auditory Spatial Intelligence via a Unified Representation from a General-Audio Encoder through Complete Alignment
sca14ffd310.description: arXiv:2611.13687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Answering spatial questions about multi-source scenes requires a model both to identify each sound and to locate it. Existing spatial audio-language models obtain spatial information from a dedicated encoder, which separates spatial and semantic processing into distinct feature spaces. We study whether a general-audio codec trained without spatial supervision can serve both purposes. A controlled layer-wise analysis shows that the frozen codec retains spatial information, with lateral cues carried by the difference between the two ear channels. This information, however, is not readily accessible: in dual-source scenes, a model trained on these features predicts left/right at chance and, on the remaining axes, assigns the detected direction
sca14ffd310.summary: AURA uses a general-audio encoder, trained without spatial supervision, to handle spatial audio question answering, arguing a frozen codec retains spatial information.
sca14ffd310.why: Indicates a single general-audio encoder may serve both semantic and spatial audio tasks, simplifying multimodal audio architectures.

s316fdbda22.title: On Private Knowledge Retrieval and Private Inference for secure multi-agent systems
s316fdbda22.description: arXiv:2611.13696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems provide a convenient framework for the massive deployment of agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs). It provides a sound framework where agents can interact with existing software to perform actions in an autonomous way. Agentic AI is the new term to denote these AI-based autonomous systems. In real multi-agent systems, agents need to deal with malicious agents some of which can exploit security vulnerabilities to do harm. A memory poisoning attack is an example of exploiting a vulnerability to modify agents knowledge and, thus, affect its behavior. In an agent, there are different types of memory systems (semantic, episodic, and short-term) which have their own characteristics and for which different memory poison
s316fdbda22.summary: The paper studies private knowledge retrieval and private inference for secure multi-agent LLM systems, addressing threats such as memory poisoning by malicious agents.
s316fdbda22.why: Highlights security risks like memory poisoning in multi-agent systems that teams deploying autonomous agents must address.

sbf40dbb689.title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits
sbf40dbb689.description: arXiv:2611.13755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum hardware can provide feedback for training circuit generators beyond the reach of exact classical simulation. We train generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) policies, transformers conditioned on molecular descriptors, to generate the state-preparation circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). Training runs first on a noiseless simulator and then with the IBM Heron processor ibm_kobe inside the loop, at 46 and 70 qubits ($1.2 \times 10^8$ shots for the four main training runs). A classical CCSD(T) reference energy of the training molecules enters only an admission gate and two auxiliary reward terms. During hardware training, a reward penalty prevents collapse to circuits that sample only the Hartree-Fock determinant. P
sbf40dbb689.summary: Researchers trained generative quantum eigensolver policies on IBM's Heron processor, with hardware in the training loop, for sample-based diagonalization of organotin hydroxides up to 70 qubits.
sbf40dbb689.why: Demonstrates hardware-in-the-loop training of circuit generators at 70 qubits, a concrete data point for quantum chemistry workflows.

s96e26867c6.title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
s96e26867c6.description: arXiv:2611.13758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weight-space programming allows language models to read a trained neural network's weights and edit them. This opens the door to ``training'' by reasoning rather than through gradient descent. Prior work has demonstrated its functionality and promise for game-playing networks and fixing specific failures in language models, even extending to diffusion models. In this work, we present its applicability to models trained on biosignal data, specifically EEG and ECG data. We show that frontier models are not only able to debug specific faults planted in biosignal-based models without being told what these faults are, but are even capable of writing all the weights of a network from scratch, given only the architecture, the task, and a minimal s
s96e26867c6.summary: The paper shows that weight-space programming, where language models read and edit trained network weights, can be applied to EEG and ECG models to debug planted faults.
s96e26867c6.why: Extends weight-editing-by-reasoning to biosignal models, an early result with limited detail on generality.

s7202f7a89c.title: DisasterAgent: An Evidence-Driven Agent for Verifiable Disaster Report Generation From Remote Sensing Imagery
s7202f7a89c.description: arXiv:2611.13776v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Remote sensing disaster assessment is moving from simple damage classification toward comprehensive report-level analysis. In this setting, responders need not only damage descriptions but also verifiable evidence to guide response and recovery. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) and tool-augmented agents offer strong multimodal reasoning and perception, but they struggle to provide the evidence required for high-stakes verification. To address these limitations, we propose DisasterAgent, an evidence-driven agent that uses a Perception-Augmentation-Generation workflow to generate verifiable disaster reports from bitemporal optical imagery. DisasterAgent first invokes a specialized vision expert toolkit in the perception phase to build a S
s7202f7a89c.summary: DisasterAgent is an evidence-driven agent that generates verifiable disaster reports from remote sensing imagery using perception-augmented tools.
s7202f7a89c.why: Shows an approach to making agent-generated assessments verifiable through evidence, relevant to high-stakes agent deployments.

sac68f60550.title: Softness is something you also need! Why compliance helps control: information metrics of a passive walker with compliant ankle
sac68f60550.description: arXiv:2611.13779v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A great gap in adaptivity, flexibility, and dexterity still exists between intelligent robots, whether they are made of rigid or (partially) compliant components, and their naturally evolved animal and vegetal counterparts. One reason could be of `paradigm' nature. On the one hand, most robots (both rigid and soft) are still designed by following a `Cartesian' approach, with top-down control and a clear mind-body separation. Designing artificial agents on the basis of the principles that we observe in biology is not an easy task. The principles of organization of animals and plants rely on morphological computation and emergence of fit behaviors from loosely coupled networks of embodied agents. Modeling and control require radically new app
sac68f60550.summary: A study of a passive walking robot with a compliant ankle uses information metrics to argue that compliance helps control.

se7605a215c.title: Bridging Graph and Pairwise Learning for Gene Regulatory Network Inference from scRNA-seq Data
se7605a215c.description: arXiv:2611.13801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivation: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) capture the underlying interactions through which transcription factors (TFs) regulate genes. Based on gene expression data, existing GRN inference approaches generally fall into two categories: graph-based methods, which model the GRN as a whole graph, and pairwise-based methods, which decompose the GRN into individual TF-target gene pairs for modeling. However, each approach exhibits limitations that are precisely the strengths of its counterpart. Graph-based methods tend to overfit due to their reliance on a single training graph, whereas pairwise-based methods benefit from abundant TF-target training pairs. In contrast, pairwise-based methods overlook the global topological structure, which is
se7605a215c.summary: The paper proposes combining graph-based and pairwise learning to infer gene regulatory networks from scRNA-seq data, addressing overfitting in graph methods.
se7605a215c.why: Offers a hybrid modeling approach for bioinformatics GRN inference, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s1ae4860748.title: Relaxing Cross-Modal Correspondence for Multimodal Remote Sensing Pretraining
s1ae4860748.description: arXiv:2611.13807v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal remote sensing pretraining commonly relies on exact instance-level correspondence across modalities, implicitly treating strictly paired observations as a prerequisite for learning transferable representations. In this work, we revisit this assumption by relaxing cross-modal correspondence from the instance level to the semantic level. We introduce Semantic Pairing (SemPair), a pairing-relaxed pretraining strategy that replaces exact instance pairs with class-consistent cross-instance pairs. To characterize the effect of correspondence relaxation, we formulate a latent-factor model that separates cross-modal dependence into shared semantic structure and instance-specific correlation, showing that SemPair preserves the former whil
s1ae4860748.summary: SemPair relaxes cross-modal pairing in multimodal remote sensing pretraining from instance-level to class-consistent semantic pairs.
s1ae4860748.why: Suggests pretraining may not need exact paired multimodal data, potentially easing dataset construction for remote sensing models.

s70c7eec9e7.title: Swanada: Split-Encoder Capability-Routed Conformer CTC and Sub-30 MB On-Device Speech Recognition Across Twelve Scripts
s70c7eec9e7.description: arXiv:2611.13814v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Client-side automatic speech recognition (ASR) across Indic and Classical scripts eliminates cloud transcription costs, network tail latency, and server-side audio retention, yet neural exports face four systems bottlenecks in browsers and mobile runtimes: (1) monolithic per-language Conformer checkpoints require ~177 MiB per script (> 2.1 GiB across 12 scripts), exhausting CacheStorage quotas; (2) static relative positional encoding tables embed 10.2-20.5 MB of FP32 constants while 1x1 Conv1d layers trigger slow or unsupported ConvInteger kernels in WebAssembly SIMD; (3) sliding-window CTC flickers on boundary tokens; and (4) mobile WebAudio pipelines suffer 44.1/48 kHz sample-rate mismatches and silent AudioWorklet stalls under iOS WKWebV
s70c7eec9e7.summary: Researchers present Swanada, a split-encoder Conformer CTC speech recognition system that runs on-device under 30 MB across twelve Indic and classical scripts.
s70c7eec9e7.why: It targets browser and mobile runtime bottlenecks like storage quotas and unsupported ops, relevant to anyone shipping client-side ASR.

se35b10d15e.title: CASCADE: Constraint-Aware SCAffolded DEcomposition for Logical Anomaly Detection
se35b10d15e.description: arXiv:2611.13820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Logical Anomaly Detection (LAD) requires verifying whether all category-specific constraints, such as object counts, pairing relations, and measurement ranges, are satisfied by a query image given only a few normal references. Recent LAD methods based on Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) formulate this as checklist verification, decomposing the decision into independent textual checks. This decomposition, however, is text-only. Every item still reads the same unmodified query image, so the LVLM must extract different forms of visual evidence from one raw image. We identify this text-image mismatch as a constraint-specific perception gap, the source of two failure modes: instance conflation for binding constraints and scale drift for cali
se35b10d15e.summary: CASCADE proposes a constraint-aware, scaffolded decomposition method for logical anomaly detection using large vision-language models with few normal references.

s1d7fcd51b4.title: MusicFlux: Flexible Conditioning for Text-Guided Music Generation and Editing
s1d7fcd51b4.description: arXiv:2611.13834v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Music editing transforms existing recordings while preserving their original attributes. Recent approaches adapt pretrained text-to-music models for tasks like inpainting, event insertion, or restoration by conditioning them with context audio.
