s2b6eba6832.description: arXiv:2607.22639v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parametric retrieval enables LLMs to retrieve tools implicitly by assigning each API a unique virtual token and training the model to generate it via constrained beam search. Toolsense shows that this regime has two critical drawbacks: it destroys parametric tool knowledge during training, and its beam-search decoding is too slow for real-time deployment. We introduce TRACE (Tool Retrieval via Augmented Chain-of-thought and Enterprise rules), a two-stage curriculum that resolves this dissociation. Stage 1 reuses the multi-format memorization SFT from ToolSense to seed tool knowledge with LoRA. Stage 2 is our core contribution: the model is trained to emit a thinking trace before producing a JSON list of tool tokens, using two data sources
s2b6eba6832.summary: TRACE proposes a two-stage curriculum for parametric tool retrieval in enterprise LLMs, aiming to preserve tool knowledge and speed up decoding versus beam search.
s2b6eba6832.why: It targets two known drawbacks of parametric tool retrieval, knowledge loss and slow decoding, relevant to enterprise agent deployments.

sdfe1290cb7.title: Messier: A High-Resolution Corpus for Cross-Benchmark Agent Evaluation
sdfe1290cb7.description: arXiv:2607.25891v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Comprehensively evaluating AI agents across interactive environments is difficult due to fragmented tasks, scaffolds, verifiers, and scoring rules. Unfortunately, existing efforts to unify these evaluations are limited in scale and domain, making costly reruns necessary and leaving available data incomparable. We introduce Messier, a unified corpus of 923,158 records spanning 30 benchmarks, 745 agents, 11,891 tasks, and 71,969 verifiers. Messier combines public evaluation results with new runs on six underrepresented professional and scientific benchmarks, standardizing their heterogeneous components into a common schema. Using this corpus, we show that frontier progress is uneven across benchmark groups, with function-calling evaluations
sdfe1290cb7.summary: Messier is a unified corpus of 923,158 agent evaluation records spanning 30 benchmarks, 745 agents, and 11,891 tasks, with new runs on underrepresented domains.
sdfe1290cb7.why: A standardized, comparable evaluation dataset could reduce costly reruns when benchmarking agents across fragmented suites.

sc588ecbbc3.title: Probing the Origins of Reasoning Performance: Representational Quality for Mathematical Problem-Solving in RL vs. SFT Fine-Tuned Models
sc588ecbbc3.description: arXiv:2607.26119v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models trained with reinforcement learning (RL) to reason step by step have been increasingly shown to outperform their supervised fine-tuned (SFT) counterparts on mathematical reasoning tasks. Yet the mechanistic basis for this improvement remains unclear. We therefore ask, what internal representational differences enable RL-trained reasoning language models to reason better? Our work presents two primary lines of evidence: First, layer-wise linear probes tend to predict answer correctness more accurately in RL-trained reasoning language models than in instruction-tuned models on synthetic math problems, although output length alone matches the DeepSeek-Math-RL probe on two templates. Second, mean ablation studies suggest
sc588ecbbc3.summary: Researchers probe internal representations of RL-trained versus SFT-trained language models to explain why RL improves mathematical reasoning.
sc588ecbbc3.why: Understanding where RL reasoning gains appear internally can guide choices between RL and SFT fine-tuning pipelines.

s41e87da7e1.title: When Words and Bodies Disagree: Realizing Verbal and Nonverbal Mismatch
s41e87da7e1.description: arXiv:2608.22731v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Traditional nonverbal behavior generation systems for virtual agents typically take utterances as input and generate behaviors that match or illustrate the spoken words. However, human nonverbal behavior is shaped by more than speech content. It is influenced by speaker roles, interpersonal relationships, social context, and cognitive and emotional states of interactants. Therefore, the nonverbal channel carries information or emotions hidden in words. Modeling these complex verbal-nonverbal mismatches is critical for realistic virtual agents, particularly in training applications. We propose a taxonomy of mismatches, strengthening, mitigating, and leaking, and evaluate whether LLMs can select contextually appropriate mismatched behaviors
s41e87da7e1.summary: Researchers study modeling verbal-nonverbal mismatch so virtual agents can generate body behaviors that differ from or contradict their spoken words.
s41e87da7e1.why: It may matter for building more realistic embodied agents, though the abstract gives little concrete technical detail.

s0b95dbf8d7.title: Learning Action Models with Conditional and Quantified Effects via Uncertainty-Guided Exploration
s0b95dbf8d7.description: arXiv:2608.30955v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate action models are critical for effective planning. Existing action-model learning methods largely assume simple action representations or become computationally intractable when learning conditional and quantified effects. We present Online Hypothesis-Driven Conditional Action Model Learning (OHCAM), an online approach for learning action models with conditional and quantified effects from limited interactions with the environment. OHCAM maintains a belief over hypothesized action models and actively selects informative actions to reduce uncertainty by maximizing disagreement among competing hypotheses, while being robust to noisy observations. To enable scalability, OHCAM begins with a small set of simple action model hypotheses
s0b95dbf8d7.summary: OHCAM is an online method that learns action models with conditional and quantified effects by maintaining beliefs over hypotheses and selecting informative actions.
s0b95dbf8d7.why: Learning richer action effects from limited interaction could make planning systems work in more complex environments.

s6508b597e0.title: Purin: A Biology-inspired Mechanism for Artificial Neural Networks
s6508b597e0.description: arXiv:2609.31235v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) usually represent neural transmission with fixed trainable weights during a training batch, which omits short-term changes in synaptic efficacy. In addition, the discrete time-step simulation requires additional temporal processing that many conventional ANN architectures do not use. To overcome these challenges, we propose Purin, a biology-inspired and ANN-compatible mechanism, that introduces synaptic efficacy modulation into conventional convolutional neural networks. Purin uses a time-interval-based abstraction for neural activities, which allows Purin to introduce short- and long-term synaptic efficacy changes without using discrete time-steps. Purin introduces a bounded factor to represent temporary
s6508b597e0.summary: Purin is a biology-inspired mechanism that adds synaptic efficacy modulation with time-interval abstraction to convolutional neural networks.
s6508b597e0.why: It proposes a drop-in way to model short-term synaptic changes in CNNs, though the abstract gives limited evidence of benefit.

s07430563ae.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Agent Distillation across Models, Artifacts, and Harnesses
s07430563ae.description: arXiv:2609.36630v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Knowledge distillation provides a teacher-student framework for transferring capabilities at reduced cost and has been widely studied for large language models (LLMs). As LLM-based agents move from response generation to sustained, closed-loop task solving, distillation expands beyond model parameters to knowledge retained in reusable resources and execution workflows. This shift from model-level to agent-level knowledge transfer supports efficient deployment, broader capability access, and continual self-evolution. However, existing surveys largely examine model distillation and agent system design separately, limiting comparison of transfer strategies across agent components. To bridge this gap, we formalize Agent Distillation as persis
s07430563ae.summary: A survey reviews agent distillation, extending knowledge distillation from model parameters to reusable artifacts and execution harnesses for LLM agents.
s07430563ae.why: It maps how agent-level knowledge transfer could cut deployment costs beyond model compression alone.

sf5f8670a0d.title: Decide, Ask, or Defer: Clinical LLMs under Incomplete Evidence
sf5f8670a0d.description: arXiv:2610.04542v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Clinical LLMs must decide not only what diagnosis to produce, but also whether the available evidence is sufficient for autonomous decision making. Binary DECIDE/ABSTAIN formulations merge distinct non decision states and do not explicitly evaluate information acquisition. We introduce a DECIDE/ASK/DEFER formulation together with a blinded protocol that prevents models from using evidence completeness metadata. We evaluate Qwen, Gemini, and GPT on 200 matched clinical evidence states constructed from DDXPlus. The models show substantial differences in action selection under identical evidence, with disagreement in 137 of 200 states. For Qwen, a matched targeted versus random analysis shows that selected information changes the likelihood
sf5f8670a0d.summary: Researchers propose a DECIDE/ASK/DEFER framework for clinical LLMs facing incomplete evidence, and evaluate Qwen, Gemini, and GPT on 200 DDXPlus-based evidence states.
sf5f8670a0d.why: Clinical deployments need models that know when to acquire more information or defer, not just decide or abstain.

sa91962390c.title: Bridging the Evidence-to-Execution Gap:A Reflective Agent for Multi-Objective Peptide Design
sa91962390c.description: arXiv:2610.06190v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models can reason over scientific literature, but textual plans do not reliably produce biological sequences with the intended properties. Sequence generators capture sequence patterns, yet they do not interpret evidence, choose interventions, or reflect on outcomes. This separation creates an evidence-to-execution gap between scientific reasoning and sequence-level control. We introduce EASER, a reflective agent that connects the two through a learned property interface. The interface consists of property-specific low-rank directions trained offline and fixed during search; an LLM controller (the controller) composes them to steer a frozen diffusion generator. From retrieved evidence, sequence context, and prior outcomes,
sa91962390c.summary: Researchers introduce EASER, a reflective agent that links LLM scientific reasoning to sequence generators via a learned property interface for multi-objective peptide design.
sa91962390c.why: Shows a method to bridge text-level reasoning and controllable sequence generation, relevant to agent designs in biology pipelines.

sa05cef414f.title: GAGR-Lab: Evaluating Joint Spatial-Geometric and Analytic Function Reasoning
sa05cef414f.description: arXiv:2610.10201v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Joint spatial-geometric and analytic function reasoning requires translating a perceived spatial configuration into a symbolic function whose executed curve satisfies geometric constraints. We present GAGR-Lab, a framework for measuring this capability through Cartesian game scenes, explicit function semantics, and authoritative Rust trajectory execution. It distinguishes spatial perception, metric grounding, geometric relations, function interpretation, function construction, and constrained synthesis. We specify four configurable scene-difficulty presets and a prospective 24-cell diagnostic design, while reporting only the subset actually evaluated. A bounded pilot of one hosted model (Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct) using two API creden
sa05cef414f.summary: Researchers present GAGR-Lab, a benchmark framework for testing joint spatial-geometric and analytic function reasoning using game scenes and Rust trajectory execution.
sa05cef414f.why: Offers a structured way to evaluate whether models can turn spatial configurations into symbolic functions that satisfy constraints.

s8ae7e35806.title: MSCR: Jointly Balancing Utilization Across Modalities and Discovering Synergistic Information
s8ae7e35806.description: arXiv:2610.24395v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In multimodal learning, modality imbalance often lets one modality dominate optimization and keeps the model from fully exploiting cross-modal interactions. Balance-oriented methods such as the Multimodal Competition Regularizer (MCR) perform well by alleviating this imbalance during training. These dynamic balancing methods, however, mainly adjust modality contributions and do not consider how imbalance affects the formation of synergistic information during fusion. Synergy is a major source of multimodal advantage, because it is predictive gain that cannot be recovered from unimodal evidence alone. We propose the Multimodal Synergistic Competition Regularizer (MSCR), a fusion method that jointly promotes balanced modality utilization an
s8ae7e35806.summary: Researchers propose MSCR, a multimodal learning method that balances modality utilization while discovering synergistic information during fusion.
s8ae7e35806.why: Addresses modality imbalance in multimodal models, which can limit gains from cross-modal interactions.

se7aa5df8e8.title: MoveBench: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Sports and Health Coaching
se7aa5df8e8.description: arXiv:2610.26185v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Despite rapid advances in large language models (LLMs), their deployment in the sports and health domain remains high-risk due to the absence of domain-specific evaluation benchmarks. Existing general-purpose benchmarks (e.g., MMLU and HELM) primarily assess broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities, but fail to capture critical domain requirements such as exercise safety, physiological appropriateness, personalization, and actionable coaching quality. This gap is particularly concerning in fitness and health applications, where incorrect or unsafe recommendations can lead to physical harm. To address this limitation, we introduce MoveBench, the first comprehensive benchmarking framework specifically designed for evaluating LLMs in sport
se7aa5df8e8.summary: Researchers introduce MoveBench, a rubric-based benchmark for evaluating LLMs in sports and health coaching, covering exercise safety and personalization.
se7aa5df8e8.why: Provides domain-specific evaluation for high-risk fitness and health deployments where general benchmarks miss key requirements.

s21a18ce45c.title: IECG: Weakly-Supervised Interpretability-Enhancing Foundation Model for Electrocardiogram
s21a18ce45c.description: arXiv:2610.28083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is a cornerstone of cardiac diagnosis, yet most machine learning methods for ECG analysis lack interpretability, limiting their clinical adoption. We present IECG, a weakly-supervised ECG foundation model that jointly performs diagnostic classification and abnormality localization without requiring manual abnormal region annotations, overcoming a long-standing bottleneck in interpretable ECG learning. Central to IECG is a weakly-supervised attention strategy that explicitly incorporates clinical priors by deriving abnormality heatmap pseudo-labels from established ECG clinical knowledge. These pseudo-labels guide the model's CLS-token attention through a KL-divergence loss, encouraging it to focus on diagnostical
s21a18ce45c.summary: Researchers present IECG, a weakly-supervised ECG foundation model that jointly performs diagnostic classification and abnormality localization without manual region annotations.
s21a18ce45c.why: Could ease interpretability barriers for clinical ECG models by reducing the need for costly abnormal-region labels.

s61708075e5.title: The Value of Memory in Language Agents
s61708075e5.description: arXiv:2610.31303v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Language agents carry information from past experience into future tasks whose demands may be unknown or change over time. We develop a decision-theoretic account of the capability available in history, retained in storage and realized through use, together with the costs of recovery and revision. Drawing on comparison of statistical experiments, information acquisition and the value of computation, we express these values in units of avoided task loss. Recovery and revision define attainable risk-cost profiles and preservation across uses. A cost-aware simulation condition and five minimal counterexamples establish how information timing, access, computation, feedback and demand shape these comparisons; a pointer with zero answer mutual
s61708075e5.summary: Researchers develop a decision-theoretic account of how language agents use stored memory from past experience, measured in units of avoided task loss.
s61708075e5.why: Gives engineers a formal way to reason about memory storage, recovery, and revision costs in agent design.

s306061a7bc.title: TACS-RF: Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave Modules
s306061a7bc.description: arXiv:2610.31882v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the framework of TACS-RF - a Tool-driven Agentic Circuit Synthesis of RF and mmWave modules. In this framework, a large-language-model (LLM) coding agent (Claude Opus 4.8) directly drives industry-standard electronic-design-automation (EDA) tools such as Cadence Virtuoso/Spectre, Calibre, Cadence EMX, and Ansys HFSS to design RF and mmWave modules. We validate the framework through the agentic design of a 240-251 GHz sub-THz transmitter in a 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS process. The agent semi-autonomously designed the sub-blocks including a 60 GHz push-push Colpitts VCO with second-harmonic extraction, multistage differential cascode power drivers, a push-push frequency doubler, a differential bowtie antenna, and all the interstage match
s306061a7bc.summary: Researchers present TACS-RF, in which an LLM coding agent drives EDA tools like Cadence Virtuoso and Ansys HFSS to design a 240-251 GHz sub-THz transmitter.
s306061a7bc.why: Demonstrates an LLM agent semi-autonomously driving industry EDA toolchains for hardware design, a practical agentic workflow.

safaf3f9e90.title: Scoped Semantic Invariance as a Foundation for LLM Reliability
safaf3f9e90.description: arXiv:2610.33267v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLMs often answer semantically equivalent queries inconsistently, even when the underlying facts are known. We formalize consistency as semantic invariance over equivalence classes of queries and show that invariance under arbitrary meaning-preserving transformations is undecidable in general. This motivates scoped semantic invariance, where model behavior is evaluated relative to bounded semantic domains. We operationalize this framework using knowledge graphs (KGs), which act as explicit semantic control structures defining local semantic constraints and grounding contexts. Across the MITRE D3FEND ontology and eight Wikidata- derived domains, we show that inconsistencies are structured rather than random, concentrating in localized hots
safaf3f9e90.summary: Researchers formalize LLM consistency as scoped semantic invariance over query equivalence classes, operationalized using knowledge graphs as semantic control structures.
safaf3f9e90.why: Offers a framework for defining and testing consistency of LLM answers to equivalent queries within bounded domains.

scfa07975d8.title: Are Spiking Neural Networks Harder to Steal? The Role of Stochastic Encoding in Model Extraction
scfa07975d8.description: arXiv:2610.36298v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine learning models deployed on edge devices are vulnerable to model stealing attacks, in which an adversary replicates a model using only its predictions. Existing defenses add mechanisms that are costly on resource-constrained hardware. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer energy-efficient inference at the edge and have been shown to leak less information about their training data than artificial neural networks (ANNs). This work investigates whether SNNs also resist model stealing and identifies the source of any such resistance. We evaluate four model stealing attacks against SNN and ANN models on three image datasets and introduce a metric that accounts for the stochastic outputs of SNNs. SNNs exhibit greater resistance than ANNs
scfa07975d8.summary: Researchers study whether spiking neural networks resist model stealing attacks better than standard networks and identify stochastic encoding as the source of that resistance.
scfa07975d8.why: Suggests a possible low-cost defense for edge-deployed models, relevant to teams protecting models on constrained hardware.

s4bb0e2304b.title: Learning Where to Trust: Reliability-Guided Expert Routing and Velocity Gating for 3D Deformable Registration
s4bb0e2304b.description: arXiv:2610.36672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deformable image registration relies on accurate anatomical correspondences. However, explicitly coupling local matching reliability with spatial context selection and deformation update strength remains insufficiently explored in learning-based registration. This challenge is particularly pronounced in homogeneous, weakly textured, and severely deformed regions, where ambiguous matches may induce erroneous deformation updates. We propose ReliMorph, a reliability-routed symmetric framework for 3D deformable registration that couples correspondence assessment with spatial context selection and update strength.Local correlation distributions characterize correspondence ambiguity using shared anatomical features with modality-specific adapta
s4bb0e2304b.summary: Researchers propose ReliMorph, a reliability-routed framework for 3D deformable image registration that couples match reliability with context selection and update strength.
s4bb0e2304b.why: Presents a technique for handling ambiguous correspondences in medical image registration, though the text offers limited deployment detail.

s195b33478f.title: SpectRAG: Weighted Chunk Graphs for Token-Budgeted Context Selection in Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s195b33478f.description: arXiv:2610.36991v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems ground large language models (LLMs) by retrieving external evidence and conditioning generation on the retrieved context. Although dense retrieval is effective for local semantic matching, independently ranked retrieval can return redundant passages, miss cross-chunk dependencies, and provide incomplete evidence for multi-hop reasoning. We propose SpectRAG, a spectral graph-augmented retrieval framework that combines hybrid candidate seeding, weighted chunk graph construction, graph-based expansion, spectral relevance propagation, and token-budgeted context selection. Document chunks are represented by dense semantic embeddings and graph-spectral coordinates derived from a weighted chunk graph
s195b33478f.summary: Researchers propose SpectRAG, a spectral graph-augmented retrieval method that builds weighted chunk graphs for token-budgeted context selection in multi-hop RAG.
s195b33478f.why: Targets redundant and incomplete retrieval in multi-hop RAG under token budgets, a common production constraint.

s3e6a1a3a3a.title: Learning to Reason from Reference Samples Alone: Reinforced Adversarial Learning for Modern LLM Post-Training
s3e6a1a3a3a.description: arXiv:2610.38851v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In many settings where LLM post-training is desirable, high-quality answers are recognizable but difficult to score with explicit rewards. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is limited to tasks where an explicit correctness signal is available. Prior adversarial approaches to training reasoning LLMs either complement verifiable rewards with co-trained critics or require reference reasoning traces. We ask whether a co-trained LLM judge can turn reference answers alone into the sole reward for on-policy post-training of reasoning LLMs. We call this method Reinforced Adversarial Learning (RAL). We first validate RAL on three verifiable tasks (integer multiplication, code-based arithmetic-expression synthesis, and SMILES-to
s3e6a1a3a3a.summary: Researchers propose using a co-trained LLM judge that scores on-policy outputs against reference answers alone, removing the need for explicit verifiable rewards or reference traces.
s3e6a1a3a3a.why: Could extend post-training to tasks where correctness is hard to verify programmatically, reducing reliance on verifiable reward setups.

s9589b21c4b.title: Low-Margin Branch Points in Deterministic LLM Deliberation
s9589b21c4b.description: arXiv:2611.00546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deterministic multi-agent LLM deliberation can exactly re- play a fixed transcript, yet exact replay alone does not test local resistance to controlled internal interventions. Because each response becomes context for later agents, a changed greedy token can redirect a transcript-mediated execution. We present a white-box audit of this local failure mode in a five-agent committee under greedy decoding. We prospectively select low- and high-margin token positions, require exact no-op re- play, inject norm-relative residual displacements, and measure first transcript divergence within ten generated tokens. Low- margin positions are more branch-sensitive than high-margin controls, while matched margin-reducing gradient directions branch subs
s9589b21c4b.summary: Researchers audit a five-agent deterministic LLM committee under greedy decoding, finding that small internal interventions at low-margin tokens can redirect transcripts.
s9589b21c4b.why: Highlights that exact replay does not guarantee robustness, which matters for auditing multi-agent LLM pipelines.

s36b5576fb2.title: MAGAR: Multimodal Agents for GUI-Based 3D Mechanical Assembly and Minimal Rework
s36b5576fb2.description: arXiv:2611.02472v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A GUI command can be correct at the interface level yet still produce an incorrect assembly. An agent must identify the relevant components, respect their structural relationships, and determine which parts should move during recovery. We introduce MAGAR-Bench, a benchmark of 4,000 multimodal samples from 26 assembly families that separates Assembly Decision, Atomic Action, and Minimal Rework. For rework, the objective counts distinct moved parts within the validated recovery candidate set for each state, rather than the number of actions. We also introduce MAGAR, a selective correction framework built on a frozen policy obtained by supervised fine-tuning. Its key design matches correction granularity to output dependencies. Structured ca
s36b5576fb2.summary: Researchers introduce MAGAR-Bench, a 4,000-sample multimodal benchmark for GUI-based 3D mechanical assembly that separates assembly decision, atomic action, and minimal rework.
s36b5576fb2.why: Provides a benchmark for evaluating GUI agents on recovery from incorrect assemblies, with rework measured by moved parts rather than actions.

s656c0fcc22.title: FORGE: Fault-Oriented Rework Code Generation for Executable Interlocking Assembly
s656c0fcc22.description: arXiv:2611.02536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models have demonstrated strong capabilities in structured reasoning and code generation, yet identifying an assembly fault does not guarantee the ability to generate executable rework programs. In interlocking assemblies, a locally plausible repair program may violate blocking dependencies, omit required recovery operations, or terminate in an incorrect configuration. We identify this challenge as fault-conditioned executable rework generation, where models must jointly reason about structural failures and generate programs that restore constrained assembly states. To benchmark this capability, we introduce FORGE-Bench, containing 4,000 tasks across 26 interlocking assemblies with five assemblies held out for evaluating ge
s656c0fcc22.summary: Researchers introduce FORGE, a method for generating executable rework programs that repair faults in interlocking assemblies while respecting blocking dependencies.
s656c0fcc22.why: Shows LLMs can find assembly faults yet still fail to produce executable repair code, a gap relevant to any LLM-driven industrial automation.

scd015ab447.title: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks
scd015ab447.description: arXiv:2611.04785v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models are candidates for collecting and analyzing records in criminal investigations and mass surveillance. Their capability and accuracy in this work cannot currently be measured. Real deployments lack the ground truth needed to score a model's conclusions, and no benchmark evaluates these capabilities in a simulated environment. We present Kierston, a city-scale simulation engine, and KierstonBench, a benchmark that tests these capabilities against known simulated events. Kierston models approximately 125,000 residents of Allentown, Pennsylvania, generating their daily activities and the telecommunications, financial, administrative and license-plate records that surveillance and investigative systems collect about them.
scd015ab447.summary: Researchers present Kierston, a city-scale simulation of Allentown, PA, and KierstonBench, a benchmark testing language models on crime investigation and surveillance tasks against known simulated events.
scd015ab447.why: Provides ground-truth evaluation for LLMs in surveillance and investigation, a sensitive use case where accuracy is hard to measure.

s990e36e8d9.title: Combining Relevant Expert Knowledge Using Mixtures of Feedback Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
s990e36e8d9.description: arXiv:2611.05664v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A neuro-symbolic system should combine only relevant answers from expert agents or other knowledge sources. Using only relevant experts for a given input query becomes ever more important for accuracy and scalability as the knowledge network grows and connects ever more knowledge sources. We extend the standard definition of relevance from the legal theory of evidence: An answer is relevant if and only if it is both probative and material for the matter at hand given the knowledge available. We apply this relevancy scheme to mixing the feedback fuzzy cognitive maps (FCMs) of real or artificial experts. The expert FCM directed causal graphs mix or combine into a common knowledge network. We compare the equilibrium limit-cycle predictions o
s990e36e8d9.summary: Researchers propose applying a legal-theory relevance standard to select only relevant expert answers when mixing feedback fuzzy cognitive maps in neuro-symbolic systems.
s990e36e8d9.why: Offers a way to filter knowledge sources by relevance, which may improve accuracy and scalability as knowledge networks grow.

sd9360ce0ca.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
sd9360ce0ca.description: arXiv:2611.06858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recursive self-improvement requires AI systems to improve the models and infrastructure used by subsequent systems. LLM compression offers a concrete efficiency objective: retain a pretrained model's behavior within a smaller model storage budget. We study whether coding agents can carry out this step autonomously. We formulate compression as a terminal task in which an agent receives a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget, then constructs compressed weights and executable inference code. The agent controls its algorithm and experiments; perplexity feedback guides search, and independent verification checks the final model. Across six agents and six model--size settings, 29 of 36 submissions pass verifi
sd9360ce0ca.summary: CompressionBench tests whether autonomous coding agents can compress pretrained LLMs within storage limits, producing compressed weights and executable inference code.
sd9360ce0ca.why: Tests whether coding agents can handle model optimization tasks end to end, relevant to efficiency work and agent evaluation.

sdb72c38858.title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency
sdb72c38858.description: arXiv:2611.07948v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, evaluating the correctness of their responses is crucial for reliable use. However, such evaluation is challenging because reference answers are rarely available in practice. Existing reference-free methods mainly rely on output signals, which may assign high scores to incorrect responses and thus do not necessarily reflect correctness. This motivates exploring the model's internal computation for complementary correctness signals. Recent studies exploit internal states, but they mainly analyze hidden-state trajectories across layers, which record only the combined updates of attention and feed-forward networks (FFNs) and overlook how these components in
sdb72c38858.summary: Circe proposes a training-free way to evaluate LLM response correctness using internal component interaction consistency rather than output signals alone.
sdb72c38858.why: Offers a reference-free correctness signal from model internals, which could help teams assess LLM outputs without gold answers.

s473743245d.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
s473743245d.description: arXiv:2611.14544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has been studied as a handwriting-recognition problem: read the move in each box and check that it is legal. This framing misses the errors that matter most. A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. One that yields a legal-but-wrong move is silent, because a legality-only pipeline accepts it and reads every later move against a wrong position. We therefore treat the task as game reconstruction and present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery (quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, pin detection) to ask not "what should be played?" but "could a human plausibly have written this?" An absurdity detector makes silent errors loud at or near where they occur, and a backward search
s473743245d.summary: Zugwise reframes digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets as game reconstruction, using computer-chess techniques to catch legal-but-wrong misreads that legality-only pipelines miss.
s473743245d.why: It shows that domain-specific validation can catch silent errors that generic legality checks accept, a useful pattern for OCR-plus-constraint pipelines.

s511f6df35f.title: Cleaning an Agent's History Hurts When the World Still Holds the Error
s511f6df35f.description: arXiv:2611.14654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents accumulate histories of their own mistakes, and a system that compacts, repairs or hands off such a history decides what it says about those mistakes while their effects stay in the world. Prior work cleans the history at a fixed world, where showing a corrected step and saying it is done move together. We ask whether the same correct content helps or hurts depending on how the history states it and what the world holds. We freeze an agent mid-task with its exact world state, edit the history or the world, and let a receiver model continue. On AgentCE-Bench, after the agent commits a wrong value, we hold the world fixed and add the correct value by two natural edits: a truthful note beside the preserved error
s511f6df35f.summary: A study finds that cleaning an agent's error history can hurt performance when the world still contains the uncorrected error, since history and world state can conflict.
s511f6df35f.why: Engineers compacting or repairing agent histories must keep them consistent with actual environment state, or corrections may degrade behavior.

s71e20d332c.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
s71e20d332c.description: arXiv:2611.14681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Today's AI workloads are rapidly changing: new models are released more often, model architectures are increasingly diverse, and traffic distributions change frequently. The challenge we face at Together AI is continual optimization for these changing workloads. Compiling a deployment into an optimized forward pass is a challenge that is well-suited for agent hill-climbing. Existing systems struggle with continual compilation due to a tradeoff between measurement throughput and fidelity. Many systems use agents to optimize individual kernels from the inference forward pass using offline benchmarks, but timings are low-fidelity because of data-dependent behavior in primitives like mixture-of-experts (MoE). On the other hand, systems use agents
s71e20d332c.summary: Together AI describes Together Compiler, a system for continually compiling and optimizing AI inference deployments as models and traffic patterns change.
s71e20d332c.why: Continual, automated inference optimization addresses shifting model and traffic mixes, relevant to teams running production inference at scale.

sf34ea82050.title: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
sf34ea82050.description: arXiv:2611.14736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Observational causal discovery often leaves causal di- rections unresolved or unstable. Large language mod- els (LLMs) can provide semantic information to resolve these directions, but incorrect proposals can exclude the true causal graph and invalidate downstream inference. We study three separate decisions: where to allocate semantic queries, which proposals to admit, and which causal graphs to retain. Our framework distinguishes population non-identifiability from finite-sample insta- bility, evaluates semantic orientation against statistical and random controls, and examines calibrated admis- sion and error-tolerant DAG retention. Experiments across benchmark networks show that semantic infor- mation improves recovery over coin-flip orien
sf34ea82050.summary: Researchers study when LLM-provided semantic priors should enter partially identified causal discovery, separating non-identifiability from finite-sample instability.
sf34ea82050.why: It offers guidance on when to trust LLM-suggested causal directions, since incorrect proposals can invalidate downstream inference.

s41ea8c0656.title: SynthCorp: A Platform for Creating Benchmarks for Data Agents
s41ea8c0656.description: arXiv:2611.14765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current benchmarks for LLM-driven data agents saturate quickly and cannot target specific capabilities. We present SynthCorp, a platform that creates customizable data estates and benchmarks by simulating how business events produce and modify corporate data over time. Each data estate combines relational databases, a document store, and a data catalog, paired with evaluation tasks and executable gold programs. First, given a scenario and target complexity dimensions, SynthCorp synthesizes reusable event types and compiles each into a program over predefined simulation primitives. Second, SynthCorp schedules event instances on a virtual calendar, interleaving routine and disruption events so that tables, documents, and catalog entries remain
s41ea8c0656.summary: SynthCorp is a platform that generates customizable synthetic corporate data estates and paired benchmarks for evaluating LLM-driven data agents.
s41ea8c0656.why: Teams evaluating data agents can use targeted, non-saturating synthetic benchmarks instead of quickly saturated public ones.

s2e48ac2769.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
s2e48ac2769.description: arXiv:2611.14766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All social interactions are situated in time. Previous studies have shown that humans are able to use implicit temporal cues, such as the duration of a pause, to infer others' mental states. But how do humans use temporal cues for dynamic, fine-grained social coordination? And can AI systems do the same, without ``experiencing'' continuous real-time as humans do? We study these questions using a cooperative card game task called The Mind, which requires players to achieve a shared goal across repeated interactions but forbids explicit communication: the only available signal is the passage of time. We evaluate 150 humans, and two classes of AI models which reflect different ways of operationalizing time in artificial systems: computer-use age
s2e48ac2769.summary: Researchers compare how humans and AI use timing cues for social coordination in The Mind, a cooperative card game that forbids explicit communication.

s9d9a277b7a.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
s9d9a277b7a.description: arXiv:2611.14769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrele
s9d9a277b7a.summary: A paper shows arena-style, Bradley-Terry-based model leaderboards are vulnerable to manipulation such as strategic voting by providers seeking higher ranks.
s9d9a277b7a.why: Teams relying on preference leaderboards to choose models should account for manipulation risk and validate with their own evaluations.

s4c55cd6f26.title: Robust Task-Aware State Estimation from Pre-trained Perception
s4c55cd6f26.description: arXiv:2611.14781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that perform state estimation using pretrained perception models, e.g., Vision-Language Models (VLMs), face the fundamental challenge that predictions are uncertain. Still, most approaches determinize these predictions into a single best-guess state and make decisions as if it were ground truth. This is brittle because when the guess is wrong, the agent's decisions may be unsafe or infeasible. At the other extreme, maintaining a full probability distribution over symbolic states is often intractable. We propose a middle path, drawing on the underlying probabilities the perception model already produces (e.g., a VLM's output-layer token distributions) to construct a $\theta$-confidence Minimal Belief Set (MBS$_\theta$), a minimal subset
s4c55cd6f26.summary: Researchers propose a middle path for robust state estimation from pretrained perception models like VLMs, avoiding both single best guesses and full intractable distributions.
s4c55cd6f26.why: Agents acting on uncertain perception outputs can become unsafe when they treat a wrong best guess as ground truth.

s321106c778.title: When Is Proof-Step Verification Worth Its Cost? Operating Requirements of Certify-or-Decline Verification for Open-Weight Mathematical Reasoning
s321106c778.description: arXiv:2611.14794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-step verification rewrites a solver's answer into typed steps and uses LLM judges to certify or decline. We evaluate this pipeline on open-weight models across GPQA, AIME-2025, and a MATH-500 subset. Certification raises answer-key-match precision by 31 percentage points on the strong GPQA configuration and 46 on AIME, while answering only 35% and 21% of attempts. On near-ceiling MATH-500, gains are at most 5 points at a loss of 13-27 points of coverage. An output-token-matched self-consistency selector obtains 82.9% precision at 35% coverage, compared with the verifier's pooled 87.6% (paired difference: +4.8 points, 95% interval [-8.2, 18.5]). A diagnostic sample reveals a distinct failure mode: 52 of 88 completed problems end in inval
s321106c778.summary: An evaluation of certify-or-decline proof-step verification on open-weight models shows precision gains at substantial coverage cost, with a self-consistency baseline competitive.
s321106c778.why: Engineers choosing verification for math reasoning must weigh precision gains against lost answer coverage and compute cost.

sd7968f8416.title: GenPFN: An In-Context Tabular Foundation Model Approach for Augmenting Small Datasets in Engineering
sd7968f8416.description: arXiv:2611.14804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Costly simulations and experiments limit the data available for engineering design. This paper proposes GenPFN, a training-free candidate generator guided by a pretrained tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) classifier with fixed weights. The context contains evaluated designs labeled desired (Class 1) or undesired (Class 0). GenPFN interpolates between desired designs and refines candidates using gated classifier gradients and Gaussian noise. Each candidate is evaluated using the problem's constraints and objective functions. Evaluated desired designs and their objective values augment the context for regression training. Evaluation spans fourteen selected problems, including a two-parameter benchmark and a 44-parameter hull problem. I
sd7968f8416.summary: GenPFN uses a pretrained tabular foundation model, TabPFN, without training to generate candidate engineering designs from small labeled datasets.
sd7968f8416.why: It suggests a training-free way to augment scarce simulation data for engineering design, reducing costly experiments.

sfaa25c7a87.title: AutoAssumption: Searching over Assumptions Discovers ML-Systems Algorithms
sfaa25c7a87.description: arXiv:2611.14844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many advances in ML systems came from breaking an assumption that earlier methods took for granted: speculative decoding dropped the assumption that a model needs one forward pass per token. Yet algorithms rarely state their assumptions, so experts and discovery harnesses search over programs, where one edit changes several design choices and gains are difficult to attribute. Searching over the assumptions themselves remains largely unexplored. Writing algorithms as proofs makes their assumptions explicit and turns algorithm design into a search over a small, structured space that an LLM can explore and a proof checker can audit. We formalize 89 algorithms from KV-cache eviction, weight pruning and speculative decoding as proof graphs with ex
sfaa25c7a87.summary: AutoAssumption searches over explicit algorithmic assumptions, framed as proofs, to discover ML systems algorithms such as speculative decoding.
sfaa25c7a87.why: Making algorithm assumptions explicit could make automated discovery of ML systems optimizations easier to attribute and reproduce.

s47fe41e7e6.title: Open Challenges and Opportunities in Human-Agent Systems
s47fe41e7e6.description: arXiv:2611.14846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly undertake extended tasks and act on people's behalf, making human-agent interaction central to their effectiveness. Successful interaction requires understanding human perspectives, coordinating complementary capabilities, and maintaining productive relationships within socio-technical environments. This paper examines how foundations developed by the Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems (AAMAS) community inform these demands. We consider interactions ranging from individual human-agent partnerships to teams and larger groups, where participants differ in their roles, decision authority, capabilities, and objectives. We organize computational approaches around the connected challenges of understanding othe
s47fe41e7e6.summary: A paper outlines open challenges in human-agent systems, drawing on AAMAS community foundations for individual partnerships and larger teams.

sa7b33ce932.title: Effective Teacher Support for Reasoning Distillation
sa7b33ce932.description: arXiv:2611.14850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forward-KL language-model distillation normally computes dense teacher and student scores over the full vocabulary at every supervised position, making training and stored teacher targets expensive. We instead distill from the teacher's highest-probability vocabulary fraction, renormalizing the retained mass as we sweep support from 100% to 0.01%. Our main study distills Qwen3 4B -> 1.7B. We confirm the broader support-reduction finding on larger Qwen3 8B -> 4B and Nemotron Nano 12B -> 9B pairs and under answer-only supervision. We evaluate generation primarily on MMLU-Pro and secondarily on GPQA-Diamond. Across the Qwen3 settings, retaining 0.01% of the vocabulary causes no observed MMLU-Pro degradation relative to full-vocabulary distillati
sa7b33ce932.summary: Researchers show that distilling from only the teacher's highest-probability vocabulary fraction can work for reasoning distillation of Qwen3 and Nemotron models.
sa7b33ce932.why: Restricting distillation support can cut training and storage cost for teacher targets without necessarily sacrificing student performance.

sa18fd36573.title: Can an AI Agent Be Epistemically Akratic? Higher-Order Evidence & the Limits of Self-Correction
sa18fd36573.description: arXiv:2611.14889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When we judge that our reasoning was defective, it seems plausible that we should abandon the conclusion it produced. This thought has special force for AI agents built to assess and correct their own work. Yet obeying such judgments can make an agent worse at distinguishing sound reasoning from defective reasoning. An AI agent may rely on information about its reasoning when deciding which conclusions to keep, while the part that judges whether those conclusions are justified cannot use that information. The agent can then exercise an epistemic competence by retaining conclusions it judges unjustified, even when its self-assessments are generally reliable. Nor is the difficulty resolved by training the agent to make its conclusions and asses
sa18fd36573.summary: A philosophical paper asks whether an AI agent that revises conclusions based on judgments of its own reasoning can become epistemically akratic.

sab7dc133c2.title: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
sab7dc133c2.description: arXiv:2611.14910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require frequent knowledge updates across heterogeneous domains, but existing editing methods fail when applied sequentially to multi-task settings. We trace this collapse to inter-domain null-space misalignment: heterogeneous tasks induce distinct Jacobian geometries, causing their common null space to shrink dramatically and leaving insufficient admissible directions for conflict-free updates. We propose the Conflict Index to quantify this geometric interference, and introduce Mu-Edit, which mitigates multi-task conflicts via (1) conflict-aware ordering to minimize cumulative interference, and (2) dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the null space when ordering alone is insufficient. Experiments across five
sab7dc133c2.summary: MuEdit introduces a Conflict Index and a multi-task editing method to handle inter-domain null-space conflicts when sequentially updating LLM knowledge.
sab7dc133c2.why: Sequential knowledge edits across domains can silently fail, so teams maintaining updated LLMs need conflict-aware editing methods.

s6d73b6b568.title: Edge-Native Multimodal RAG: Hardware-Aware Quantization and Architectural Optimization for Consumer GPUs
s6d73b6b568.description: arXiv:2611.14924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deployment of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for Edge-AI is constrained by memory and bandwidth limitations. A standard 7B parameter model consumes 14 GB Video Random Access Memory (VRAM) in half-precision (FP16), precluding co-location of vector indices and Key-Value (KV) caches. This paper presents an engineering integration and empirical evaluation of a multimodal RAG framework optimized for consumer-grade Turing hardware (e.g., NVIDIA Tesla T4). Our system-level analysis identifies a critical trade-off: while generative pre-trained transformer quantization (GPTQ) offers superior throughput (51.6 tok/s), it exhibits significant context instability at 2048+ tokens on Turing architectures. Conversely, NormalFloat 4-bit (NF4) maintains
s6d73b6b568.summary: Researchers present an edge-native multimodal RAG framework optimized with hardware-aware quantization for consumer Turing GPUs such as the NVIDIA Tesla T4.
s6d73b6b568.why: Shows memory-constrained RAG deployment on consumer GPUs is feasible, with trade-offs between quantization and architecture that matter for edge deployments.

s828ffb4f67.title: Provably Optimal HBT Legalization in Seconds: Certified Optima Reveal Where the Headroom Really Lies
s828ffb4f67.description: arXiv:2611.14928v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid bonding terminal (HBT) legalization assigns every terminal of a face-to-face 3D IC to its own pitch-grid site with minimum total Manhattan displacement. Open3DBench reports that a reinforcement-learning (RL) legalizer reduces displacement by 19-22% relative to a sliding-window (SW) heuristic, but none of its legalizers is publicly released. We ask how much displacement any legalizer can still recover. We build an open benchmark of 21 design/pitch instances from Open3DBench placement data, with reconstructed greedy, SW (ViaLegal-style) and BTAssign-style baselines, and GEO-Exact, an exact solver that runs successive shortest augmenting paths over lazily generated spatial candidate edges. An independent dual certificate proves its assign
s828ffb4f67.summary: Researchers build an open benchmark of 21 hybrid bonding terminal legalization instances and compute provably optimal displacement results for 3D IC placement.
s828ffb4f67.why: Provides certified optimal baselines showing how much headroom remains for 3D IC legalizers, which helps chip design teams judge heuristics.

sb2f19aaee8.title: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training
sb2f19aaee8.description: arXiv:2611.14942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does multimodal training shape how a language model thinks, even when the input is text only? We test this with targeted causal ablations across 10 multimodal configurations from 6 model families, with matched text-only backbones and cross-family transfer controls. We contrast spatial-imagery tasks that invite mental scene construction with symbol-manipulation tasks solvable by symbolic rules alone. We identify a vision-language axis in hidden-state space and ablate its projection at inference. In Chameleon-7B, this ablation drops accuracy on BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) navigate by 27.6 pp while leaving boolean expressions intact (+5.6 pp), a 33.2 pp double dissociation. The effect is direction-specific and layer-localized, extends to mental-simulat
sb2f19aaee8.summary: A study finds multimodal training shapes text-only reasoning in language models, with a vision-language axis in hidden states affecting spatial-imagery task accuracy.
sb2f19aaee8.why: Suggests multimodal training can change how models reason on text alone, relevant to model selection and interpretability work.

sbfec2ce0ac.title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
sbfec2ce0ac.description: arXiv:2611.14949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying and solving partial differential equations (PDEs) from sampled solution data often requires substantial expert effort in equation discovery, coefficient estimation, and numerical solver configuration, especially under noise and distribution shifts. Can large language model (LLM) agents automate this workflow accurately and efficiently? To investigate this question, we introduce \bench{}, a benchmark of 1,001 cases spanning 42 equation templates, including both classical and fractional PDEs. It provides three evaluation settings: Full evaluates performance on noise-free solution data; Noisy tests robustness to Gaussian noise with an RMS equal to 50\% of the clean-signal RMS; and Hard-OOD tests challenging out-of-distribution genera
sbfec2ce0ac.summary: Researchers introduce RSI-PDEbench, a 1,001-case benchmark testing whether LLM agents can self-improve at identifying and solving partial differential equations.
sbfec2ce0ac.why: Offers a concrete evaluation for agentic scientific-computing workflows, useful for teams assessing agents on numerical and modeling tasks.

s4e7ee37c9b.title: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
s4e7ee37c9b.description: arXiv:2611.14960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents can solve a task well before they stop working on it. We characterize \emph{termination lag}--the number of steps between an agent's first correct patch and the end of its run--across five models, two agent frameworks, and three SWE-bench datasets by recording and testing every distinct repository patch generated during execution. Our analysis reveals that 38--82% of successful runs achieve a correct solution on their initial source-code edit. However, agents continue to expend substantial effort after correct patches, with post-solution steps accounting for a median of 35--37% for Qwen3-Coder and 54--60% for Laguna-XS.2 in successful runs on SWE-bench Verified and Multilingual. Agents spend most of these additional steps verify
s4e7ee37c9b.summary: A study of coding agents finds 38–82% of successful runs hit a correct patch on the first source edit, yet agents keep working afterward.
s4e7ee37c9b.why: Highlights wasted compute and cost in coding agents after a correct fix, pointing to termination logic as an engineering lever.

s058755f3a6.title: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
s058755f3a6.description: arXiv:2611.14965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parallel test-time scaling (TTS) has been shown to enhance reasoning in large language models by generating and aggregating multiple independent reasoning paths. Internal confidence scores can further improve this process by identifying paths of varying quality. However, existing methods remain computationally inefficient, as low-quality paths are fully expanded before being evaluated. In this work, we aim to improve the use of internal confidence signals for better model performance and computational efficiency. We begin by offering a new perspective on the role of confidence in aggregation, showing that it is most impactful for questions near the decision boundary. Notably, when amplified by multi-sample aggregation, even small confidence s
s058755f3a6.summary: Researchers propose prefix-guided sampling that uses early internal confidence signals to prune low-quality reasoning paths in parallel test-time scaling.
s058755f3a6.why: Could cut inference compute for parallel reasoning by stopping weak paths early rather than fully expanding them.

s571a5839a2.title: Same Task, Different Statement: When and How Reformulation Helps LLM Problem Solving
s571a5839a2.description: arXiv:2611.14997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When people face a hard problem, they often restate it in a clearer way before solving it. We study whether the same habit helps large language models by rewriting the statement of a problem. A legal rewrite must keep the meaning, the constraints, and the correct answer unchanged. We test three kinds of rewrites. Decomposition makes hidden subgoals explicit. Typed Reformulation casts the task into a more suitable solving frame. Concept Reduction removes surface detail and exposes the task structure. We evaluate them on eight math, logic, and code benchmarks with eight models, all under the same chain-of-thought solving prompt. The effect is large but depends on the problem type. An oracle that picks the best rewrite after the fact raises accu
s571a5839a2.summary: A study tests whether rewriting problem statements via decomposition, typed reformulation, or concept reduction improves LLM problem solving across eight benchmarks.
s571a5839a2.why: Offers a low-cost prompt-level technique that may improve reasoning accuracy, though gains depend on when rewrites help.

s71bb835ad0.title: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
s71bb835ad0.description: arXiv:2611.15006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly interact with tools and environments, yet plausible model decisions do not always translate into successful execution due to tool-call mismatches, interrupted workflows, and unsupported completion claims. We present EvoX, a Rust-based, multi-model agent runtime guided by The Second Policy, which views the harness as an Operational Policy complementing the foundation model's Semantic Policy. EvoX combines model-facing guidance with deterministic runtime control through three complementary mechanisms: Action Realization, Execution Continuity, and Outcome Grounding. To evaluate harnesses without suppressing their native behaviors, we introduce Contrast, a controlled and auditable framework integrati
s71bb835ad0.summary: EvoX is a Rust-based multi-model agent runtime that adds deterministic runtime control to LLM agent harnesses to address tool-call mismatches and false completion claims.
s71bb835ad0.why: Frames the agent harness as a runtime policy with deterministic controls, a design pattern relevant to reliable agent system builders.

s2849eca969.title: Science Prediction Universe
s2849eca969.description: arXiv:2611.15049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humanity has long sought to explain natural phenomena. Reliable prediction of experimental outcomes is a central test of our understanding of the processes that produce them. If artificial general intelligence (AGI) is to surpass human scientific capabilities, it must also predict experimental outcomes more reliably than humans. Such capabilities could accelerate scientific discovery across disciplines, help address humanity's most pressing challenges, and improve human well-being. We introduce Science Prediction Universe (SPU), a benchmark of hidden experimental outcomes with 100 public verified tasks from chemistry, materials science, biology and medicine, and 16 private tasks from unpublished wet-lab experiments. Given an experimental setu
s2849eca969.summary: Researchers introduce Science Prediction Universe, a benchmark for evaluating whether AI can predict experimental outcomes more reliably than humans.

sfe6ed93738.title: Advancing Weighted Partial MaxSAT Solving via Differentiable GPU Guidance
sfe6ed93738.description: arXiv:2611.15091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a GPU-CPU hybrid framework for Weighted Partial MaxSAT (WPMAX-SAT) that complements state-of-the-art CPU solvers with differentiable GPU optimization. The GPU stage directly optimizes instance-specific categorical decision parameters without a training dataset or a pretrained predictive model. The central challenge in extending differentiable optimization to WPMAX-SAT is the hard/soft clause asymmetry: hard clauses represent inviolable feasibility constraints while soft clauses carry weights. We introduce a hierarchical differentiable loss that prioritizes hard clause satisfaction before optimizing the weighted soft objective, ensuring that GPU gradient descent leans towards the constraint structure of WPMAX-SAT. Our framework tran
sfe6ed93738.summary: A GPU-CPU hybrid framework for weighted partial MaxSAT adds differentiable GPU optimization that complements state-of-the-art CPU solvers without training data.
sfe6ed93738.why: Shows GPU-based differentiable methods can complement classical combinatorial solvers, relevant to teams working on optimization workloads.

s061a5fe077.title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
s061a5fe077.description: arXiv:2611.15094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. Developing models that can interpret complex examinations and communicate their findings in the context of clinical decisions remains a major challenge. Here, we show that Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care, can interpret complete imaging examinations and engage in natural language conversations about their findings. Across
s061a5fe077.summary: Researchers report Neuro-VL, a vision-language model for neuroimaging that aims to interpret complex clinical exams and communicate findings in clinical context.
s061a5fe077.why: Demonstrates domain-specialized vision-language models for medical imaging, a signal for healthcare AI product development.

s85204b8367.title: GuardianAgentFlow: Multi-Agent Coordination for Web Privacy Protection
s85204b8367.description: arXiv:2611.15097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents need to use private context without unnecessarily disclosing it. Effective protection must distinguish between requests that may be sent after sanitization and those that must be withheld, while preserving the information needed for authorized tasks. We present GuardianAgentFlow, a multi-agent framework that mediates outgoing Web requests through an explicit release contract. A dedicated restriction check grounds permission in the user's instruction; a shared protection scope aligns rewriting with disclosure checking; and candidate-grounded feedback guides revision before transmission. Experiments on Web requests with human-reviewed intent labels show improved request-contract success, while controlled comparisons and role ablation
s85204b8367.summary: GuardianAgentFlow is a multi-agent framework that mediates outgoing web requests from web agents through an explicit release contract to protect private data.
s85204b8367.why: Addresses privacy leakage risks in web agents that handle sensitive user context, a concern for agent product design.

s22e69d5dd3.title: Expanding the Decision Space of Pretrained Models through Structured Re-Decoding
s22e69d5dd3.description: arXiv:2611.15109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Native decoders limit how pretrained models combine local predictions under new structural constraints. We introduce Structured Re-Decoding (SRD), a training-free framework that constructs local candidates from model scores, samples, or external specifications, jointly optimizes their selection, and verifies reconstructed outputs. We show that candidate recombination expands feasible support and can improve attainable reward under a fixed KL divergence budget. Across molecular generation, protein design, RNA structure prediction, and antibody modeling, SRD enables improved structured inference, including verified molecules absent from the original sample pool. External chemical templates further extend SRD to noncanonical amino acids, peptide
s22e69d5dd3.summary: Structured Re-Decoding is a training-free framework that recombines local candidates from pretrained models under structural constraints, tested on molecular, protein, and RNA tasks.
s22e69d5dd3.why: Offers a training-free way to satisfy structural constraints in generation, potentially useful for scientific design pipelines.

s33542c0c9b.title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
s33542c0c9b.description: arXiv:2611.15178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning sharpens LLM reasoning, but parameter updates are expensive, forgetful, and opaque; training-free libraries swap gradients for a textual store but still use trajectory-level, correlation-based admission and flat structure. To address both, we propose HyperSkill, a Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO framework that keeps the backbone frozen and replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library, where skills are advantage-bearing nodes and compositions are hyperedges. It has three components: training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them;
s33542c0c9b.summary: HyperSkill proposes training-free omnimodal GRPO that keeps the backbone frozen and evolves a hypergraph-indexed skill library through textual edits instead of gradient updates.
s33542c0c9b.why: Suggests a way to improve reasoning without expensive parameter updates, though the text gives limited evidence of results.

s57f634656f.title: WordInferBench: Can Agents Infer How to Edit from Word Document Context?
s57f634656f.description: arXiv:2611.15189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Document editing is among the most common knowledge-work tasks, yet existing benchmarks for evaluating autonomous agents on Word document editing provide fully specified attribute-modification instructions. They do not evaluate agents' ability to infer the appropriate attributes from document context, a capability essential in real-world editing where users expect consistency without spelling out every attribute. We introduce WordInferBench, a benchmark comprising 280 base document-editing instances, each paired with three instruction conditions: descriptive (the instruction explicitly lists every attribute change), referential (the instruction points to another object as an exemplar), and inferential (the agent must examine document context
s57f634656f.summary: WordInferBench is a 280-instance benchmark testing whether agents can infer appropriate Word document attribute edits from document context rather than explicit instructions.
s57f634656f.why: Targets a realistic gap in document-editing agents, where users expect consistency without spelling out every attribute.

s5f213382ce.title: AFTER: A World Model with Adaptive Fast--Slow Timescales for Error-Driven Retention
s5f213382ce.description: arXiv:2611.15215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In robotics and embodied AI, a core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics during interaction. For instance, when a robotic arm grasps an object with an unknown payload, the robot dynamics change suddenly. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to simultaneously satisfy three critical requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, reacting promptly to sudden changes to curb prediction error accumulation; stability, distinguishing persistent changes from transient disturbances to prevent incorrect updates; and persistence, retai
s5f213382ce.summary: Researchers propose AFTER, a world model with adaptive fast-slow timescales to adapt to sudden, persistent, initially unknown robot dynamics changes like unknown payloads.
s5f213382ce.why: Robots that grasp unknown-payload objects need models that adapt quickly, since accumulated prediction errors during rollouts can mislead actions.

s2280e8a081.title: guardscope: Measuring Which Actions Runtime Controls Check in LLM Agent Systems
s2280e8a081.description: arXiv:2611.15223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-language model (LLM) agents execute actions on external systems through tool calls, and enterprises deploy runtime controls, such as agent gateways, to check this behavior in real time. However, a control can only evaluate the actions that cross the point where it is placed, and an agent can act through more paths than the tool-call channel; no existing work measures this coverage against kernel-level ground truth. In this paper, we present guardscope, a framework that makes this coverage measurable. guardscope works in two stages: a static stage that predicts which of an agent's 15 action paths a control can check from its source, and an empirical stage that runs a fixed workload on a deployment that realizes one of eight topology desi
s2280e8a081.summary: Researchers introduce guardscope, a framework measuring which LLM agent actions runtime controls like agent gateways actually check, against kernel-level ground truth.
s2280e8a081.why: Gateways only inspect actions crossing their placement point, so teams relying on them may have coverage gaps that this method makes measurable.

s33b0e0827c.title: Can MLLMs Reason over Surround-View Driving Videos? A Multi-View Autonomous Driving QA Benchmark
s33b0e0827c.description: arXiv:2611.15225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surround-view video understanding in autonomous driving is a crucial capability for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to achieve reliable driving reasoning. Real-world driving often requires information beyond the front-view camera. Existing MLLMs primarily focus on front-view information, while their spatio-temporal understanding and reasoning abilities remain unknown. To address this gap, we propose MVDriveBench, a high-information-density video QA benchmark for autonomous driving, characterized by synchronized surround-view inputs, spatio-temporal understanding, and reasoning-chain-oriented evaluation. We design 12 categories of QA tasks that cover the complete reasoning pipeline from low-level visual perception to high-level drivin
s33b0e0827c.summary: Researchers present MVDriveBench, a video QA benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs can reason over synchronized surround-view autonomous driving footage.
s33b0e0827c.why: It exposes whether MLLMs handle non-front-view information, a gap relevant to teams evaluating vision models for driving.

sd59d8e211f.title: Towards Robust Vision-Language Reasoning: A Multi-Stage Optimization Pipeline with Masked Diffusion Model
sd59d8e211f.description: arXiv:2611.15238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete diffusion generation is emerging as a competitive alternative to autoregressive generation by denoising the entire token sequence through iterative refinement. Its global planning and progressive correction capabilities are particularly well suited to autonomous driving. However, transferring this generation paradigm from general-purpose settings to driving introduces substantial domain gaps in both training and inference. To unlock its potential, we propose a multi-stage optimization pipeline for standard vision-language model architectures, without auxiliary action experts or specialized mixture-of-experts Transformer, spanning post-training and inference. During supervised fine-tuning, we optimize the representation of planning in
sd59d8e211f.summary: Researchers propose a multi-stage optimization pipeline for masked diffusion vision-language models to improve robust reasoning for autonomous driving.
sd59d8e211f.why: Shows how discrete diffusion, an autoregressive alternative, can be adapted to driving despite domain gaps in training and inference.

s6e3be935c1.title: Verify by Doing: Co-Evolving Agent Execution and Evaluation without External Feedback
s6e3be935c1.description: arXiv:2611.15276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent self-improvement requires feedback about task success, yet external feedback may be unavailable at test time. Agents must then infer success from observable evidence, and incomplete verification can misguide subsequent updates. We introduce Verify by Doing (VbD), a method that co-evolves Actor and Evaluator harnesses within a single task while keeping model weights fixed. The Evaluator actively inspects artifacts and environment state with tools; its findings ground an internal signal for output selection and guide updates to both execution and verification procedures. Proposed Evaluators undergo comparative review on common candidates, while Actor updates require support from their own fresh outputs. Across AutomationBench, $\tau^3$ Ba
s6e3be935c1.summary: Researchers propose Verify by Doing, which co-evolves agent Actor and Evaluator harnesses within a task using model weights fixed, without external feedback.
s6e3be935c1.why: Enables agent self-improvement when external task-success feedback is unavailable at test time, relevant to deploying agents without labeled outcomes.

s6c72564d8e.title: Where Autonomy Belongs: A Separation of Powers for Agentic Program Evolution
s6c72564d8e.description: arXiv:2611.15309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-driven program evolution rests on three decisions: govern directs the search from accumulated evidence, propose constructs the next candidate, and judge settles validity and fitness. All three appear in every system, and existing work splits into two lines over who makes each. Controller-centric systems strengthen govern and neglect the autonomy of propose, which caps what evolution can reach. Agent-centric systems let a coding agent take over both govern and propose, at a cognitive and computational cost. Neither line protects the independent authority of judge, so benchmark reliability suffers. These failures share one root: autonomy is misallocated across the three decisions. We address this problem with EvoTrias, a separation-of-power
s6c72564d8e.summary: The paper proposes a separation-of-powers design for LLM-driven program evolution, splitting govern, propose, and judge roles across independent components.
s6c72564d8e.why: Offers an architectural argument for keeping evaluation independent from code-generating agents in automated program search systems.

se0544ad648.title: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models
se0544ad648.description: arXiv:2611.15315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models evolve, but the observations, revisions, and context accumulated through user interactions should remain usable. Each new model must be able to retrieve past evidence, track revisions, and add new observations. We present MIGRO, a decoupled long-term memory system that treats experience as a persistent state shared across successive language models. MIGRO follows a simple principle: preserve historical evidence exactly, organize it approximately, and decide what to retrieve only when the question is known. We call this asymmetric fidelity with deferred selectivity. A shared semantic index supports retrieval, while exact records retain observations and their historical relationships. Because models differ in vocabulary and toke
se0544ad648.summary: Researchers present MIGRO, a decoupled long-term memory system that keeps interaction history as persistent state shared across successive language models.
se0544ad648.why: Decoupling memory from the model could let teams swap models without losing accumulated user context and evidence.

se6345e4ea0.title: A physics-constrained deep reinforcement learning method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes
