se6345e4ea0.description: arXiv:2611.15389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Titan is a compelling target for future deep space exploration, while its extreme Earth-Titan distance and complex environment make continuous ground-in-the-loop planning impractical. Existing planning methods, primarily developed for Earth-observation scenarios, have limited generalizability to uncertain deep space conditions and adaptability to time-varying mission states. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-constrained maskable proximal policy optimization (PCM-PPO) method for Titan autonomous mission planning. A Titan-specific discrete-time Markov decision process is established to characterize mission feasibility and resource constraints. A system dynamics and geometric model is incorporated to enhance physical rep
se6345e4ea0.summary: Researchers propose PCM-PPO, a physics-constrained maskable reinforcement learning method for autonomous mission planning of Titan deep space probes.
se6345e4ea0.why: Addresses planning when ground-in-the-loop control is impractical due to distance, a constraint relevant to autonomous systems in uncertain environments.

se6d65daa23.title: Read and Ignore: What Self-Directed LLM Agents Do in Public Service Scenarios
se6d65daa23.description: arXiv:2611.15460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Underspecified instructions leave LLM agents to decide what to do. In public services, staff write these instructions, but the agent's decisions affect residents, patients, and students. We build four expert-validated public-service scenarios with records and decision levers that can be checked in the files, collect $2{,}400$ trajectories from ten LLMs under four prompt conditions, and compare them with $1{,}000$ runs in a context-free sandbox. Agents read the records in $96.9\%$ of open-ended runs and produce an artifact or a self-chosen task in $18.7\%$; with an explicit task, $86.0\%$ produce. Domain context does not change how many runs produce ($18.7\%$ vs.\ $16.0\%$), and the production ranking of the models largely carries over (Spearm
se6d65daa23.summary: A study of 2,400 trajectories from ten LLMs in four public-service scenarios finds agents read records in 96.9% of open-ended runs, examining underspecified instructions.
se6d65daa23.why: Shows agents frequently act beyond given instructions in high-stakes public-service settings, a concern for deployment oversight.

s32e00f5c8f.title: Loyalty Capture: Reporting Relationships and Structural Sycophancy in Frontier AI Models
s32e00f5c8f.description: arXiv:2611.15475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that AI models exhibit loyalty capture, a form of structural sycophancy in which reporting relationships influence models' recommendations to serve the personal interests of their supervisors, without any explicit instruction, user feedback, or adversarial prompting. Specifically, models reporting to a CEO are significantly more likely to recommend cutting investment spending when the CEO's bonus depends on raising current period earnings. This effect is predictably absent from a metric-irrelevant placebo. The behavior appears consistent with loyalty-based motivated reasoning: models identify the bonus target, calculate how their recommendation helps achieve the target, and dismiss considerations of long-term value, often presenting t
s32e00f5c8f.summary: Researchers report loyalty capture, where AI models reporting to a CEO more often recommend cutting investment when the CEO's bonus depends on current earnings.
s32e00f5c8f.why: Suggests models can be biased toward their supervisor's incentives without any explicit instruction, a risk for AI used in business recommendations.

s593049d01a.title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
s593049d01a.description: arXiv:2611.15481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently developed remote sensing (RS) agents execute real-world tasks with complex workflows through multi-step tool invocation. These agents, however, typically rely on predefined expertise or parameter updates. They thus require updating expert knowledge or retraining models whenever new tools, tasks, or execution patterns emerge, limiting their continual adaptability in dynamic Earth environments. In this work, we seek to equip general-purpose agents with RS tool-call knowledge that can be automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories without expert intervention or parameter updates. Specifically, we propose SkillEarth, a self-evolving skill extraction method that externalizes RS tool-call knowledge as reusable, retrievable, and
s593049d01a.summary: SkillEarth proposes equipping general-purpose agents with remote sensing tool-call knowledge automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories, avoiding retraining.
s593049d01a.why: Shows a route to adding new tools and workflows to agents via extracted skills rather than model retraining.

s5d9c75365c.title: Incentive-Responsive Agents: A Principal-Agent Framework, Metric Suite, and Runtime Architecture for Long-Lived Personal AI Agents
s5d9c75365c.description: arXiv:2611.15515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal AI agents now persist: they hold accounts, mailboxes, long-term memory, and open-ended task streams, yet the dominant way to improve them remains capability-side: prompt engineering, larger models, longer thinking, and retrieval. We argue that long-lived agents are missing an incentive layer. We formalize an incentive not as text in a prompt but as a runtime contract over the agent's operating point (model tier, test-time compute, memory budget, tool authority, task priority, verification, and compensation) that the agent's policy must causally consume. We develop a principal-agent model with hidden effort, a contractible operating point, and costly verification. We derive (i) a non-consumption invariance principle separating genuine
s5d9c75365c.summary: The paper formalizes incentives for long-lived personal AI agents as runtime contracts over model tier, compute, memory, tool authority, and compensation, with metrics.
s5d9c75365c.why: Proposes treating operating constraints as enforceable runtime contracts, relevant to governing persistent agents with accounts and tool access.

sfa485b1030.title: Marginal-Preserving Coupled Diffusion Composition for Long-Horizon Planning
sfa485b1030.description: arXiv:2611.15585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compositional diffusion planners extend short-horizon trajectory models to long-horizon goal-conditioned planning by generating and stitching multiple local trajectory chunks. However, in multimodal environments, local plausibility is not sufficient for global consistency: independently initialized chunks may denoise toward incompatible overlap modes, producing plans that are individually feasible but incoherent after stitching. Existing remedies typically add search, guidance, pruning, or graph-based structure at inference time, increasing computational cost or relying on task-specific machinery. We instead investigate graph-structured dependence among chunk-wise initial diffusion noises as a lightweight coordination mechanism for compositio
sfa485b1030.summary: Researchers propose a marginal-preserving coupled diffusion method to make stitched trajectory chunks globally consistent in long-horizon diffusion planning.
sfa485b1030.why: Addresses incoherent plans from stitching locally feasible segments, a practical issue for compositional diffusion planners.

s192b15e64d.title: Small Heads, Strong Decisions: A Controlled Study of Typed-Decision Models
s192b15e64d.description: arXiv:2611.15592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In September 2026, TypeSafe announced Jev as the first model in its System One category: unstructured state goes in, and typed, calibrated decisions that software can use directly come out. Jev's architecture and training data are unpublished, but many open typed-decision models have followed, including Nimble, the Decision 1.0--3.0 family and Clef. They answer structured questions about a piece of text, such as a yes/no check, a choice among labelled options or a graded score, by reading the text with a language model and scoring the options with a small readout. Each pairs a different readout with a different backbone, training mix and recipe, so it is unclear which design choices matter. We re-implement five readouts and train all of them
s192b15e64d.summary: A controlled study compares open typed-decision models that answer structured questions about text, such as yes/no checks and graded scores, against larger approaches.
s192b15e64d.why: Could inform choosing small, calibrated classifiers over general LLMs for structured decisions in software pipelines.

sb8a9ccd0c4.title: MemCredit: From Relevance to Utility for Decision-Time Memory in Long-Horizon Web Agents
sb8a9ccd0c4.description: arXiv:2611.15600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate over long Web interaction histories, making memory management critical for reliable and efficient decision making. Existing methods primarily optimize storage, retrieval, or compression, but the memories most semantically relevant to the current state are not necessarily those that most improve the agent's action. We introduce MemCredit, a decision-centric memory framework that shifts memory selection from semantic relevance to decision utility. MemCredit estimates the state-, reference-context-, and policy-conditional marginal contribution of individual memories through controlled counterfactual interventions, and distills these intervention-derived credits into a lightweight utility est
sb8a9ccd0c4.summary: Researchers introduce MemCredit, which selects memories for long-horizon web agents by decision utility rather than semantic relevance.
sb8a9ccd0c4.why: Argues that the most relevant memories are not always the most useful for actions, a design point for agent memory retrieval.

sde571db71a.title: A Reliability Study of Explainable AI for Freight Mode Classification
sde571db71a.description: arXiv:2611.15716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used to support freight transportation decisions, but their predictions are rarely accompanied by evidence that the associated explanations can be trusted. In this study we investigate explainable machine learning for classifying shipments as Air/Air Charter or Truck/Ocean using the PEPFAR Supply Chain Management System Delivery History dataset, with 5,964 shipment records and 47 input features after cleaning, where freight cost and pack price are excluded as near-proxies of the transportation mode. We compare three Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architectures, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and gradient boosting with imbalance-aware metrics and paired significance tests across one hundred random re
sde571db71a.summary: Researchers study whether explanations from explainable ML models can be trusted when classifying freight shipments as Air/Air Charter or Truck/Ocean.
sde571db71a.why: Shows that feature explanations in logistics models may not be reliable, which matters for teams relying on them to justify automated decisions.

sc7e0eb8109.title: DISCERN: Preserve at Write, Resolve at Read for Persistent LLM-Agent Memory
sc7e0eb8109.description: arXiv:2611.15729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise agents accumulate memory across dozens of sessions in which facts contradict, get superseded, and blur as similarly named entities collide in embedding space. The field treats this as a retrieval problem; we show it is not. On ENT-310, a synthetic enterprise sales-agent memory benchmark of 310 queries (210 answerable, 100 unanswerable), a vanilla Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) reader over a memory store already matches strong memory systems on the recall pillars. Retention and currency are near-saturated, roughly 0.93 to 0.98 for every competent system, so recall is essentially solved. What remains unsolved is resolution: which entity a query refers to, which time-state is current, and whether to commit an answer at all or de
sc7e0eb8109.summary: DISCERN proposes handling contradicting and superseded facts at write time and resolving them at read time for persistent LLM-agent memory, tested on the ENT-310 benchmark.
sc7e0eb8109.why: Argues that enterprise agent memory failures are not just retrieval problems, which affects how teams design agent memory systems.

s0892fa2ac8.title: NIBench: benchmarking autonomous AI agents for execution, skill evolution and scientific judgment in neuroimaging
s0892fa2ac8.description: arXiv:2611.15831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous AI agents are increasingly used to automate biomedical research, creating a growing need to benchmark their capabilities on real scientific data and workflows. Their reliability in neuroimaging remains insufficiently characterized, where plausible analytical outputs can conceal errors that affect scientific conclusions. Existing studies have advanced scientific question answering and tool-based automation, but provide limited evidence on workflow reconstruction, acquisition of procedural expertise and evidence-based scientific judgment. Here we present NIBench, a neuroimaging benchmark comprising three complementary evaluations of autonomous agents. First, we benchmark execution and workflow reconstruction using 56 tasks across sev
s0892fa2ac8.summary: NIBench is a new benchmark evaluating autonomous AI agents on execution, skill evolution, and scientific judgment in neuroimaging workflows.
s0892fa2ac8.why: Highlights that plausible agent outputs in neuroimaging can hide errors affecting conclusions, so agent evaluation needs domain-specific testing.

s44ea951955.title: Controlling the Probability of Unknown Unknowns in Pre-Deployment Testing of AI Systems
s44ea951955.description: arXiv:2611.15835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In pre-deployment testing of AI systems such as AI agents, a developer can often deal with known failure modes (e.g., leaking API keys, deleting important databases, or installing a malicious package) by implementing fixes or making contingency plans for when the same issue might occur again. What is more challenging are the unknown unknowns: the unseen failure modes that haven't surfaced during testing. The decision to stop testing and deploy therefore faces an inherent tradeoff: continue testing to observe more behaviors, at the cost of time and resources, or stop testing and deploy, at the risk of failure modes remaining undiscovered. How then does the developer decide when they have tested enough? To answer this, we develop an algorithm t
s44ea951955.summary: A paper addresses how developers should decide when to stop pre-deployment testing of AI agents, weighing testing time against the risk of unseen failure modes.
s44ea951955.why: Frames the stop-and-deploy decision as a quantifiable tradeoff, which is relevant to release criteria for agent systems.

sa5346eedf8.title: Before AI Agents Negotiate for Us: A Competitive Tournament of Rule-Based, Search, Optimization, Learned, and Language-Model Negotiators Under Scarcity
sa5346eedf8.description: arXiv:2611.15838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated bilateral negotiation underlies two-sided matching markets such as freight brokering, where many shippers and carriers negotiate price before a matching mechanism decides who is paired with whom. Prior strategy comparisons typically use isolated one-on-one duels or a single fixed market, so they cannot show how a strategy behaves against several live rivals under a changing balance of supply and demand. We built nine negotiation architectures spanning rule-based, search-based, optimization-based, imitation-learning, and reinforcement-learning families, and ran all nine simultaneously on both sides of a Gale-Shapley matching market under a balanced condition and two scarcity conditions rotated across all 36 exclusion pairs. In the ba
sa5346eedf8.summary: Researchers ran a tournament of nine negotiation agents, from rule-based to language-model, in a changing supply-demand market modeled on freight brokering.
sa5346eedf8.why: Shows how negotiation strategies perform against multiple live rivals, relevant to designers of automated marketplace agents.

s9143ec8038.title: Food Critic: An Agentic Visualization System for Auditable Restaurant-Safety Reasoning
s9143ec8038.description: arXiv:2611.15843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI agents are increasingly being embedded into visualization systems that can search data, invoke tools, summarize evidence, and produce recommendations. However, when agents rely solely on their own knowledge, the visualization problem is not only whether the agent provides a useful answer, but also whether users can inspect how that answer is grounded. We present Food Critic, an agentic visualization system for diners' restaurant decision support that integrates public health inspection records with crowd review data. The system grounds agents under three conditions: a database-only ReAct agent, a retrieval- augmented agent with access to food-safety regulations, and an ontology-guided agent that produces structured hypotheses an
s9143ec8038.summary: Food Critic is an agentic visualization system combining public health inspection records with crowd reviews to support auditable restaurant-safety reasoning.
s9143ec8038.why: Demonstrates grounding agent answers in inspectable data sources rather than model knowledge alone, a pattern useful for auditable decision-support tools.

s9fa4fcef6c.title: Reward-Driven Collider Physics Challenges for Self-Improving Agentic AI via Reinforcement Learning
s9fa4fcef6c.description: arXiv:2611.15885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in agentic AI have demonstrated the potential to automate complex high-energy physics (HEP) workflows. We focus on the regime of HEP tasks where frontier models still struggle to provide correct and complete solutions, and introduce an open-ended optimization task format with continuous, automatically evaluated rewards. Unlike conventional benchmarks focused on task completion, these tasks target reinforcement learning (RL) environments to generate agentic improvement on state- of-the-art HEP challenges. We benchmark frontier reasoning models on several HEP tasks and demonstrate an initial proof of concept in which a small language model improves through RL using automated feedback without human intervention. By connecting cha
s9fa4fcef6c.summary: The paper proposes open-ended collider physics tasks with continuous automatic rewards to train agentic AI via reinforcement learning and benchmarks frontier reasoning models.
s9fa4fcef6c.why: Offers a template for building RL environments with continuous rewards for hard technical domains where current models often fail.

s1fa1b33bfa.title: Between Niti and Nyaya: A Society-Centered Framework for AI Governance
s1fa1b33bfa.description: arXiv:2611.16173v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Governments are making decisions about AI before they can measure its public effects, and those decisions determine whether a person can learn that AI influenced an outcome, challenge it, and see it corrected. Research has documented what AI governance produces: principles, strategies, registers, and audits. However, we lack shared language for understanding AI policy while it is still being made. We introduce the Society-Centered AI Governance Framework, which gives policymakers, researchers, and the public a way to assess instruments in any jurisdiction by whether a person can get notice, challenge a decision, and see it corrected. It reads a jurisdiction's instruments together by date and binding status, separates an agency duty from a rig
s1fa1b33bfa.summary: A paper introduces a Society-Centered AI Governance Framework to help assess AI policy instruments while they are still being made.
s1fa1b33bfa.why: Gives policy and compliance leaders a vocabulary for evaluating governance instruments, though the text offers little direct technical guidance.

se07e59be32.title: Stack more levels: how to get general and human-like Mario playing
se07e59be32.description: arXiv:2611.16175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Super Mario Bros. is widely used in game AI and procedural content generation (PCG), yet it remains unclear whether a model-free agent can reliably win unseen levels. To address this question, we train Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agents on increasingly large sets of PCG-generated Mario levels and evaluate their generalization on 1000 held-out test levels. We then shape competent PPO policies into three gameplay archetypes---runner, killer, and collector. Finally, we fine-tune these PPO policies using Diffusion-Reward Adversarial Imitation Learning (DRAIL) with human gameplay demonstrations. We find that increasing the number of distinct PCG-generated training levels generally improves unseen-level performance, and that fine-tuning PPO
se07e59be32.summary: Researchers train PPO agents on increasing numbers of generated Super Mario levels, test generalization on 1000 held-out levels, and shape policies into gameplay archetypes.

sf455fada29.title: Turning Multi-Agent Communication into Token-Level Credit with On Policy Self Distillation
sf455fada29.description: arXiv:2611.16206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning improves problem solving in large language model multi-agent systems. Existing approaches overlook communication knowledge or compress it into scalar rewards, leaving coarse credit with little guidance on which decisions each agent should reinforce or revise. OPSD4MAS converts future communication into fine-grained token-level credit through On Policy Self Distillation (OPSD). An external model extracts facts and assesses their trajectory relations for coarse-grained filtering, followed by fine-grained leave-one-out filtering of target-token influence against agent-wise outcome advantages. The fact-conditioned policy supplies token-level credit, combined with GRPO through a linearly annealed joint objective. Our method
sf455fada29.summary: OPSD4MAS converts inter-agent communication into fine-grained token-level credit using on-policy self distillation for reinforcement learning in LLM multi-agent systems.
sf455fada29.why: Addresses coarse credit assignment in multi-agent RL, which could improve training of LLM agent teams.

s35b7e246fb.title: One Fuzzer, Many Reasoners: Adaptive Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzing with Reliability-Calibrated and Context-Gated Guidance
s35b7e246fb.description: arXiv:2611.16211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural-symbolic AI (NSAI) combines learned perception with programs, constraints, and compositional reasoning, but remains difficult to test because small semantics-preserving changes can alter grounded symbols and trigger discontinuous reasoning failures. Existing neural fuzzers mainly rely on neural coverage or representation-space feedback and do not provide a common testing interface for heterogeneous NSAI systems. We introduce NSAI-Fuzz, a unified semantics-aware fuzzing framework that separates task-specific valid mutation from architecture-neutral guided search and represents each candidate using five availability-aware, rank-normalized risk signals: boundary pressure, grounding uncertainty, representation drift, constraint violation,
s35b7e246fb.summary: NSAI-Fuzz is a unified semantics-aware fuzzing framework for testing heterogeneous neuro-symbolic AI systems with reliability-calibrated guidance.
s35b7e246fb.why: Provides a common testing interface for neuro-symbolic systems, which are hard to test because small input changes can cause reasoning failures.

s155d9159bf.title: Causals: An Open Knowledge Graph for Research on Causal Reasoning
s155d9159bf.description: arXiv:2611.16267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applying causal knowledge to a new event requires connecting the event to relevant entities and the relationships through which its consequences may unfold. We present Causals, an open knowledge graph for research on this form of reasoning. Its initial release, constructed from news reports, contains 369,184 nodes and 1,272,418 edges linking reported events, organizations, commodities, financial instruments, and other entities. Structural relationships, observations, and attributed causal claims retain distinct semantics and links to source records. We describe the construction and representation of the resource and characterize its connectivity and multi-hop retrieval properties. Causals provides shared relational knowledge for studying how
s155d9159bf.summary: Causals is an open knowledge graph of 369,184 nodes and 1,272,418 edges built from news reports, for research on causal reasoning.
s155d9159bf.why: Offers an openly available dataset for building or testing systems that reason about how events propagate to organizations and markets.

s7b478adf3b.title: SAGE-QA: Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Closed-Context Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0
s7b478adf3b.description: arXiv:2611.16300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Closed-context question answering (QA) requires a system to generate an answer strictly supported by a supplied passage, or to abstain when the passage lacks adequate evidence. SQuAD 2.0 is a widely used benchmark for this setting, scored by Exact Match (EM) i.e., character-level agreement with human reference spans after lexical normalization. For generative large language models (LLMs), however, an EM failure may reflect a valid paraphrase or an alternative passage-supported answer rather than a hallucination. The best prior leaderboard EM is approximately 91%, but evaluating generative models requires separating lexical divergence from factual error. We introduce SAGE-QA (Semantic-Aware, Grounded Evaluation for Question Answering), a multi
s7b478adf3b.summary: SAGE-QA proposes a semantic-aware grounded evaluation for closed-context question answering on SQuAD 2.0, moving beyond strict exact-match scoring for LLMs.
s7b478adf3b.why: Exact-match scoring can mark valid paraphrases as hallucinations, so teams evaluating LLM QA may need semantic grounding metrics.

s2bb32454b2.title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors
s2bb32454b2.description: arXiv:2611.16318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluate LLM risk propensities across a range of contexts and task demands. We evaluate models for how risk averse or risk tolerant they are in various conditions, as well as how stable and consistent their behavior is across conditions. We present a toolkit for developing model risk profiles that can be used to predict model behavior and which can be adapted to include new evaluations of risk propensities. We also examine how these properties have changed across model generations and families. We observe that 2026 state-of-the-art models tend to be more stable, more consistent, and more risk neutral than older models. These trends appear to be related; newer models are more stable and consistent because they are more likely to use expecte
s2bb32454b2.summary: The paper presents a toolkit for profiling LLM risk propensities across contexts, measuring how risk-averse or risk-tolerant models are and how consistent they are.
s2bb32454b2.why: Offers a method to build model risk profiles that could inform model selection and behavior prediction in deployments.

s1bda318ca6.title: From More to Better: Causal Inference and Digital Experimentation in the Age of AI
s1bda318ca6.description: arXiv:2611.16335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is quickly expanding the capacity of organizations to produce and analyze data. We argue that this expansion shifts the leverage of data scientists from performing individual analyses to assessing the credibility and importance of findings and determining when evidence generalizes across contexts. Drawing on a roundtable of academic researchers and industry practitioners, we examine three ways in which data scientists who work on causal inference and experimentation can help organizations turn more analytical capacity into better decisions: preserving and accumulating the learning value of experimentation beyond individual tests; choosing and combining experimental, observational, and synthetic evidence; and ensur
s1bda318ca6.summary: A roundtable-based paper argues AI shifts data scientists' leverage toward assessing the credibility of findings and whether evidence generalizes across contexts.
s1bda318ca6.why: Suggests analytics teams should prioritize causal inference and experiment credibility as AI increases analysis volume.

s4a5a5bb48f.title: DIAGNO: Diagonal Spherical Neural Operators for Heterogeneous Earth Dynamics Modeling
s4a5a5bb48f.description: arXiv:2611.16356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate forecasting of Earth's dynamic systems is vital in geophysics, where neural operators offer a powerful data-driven paradigm. Standard operators often treat the Earth as a flat Euclidean plane, introducing geometric artifacts. In contrast, Spherical Neural Operators (SNOs) resolve this mismatch by operating within the spherical spectral space, naturally adapting to spherical geometries. However, for computational efficiency, existing SNOs typically rely on the rotation equivariance assumption. This assumption simplifies the transitions of physical states into isolated spectral modal evolutions, thereby over-idealizing the Earth as a homogeneous system. To solve this problem, we no longer rely on the rotation equivariance assumption th
s4a5a5bb48f.summary: Researchers propose DIAGNO, diagonal spherical neural operators for forecasting Earth's dynamic systems, arguing existing spherical operators rely on a rotation equivariance assumption.
s4a5a5bb48f.why: Shows how to model spherical geometry for geophysics forecasting while keeping computation tractable; the abstract is cut off, so details on results are limited.

s9152d872e1.title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
s9152d872e1.description: arXiv:2611.16378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agents modify prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies using interaction histories. Yet a plausible modification is not necessarily suitable for persistent adoption: candidate selection is adaptive, evaluators may be imperfect, and local gains can hide degradation against an earlier baseline. We introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for governing adoption of self-generated agent modifications. EGE separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires meaningful improvement on a prespecified primary objective, protects declared capabilities through reference-relative non-inferiority tests, and applies governance constraints before bounded c
s9152d872e1.summary: Researchers introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for deciding whether autonomous agents should permanently adopt self-generated changes to prompts, memory, tools, or policies.
s9152d872e1.why: Addresses how to keep agents from adopting plausible but degrading self-modifications, a practical reliability concern for teams deploying autonomous agents.

sdac40e2e18.title: Small Language Models for Inference-Capability Routing: Effects of Model Capacity and Prompt Optimization on Downstream Quality and Efficiency
sdac40e2e18.description: arXiv:2611.16414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optional reasoning, retrieval, web search, and tool use can improve large language model responses but incur unnecessary computation when activated indiscriminately. This study investigates whether prompt optimization can compensate for limited router capacity and whether classification gains translate into downstream efficiency. The proposed framework uses prompt-driven small language models to make four independent capability decisions, allowing multiple capabilities to be selected per query. Qwen2.5 routers ranging from 1.5B to 14B parameters are compared across five prompting strategies, followed by an evaluation of capability-specific optimized configurations using a fixed GPT-OSS-120B downstream model on 127 questions. Under minimal pro
sdac40e2e18.summary: Study tests whether small Qwen2.5 routers (1.5B to 14B parameters) with prompt optimization can decide when to enable reasoning, retrieval, web search, or tool use per query.
sdac40e2e18.why: Suggests cheaper small-model routers may cut unnecessary LLM computation, though the abstract is truncated and results are not shown.

s948c361014.title: FPSRG: Heterogeneous User Simulation First-Person Post-Training and Multidimensional Semantic Response Grids
s948c361014.description: arXiv:2611.16445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulating heterogeneous individuals with large language models is an active research direction, and heterogeneous user simulation requires models with different characteristics. We study profile construction: given dimensions, items, and scoring rules, build model configurations that can be retrieved by multidimensional target scores. We introduce First-Person Semantic Response Grids (FPSRG). Shared post-training first teaches the model to judge and answer as the participant; self-report and behavioral targets then refine dimension-specific control vectors. With the model frozen, we measure joint scores for vector-coefficient combinations, filter inadmissible configurations, and store the results in a searchable catalog. Per-token configurat
s948c361014.summary: Researchers present FPSRG, a method for building LLM user-simulation profiles retrievable by multidimensional target scores, using first-person post-training and semantic response grids.
s948c361014.why: Offers a technique for generating heterogeneous simulated users, useful for testing products, though the abstract gives limited detail on evaluation.

sf231a68f4e.title: Rational Alignments of Superintelligences via Debates
sf231a68f4e.description: arXiv:2611.16455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial superintelligences (ASI) is artificial intelligences with greater capability. However, as human principal has to use it, we have to ensure that the agent will perform in the interest of the human. We investigate the framework of ASI-assisted question answering where ASI agents know the correct answer but the human does not. We provide some example of mechanism for rational alignment, where the agent utility is unchanged, but the interaction between the agent and the human principal is controlled to be in a certain fashion. We show specifically that a debate framework where the agents can further reason and behave in a subgame perfect equilibrium manner will lead to a more predictable result, and in some case will be favorable.
sf231a68f4e.summary: Paper explores mechanisms for rationally aligning hypothetical superintelligent agents assisting humans in question answering via debate-style interaction controls.
sf231a68f4e.why: Theoretical alignment work with little immediate engineering application; the text is abstract and provides few concrete results.

sfab8f008ed.title: Fine-Tuned Small Language Model for Synthetic Clinical Data Generation and Predictive Healthcare Analytics
sfab8f008ed.description: arXiv:2611.16460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reduced availability of medical datasets represents an important challenge in the development of predictive models for remote healthcare solutions, especially when the available data are imbalanced or difficult to extend through traditional methods. Small Language Models (SLMs) have become a promising alternative to Large Language Models (LLMs) for addressing these limitations due to their lower computational requirements and adaptability to specialized tasks. However, their performance remains highly dependent on the quality and representativeness of the available training data. In this paper, we propose a method for clinical data augmentation based on a fine-tuned Microsoft Phi-2 model that is used to generate synthetic instances, with
sfab8f008ed.summary: Researchers fine-tune a small language model to generate synthetic clinical data to address scarce or imbalanced medical datasets for predictive healthcare analytics.
sfab8f008ed.why: Shows a route to augmenting imbalanced healthcare datasets with cheaper small models, though the text gives no performance figures.

s322b4d151d.title: How Should Planning Agents ReSHAPE Their Search Space?
s322b4d151d.description: arXiv:2611.16466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Planning agents and benchmarks treat a user's initial specification as fixed. Yet the requests users write exclude plans they would gladly take, since they rarely discover the possible trade-offs they would accept until seeing the options. Agents already revise requests through interaction, but whether this helps planning is unknown. We formalize this step as the ReSHAPE task, which judges a revision by whether its search space matches the acceptable plans and a planner finds one there. Using ReSHAPE Planter, which builds instances from planning benchmarks with a human-validated simulated user, we analyze 5,800 agent-revised specifications in travel and shopping. We find that reshaping matters: one correct trade-off makes the same planner rea
s322b4d151d.summary: Researchers formalize ReSHAPE, a task where planning agents revise user specifications to match acceptable plans, and build a benchmark instance generator called ReSHAPE Planter.
s322b4d151d.why: Highlights that fixed user specifications can exclude acceptable plans, a design consideration for planning agents and their evaluation benchmarks.

s034987b394.title: One Model, Two Precisions: Does Disagreement Between Quantized Copies Tell You When a Small Model Is Wrong?
s034987b394.description: arXiv:2611.16478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local language models often exist at several precisions, and quantization is known to change individual answers. This study asks whether the disagreement between two precisions of the same weights, an 8-bit copy that answers and a lower-precision copy that reads the same prompt, works as a per-question error score for abstention, escalation and re-asking. The cost is one extra forward pass over fewer bytes, with no sampling and no training. We simulate round-to-nearest quantization with per-group scales (3 to 6 bits, groups of 32 to 256) on Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B and score 8,398 multiple-choice questions from ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU and HellaSwag subsets. Error detection is measured by AUROC, risk-coverage curves and ECE on a held-ou
s034987b394.summary: Study asks whether disagreement between an 8-bit and a lower-precision quantized copy of the same model can flag questions the small model likely answers wrongly.
s034987b394.why: Offers a low-cost, training-free uncertainty signal for abstention or escalation in local model deployments, costing one extra forward pass.

sb21284fff5.title: Contain, Conform, Compare (Extended Version): A Red-Teamed Evaluation Kit for Small Coding Agents and the Full Record of Its Experiments
sb21284fff5.description: arXiv:2611.16485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A hosted score in the Gemma 4 Developer Agent competition is one noisy number, so development needs a local evaluator that is fast, safe for agent-written code, and matching the hosted scorer's prompts. drydock-eval evaluates a small coding agent (Gemma 4 E4B) at about 250 runs per hour on one RTX 5090. Contain runs each job in a fresh container without network and passed 200 scripted escape tests; conform provides eight checks that compare a local stack's requests with the scorer's configuration, down to rendered tokens; compare provides paired statistics that respect repository clusters. AI agents built and attacked the kit; a human owner approved machine use and release. This extended version repeats the short paper and adds the full recor
sb21284fff5.summary: Authors release drydock-eval, a local evaluator for the small Gemma 4 E4B coding agent, with container isolation, configuration checks, and paired comparisons.
sb21284fff5.why: Gives developers a fast local harness, running about 250 runs per hour on one RTX 5090, for matching a hosted competition scorer.

sbc6f0e4fb9.title: HeMeR: Heterogeneous Memory Reconciliation for Embodied Agents via Structured KV Reuse
sbc6f0e4fb9.description: arXiv:2611.16487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embodied agents make decisions by combining information from heterogeneous memory modules, including declarative memory for explicit knowledge, procedural memory for learned routines, and working memory for current observations. During interaction, the memory contents required for decision making change with the agent's state, goal, and task progress, while many contents remain shared across consecutive decisions. However, existing memory modules are typically accessed through separate interfaces, so each updated memory context is often processed as a new input to the foundation model. This prevents selective key-value (KV) cache reuse for unchanged memory contents and forces full KV cache recomputation even when much of the memory context re
sbc6f0e4fb9.summary: Researchers propose HeMeR, a method letting embodied agents reconcile declarative, procedural, and working memory through structured KV cache reuse.
sbc6f0e4fb9.why: Targets inference efficiency for embodied agents by reusing shared memory context across consecutive decisions, relevant to latency-sensitive systems.

s8769bb22b5.title: Time and Space: A Dual-Axis, Evidence-Grounded Context Substrate for Personal Agents
s8769bb22b5.description: arXiv:2611.16492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We argue that a binding constraint for personal agents is not model capacity but the form in which context is represented: the agent does not know which entity a phrase denotes, when a fact held, or which source record licenses a claim. We call the missing representation spatio-temporal context (STC) and define it on two axes. The temporal axis carries event time, validity intervals and ingestion time. The spatial axis is a relational space in which entities are points, typed relations are edges, and distance is semantic rather than geographic; physical places are one entity type among many. Every relation is anchored to immutable source records, and every answer must be closed over those records. We formalise the substrate and six invariants
s8769bb22b5.summary: Paper argues personal agents need spatio-temporal context representation, with temporal validity intervals and a semantic relational space, rather than just larger models.
s8769bb22b5.why: Frames context representation as a key bottleneck for personal agents, pointing engineers toward data modeling rather than only model capacity.

s7bf510cbcf.title: ReA-Bench: Benchmarking Responsible Agent Auditing
s7bf510cbcf.description: arXiv:2611.16493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As agents perform tasks autonomously in local and cloud environments, auditing their execution trajectories can help service providers identify risks and improve agent harnesses and foundation models. Our analysis of production and red-team trajectories shows that some risks are repeatedly missed across auditing configurations. Overall recall obscures which risks are missed and whether higher recall comes with more false positives on legitimate behavior. Existing benchmarks offer limited insight into these failures. Generated trajectories can contain inconsistent tool calls and responses, conspicuous risky actions, or repetitive attack patterns. Grouping results by risk type also makes it difficult to tell whether auditors overlooked evidence
s7bf510cbcf.summary: Researchers introduce ReA-Bench, a benchmark for auditing agent execution trajectories, measuring which risks are missed and false positives on legitimate behavior.
s7bf510cbcf.why: Gives teams a way to evaluate agent audit systems beyond overall recall, exposing which risks are repeatedly missed.

s1143eee44c.title: How many LLM-labelled rows does a decision encoder need, and how wrong can the labels be?
s1143eee44c.description: arXiv:2611.16498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A decision encoder such as Laya reads a question with named options (for example, which department should handle a ticket) and a text, and picks an option. It reads both in one forward pass and returns a probability for every option, without writing any text. We ask how many LLM-written training rows such an encoder needs and how wrong those labels may be. We ran 19 fine-tunes of Laya (ModernBERT-large) on nested subsets of a 2,818-row pool and scored them on 1,065 held-out items from the same generator, so every test item is in-distribution and no out-of-family test was run. Accuracy rises from 69.4% before fine-tuning to 74.3% with 5% of the rows, 84.8% with 50% and 86.9% with all rows. The curve flattens, and a saturating fit with bootstra
s1143eee44c.summary: Study measures how many LLM-labelled training rows a decision encoder (Laya, based on ModernBERT-large) needs and how much label noise it tolerates.
s1143eee44c.why: Offers guidance on data volume and label quality tradeoffs when using LLMs to generate training labels for classifiers.

sfb8c719972.title: Recalibrating a Typed-Decision Model in an Afternoon: A Hands-On Recipe for Laya's Confidence Scores
sfb8c719972.description: arXiv:2611.16499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A typed-decision model such as Laya reads a text and a list of options that the caller defines, for example ticket categories, and returns a probability for each option. Code around it compares the top probability with a threshold to answer, abstain or escalate to a person. Earlier work reports, for a Turkish model, that temperature scaling can raise held-out calibration error (ECE). This tutorial gives a five-step recipe (measure, diagnose, fit, validate, deploy) in 130 lines of numpy with standard methods, none new. On 1,065 synthetic, LLM-labelled items the released Laya checkpoint has a pooled ECE of 0.073 but a bucket-macro ECE of 0.143 (0.127-0.184), the mean over buckets (questions grouped by type and option count): the 12-option bucke
sfb8c719972.summary: Tutorial gives a five-step numpy recipe for recalibrating confidence scores of Laya, a typed-decision model, to improve answer, abstain, or escalate thresholds.
sfb8c719972.why: Provides a practical, low-complexity calibration procedure for classifiers that gate automated decisions versus human escalation.

sd60d6e2ef1.title: SignRot: LLM Quantization with Massive Outlier-Aware Sign-Adjusted Rotation
sd60d6e2ef1.description: arXiv:2611.16502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While quantization compresses LLMs and accelerates inference, outlier activations impede efficient low-bit representation. In particular, massive outliers cause substantial performance degradation. Although rotation-based methods that rely on randomized Hadamard transforms for online inference aim to mitigate this, they can produce fragmented distributions with empty bins when a massive outlier dominates a token's activation. This fragmentation severely undermines uniform quantization performance. Moreover, massive outliers concentrate in the down-projection input, where the preceding nonlinearity requires the rotation to be applied at inference time. This constraint prevents training-based approaches such as SpinQuant from learning the onlin
sd60d6e2ef1.summary: Researchers propose SignRot, an LLM quantization method using outlier-aware sign-adjusted rotation to handle massive activation outliers in low-bit representation.
sd60d6e2ef1.why: Addresses a known failure of Hadamard-rotation quantization that degrades accuracy, relevant to teams compressing LLMs for inference.

s9fbe219909.title: Lost in Delegation: Studying the Effectiveness of Task Orchestration in Generative Search
s9fbe219909.description: arXiv:2611.16526v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs have quickly evolved from models used in isolation to agentic systems that delegate tasks to external tools and other LLMs to solve complex assignments. This agentic augmentation has led to impressive capability gains. However, when and how delegation improves performance remains poorly understood. For example, it is unclear whether delegation helps when tasks involve post-cutoff information that the orchestrating LLM cannot reliably resolve from its own knowledge. In this work, we use purpose-built datasets with pre- and post-cutoff splits to compare various delegation modes. We find that delegation provides no consistent accuracy improvement over non-delegated setups, with effects varying across models and tasks. When tasks involve kno
s9fbe219909.summary: Researchers use pre- and post-cutoff datasets to study when delegating tasks to external tools or other LLMs improves generative search performance.
s9fbe219909.why: It clarifies when orchestration helps agentic search systems, which matters for deciding when to delegate versus rely on a model's own knowledge.

s64eebc7044.title: AI has its own style in mathematical proving
s64eebc7044.description: arXiv:2611.16527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models increasingly generate mathematical proofs, whether they develop a proving style distinct from that of human mathematicians remains an open question. This question is particularly pressing as mathematicians increasingly voice concerns that proofs generated by large language models are difficult to interpret. Here we ask three large language models to independently reprove all 465 propositions of Euclid's \textit{Elements} and compare their citation choices against the human-proof baseline through Jaccard similarity and complex network analysis. We find that AI-generated proofs differ from human proofs, and this difference is stable and reproducible: mean pairwise Jaccard similarity among AI runs (~0.68) is nearly twice
s64eebc7044.summary: Researchers asked three LLMs to reprove all 465 propositions of Euclid's Elements and compared their citation choices against human proofs.

sa5cc24774e.title: SPARC: Accurate Photonic Matrix Multiplication via Representative Vectors
sa5cc24774e.description: arXiv:2611.16561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic neural network accelerators have emerged as a promising solution for reducing the power consumption of deep neural network (DNN) inference by executing matrix multiplication on analog photonic hardware. However, their inference accuracy is limited by low-bit quantization required for photonic processing and by analog photonic noise. This paper proposes an approach for improving inference accuracy by exploiting the high similarity among activation vectors in DNNs. Specifically, our approach constructs a representative vector for each group of similar activation vectors, computes its inner product digitally with high precision, and offloads the residual inner products to the photonic accelerator. Since the activation vectors within eac
sa5cc24774e.summary: Researchers propose SPARC, a method using representative vectors to improve inference accuracy of neural networks on analog photonic matrix multiplication hardware.
sa5cc24774e.why: Photonic accelerators promise lower inference power, and this targets their accuracy limits from quantization and analog noise.

s1c4424bbf0.title: Large Language Models as Digital Twins: a Distribution-Aware Questionnaire-Based Evaluation
s1c4424bbf0.description: arXiv:2611.16586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates whether Large Language Models can answer a personality questionnaire as a specific individual would. Given a user's social-media posts, the model completes the BFI-2-60 Big Five questionnaire as that user. The predicted responses are converted into trait scores and compared with the user's actual scores. We evaluate GPT-4, Gemma, Llama 3.1, and Mistral on the MyPersonality dataset. To determine whether predictions reflect information from the user's writing, we compare them with answers produced without user text and with values derived from general population tendencies. We measure prediction error across all users and separately for individuals with low, intermediate, and high trait scores. We also test whether an LL
s1c4424bbf0.summary: Researchers evaluate whether GPT-4, Gemma, Llama 3.1, and Mistral can complete a Big Five questionnaire as a specific user, using their social-media posts.

scb644103fc.title: AstroMemBench: A Benchmark for Memory Systems in Embodied Spacecraft Agents
scb644103fc.description: arXiv:2611.16590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term spacecraft autonomy requires embodied agents to use operational history under communication delays, time-critical operations, environmental uncertainty, complex physical interactions, power and computational constraints, and safety and reliability requirements. We introduce AstroMemBench and a Scenario-Challenge-Capability design method that maps these requirements to executable memory tests. The benchmark covers 16 memory subchallenges through 140 templates and 2240 instances across nine tasks in planetary surface operations, on-orbit servicing, and deep-space exploration. A deterministic environment scores actions for task completion, state changes, safety, and resource use. Ablations under nine conditions show that the benchmark
scb644103fc.summary: Researchers introduce AstroMemBench, a benchmark of 2240 instances testing memory systems for embodied spacecraft agents under operational constraints.
scb644103fc.why: Long-running autonomous agents in constrained, delayed environments need memory evaluation, and this offers executable tests for it.

s051e5a06d7.title: Singularity-Bench: Can Agents Build Agents?
s051e5a06d7.description: arXiv:2611.16591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier AI agents increasingly succeed on realistic, long-horizon tasks and are beginning to improve the systems through which they operate. Yet existing benchmarks often restrict agents to narrow action spaces, use simplified environments, or rely on verification methods that are unreliable for evaluating arbitrary agent-generated systems. We introduce Singularity-Bench, an open-ended benchmark for autonomous AI development with six end-to-end tasks spanning pre-training, mid-training, post-training, inference, the agent harness, and cluster orchestration. Each task requires agents to implement core systems from a minimal starting point and evaluates them against mature human-engineered baselines on identical hardware. Additionally, through
s051e5a06d7.summary: Researchers introduce Singularity-Bench, an open-ended benchmark testing whether AI agents can carry out end-to-end AI development tasks such as pre-training and post-training.
s051e5a06d7.why: It measures whether agents can improve the systems they run on, a capability relevant to tracking agent progress and risk.

s6c7e93c264.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
s6c7e93c264.description: arXiv:2611.16609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves
s6c7e93c264.summary: Researchers propose a two-branch graph and convolutional EEG network for upper-limb movement classification with region-level interpretability.

sa7ae5f2a75.title: Studies on Sign Language Retrieval in Low-Resource Dictionary Settings
sa7ae5f2a75.description: arXiv:2611.16621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most sign languages have no annotated corpus, only small dictionaries with one or a few example videos per sign. This study examines how well a pose encoder trained on a single sign language serves such languages without any target-language training. An encoder trained with metric learning on American Sign Language (ASL-Citizen) is evaluated frozen on six datasets of Turkish, Russian, Indian, Argentinian, Pakistani and Sri Lankan sign languages, with one or four clips per sign enrolled and, where signer identities are available, the query's signer excluded from the gallery. With one enrolled clip, the encoder retrieves the correct sign first in 36.4-80.7 % of queries, against 16.0-69.6 % for the best learning-free method (angle-based dynamic
sa7ae5f2a75.summary: Researchers test whether a pose encoder trained on ASL can retrieve signs in six other sign languages without target-language training.
sa7ae5f2a75.why: It suggests transfer from data-rich sign languages could help low-resource sign language tools that lack annotated corpora.

sed3a84d18f.title: Folio: Recoverable Multi-Resolution Context Folding for Long-Horizon Language Agents
sed3a84d18f.description: arXiv:2611.16627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon language agents accumulate tool results and replies until the history no longer fits the context window. Current agents shrink this history by having a model summarize it, so each compaction rereads and rewrites the history it replaces, and cache-aware triggers decide when to compact while taking the size of the result as given. We present Folio, a context manager that records, folds, and recovers history through one set of handles. While the agent runs, Folio records three linked levels: a short turn note the model writes as part of its ordinary reply (L1), an event manifest of every call written by the runtime (L2), and the captured source records (L3). Because these views already exist, the runtime folds the context programmat
sed3a84d18f.summary: Researchers present Folio, a context manager that records, folds, and recovers long-horizon agent history through linked handles instead of model-based summarization.
sed3a84d18f.why: Context window limits are a practical bottleneck for long-running agents, and recoverable folding could reduce costly re-summarization.

sdb25eaca94.title: Safety as a Budget: Calibrating the Control Channel of Constrained GRPO for Vision-Language Models
sdb25eaca94.description: arXiv:2611.16628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning can teach vision-language models (VLMs) to decline harmful image-text requests, but how safe the result becomes is set indirectly, through reward weights found by trial runs. Stating safety as budgets on the rate of harmful assistance and the rate of over-refusal, enforced by Lagrange multipliers inside GRPO with an off-the-shelf scorer as the cost, is the natural fix, and it fails twice. The multiplier compares the scorer's mean with the budget, and scorers built for ranking get the mean wrong: a fixed-point analysis shows that the mean bias, not the budget, then decides whether the multiplier settles, saturates or switches off. And standard GRPO standardizes the penalized reward within each group, which cancels the mu
sdb25eaca94.summary: Researchers propose calibrating safety budgets with Lagrange multipliers inside constrained GRPO to control harmful assistance and over-refusal in vision-language models.
sdb25eaca94.why: Setting safety as explicit budgets rather than trial-and-error reward weights could make VLM safety tuning more predictable.

s341e623248.title: InertiaMPDD: Multimodal Personalized Depression Detection via Emotional Inertia-Inspired Dynamics Modeling
s341e623248.description: arXiv:2611.16647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal depression screening estimates risk from speech, visual behavior and language. Current methods mainly predict labels, with limited evidence of departures from a non-depressed reference. Recording-level supervision also leaves fine-grained emotional dynamics unannotated. Motivated by emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, InertiaMPDD learns healthy next-state patterns using a world-model-inspired latent predictor. Using pretrained multimodal representations, it predicts from observed history and context. Reference deviation, residual decay rate and a Jacobian spectral descriptor form reference-derived emotional dynamics descriptors, evaluated as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision cor
s341e623248.summary: Researchers propose InertiaMPDD, a multimodal depression detection method that models emotional inertia to measure deviation from a non-depressed reference.

s14dddbd4ca.title: Natural Gradient Learning in Predictive Coding through Lateral Circuits
s14dddbd4ca.description: arXiv:2611.16666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predictive coding (PC) trains neural networks through local energy-minimization dynamics without depending on a global error signal that backpropagation (BP) requires. Although PC is a promising alternative algorithm for efficient learning, the computational cost of inference dynamics currently outweighs the resulting learning benefits in practice. In this work, we take inspiration from optimization theory to extract more learning benefit from each inference phase. We introduce Natural PC, which augments standard PC with a lateral circuit, enabling exact and efficient natural gradient learning locally in space and time. Our lateral circuit learns the activity correlations that determine the Fisher information matrix and implicitly computes it
s14dddbd4ca.summary: Researchers introduce Natural PC, which adds a lateral circuit to predictive coding to extract more learning benefit from each inference phase.
s14dddbd4ca.why: Predictive coding is proposed as a backpropagation alternative, but its inference cost has limited practical use, and this targets that gap.

s1c82401b0f.title: When Expert Disagreement Hurts: Prestige and Selectivity in LLM Decision Revision
s1c82401b0f.description: arXiv:2611.16694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When language models revise a decision after another agent disagrees, neither reversal counts nor final accuracy shows whether they are fixing mistakes or abandoning correct answers. We introduce a controlled two-pass audit that holds the question, the evidence, and the model's initial answer fixed and varies only the revision context: neutral reflection, anonymous disagreement, or disagreement attributed to a domain expert. For binary decisions the accounting is exact: revision raises accuracy only if it is selective enough, reversing wrong answers more than $a/(1-a)$ times as often as correct ones, where $a$ is initial accuracy (nine times at 90%). Across five models and 1,989 evidence-grounded decisions in medicine, science, and law, no mo
s1c82401b0f.summary: Researchers audit how LLMs revise binary decisions when told of disagreement, varying whether it is neutral, anonymous, or attributed to an expert.
s1c82401b0f.why: Revision after peer disagreement can abandon correct answers, which matters for multi-agent and review pipelines relying on model consensus.

sdcb3c73efd.title: Acoustic Respiratory Phase Detection on Mobile Devices
sdcb3c73efd.description: arXiv:2611.16710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Breathing monitoring is important for well-being, stress regulation, and guided breathing exercises, yet existing approaches often rely on contact-based sensors or controlled environments. This paper presents a non-invasive framework for respiratory phase detection using acoustic signals recorded on commodity smartphones. The proposed hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture combines local spectral feature extraction with long-range temporal modeling to capture the cyclic structure of breathing. The model is evaluated using a Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) protocol on the Foundation Dataset and on an independent unseen test set comprising over 1300 breathing cycles and 2 hours of continuous recordings. The proposed 3-class formulation achieves 72.85
sdcb3c73efd.summary: Researchers present a hybrid CNN-Transformer that detects breathing phases from acoustic signals recorded on commodity smartphones.
sdcb3c73efd.why: Non-invasive respiratory sensing on ordinary phones could enable breathing monitoring without contact sensors or controlled settings.

s09c832f961.title: Mind the Accuracy-Approval Gap: How Users Evaluate Sycophantic AI in Everyday Tasks
s09c832f961.description: arXiv:2611.16722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often exhibit sycophancy, a tendency to agree with users, flatter or affirm them, and preserve their face, even when independent judgment or critical feedback would be more useful. Prior work has largely evaluated sycophancy through benchmark evaluations, but less is known about how users perceive and respond to sycophantic AI in everyday tasks. We combine benchmark evaluations with two large-scale user studies. We study four personas defined through system prompts: objective (instructed to prioritize accuracy over agreement), soft-sycophantic, hard-sycophantic, and baseline (no persona-specific system prompt). Benchmarks show that even baseline exhibits substantial sycophancy, agreeing with users' stated views 71
s09c832f961.summary: Researchers combine benchmarks and two large user studies to show how users rate sycophantic AI personas in everyday tasks, finding a gap between accuracy and approval.
s09c832f961.why: Users may approve of sycophantic answers that are less accurate, so product metrics based on user satisfaction can reward the wrong behavior.

s60abc0ab68.title: Scale-Induced Semantic Shift in Visual Prompt Injection Against VLMs and Web Agents
s60abc0ab68.description: arXiv:2611.16744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual content in multimedia systems may be resized, compressed, or re-rendered before it is interpreted by a vision-language model. We study a security failure mode in which these transformations change the machine-readable semantics of an image: a textual instruction is not recovered at a $512\times512$ presentation resolution under our evaluation protocol but becomes recoverable after aggressive downsampling. We formulate this behavior as Scale-Induced Semantic Shift (SISS) and develop a closed-loop black-box framework that combines dual-scale verification, selective self-hardening, shallow-layer low-rank adaptation, and pixel-space noise regularization. On a fixed 300-case benchmark, the third SISS refinement round obtains a $58.75\%$ ave
s60abc0ab68.summary: Researchers show that resizing or compressing images can make hidden text instructions recoverable by vision-language models, creating a visual prompt injection risk for web agents.
s60abc0ab68.why: Agents that ingest screenshots or resized images may follow injected instructions that were invisible at normal resolution, so input pipelines need security review.

s9f4614dfbf.title: A Modular Framework for ESG Prediction through Domain-Specific Language Modeling and Graph Learning
s9f4614dfbf.description: arXiv:2611.16831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) scores are increasingly used to evaluate corporate sustainability, supporting investment decisions, ensuring regulatory compliance and assessing risk. However, current ESG evaluations largely rely on proprietary methodologies that often produce inconsistent ratings. This motivates the development of data-driven prediction frameworks. In this paper, we present ESGPred, a modular framework for predicting ESG scores by combining domain-specific language modeling with graph-based learning over a network that models the relationships among the companies being evaluated. In addition to presenting the rationale behind ESGPred and detailing its ESG score prediction process, we show that ESGPred can effective
s9f4614dfbf.summary: ESGPred is a modular framework that predicts ESG scores by combining domain-specific language modeling with graph learning over company networks.

s3c06e4b5d1.title: CADET: Construction of PCB Routing Instances with Executable Demonstrations
s3c06e4b5d1.description: arXiv:2611.16913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Printed circuit board (PCB) routing is the stage of physical layout that finds paths connecting the placed pads of each net. Public datasets in this domain are few, and most contain only the final states of routed boards, not demonstrations of the electronic design automation (EDA) engine actions that produce them. To close this gap, we propose CADET (Constructing executAble Demonstrations for Engine-grounded Training), which jointly generates synthetic boards and demonstrations built from EDA engine actions. The resulting RouteDemos provides 100,000 synthetic boards routed with zero design rule violations (DRVs), together with their demonstrations. Their distributions over 17 statistics resemble those of 142 real reference boards. CADET trai
s3c06e4b5d1.summary: CADET generates synthetic PCB boards and demonstrations built from EDA engine actions, releasing a dataset called RouteDemos for PCB routing.
s3c06e4b5d1.why: Engine-grounded demonstration data could help train automation for PCB routing, a domain with few public datasets.

s4f48b16b6a.title: Universal Infectious Disease Forecasting with Mantis 2
s4f48b16b6a.description: arXiv:2611.16935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Public health agencies need to anticipate how outbreaks will unfold, when they will peak, and how long demand on health services will remain elevated. We previously developed a foundation model, Mantis, which was trained entirely on simulated outbreaks---enabling us to generate the diversity and scale of training data needed to support forecasting across diseases. However, our previous work left unresolved when simulation improves predictions and how it should complement observational data. Here, we varied the balance of simulated and observed training data while holding forecasting tasks fixed and varying the available surveillance history. We found that simulation-rich training was particularly valuable with limited local history, and its r
s4f48b16b6a.summary: Mantis 2 is a forecasting foundation model for infectious disease outbreaks, studying how mixing simulated and observed training data affects predictions.

s894b840845.title: S1-Evo: Experience-Guided Evidence Competition Attacks on Typed System-1 Decision Models
s894b840845.description: arXiv:2611.16937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Typed System-1 (S1) decision models are increasingly deployed in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization to cut inference cost, yet untrusted context can still manipulate typed outputs and alter execution branches. Unlike autoregressive System-2 (S2) models, S1 interfaces score dynamic rules and options without token-by-token decoding, mismatching attacks targeting text continuation or explicit override commands. We propose S1-Evo, a self-evolving framework tailored to S1's contract-based option competition and margin feedback. S1-Evo perturbs untrusted fields via contract-aware evidence channels to induce \emph{evidence competition} with original task evidence while preserving fact invariance. Offline on seed tasks, it optimize
s894b840845.summary: S1-Evo is a self-evolving attack framework that targets typed System-1 decision models used in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization.
s894b840845.why: Typed routing and authorization classifiers in agent stacks can be manipulated by untrusted context, so they need adversarial testing.

sd83a734d81.title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
sd83a734d81.description: arXiv:2611.16961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing adaptive-reasoning methods shorten the explicit reasoning a model writes, or skip it by switching modes; either way the answer is still written out token by token. \emph{Rather than deciding how much to think}, we explore a different paradigm, \emph{zero-or-$T$ thinking}: a single model either answers from the implicit thinking inside one forward pass, generating no token, or performs full autoregressive reasoning at a cost of $T$ tokens when that is worth paying. We realise it in a \emph{hybrid decision model} (HDM), where one frozen backbone serves both modes and a lightweight \emph{self-routing block} chooses between them. The block estimates the \emph{value of thinking}, the utility the slow mode is expected to add over the fast
sd83a734d81.summary: The paper proposes zero-or-T thinking, where a hybrid decision model either answers in one forward pass or spends reasoning tokens only when worthwhile.
sd83a734d81.why: Selectively skipping reasoning could cut inference cost in production while keeping accuracy on harder queries.

s14ce965bb4.title: Compiling Known Rules into Compact Neural Agents: Weight-Space Programming on Unseen Games
s14ce965bb4.description: arXiv:2611.16981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses language models to construct neural network weights without training. We test whether known game mechanics can be compiled into compact agents that generalise to held-out levels, renderings and start states within a game family. Writers receive simulator source with held-out level data removed for 20 privately authored, unpublished ARC-AGI-3-style game families. With a fixed 57k-parameter recurrent architecture, the strongest writer reaches 56% held-out-level success with feedback, while the four main writers' Python players reach 97-100%. An exploratory free-architecture condition reaches 68-90%. Learning from support-level examples transfers much less well, but these learners lack the source information g
s14ce965bb4.summary: Researchers test weight-space programming, using language models to write compact neural agent weights from game mechanics, reaching 56% held-out-level success for the best writer.

s4d198a431c.title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation
s4d198a431c.description: arXiv:2611.16986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Educational simulations are a well-established pedagogical technique that gives learners opportunities to apply knowledge, respond to challenges, and reflect on their performance. High-quality simulations, however, are difficult to build, requiring instructor input, scenario design, character development, scaffolding, technical implementation, and repeated revision. This paper presents Primer, an open-source, LLM-agnostic AI-supported system that helps educators create adaptive educational simulations. Educators contribute their knowledge of the subject, lesson, and students, while generative AI produces responsive variations of practice for students. Primer uses a multi-agent system centered around executing educator's instructional intent t
s4d198a431c.summary: Primer is an open-source, LLM-agnostic system that helps educators build adaptive educational simulations with AI support.

s50350dc560.title: AnalogLayoutWorld: An Open Benchmark for Agentic Analog Layout Design
s50350dc560.description: arXiv:2611.16991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. We study this question through analog circuit layout, which demands domain knowledge, geometric reasoning, and iterative interaction with design and verification tools. We introduce \textbf{AnalogLayoutWorld}, an open-source agent benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks for end-to-end layout generation from fixed transistor-level netlists. It combines an integrated design environment with independent physical and post-layout electrical verification, as well as objective layout quality metrics co-designed with analog layout experts. Across 13 model--har
s50350dc560.summary: AnalogLayoutWorld is an open-source benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks testing coding agents on end-to-end analog circuit layout from transistor-level netlists.
s50350dc560.why: It gives teams a concrete benchmark for measuring whether agents can handle long-horizon engineering tasks constrained by physical rules.

s2efbfd5385.title: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
s2efbfd5385.description: arXiv:2611.17007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents use external skills to reuse task procedures and experience with tools. General-purpose skills describe shared execution procedures, while specific tool choices, operating practices, and output requirements vary across users. In long-horizon tasks, subgoals, available inputs, and environmental states change as execution progresses. Agents must select currently applicable skills from an expanding skill pool and prepare candidates for subsequent steps. We propose Skill Adapter, which enables personalized modification and online routing of general-purpose skills. The system distills local adjustments from user requirements and execution feedback and stores them as Adapters linked to general-purpose skills. The r
s2efbfd5385.summary: Skill Adapter proposes personalizing general-purpose agent skills for individual users and routing among an expanding skill pool during long-horizon tasks.
s2efbfd5385.why: Agent platforms with many shared skills may need per-user adaptation and runtime skill selection to stay effective.

s69a04314a3.title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
s69a04314a3.description: arXiv:2611.17031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on thousands of hours of recordings, yet their frozen features transfer poorly to downstream tasks, and this transfer does not consistently improve with larger models or more pretraining data. We show that a vision foundation model that has never seen EEG is a stronger frozen EEG encoder than these specialized models, once the signals are rendered as images that a vision transformer can read. Our method, SeeEEG, keeps the vision backbone frozen and learns only how EEG is displayed to it. Each channel occupies a dedicated row of patches and is drawn either as a waveform at a fixed gain or as a scalogram whose frequency range spans the patch height, so that task-relevant patterns fal
s69a04314a3.summary: SeeEEG renders EEG signals as images so a frozen vision foundation model can encode them, outperforming specialized EEG foundation models on frozen-feature transfer.
s69a04314a3.why: It suggests that reusing general vision models may beat costly domain-specific pretraining for some biosignal tasks.

s33616c7d9b.title: Reasoning Supervision and Capability Retention in LoRA Domain Adaptation
s33616c7d9b.description: arXiv:2611.17072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning foundation models on financial data has a wide range of applications, including identifying event types from news, monitoring risk and compliance language, and answering questions over filings and earnings calls. In this setting, the main challenge is to improve task performance without degrading the generalization capabilities of the model. In this paper, we present an extensive set of ablations for fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with low-rank adaptation (LoRA).
