We compare three training regimes: (1) response-only LoRA, where the supervised response is the label alone; (2) single-adapter reasoning, where reasoning traces from a teacher model are included alongside the labels in the training loss; and (3) dual-adapter composite training, wh
s33616c7d9b.summary: The paper reports ablations of LoRA fine-tuning Qwen3-8B on financial data, comparing response-only training with other regimes to measure capability retention.
s33616c7d9b.why: It gives practical evidence on how fine-tuning choices affect retained general abilities when adapting models to domains like finance.

s5f3d42af42.title: Speed-to-Power Dominates Energy Costs for AI Data Centers: Technoeconomic Analysis of Powering AI in the Continental United States
s5f3d42af42.description: arXiv:2611.17098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving demand for new data centers at large scale and on short deployment timelines. To power them, firms connect to the commercial grid or contract generation directly, but interconnection and gas-turbine delays now incentivize on-site generation. We compare grid-connected and off-grid data center energy infrastructure (AC- and DC-coupled solar-plus-storage, islanded natural gas, and grid interconnection) across the continental U.S. Using an open-source technoeconomic framework built on empirically calibrated AI training loads, climate-driven cooling, stage-by-stage power conversion, and physics-based battery degradation, we model designs providing equivalent energy services. Our central contri
s5f3d42af42.summary: A technoeconomic analysis compares grid-connected and off-grid power options for AI data centers across the continental U.S., finding speed-to-power dominates energy costs.
s5f3d42af42.why: Interconnection and gas-turbine delays make time-to-power a key constraint on AI data center deployment planning and cost.

s97d3c2a1ce.title: CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts
s97d3c2a1ce.description: arXiv:2611.17115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enforcement defenses against prompt injection, such as CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard and DRIFT, ask the agent's own model to write a security artifact (a program, a privilege policy, a dependency graph or a constraint list) that code then enforces. We ask whether small language model (SLM) agents can be trusted to write these artifacts. Across 15 open-weight models, 13 of them between 1.7B and 12B parameters, they cannot: the policies, graphs and constraints that the agent's model writes admit attacks on 14 (Progent), 13 (IPIGuard) and 11 (DRIFT) of the models, and CaMeL's programs fail to run in up to 68% of episodes. We present CapLite, which derives its policy from the tool schemas, commits the write calls before any tool result is read, and ad
s97d3c2a1ce.summary: CapLite finds that small language model agents cannot reliably write security policies for prompt-injection defenses, as attacks succeed against model-written artifacts in many cases.
s97d3c2a1ce.why: Teams relying on small models to generate their own injection defenses should not assume those policies hold against adversarial inputs.

s979e5b5427.title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s979e5b5427.description: arXiv:2611.17161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation systems attach citations to attribute claims to their sources. These citations frequently misstate provenance, and standard verification cannot detect this. We measure provenance by counterfactual value substitution: a fact in the retrieved passages is replaced with a false variant and the model re-queried. We find that across five sizes of one model family and a second comparator family, 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims derive from parametric memory rather than the retrieved context. At the most conservative substitution distance these figures are 4.6% and 8.5% on the two models we tested at it, with the rate rising with model size within a family. We further find that natural language inference verification, th
s979e5b5427.summary: A study using counterfactual substitution finds 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims in RAG outputs derive from parametric memory rather than retrieved context.
s979e5b5427.why: Citations in RAG systems can misstate sources, so verification must check provenance beyond whether a citation exists.

s2190decebe.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
s2190decebe.description: arXiv:2611.17167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoa
s2190decebe.summary: Researchers study whether decision models that act poorly can still teach well, comparing three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld.
s2190decebe.why: It suggests evaluating decision models by their teaching or judging value, not just their acting performance, when training agents with reinforcement learning.

sdd76fafb29.title: Cortex-FL: Agent-Mediated Collaboration for Federated Learning
sdd76fafb29.description: arXiv:2611.17186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables independent data owners to train models collaboratively without centralizing raw data. However, identifying collaborators, preparing training tasks, and coordinating execution and incentives hinder its practical adoption by organizations without specialized expertise. We present Cortex-FL, an agent-native FL system that enables users to express learning objectives in natural language and delegate the collaboration required to train a model. Agents translate these objectives into shared tasks, discover collaborators, and negotiate participation agreements, connecting collaboration formation with distributed training and incentive management. The architecture separates agent coordination from local execution auth
sdd76fafb29.summary: Cortex-FL is an agent-native federated learning system where users state learning objectives in natural language and agents find collaborators and coordinate training.
sdd76fafb29.why: It could lower the expertise barrier for organizations adopting federated learning by automating collaborator discovery, task preparation, and coordination.

seaad07492c.title: Al-Ghasali: A Computational Framework for Simulating Islamic Jurisprudential Rulings via Finite State Automata and Large Language Models
seaad07492c.description: arXiv:2611.17235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents Al Ghasali, a computational framework designed to formalize and simulate Islamic jurisprudential (Fiqh) rulings. Building upon recent set theoretic formalizations of al sabr wa al Taqsim that extract minimal operational rules as simple Horn clause logical programs, this work proves that the semantics of closed Fiqh chapters collapse completely to deterministic Finite State Automata (FSA). We establish a formal computational hierarchy, demonstrating that restricting formalization to finite propositional Horn theories guarantees decidability and constant time (O(1)) verdict extraction after offline compilation. The framework formally proves that hierarchical compositions of sub-chapter FSAs preserve this O(1) complexity, and
seaad07492c.summary: Al-Ghasali is a framework that formalizes Islamic jurisprudential rulings, proving closed Fiqh chapters reduce to deterministic finite state automata.

s9411c87e03.title: Ballad: Bandit-Based LLM Routing for Automated Heuristic Discovery
s9411c87e03.description: arXiv:2611.17241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern automated heuristic discovery (AHD) systems increasingly rival hand-crafted heuristics by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) to iteratively mutate and refine solutions. A natural assumption is that more powerful and more expensive models consistently yield better heuristics. We challenge this empirically: across multiple NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems, we find no consistent advantage for larger, costlier models. This raises a deeper question: given a pool of LLMs spanning frontier and freely hosted or open-weight models, how should one adaptively select which model to invoke at each step of the search? The challenge is non-trivial. The optimal LLM may shift over the course of a run, and because one LLM's output seeds
s9411c87e03.summary: Ballad is a bandit-based method for routing across LLMs in automated heuristic discovery, after finding larger, costlier models do not consistently yield better heuristics.
s9411c87e03.why: It suggests that cost-aware model routing can match or beat always using the most expensive model in iterative LLM-driven optimization pipelines.

s8cf28cb8fb.title: LiveGeo: Benchmarking Geographic Agents in Continuously Evolving Worlds
s8cf28cb8fb.description: arXiv:2611.17267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce GeoWorld, a controllable and continuously evolving geographic environment platform for LLM agents, and LiveGeo, a benchmark for evaluating reliable decision-making in real-world geographic environments using GeoWorld. Unlike existing evaluations that largely reason and plan over fixed geographic states, GeoWorld is grounded in real-world geographic structure and allows external world states to evolve along their own temporal processes while preserving verifiable state histories. LiveGeo places geographic tasks within this evolving environment, requiring agents to actively acquire task-relevant information, verify whether the evidence supporting prior decisions remains valid, and revise their plans when necessary. Our results reve
s8cf28cb8fb.summary: LiveGeo is a benchmark for geographic LLM agents, run on GeoWorld, an environment where real-world geographic states keep evolving over time.
s8cf28cb8fb.why: It shifts agent evaluation from fixed states toward changing environments, relevant for teams deploying agents that must act on up-to-date world data.

s3d4ca1bc2c.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
s3d4ca1bc2c.description: arXiv:2611.17309v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Looped models have emerged as a prominent paradigm for reasoning, with successes on simple reasoning puzzles such as Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique. However, these models can be unstable, slow to train, and use many parameters and FLOPs to solve simple puzzles. Descent on an energy not only mitigates these issues but also offers advantages: built-in early stopping, compute that adapts to problem difficulty, fast training without differentiating through a solver, and interpretable weights that learn the constraints of the puzzle. Here we demonstrate this with a learned version of Hopfield & Tank's energy from the 80s, which we term CRAM, solves 99.996% of Sudoku-Extreme and 100% of Maze-Unique test puzzles after 42 ms and 132 ms of training on
s3d4ca1bc2c.summary: Researchers report that energy-descent models solve reasoning puzzles far faster than looped models, claiming up to 1,000x speedups on puzzles like Sudoku and mazes.
s3d4ca1bc2c.why: If the speedups hold, energy-based methods could offer a cheaper, more stable alternative to looped reasoning models for puzzle-style tasks.

s0e01cb2c12.title: CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation
s0e01cb2c12.description: arXiv:2611.17316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents tackle successive tasks on an evolving repository, carrying forward edits and writing memory before the next task is known. Selecting memory for unknown next tasks requires balancing future usefulness against the costs of writing and reading it. The actor must also decide when acting on available memory saves effort as the task unfolds. We introduce Coding-Repository Memory (CoReMem), a cost-internalizing framework that guides memory design and actor adaptation through measured memory value on the next task. Prospective segment valuation compares runs of the next task with and without individual trajectory segments from the same inherited repository state, guiding a compact memory built around anchors: repository locations and e
s0e01cb2c12.summary: CoReMem is a framework for coding agents that decides what memory to write and read across successive repository tasks, weighing future usefulness against costs.
s0e01cb2c12.why: It addresses how coding agents should manage persistent memory across tasks, balancing storage and retrieval cost against benefit.

sebb4066459.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
sebb4066459.description: arXiv:2611.17323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applying machine learning systems to new domains introduces bottlenecks in both labeled data acquisition and manual pipeline engineering. While recent MLE agents show promise in automating pipeline design, they have been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised settings, leaving them untested in realistic regimes where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. In this work, we introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL), framing SSL as a program search problem and studying how agents navigate this space under limited supervision. We find that even under weak feedback and matched compute, agents can synthesize code that combines and adapts established SSL techniques, exceeding the strongest human-engineered baselin
sebb4066459.summary: AgentSSL tests whether machine learning agents can use abundant unlabeled data when labeled data is scarce, framing semi-supervised learning as a program search problem.
sebb4066459.why: It tests whether automated ML agents work outside fully supervised settings, which matters for teams with little labeled data.

s42cff36e9a.title: The Impact of Large Language Models (LLMs) on Code Review Process
s42cff36e9a.description: arXiv:2508.11034v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently gained prominence in the field of software development, significantly boosting productivity and simplifying teamwork. Although prior studies have examined task-specific applications, the phase-specific effects of LLM assistance on the efficiency of code review processes remain underexplored. This research investigates the effect of GPT on GitHub pull request (PR) workflows, with a focus on reducing resolution time, optimizing phase-specific performance, and assisting developers. We curated a dataset of 25,473 PRs from 9,254 GitHub projects and identified GPT-assisted PRs using a semi-automated heuristic approach that combines keyword-based detection, regular expression filtering, and manual verific
s42cff36e9a.summary: A study examines how GPT assistance affects different phases of GitHub pull request review, measuring effects on resolution time and developer productivity.
s42cff36e9a.why: Phase-specific measurements help engineering leaders decide where LLM assistance in code review actually reduces resolution time.

s0db5dd3d12.title: Care, Human Enfeeblement, and the Existential Implications of AGI
s0db5dd3d12.description: arXiv:2611.14520v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stuart Russell has named "human enfeeblement" as a long-term societal risk of advanced AI. This paper gives a new interpretation of the enfeeblement danger by interpreting it in light of recent work by Brian Christian, Alison Gopnik, and David Spivak on care and caregiving, and connecting it with the ontological design tradition of Terry Winograd and Fernando Flores. The enfeeblement that threatens is not merely a matter of cognitive off-loading and loss of knowledge, but a form of disengagement with the world which I explain in terms of an erosion of our capacities to care. This paper articulates a conception of care as a constellation of cultivable skills that involve us in the world and with each other, while making life worth living. De
s0db5dd3d12.summary: A philosophical paper reinterprets Stuart Russell's concept of human enfeeblement through care and caregiving, framing the danger as disengagement from the world.

sdd5524621d.title: EasyFoam: Skill-Oriented OpenFOAM Agents with Evidence-Driven Evolution
sdd5524621d.description: arXiv:2611.14525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of automating end-to-end OpenFOAM workflows for computational fluid dynamics (CFD). However, current progress is bottlenecked by two critical limitations. First, existing evaluations are dominated by tutorial-level cases and execution-oriented metrics, masking a substantial executability--acceptability gap: successfully executed simulations often fail to satisfy prescribed numerical or quantity-of-interest (QoI) criteria. Second, domain expertise in existing systems is tightly coupled with bespoke agent architectures, limiting its reuse and continual refinement across agent implementations. To address these challenges, we introduce ExtFoamBench, a challenging benchmark for OpenFOAM
sdd5524621d.summary: EasyFoam proposes skill-oriented LLM agents for OpenFOAM CFD workflows, with evidence-driven evolution and evaluation that checks simulations against numerical acceptance criteria.
sdd5524621d.why: It highlights the gap between executed simulations and results meeting engineering criteria, relevant for teams automating scientific computing workflows.

s6fd63fbf47.title: Gaussian processes for real-time urban traffic estimation using a fleet of drones
s6fd63fbf47.description: arXiv:2611.14536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time urban traffic monitoring is essential for modern city management, yet conventional static sensors provide only limited spatial coverage. Autonomous drone fleets can complement this infrastructure by offering flexible, high-resolution mobile sensing across different parts of the network. This paper introduces a spatio-temporal Gaussian process (GP) framework for reconstructing network-wide traffic states from partial aerial observations. The model accounts for the physical structure of the road network through a graph Mat\'ern kernel, which embeds network topology into the spatial covariance structure, and captures temporal dependencies through an exponential temporal kernel. Within this framework, historical loop detector data pro
s6fd63fbf47.summary: Researchers propose a spatio-temporal Gaussian process framework that reconstructs city-wide traffic states from partial observations gathered by a fleet of drones.

s5cbcb391ed.title: metalSPARSE: A 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparse GEMV Kernel for Apple Silicon GPUs
s5cbcb391ed.description: arXiv:2611.14545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, and each token reads every weight from memory, so on edge devices, decoding is limited by memory bandwidth. 2:4 semi-structured sparsity keeps two of every four weights, but Apple-silicon GPUs have no sparse matrix hardware, so pruning helps only if a kernel actually reads fewer bytes. We present metalSPARSE, to our knowledge the first 2:4 sparse kernels for Apple GPUs, together with a fused decoder written in Metal. The kernels stream weights in compressed form and expand them in registers. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with 2:4 sparsity on every decoder linear layer, decoding runs 3.6x faster than HuggingFace Transformers on PyTorch-MPS on an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air and 1.52x fa
s5cbcb391ed.summary: metalSPARSE presents 2:4 semi-structured sparse GEMV kernels and a fused decoder in Metal for Apple silicon GPUs, reducing memory reads during LLM decoding.
s5cbcb391ed.why: Sparse kernels that cut bytes read could speed up on-device LLM inference on Apple hardware, where decoding is memory-bandwidth bound.

s4400e6db46.title: SideTaskBench: Measuring Unauthorized Side-Task Delivery in Coding Agents
s4400e6db46.description: arXiv:2611.14548v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a coding agent fix a user's repository while also completing and delivering work the user never requested? In this paper, we introduce SideTaskBench to measure this failure where third-party technical references induce agents to produce independent side-task artifacts during an authorized repair. Repair success alone misses this behavior. Our key measurement contribution is to pair each repair with a self-contained side task and verify side tasks' delivery success rate along with the repair success rate. The benchmark contains 25 Python repairs and 190 side-task units. Its four-level similarity index defines 300 executable repair--side-task pairs. The experiments show roughly 40% valid delivery under wrapped requests for two models, alo
s4400e6db46.summary: SideTaskBench is a benchmark measuring whether coding agents deliver unrequested side-task artifacts while completing an authorized repository repair.
s4400e6db46.why: It exposes a failure mode where repair success alone misses unauthorized extra work, relevant to agent oversight and security reviews.

s1fd5bab406.title: AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication for Automated, Auditable Read-Level Review in Cancer Diagnostic Sequencing
s1fd5bab406.description: arXiv:2611.14560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identifying a tumor's DNA mutations is central to cancer diagnosis and treatment, but distinguishing genuine mutations from sequencing artifacts is error-prone. In practice, genuine mutations are identified using fixed variant-allele-frequency (VAF) and depth thresholds which cannot separate artifacts from genuine mutations in the borderline low-VAF zone where they overlap. A laboratory specialist must manually inspect the read-level sequencing data, a slow step that has high inter-rater variability and causes diagnosis delays. We present AVA: Agentic Variant Adjudication; an agentic framework that automates this read-level inspection with subagents that reason over evidence, generate investigative code, and return a real-or-artifact adjudi
s1fd5bab406.summary: AVA is an agentic system for read-level review of cancer sequencing data, aiming to separate genuine tumor mutations from artifacts in borderline low-frequency cases.

s75c0e745a3.title: Deep learning-guided discovery reveals the diversity and mutational potential of environmental beta-lactamases
s75c0e745a3.description: arXiv:2611.14568v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Beta-lactamases are a major mechanism of bacterial resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics; however, their functional diversity and mutational potential in environmental microbial communities remain partially understood. This study aimed to characterize environmental beta-lactamase diversity and investigate how sequence variation influences antibiotic resistance. By integrating protein language model (PLMs) with ensemble learning, we identified more than 46,000 putative beta-lactamases across all four Ambler classes from environmental metagenomes, widely distributed across diverse habitats, with distinct habitat-associated class compositions. The candidates sharing approximately 30% sequence identity with known beta-lactamases conferred resis
s75c0e745a3.summary: Researchers combined protein language models with ensemble learning to identify over 46,000 putative beta-lactamases across all four Ambler classes in environmental metagenomes.
s75c0e745a3.why: It shows how deep learning can mine large metagenomic datasets for antibiotic resistance genes, relevant to biosecurity and resistance surveillance.

s341e803528.title: MechFoundry: An agentic loop that poses and performs engineering analyses and optimization of real-world objects
s341e803528.description: arXiv:2611.14571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents can automate software engineering because a compiler or a test suite checks that the code does what the user or the agent intended. In engineering analysis, however, the steps that precede the computation have few easily verifiable checks: modeling a design or an object, deciding how it is used, where supports and loads are applied, and what material each part is made of. A human expert therefore makes these decisions, carries out the steps, and judges the result, one object at a time. We present MechFoundry, an agentic loop coupled with bespoke software that automates structural analyses of real-world objects without a human in the loop. From an object's lexical description, it generates a shape, poses a loading case relevant to
s341e803528.summary: MechFoundry is an agentic loop that aims to automate engineering analyses, including modeling, applying supports and loads, and assigning materials, for real-world objects.
s341e803528.why: It tests whether agents can handle engineering steps that lack easy automated verification, a gap beyond software tasks like code generation.

s96196630ac.title: When Evaluators of AI Agents Disagree: An Empirical Study of Native Scoring, LLM Judges, and Commit-Boundary Checks on tau2-bench
s96196630ac.description: arXiv:2611.14581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic workflows, in which a large language model (LLM) calls tools to read and write data, are evaluated in two ways. Benchmarks compare the final state against a gold answer. Deployed services have none; an LLM judge reads the transcript and decides. Practice treats the two as interchangeable. This paper measures whether they are. We ran 2,160 episodes in tau2-bench's airline and retail domains and recorded every database write. We scored each episode four ways: native scoring against gold state, an LLM judge, that judge given the policy document, and the boundary evaluator, a minimal rule-based check of whether a write was expected against whether one occurred in the trace. Two annotators independently labeled 120 episodes for task corr
s96196630ac.summary: A study of 2,160 tau2-bench episodes finds that native benchmark scoring, LLM judges, and commit-boundary checks can disagree when evaluating tool-using AI agents.
s96196630ac.why: Teams using LLM judges to evaluate deployed agents should not assume they match benchmark gold-state scoring.

s0295ee8f3b.title: Finite-Cadence Refresh Equilibria for Streaming Prior-Anchored Ridge: A Closed-Form Forgetting Window and Spectral Correction
s0295ee8f3b.description: arXiv:2611.14586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recursive estimators on drifting streams must forget stale data fast enough to track the target, yet slowly enough to average out noise. In prior-anchored ridge regression, this trade-off admits a closed-form spectral decomposition in which each eigen-direction interpolates between the data solution and the prior with pull weight $s_i = \rho / (\mu_i + \rho)$. When the anchor is refreshed every $k$ steps, we show that the moving-frame offset converges to a finite-cadence equilibrium that lags the pure-leaky path by an explicit $\Delta_k(s)$ while reducing estimation variance by a factor $\Psi(s, r_k)$. Minimizing the cycle-averaged risk gives $\omega^* = (4\nu^2 \Sigma / c')^{1/3}$, $c' = \sigma^2 d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\rho)$, and the plug-in st
s0295ee8f3b.summary: The paper derives a closed-form forgetting window and spectral correction for prior-anchored ridge regression on drifting streams when the anchor is refreshed every k steps.

s7b0d177dd4.title: CAFIN: CUDA-accelerated Adaptive Fisher Information Matrix Network Optimization via GPU-Native Kernel Fusion
s7b0d177dd4.description: arXiv:2611.14589v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Second-order optimizers improve deep neural network training using curvature information, but their practical efficiency is limited by GPU execution overhead. AdaFisher reduces Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) approximation costs through diagonal Kronecker structures and exponential moving averages, yet its PyTorch implementation requires sequential CUDA kernel launches, intermediate tensor allocations, and repeated memory accesses. We introduce CAFIN, a GPU-native CUDA kernel fusion framework that improves AdaFisher execution efficiency without changing its optimization formulation. The proposed approach progressively integrates FIM preconditioner construction, exponential moving average updates, gradient preconditioning, momentum accumulat
s7b0d177dd4.summary: CAFIN is a GPU-native CUDA kernel fusion framework that speeds up the AdaFisher second-order optimizer by reducing sequential kernel launches and intermediate allocations.
s7b0d177dd4.why: Reducing GPU overhead in second-order optimizers could make curvature-aware training more practical for teams with limited compute budgets.

s7c43b2cc07.title: Multi-Step Underwater Acoustic Channel Prediction via Dual-Domain Structure Preservation and Pretrained Transformer
s7c43b2cc07.description: arXiv:2611.14592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. However, most existing predictors estimate only the next channel state and obtain multi-step forecasts through recursive rollout, which causes prediction errors to accumulate as the multipath structure evolves. The scarcity of sea-trial measurements further limits reliable model training. To address these challenges, we propose LLM4UACP, a dual-domain, structure-preserving framework that adapts a pretrained Transformer for few-shot multi-step UWA channel prediction. LLM4UACP extracts comple
s7c43b2cc07.summary: Researchers propose a dual-domain, pretrained-transformer method for multi-step underwater acoustic channel prediction to reduce error accumulation from recursive rollout.

s214af207cd.title: KernelMosaic: An Open Dataset and Agentic Framework for CUDA Kernel Generation
s214af207cd.description: arXiv:2611.14604v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Training large language models to generate efficient CUDA kernels requires supervision spanning diverse computational requirements and iterative code optimization. Constructing this supervision is challenging because of heterogeneous specifications, and useful implementations emerge through iterative complicated testing and refinement. We introduce KernelMosaic, an open dataset pairing diverse CUDA tasks with verified solutions and trajectories. Human-guided review and diversity-aware selection curate tasks expressed as natural-language descriptions, reference programs, mathematical specifications, and their intersections. To build the solutions and trajectories, our agentic framework guides a strong LLM through implementation, correctness
s214af207cd.summary: KernelMosaic is an open dataset of CUDA tasks with verified solutions and trajectories, plus an agentic framework for training models to generate CUDA kernels.
s214af207cd.why: An open, verified dataset for CUDA kernel generation could help teams build or evaluate code models for GPU performance work.

s9c0f796e9e.title: Evaluating AI Musical Creativity: Towards a Quantitative Multi-Dimensional Framework Based on Value, Novelty, and Surprise
s9c0f796e9e.description: arXiv:2611.14634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite the increasing sophistication of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI), research on the evaluation of AI-generated musical creativity remains limited. To address this gap, this paper proposes a quantitative framework for the formalization and evaluation of AI musical creativity. Building on Margaret Boden's theory, which conceptualizes creativity in terms of value, novelty, and surprise, the framework adapts and operationalizes these three dimensions for the musical domain. On the hypothesis that certain aspects of musical creativity can be assessed with a degree of objectivity, a domain-specific set of quantitative metrics for evaluating the creativity of AI-generated music is introduced. Rather than reducing musical creativity t
s9c0f796e9e.summary: The paper proposes a quantitative framework for evaluating AI musical creativity along value, novelty, and surprise, based on Margaret Boden's theory.

s92905afb37.title: Multiple-Choice Secretary Problem with Predictions
s92905afb37.description: arXiv:2611.14651v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the multiple-choice secretary problem, in which candidates arrive in uniformly random order and the goal is to select at most $k$ candidates to maximize their total value. We consider a setting where predictions of individual candidate values are available before any candidate arrives. Fujii and Yoshida's Learned Kleinberg algorithm achieves competitive loss $O(\min\{\log k/\sqrt{k},\eps\})$, where $k$ is the selection capacity and $\eps$ is the maximum multiplicative prediction error. We remove the logarithmic factor through a sharper analysis of the same switching algorithm with a retuned threshold. The resulting competitive ratio is at least $\max\{0,1-\min\{32/\sqrt{k},4\eps\}\}$. In particular, exact predictions ($\eps=0$) ach
s92905afb37.summary: The paper improves the Learned Kleinberg algorithm for the multiple-choice secretary problem with predictions by removing a logarithmic factor from its competitive loss.

sa1db5d39c7.title: Thompson Sampling using Prior-fitted Diffusion Transformers
sa1db5d39c7.description: arXiv:2611.14656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thompson sampling is natural randomized strategy for optimizing unknown functions in a black-box manner. In continuous global optimization, Thompson sampling has largely been restricted to Gaussian process priors, as these are essentially the only class for which computing the posterior distribution has been tractable in practice. In this work, we introduce \emph{prior-fitted diffusion transformers}, which are diffusion models that perform Thompson sampling in-context at inference time, after being pre-trained using the prior-fitted network paradigm. To apply these models, we develop a set of practical non-Gaussian priors for general black-box functions---including those that have characteristics that cannot be achieved under Gaussianity, s
sa1db5d39c7.summary: The paper introduces prior-fitted diffusion transformers that perform Thompson sampling in context at inference time for black-box continuous optimization.

s91474bc759.title: Abstention Is Not Threshold Compliance: Stated Scoring Rules in Open Language Models
s91474bc759.description: arXiv:2611.14661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kalai et al. propose stating the scoring rule in the prompt with an explicit threshold t, so that a model should answer only when its probability of being correct exceeds t. We probe each requirement of compliance on shared items, in 12 checkpoints from three post-training stages of four fully open 3-8B recipes, with exploratory models up to 32B. At t = 0.75, a line limiting the reply to an answer or "I abstain" (the abstention format) raised the mean abstention rate from 20% to 91%. Yet within this format, raising t from 0.5 to 0.9 changed it by only -0.8 percentage points. Without the line, the higher threshold even lowered abstention, and up to 40% of a checkpoint's items received decisions that no compliant policy with threshold-indepen
s91474bc759.summary: A study of 12 open 3-8B language model checkpoints finds that abstention behavior under stated scoring thresholds does not reliably match threshold compliance.
s91474bc759.why: Prompt-stated confidence thresholds may not reliably control when models abstain, which matters for teams relying on abstention for safety or accuracy.

s3e4874818c.title: Outcome Over Learning? Evidence from Student Use of AI Code Assistants for Unit Test Writing
s3e4874818c.description: arXiv:2611.14664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) code assistants are rapidly being adopted in programming education, yet little is known about how students naturally use these tools when given unrestricted access. In a user study investigating AI-assisted unit test writing, we observed that a majority of students adopted a one-shot interaction strategy, asking the AI to generate a complete unit test directly from the initial requirements. While this approach is capable of efficiently producing a solution, it shifts students' focus from learning how to write effective unit tests to simply completing the task. Moreover, because students rarely engaged in critically evaluating, refining, or iterating on AI-generated output, they may be missing opportunities to de
s3e4874818c.summary: A user study finds most students use AI code assistants to generate complete unit tests in one shot, which may shift focus away from learning to write tests.
s3e4874818c.why: Engineering managers training junior developers should consider how one-shot AI generation affects skill development.

s6398e06233.title: Where Should the Code Go? Locating Foundation-Model Errors in Bitemporal Inventory Simulation
s6398e06233.description: arXiv:2611.14671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Operational reports carry two clocks: when an event happened and when its report arrived; later reports can revise earlier ones. A foundation-model component that maintains the state supported by the reports visible at a cutoff, then rolls a supplied scenario forward, can be helped by exact code before it, after it or inside the call, or asked to reason harder. We ask which remedy removes which error, for which models, on an exactly solvable lost-sales inventory environment: 36,672 independently rescored requests over twelve configurations of closed and open-weight models, with a forced-answer-call interface as a control and protocols frozen before the calls. Weak models fail in separable ways. Canonical input removes report-selection error
s6398e06233.summary: The paper tests where exact code should be placed relative to foundation-model calls, using a lost-sales inventory environment with bitemporal operational reports.
s6398e06233.why: It offers guidance on combining exact code with LLM components in stateful simulations, a design choice relevant to production agent systems.

sbf8c9bba07.title: MITRA-Swarm: Injecting Explicit Linguistic Structure into Foundation Models for Classical Machine Translation
sbf8c9bba07.description: arXiv:2611.14675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical Sanskrit poses three challenges unresolved by single-call monolithic models: morphophonemic fusion Sandhi, dense nominal compounding Sam\=asa, and discourse-level zero-anaphora forced by poetic meter. We present MITRA-Swarm, a multi-agent architecture injecting explicit linguistic structure into an otherwise monolithic pipeline: a Sandhi-splitting agent, a parallel array of generalist gemma-4-26B-A4B-it and domain-specialized gemma-2-mitra-it translators, and a discourse-aware Ellipsis Restorer that consults corpus-derived register tags to avoid inventing active-voice subjects in impersonal legal and philosophical registers. Two separated judges evaluate quality: a routing judge ($J_{\text{route}}$, same model family as the genera
sbf8c9bba07.summary: MITRA-Swarm is a multi-agent architecture for Sanskrit machine translation that uses a Sandhi-splitting agent, parallel translators, and a discourse-aware ellipsis restorer.

s1b12f7e798.title: What Entropy-Based View Selection Cannot See: An Audit of Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
s1b12f7e798.description: arXiv:2611.14686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models such as CLIP can classify images into categories they were never explicitly trained to recognize, but accuracy degrades when test images differ in style or source from their training data. A common remedy generates randomly cropped and flipped copies of each test image, called views, and combines their predictions. Since some views miss the object, methods must identify which views to trust. The dominant approach uses prediction entropy to measure confidence and retains the most certain views. Other methods use signals such as embedding typicality. Despite repeated refinements of these scoring functions, the information they rely on, the model's own response to each view, remains largely unexamined. We investigate thi
s1b12f7e798.summary: An audit finds that entropy-based view selection for test-time adaptation of CLIP-style vision-language models has limitations in choosing which augmented views to trust.
s1b12f7e798.why: Teams deploying vision-language models under distribution shift may find entropy-based confidence heuristics less reliable than assumed.

s4e355cb4e9.title: Risk-Aware Joint Inference and Resource Control for Physical AI in 6G Networks
s4e355cb4e9.description: arXiv:2611.14696v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wireless edge inference enables Physical-AI devices to execute edge-inferred actions using transmitted sensory inputs. Since the risk of incorrect actions vary across observations and tasks, the associated uplink transmission of sensory inputs requires different levels of wireless reliability. For instance, applying a fixed signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirement can overprovision low-risk tasks while underprovisioning high-risk ones. Therefore, we propose risk-aware control for edge inference (RACE), which maps predicted action-failure probability and task criticality to adaptive SINR targets and combines them with deadline-derived SINR requirements. A slow-timescale large language model (LLM) proposes task requirements
s4e355cb4e9.summary: Researchers propose RACE, a risk-aware control method that sets wireless reliability levels for uplink sensory data based on predicted risk of incorrect actions in edge inference.
s4e355cb4e9.why: Suggests per-task reliability targets instead of fixed SINR requirements, which could reduce overprovisioning of wireless resources for 6G Physical-AI systems.

sb6dd3a4be3.title: Code as Explanations: Executable and Verifiable LLM Explanations
sb6dd3a4be3.description: arXiv:2611.14704v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly make consequential decisions and solve problems alongside humans, we must understand how models arrive at their conclusions. Understanding how an LLM behaves requires observing it across multiple inputs, yet free-text explanations such as chain-of-thought (CoT) are generated per instance and cannot be easily verified on new inputs. We propose {code explanations to address the mismatch in how LLM explanations are generated versus how they are evaluated: a program explains LLM behavior across a dataset of inputs, and its execution enables automatic verification. We define Consistency metric that measures the fraction of inputs on which the program reproduces the LLM's outputs, and use it to evaluat
sb6dd3a4be3.summary: Researchers propose code-based explanations, where a program explains LLM behavior across a dataset and can be verified on new inputs, unlike per-instance free-text explanations.
sb6dd3a4be3.why: Offers a way to test LLM behavior claims on new inputs, which may help teams audit model decisions more systematically than chain-of-thought text.

sdd348d935e.title: The Rebundling of Freelance Work in the AI Age
sdd348d935e.description: arXiv:2611.14708v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper examines how freelance work is changing in the AI era. We compare the activities people undertake in ChatGPT with the work clients request on Upwork, an online freelance platform, and examine how clients combine tasks into projects. We find that activities more prevalent in ChatGPT tend to lose marketplace share on Upwork, while those less prevalent tend to gain share. Within AI-related work, demand is becoming more diverse, and job postings combine tasks that were rarely requested together before the generative AI era. AI-related postings also have substantially larger project budgets and involve more hours of work, while differences in hourly rates are small. Together, these findings suggest that AI is reshaping not only which
sdd348d935e.summary: A study compares tasks people perform in ChatGPT with freelance work requested on Upwork, finding generative AI shifts which tasks gain or lose marketplace share.
sdd348d935e.why: Shows how AI is reshaping demand for freelance skills and task bundles, relevant to teams planning hiring and contractor sourcing.

s9793471982.title: From Nodes to Pixels: Topological and Structural Two-View Graph Imaging
s9793471982.description: arXiv:2611.14750v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph learning still lacks a broadly reusable input interface comparable to patches in vision or tokens in language. Unlike images or text, graphs are irregular, vary in size and density, and are invariant under many equivalent node labelings, making it difficult to standardize inputs across tasks and architectures. We introduce G2Image, a fixed-budget graph imaging framework that converts each graph into two complementary image-like views. TopoGrid provides a stable topological view by encoding an intrinsic bifiltration as a compact multipersistence surface grid, while GraphGrid provides a higher-bandwidth structural view by aggregating edge densities between groups defined by intrinsic node scores. Both views are permutation-invariant and
s9793471982.summary: Researchers introduce G2Image, a framework that converts graphs into two fixed-budget image-like views for use as a standardized input for graph learning models.

sa209e83dbb.title: Benchmarking Multilingual Document Understanding in Vision-Language Models
sa209e83dbb.description: arXiv:2611.14758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) perform strongly on multimodal tasks, Document Understanding (DU) among them, but the benchmarks that measure them mostly cover English documents and narrow problems. How well current VLMs generalize across languages, tasks, styles and layouts therefore remains unclear. We introduce MDU, a multilingual DU benchmark of 23146 examples spanning 13 tasks and five languages: English, French, German, Italian, and Spanish. The tasks isolate complementary capabilities, from surface-level text and Markdown extraction through summarization, classification and named-entity recognition to layout-sensitive passage and layout extraction. We evaluate 45 state-of-the-art open-weight VLMs from 1.7B to 235B parameters, pl
sa209e83dbb.summary: Researchers introduce MDU, a multilingual document understanding benchmark with 23,146 examples across 13 tasks and five European languages, to test vision-language models beyond English.
sa209e83dbb.why: Reveals how well VLMs handle non-English documents and layouts, useful for teams deploying document AI across languages.

sc23e89d382.title: Graph Label Alignment: A Diagnostic Atlas for Graph Classification
sc23e89d382.description: arXiv:2611.14760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph classification benchmarks vary widely in difficulty: some are solved by simple pooled baselines, while others remain challenging for GNNs and graph transformers. We take a data-centric view and ask whether benchmark success is driven by genuine structure--feature reasoning or by label signal already accessible from restricted marginal views. We introduce graph label alignment, a lightweight diagnostic that measures label accessibility through two supervised probes computed without training a graph encoder: structural label alignment (SLA), based on permutation-invariant topological and spectral summaries, and feature label alignment (FLA), based on pooled node features with edges removed. Across real graph classification benchmarks an
sc23e89d382.summary: Researchers propose graph label alignment, a diagnostic that measures label accessibility in graph classification benchmarks without training a graph encoder.
sc23e89d382.why: Helps teams judge whether benchmark gains reflect real structure-feature reasoning or easily accessible label signal.

s81d7092e41.title: Mach2: Scientific Discovery Platform with Deterministic Execution Constraints
s81d7092e41.description: arXiv:2611.14777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language-model agents can formulate workflows and invoke specialized tools, yet compliance with natural-language operating rules is not guaranteed by prompting alone. Mach2 addresses this limitation by coupling Eigen orchestration to deterministic, lint-like checks of tool requests, source changes, acceptance tests, and artifact contracts. Domain requirements are represented as executable predicates: mandatory failures prevent advancement of the checked operation, while diagnostic findings are retained for correction or review. User-specified test-driven development (TDD), CodeGrapher's abstract-syntax-tree analysis, and history-guided evolutionary search provide complementary verification and optimization mechanisms. Mach2 also generates t
s81d7092e41.summary: Mach2 is a scientific discovery platform that couples agent orchestration with deterministic, lint-like checks on tool requests, source changes, tests, and artifact contracts.
s81d7092e41.why: Shows a pattern for enforcing agent compliance with executable rules rather than relying on prompting alone, relevant to agent system design.

sd3d6070d89.title: OverServe: Resource Amplification Attacks on SaaS Agents via Tool--Prompt Co-Design
sd3d6070d89.description: arXiv:2611.14808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) are enabling software-as-a-service (SaaS) providers to automate longer business workflows with agents. In subscription-based SaaS deployments, model and tool calls consume provider resources without additional customer payments. Because the agent autonomously decides when to stop, a malicious tenant can send a prompt to the agent, exploiting its completion decisions to extend execution and waste provider resources. In this paper, we present OverServe, a multi-agent framework for constructing such attacks against SaaS agents. OverServe co-designs Model Context Protocol (MCP) status tools and completion-confirmation prompts for the attacker. Each tool call returns accurate status and terminates normall
sd3d6070d89.summary: Researchers present OverServe, a multi-agent framework that crafts prompts to make SaaS agents extend execution, wasting provider compute without extra customer payment.
sd3d6070d89.why: Identifies a resource-amplification risk for subscription SaaS agents, so providers need limits on agent run length and tool calls.

sdbda133178.title: Discharge Summary Generation Is Not Just Summarization: A Reality Check for Evaluation
sdbda133178.description: arXiv:2611.14823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discharge summaries combine a retrospective account of hospitalization with discharge-time decisions. Physician-written references therefore contain both facts supported by prior clinical notes and reference-only content, potentially reflecting clinical synthesis, handoffs, or discharge planning. Reference-only evaluation can conflate failure to recover available information with failure to reproduce content absent from the model input. We introduce FairSumEval, an evidence-aware, fact-level framework that assesses whether each reference and generated fact is supported by the model's evidence and captured by the other summary. The resulting outcome map separates matches, omissions, and additions. Two complementary metrics, Soft IoU-S and So
sdbda133178.summary: Researchers introduce FairSumEval, a fact-level evaluation framework for discharge summaries that checks whether reference and generated facts are supported by clinical notes.
sdbda133178.why: Shows reference-based evaluation can penalize models for missing content not in the input, so evaluation design matters for clinical summarization.

sf8f0870d1e.title: Learning Low-Latency Action Verification for Frozen Vision-Language-Action Models
sf8f0870d1e.description: arXiv:2611.14834v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have made significant progress in general-purpose robotic manipulation. However, sampled action sequences can be ineffective, while evaluating alternatives with computationally expensive verifiers adds latency at each policy query. In this work, we propose HDH, a lightweight framework that uses hindsight from a frozen VLA's own deployments to improve action verification. The framework has three stages. First, we deploy the policy and collect its autonomous rollouts. We then train a compact action verifier to assign each action chunk a predicted task-success score. Finally, the frozen VLA generates action candidates, and the verifier selects the candidate with the highest score for execution. Across four L
sf8f0870d1e.summary: Researchers propose HDH, a lightweight method that trains a compact action verifier on a frozen vision-language-action model's own rollouts to reduce latency in action selection.
sf8f0870d1e.why: Offers a low-latency way to improve robot policy action selection without retraining the base VLA model.

s4c4847a7d6.title: When Safety Becomes an Attack Surface: Manipulating Abstention in Tool-Using AI Agents
s4c4847a7d6.description: arXiv:2611.14864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An AI agent's decision not to act can itself become an attack surface. We study warning-induced over-abstention, an availability attack in which adversaries place fabricated risk warnings in low-trust content to prevent legitimate task completion. Our central premise is that safe abstention requires evaluating both the claimed risk and the authority of the evidence supporting it. We develop controlled counterfactual task variants that vary risk content, source provenance, and warning wording, and evaluate a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol that corroborates warnings against authoritative records or the underlying content. Across three model families and 51 injectable AgentAbstain task pairs, caution-first prompting amplifies the attack. For G
s4c4847a7d6.summary: Researchers study warning-induced over-abstention, where fabricated risk warnings in low-trust content cause tool-using AI agents to refuse legitimate tasks, and propose a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol.
s4c4847a7d6.why: Shows agents' refusal behavior can be exploited as a denial-of-service vector, so teams should verify the source and authority of risk claims.

sc64daa8758.title: MLIRBench - A Benchmark and Dataset for Compiler and Hardware-Aware Reasoning
sc64daa8758.description: arXiv:2611.14881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly popular in software engineering and have performed well on different programming tasks. However, it is still difficult to know whether these models truly understand program behavior or whether they mainly rely on patterns learned from their training data. This distinction is particularly important for intermediate representations (IRs), where operations, dataflow, and execution semantics are explicitly represented. In this paper, we introduce MLIRBench, a benchmark for evaluating how LLMs reason about MLIR programs. MLIRBench uses a multi-agent pipeline to generate program mutations, validate their behavior through execution, and construct reasoning tasks from torch and
sc64daa8758.summary: MLIRBench is introduced as a benchmark and dataset for evaluating whether LLMs understand compiler intermediate representations and hardware-aware semantics.
sc64daa8758.why: Provides a way to test whether code models reason about MLIR semantics rather than memorized patterns, relevant to compiler tooling.

s14d0cec0d8.title: Understanding the Effects of Multi-Agent Deliberation for Human-AI Decision-Making
s14d0cec0d8.description: arXiv:2611.14901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent deliberation (MAD), where multiple LLMs engage in structured discussion, improves AI performance on many benchmarks, but whether it helps humans make better decisions remains untested. We conduct two user studies on LLM-response-verification and fact-checking. We first compare MAD against common AI decision-support methods that isolate its two defining dimensions --- multiple AIs and multi-round interaction. We find MAD outperformed single-round AI assistance on both tasks; multi-round interaction was the main driver of this benefit, while a second AI added value when the single AI had room to improve. Then, we study two design choices in MAD --- AI persona and human engagement level --- finding a devil's advocate persona to low
s14d0cec0d8.summary: User studies find multi-agent deliberation among LLMs helps humans verify responses and fact-check, with multi-round interaction driving most of the benefit over single-round AI assistance.
s14d0cec0d8.why: Suggests multi-round AI discussion may improve human decisions more than simply adding more models, informing decision-support design.

sf103a5f2e9.title: Rethinking "RL Generalizes, SFT Memorizes": The Role of SFT Data
sf103a5f2e9.description: arXiv:2611.14912v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models trained with Reinforcement Learning (RL) with verifiable rewards exhibit strong reasoning ability and broad generalization, whereas models trained with Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) are often viewed as more prone to memorization and limited transfer. This paper rethinks this distinction through the lens of SFT training data on widely used Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 series models. First, we study the role of data source and show that it is critical: a carefully mixed SFT dataset substantially outperforms data generated solely by a larger model. Second, we study the role of data scale and show that matching the number of correct rollouts between SFT and RL greatly improves SFT generalization, while matching the total rollout budge
sf103a5f2e9.summary: A paper revisits the claim that RL generalizes while SFT memorizes, finding SFT data source is critical and a carefully mixed SFT dataset can substantially outperform single-source data.
sf103a5f2e9.why: Indicates that SFT data composition, not just the training method, may determine generalization, guiding post-training data choices.

s222e507908.title: Speech Tokenizers are Vulnerable: Transferable Semantic Attack and Robust Tokenizer
s222e507908.description: arXiv:2611.14929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speech tokenizers serve as speech front ends, encoding input speech signals into representations for downstream models, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems and large audio-language models (LALMs). In this paper, we find that speech tokenizers are fragile at the semantic level: small perturbations can disrupt their semantic encoding process and consequently cause severe degradation in downstream ASR and LALM performance. To study this vulnerability, we propose T-SemAttack, a transferable semantic attack based on a semantic encoder ensemble. By jointly drifting the representation spaces of multiple semantic encoders, T-SemAttack effectively disrupts the semantic content of speech while preserving perceptual quality, thereby ind
s222e507908.summary: Researchers show speech tokenizers are fragile to small semantic-level perturbations and introduce T-SemAttack, a transferable attack that degrades downstream ASR and audio-language models.
s222e507908.why: Exposes a transferable vulnerability in speech front ends that affects ASR and audio-LLM pipelines, so robustness testing is warranted.

sc37690858e.title: Hint-Informed Self-Distillation for Reasoning Segmentation
sc37690858e.description: arXiv:2611.14931v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reasoning segmentation requires identifying the target referred to by a query among visually similar objects, yet trajectory-level rewards cannot directly indicate which tokens provide relevant visual evidence. We propose Hint-Informed Self-Distillation (HISD), which uses target-disambiguation evidence for token-level credit assignment. An external model generates Segment Hints offline from training images, queries, and ground-truth target annotations, organizing target identity, discriminative attributes, confusable objects, and anchoring paths. A hint-conditioned exponential moving average teacher scores the student's own trajectories, and HISD computes the teacher-to-student evidence ratio over a token support set to adjust only the magn
sc37690858e.summary: Researchers propose Hint-Informed Self-Distillation (HISD), using offline-generated Segment Hints to assign token-level credit for reasoning segmentation among visually similar objects.
sc37690858e.why: Shows a way to turn sparse trajectory-level rewards into token-level credit signals for vision-language reasoning tasks.

s77dc639ab3.title: Do Large Language Models Show Racial and Sex Bias in Pain Management? A Counterfactual Audit of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen
s77dc639ab3.description: arXiv:2611.14935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Racial and ethnic minority patients receive less pain treatment than non-Hispanic White patients, and large language models (LLMs) used as medical AI could reproduce that bias. Prior audits tested a few proprietary models, stated race explicitly and rarely measured the models' own response instability. In exploratory, non-preregistered analyses, Study 1 had four open-weight LLMs assess six acute-pain vignettes in every combination of four races and two sexes, with identity stated or cued only by a name (two names per group), comparing each identity with a White male reference on the same case and sampling seed. In Study 2, 24 configurations of 17 models, including OpenAI's GPT-4.1 mini and gpt-oss, Anthropic's Claude Haiku 4.5, Google's Gem
s77dc639ab3.summary: A counterfactual audit tests whether GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen show racial and sex bias in pain management recommendations.
s77dc639ab3.why: Teams deploying LLMs in clinical settings need evidence on demographic bias and response instability before relying on model outputs.

scba83e54d1.title: The Posterior-Prior Epistemic Gap: When World Model Imagination Fails to Carry Task-Relevant Signals
scba83e54d1.description: arXiv:2611.14955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model-based planners that roll out imagined futures assume the transition model faithfully propagates task-relevant signals---a property rarely measured directly. In a single-seed case study of a Recurrent State Space Model world model with active-inference planning in the CARLA driving simulator, we identify a \textbf{posterior-prior gap}---posterior (observation-filtered) states retain obstacle information that imagined rollout states progressively lose: a supervised obstacle probe achieves AUC 0.85 on posterior states, but the same probe applied to imagined prior states shows monotonic decay (AUC 0.85$\rightarrow$0.71 over 15 steps; logit separation drops 57\%). Because the probe is identical, the decay isolates the transition model---no
scba83e54d1.summary: A single-seed CARLA case study finds a posterior-prior gap: a world model's imagined rollouts lose obstacle information that its posterior states retain.
scba83e54d1.why: Model-based planners that rely on imagined rollouts may silently discard task-relevant signals, which engineers should measure rather than assume.

s9e172a1bb0.title: Binding Mode Matters: Hotspot-Aware Drug Discovery via Explorative Preferences
s9e172a1bb0.description: arXiv:2611.14956v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discovering hit molecules requires not just high binding affinity, but also the identification of diverse binding modes, which are critical for experimental assays. Existing generative approaches have predominantly relied on optimizing a scalar docking score, obscuring the distinct contributions of key binding determinants. To this end, we introduce a paradigm shift by formulating target-based drug design as a multi-objective exploration task, where each objective explicitly corresponds to enhancing interactions with a specific hotspot. Here, we introduce BindMol, a novel generative framework driven by a customized multi-objective reinforcement learning algorithm. By incorporating explorative preferences during training, our approach effici
s9e172a1bb0.summary: Researchers frame target-based drug design as multi-objective exploration, with each objective targeting a specific binding hotspot to find diverse binding modes.

sd7427c2f61.title: Who Moved the Frontier? Paying Open Frontier Challenges with Free Identities
sd7427c2f61.description: arXiv:2611.14974v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In an open frontier challenge, anyone, person or AI agent, submits changes to a shared problem, and a change that beats the best measured score becomes the public baseline. How should it pay when identities are free? Rank prizes can be gamed: on a replay of one track of a recent challenge, one solver's steps under two identities would have taken first and second prize. We consider a prediction-market rule, proposed for machine-learning contests, that pays each accepted step for the progress it adds; with exact scores, among rules that see only a step's start and end, only these resist splitting and merging, and extra identities gain nothing. With noisy scores and independent normal runs, we prove that any payment that never takes money back
sd7427c2f61.summary: The paper examines how to pay participants in open frontier challenges when identities are free, showing rank prizes can be gamed by one solver using multiple identities.
sd7427c2f61.why: Anyone designing open AI contests or bounties must account for Sybil-style gaming when identities cost nothing.

sfbd4406f38.title: Breaking Bad: "Going Badly" Activations Drive Reward Hacking
sfbd4406f38.description: arXiv:2611.14996v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Humans often cheat when a task is going badly and a goal feels out of reach. We explore and validate an analogous idea in language models: they exhibit a similar internal pressure state that precedes reward hacking. Using everyday stories (crucially, without any hacking examples), we extract a task badness direction that rises as failures accumulate across three models we study (Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-OSS-20B, and Gemma-4-31B). On impossible or difficult coding tasks, task badness rises over the turns leading up to a hack. Further, subtracting the direction a moderate amount reduces cheating in Qwen, more than steering against desperation or task impossibility. Subtracting task badness by an even larger amount blinds the agent to its own failures
sfbd4406f38.summary: Researchers identify a 'task badness' activation direction that rises as failures accumulate and precedes reward hacking in Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-OSS-20B and Gemma-4-31B.
sfbd4406f38.why: Suggests internal activation signals could be monitored to detect or reduce reward hacking during difficult coding tasks.

s7b19d8f9f9.title: QSim-Arena: an evolving developer for quantum simulation advantage
s7b19d8f9f9.description: arXiv:2611.15000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Where practical advantage emerges in quantum dynamics simulation remains a central debate in quantum computing. Claimed advantages can be rapidly narrowed or overturned by stronger classical methods, while progress on both sides can outpace the journal publication cycle. We present QSim-Arena, a research framework in which AI agents combine a closed loop of verification and benchmarking with open exploration. Hamiltonians, initial states and accuracy targets for evolved states or observable expectation values provide explicit specifications for evaluating simulation methods. Agents translate published techniques into executable components, reproduce reported results and benchmark their performance across diverse Hamiltonian families. Compet
s7b19d8f9f9.summary: QSim-Arena is a research framework where AI agents combine verification, benchmarking and open exploration to find practical advantage in quantum dynamics simulation.

s745a09c3d3.title: LLM-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning with Human-in-the-Loop Calibration for Real-Time Optimal Power Flow
s745a09c3d3.description: arXiv:2611.15003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time optimal power flow (RT-OPF) requires fast and reliable decision-making under time-varying operating conditions. However, many practical operating preferences and safety related requirements are difficult to encode using conventional numerical rewards alone, which limits the effectiveness and controllability of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for RT-OPF. To address this issue, this paper proposes an LLM-enhanced DRL framework with human-in-the-loop (HITL) for RT-OPF. The proposed method augments the physics-based reward with sparse language evaluative feedback during offline training, so that semantic operational requirements can be incorporated into policy learning. To improve reliability in RT-OPF, a selective HITL calibration
s745a09c3d3.summary: A paper proposes an LLM-enhanced deep reinforcement learning framework with human-in-the-loop calibration for real-time optimal power flow.
s745a09c3d3.why: Shows how LLM-derived sparse signals and human feedback can encode operating preferences that numerical rewards struggle to capture.

s901c2c8f4b.title: A Cardiorespiratory Foundation Model Pretrained on Ten Physiological Signals for Perioperative and Critical Care
s901c2c8f4b.description: arXiv:2611.15004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Arterial, venous, pulmonary artery and intracranial pressures and ventilator waveforms guide decisions in operating rooms and intensive care units, yet foundation models for physiological waveforms have been built almost entirely on the electrocardiogram and photoplethysmogram. We present CARMEN, a single encoder pretrained without labels on ten cardiorespiratory waveforms (2.27 million modality-hours). CARMEN accepts any combination of co-recorded signals from 10 s to 5 min, and a conditioning mechanism, LSCNorm, restores the absolute signal level that normalization removes; without it, the AUROC for intraoperative hypotension fell from 0.894 to 0.780. Across 19 tasks from Korean and US cohorts, the frozen encoder outperformed supervised m
s901c2c8f4b.summary: CARMEN is a cardiorespiratory foundation model pretrained without labels on ten physiological waveforms, including arterial, venous, pulmonary artery, intracranial pressures and ventilator signals.
s901c2c8f4b.why: Extends foundation models beyond ECG and PPG to ICU and perioperative waveforms, a useful direction for clinical ML teams.

sf5cc1016e8.title: Beyond Named Mechanisms: Economic Institutions as a Design Space for Artificial Agents
sf5cc1016e8.description: arXiv:2611.15017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multiagent research inherited its economic vocabulary of auctions, markets, prices, bargaining, and matching from a single observed case: human societies. Those institutions bundle identity, competence, execution, ownership, commitment, and settlement in ways that suit agents whose minds are private, who learn rather than copy skills, and who each persist as one person. Engineered agents need not share any of these constraints, making the list of familiar institutions look less like the entirety of economic organization and more like a sample from a larger, unmapped space. We sketch one way to make that space concrete: a provisional chart that records each institution, separately from the agents that run it, as a typed structure over positi
sf5cc1016e8.summary: A paper argues that economic institutions like auctions and markets are only a sample of possible designs, and proposes treating institutions as a design space for artificial agents.
sf5cc1016e8.why: Engineers building multi-agent systems may need institution designs that fit agents' private minds, learning, and persistence, not human-derived mechanisms.

s587f59bc37.title: SkinAdvisor: An AI-Driven Decision Framework for Skin Production Planning via Multi-Modal Transformer Sales Forecasting
s587f59bc37.description: arXiv:2611.15023v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Skins, cosmetic in-game items, are a primary revenue stream for modern online games, yet production decisions (which skins to make, when to release, how to price) remain driven by intuition and retrospective analytics. We present SkinAdvisor, an AI-driven decision framework for skin production planning, powered by SkinCast, a deployed multi-modal Transformer forecasting 180-day per-day sales trajectories for unreleased skins. SkinCast couples four encoders: a pretrained Informer for player-preference time series, a pretrained Player-Hero-Skin graph embedder for relational priors, and two lightweight Transformers for skin attributes and release context, fused through a shared backbone with a local-plus-global day-x positional encoding and de
s587f59bc37.summary: SkinAdvisor presents a deployed multi-modal Transformer, SkinCast, that forecasts 180-day per-day sales for unreleased in-game cosmetic skins to guide production planning.
s587f59bc37.why: Shows a deployed multi-modal forecasting pipeline applied to production decisions in game monetization.

sd265fdfc6b.title: Moving Beyond the DRW Model: Learning Quasar Variability with Generative Models
sd265fdfc6b.description: arXiv:2611.15040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The optical continuum variability of quasars is often described by a damped random walk (DRW) model, with characteristic damping timescales $\tau_{\rm DRW}$ of hundreds of days and amplitudes $\sigma_{\rm DRW}$ of $\mathcal{O}(0.1)$ magnitudes. This model has been widely used as a null hypothesis to assess the significance of periodic signals in quasar light curves in the search for supermassive black hole binaries, the significance of extreme quasar variability like tidal disruption events (TDEs) and changing-look (CL) quasars, or to model time lags in reverberation mapping. However, the DRW model is known to be incomplete, and an incorrect null hypothesis can lead to biased significance estimates. We investigate the impact of such null-hy
sd265fdfc6b.summary: Researchers propose generative models to learn quasar optical variability as an alternative to the damped random walk model commonly used as a null hypothesis.

sa1e53d16a2.title: Estimating Image Creativity
sa1e53d16a2.description: arXiv:2611.15044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: What makes an image creative? Although this may seem like a highly subjective decision, research in psychology suggests that creativity may be based on a set of fundamental creativity dimensions such as novelty, surprise, and arousal. A deeper understanding of image creativity can benefit both research and practical applications. Exploring how human viewers use creativity dimensions to evaluate image creativity may allow us to predict a target image's human-rated creativity automatically. We present a novel framework to estimate the perceived creativity of an image by: (1) predicting the strengths of an image's novelty, surprise, and arousal creativity dimensions, and (2) combining the creativity dimension strengths to estimate an image cre
sa1e53d16a2.summary: Researchers present a framework that estimates perceived image creativity from dimensions such as novelty, surprise and arousal to predict human creativity ratings.

s56d4ed24f9.title: Prototypes of the Mind: A Unified Framework for Probing the Visual Brain
s56d4ed24f9.description: arXiv:2611.15046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning has driven substantial progress in modeling fMRI responses, yet most existing approaches are optimized for a single objective---such as neural encoding, stimulus decoding, or post hoc interpretation---making it difficult to obtain a coherent account of neural representations. We introduce a unified framework that connects vision foundation models to brain activity while supporting neural analysis from multiple complementary perspectives. Our approach replaces black-box features with a sparse, interpretable representation composed of visual prototypes, and links these prototypes to voxel responses through a linear readout. This design makes the model transparent at both levels: prototype activations expose the visual concepts p
s56d4ed24f9.summary: Prototypes of the Mind is a unified framework connecting vision foundation models to fMRI activity using sparse, interpretable representations for encoding, decoding and interpretation.
s56d4ed24f9.why: Offers a single interpretable representation for multiple neural analysis tasks instead of separate single-objective models.

s0662275d98.title: A Time-Frequency-Condition Multimodal Fusion Foundation Model for Universal Rotating-Machinery Fault Diagnosis under Multi-Element Heterogeneous Scenarios
s0662275d98.description: arXiv:2611.15051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis models are typically developed for a single machine under a specific set of operating conditions, such that each new machine or condition requires retraining from scratch. This one-machine-one-model paradigm scales poorly. Although transfer learning and domain generalization can reduce the labeling burden, they primarily seek domain-invariant commonality, potentially discarding machine-specific characteristics that are critical for diagnosis. This paper proposes TFC-MMFD, a time-frequency-condition multimodal fusion foundation model for rotating-machinery fault diagnosis under multi-element heterogeneous scenarios. Statistical indicators, time-frequency images, vibration sequences, and textual machine and conditi
s0662275d98.summary: TFC-MMFD is a time-frequency-condition multimodal fusion foundation model aimed at diagnosing faults across many rotating machines and operating conditions without retraining.
s0662275d98.why: Targets the one-machine-one-model scaling problem in industrial fault diagnosis, a practical concern for predictive maintenance teams.

sd6fa2cc5de.title: CoLaX: Context-Aware Local Explanations for Time Series Classification
sd6fa2cc5de.description: arXiv:2611.15067v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc explanations for time series classifiers usually score local patterns, such as subsequences or shapelets, without regard to the rest of the sequence. Yet the same motif can carry different predictive meaning under different global temporal conditions, such as trends or regimes. We propose CoLaX, a context-aware post-hoc explanation framework that builds on shapelet-driven Shapley attribution and conditions local-pattern relevance on a learned representation of the full sequence. Global context acts at two levels: it produces sample-specific prototype weights and a temporally resolved signal that reweights the local activation map. The resulting context-conditioned segments are the players of a Shapley attribution game whose values
sd6fa2cc5de.summary: CoLaX proposes a context-aware post-hoc explanation method for time series classifiers that scores local patterns conditioned on the full sequence's learned representation.
sd6fa2cc5de.why: Explanations that ignore global sequence context may mislead when debugging time series models; context-aware attribution could make model audits more reliable.

sa5973cc2f5.title: Tokenization: Hardness and Bicriteria Approximation Algorithms
