s7ceca5cb62.summary: DuoJEPA trains separate self-supervised encoders per modality and adds a translation layer so embeddings can be mapped across unaligned spaces for retrieval and classification.
s7ceca5cb62.why: It suggests cross-modal tasks may not require aligning encoder embedding spaces, which could change how multimodal systems are built.

sf09c9ad79f.title: What Roles Do System Prompts Really Assign? Validating and Steering Occupational Role Vectors in LLMs
sf09c9ad79f.description: arXiv:2611.15989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Applications built on large language models assign the model a role through its system prompt, intending to shape how it responds for their use case. We introduce a validation framework for extracting and injecting occupational role vectors, activation-level directions that capture how someone in a given occupational role would distinctively respond to a task or question. We validate these vectors through two complementary lenses, on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The interpretability lens asks whether each vector is a stable, separable, domain-consistent representation of its role: extracted vectors are highly reproducible across repeated runs and sampling temperatures, remain separable even for very similar roles, and agre
sf09c9ad79f.summary: Researchers introduce a framework to extract and inject occupational role vectors from system prompts, testing them on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
sf09c9ad79f.why: Steering model behavior through role vectors could help teams verify that system prompts actually shape model responses as intended.

s1e9f25e694.title: Fit-LRP: Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes for Neural Network Verification over Non-Convex Regions
s1e9f25e694.description: arXiv:2611.16003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: State-of-the-art neural network verifiers evaluate linear relaxations over axis-aligned bounding boxes. However, verification domains in cyber-physical systems are rarely boxes. Reachability specifications, obstacle-avoidance constraints, and neural Lyapunov certificates typically yield oblique or non-convex polyhedral regions, over which box-based bounds become extremely loose. This paper proposes Fit-LRP (Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes), a framework the implements exact optimization of affine bounds over non-convex domains (represented by unions of polytopes) by solving a sequence of small, low-dimensional linear programs. Our approach seamlessly enhances the final optimization step of LiRPA and $\alpha,\! \beta$-CROWN branch-and
s1e9f25e694.summary: Fit-LRP proposes exact optimization of affine bounds over non-convex polytope regions to tighten neural network verification beyond axis-aligned boxes.
s1e9f25e694.why: Tighter verification over realistic cyber-physical constraints could make safety certification of neural controllers more practical.

s472f6c53fd.title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
s472f6c53fd.description: arXiv:2611.16009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official
s472f6c53fd.summary: A controlled study dissects designs of GPT-6 robot-use agents on RoboDojo, testing harness, action interface, experience reuse, and scene geometry in one framework.
s472f6c53fd.why: Isolating which design choices drive gains helps engineers build robot agents without relying on confounded benchmark comparisons.

s6b43bb15a5.title: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
s6b43bb15a5.description: arXiv:2611.16010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language moved from many task-specific models to one unified model: a single generative model with a single generative training task that handles all of them within the same backbone, and keeps improving with data, parameters and compute. We believe the bitter lesson applies just as much to computer vision, 3D and spatial understanding, in the end to visual intelligence: the effort should go into general architectures that solve all these tasks in a unified way, and into scaling them, rather than into task-specific designs. We test this on monocular geometry, a task that has belonged to specialised architectures for years. Iris-Z is a general image generator that produces appearance and geometry together. A single backbone denoises, reasons
s6b43bb15a5.summary: Iris-Z proposes scaling a single generative model for vision, 3D, and spatial understanding instead of task-specific specialist models.
s6b43bb15a5.why: It argues for unified architectures over task-specific designs in computer vision, which could shape how vision systems are built and scaled.

s563f988ce4.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup
s563f988ce4.description: arXiv:2611.16013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Genetic Programming (GP) is a search paradigm inspired from natural evolution for the automated discovery of expressions, functions, and computer programs. Cartesian GP (CGP) is a flavor of GP that uses a graph-based model to encode candidate programs, as contrasted to the conventional Tree-based GP (TGP). Since its inception two decades ago, CGP has predominantly been analyzed empirically, thus little is known regarding its theoretical performance guarantees. This paper analyzes CGP for the Max problem, which has been only rigorously studied for TGP with a proven expected runtime superlinear in the optimal program length $n$. We prove that the expected time for the ($1$+$1$)~CGP employing common mutation operators to evolve an equivalent o
s563f988ce4.summary: A theoretical paper proves an exponential runtime speedup for Cartesian Genetic Programming on the Max problem, compared with prior analyses.
s563f988ce4.why: Formal runtime guarantees for CGP are rare, though the work is theoretical and its direct engineering impact is limited.

sca34db0112.title: Scaling public input on AI policy with pluralistic agents
sca34db0112.description: arXiv:2611.16028v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI is being deployed across a vast range of application domains, cultural environments, and human stakeholders. Safe and responsible AI development requires continuously accounting for diverse perspectives. We develop and test pluralistic agents, AI agent representatives that deliberate on behalf of individuals to align AI systems with diverse human perspectives. Pluralistic agents could help people contribute to many more discussions than they could directly participate in, on technical topics that would require training, and on policy choices that rely on private information that corporations and governments cannot readily share. Our experiments identify opportunities, risks, and perceptions of pluralistic agents. Agents were able to reli
sca34db0112.summary: Researchers develop pluralistic agents that deliberate on behalf of individuals to gather diverse public input on AI policy and alignment.
sca34db0112.why: Scalable public input mechanisms could inform how organizations incorporate diverse stakeholder perspectives into AI policy decisions.

sf127d3b04f.title: Pyramidal Columns Acting as Attention Heads
sf127d3b04f.description: arXiv:2611.16057v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can the functional architecture of a Transformer attention head be given a biological construction? More specifically, could a suitable group of pyramidal columns in posterior temporal language regions (PTLRs) constitute the biological construction of a neuromorphic mechanical realization of an attention head, under a mathematical instantiation that need not coincide with its standard Transformer instantiation? This paper investigates this hypothesis by examining possible correspondences between the functional organization of attention heads and neurophysiological mechanisms operating within and across pyramidal columns involved in human language processing. Our analysis builds on a mechanical-structural description of Transformer attention
sf127d3b04f.summary: A paper explores whether pyramidal columns in language regions of the brain could biologically realize a Transformer attention head.
sf127d3b04f.why: This is a theoretical neuroscience hypothesis with little direct bearing on engineering practice.

sac5a8d770e.title: Human Capital in Context: What Employment Survival Reveals About Worker-Firm Match
sac5a8d770e.description: arXiv:2611.16058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There is no best worker in general, only a best worker for a particular firm. We develop a measure of worker-firm match quality that treats fit as a property of the pair, learned from the survival of employment relationships. A two-tower neural network embeds workers, from their career histories and current positions, and firms, from their characteristics and business descriptions, into a common space, and match quality is the cosine similarity of the two vectors. The measure takes its functional form from the skill-weights model of firm-specific human capital, and its only estimated objective, a separation hazard, from the view of the job match as an experience good. Estimated on more than a billion person-periods covering 101 million work
sac5a8d770e.summary: Researchers propose a worker-firm match quality measure learned from employment survival, using a two-tower neural network over career histories and firm descriptions.
sac5a8d770e.why: Match-quality modeling could inform hiring and workforce analytics, though it raises fairness and privacy questions the summary does not address.

seab4410bf2.title: Tokenized Reward Systems for Federated Learning: The Privacy vs. Fairness Tradeoff
seab4410bf2.description: arXiv:2611.16065v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Federated learning (FL) systems increasingly rely on blockchain based reward mechanisms to incentivize participation while preserving data privacy. We design and empirically evaluate two complementary Solidity smart contracts for FL reward distribution: the first one that allocates rewards proportionally to a publicly disclosed quality score, and a privacy preserving variant that hides individual quality scores behind a zero-knowledge (ZK) proof of a threshold condition. Both contracts mint a non transferable, use-and-burn token maintaining a trustless incentive structure. We evaluate the two designs through MNIST training with adversarial behavior, including Sybil attacks, zero gradient and random noise, across three independent random see
seab4410bf2.summary: Researchers design and evaluate Solidity smart contracts for federated learning rewards, including a zero-knowledge variant that hides individual quality scores.
seab4410bf2.why: It shows a concrete tradeoff between privacy and fairness in incentive design for federated learning systems built on blockchain.

sc4a122493a.title: Agentic Computational Algebra
sc4a122493a.description: arXiv:2611.16073v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We explore the use of AI agents for solving computational problems in algebra. For the problems we consider, the main challenge is not correctness but \emph{time}: general-purpose algorithms are guaranteed to provide correct solutions but can be prohibitively slow, while reformulations that exploit special structure often allow solving a problem much faster. We propose to use this setting to evaluate how effectively agents discover and exploit structure within and across tasks to reduce computational costs. More broadly, computational algebra supplies infinitely many problems with independently verifiable answers and systematically controllable structure and difficulty. To illustrate these possibilities, we use benchmark families of systems
sc4a122493a.summary: Researchers propose evaluating AI agents on computational algebra tasks, where the challenge is speed rather than correctness, measuring whether agents find and exploit problem structure.
sc4a122493a.why: It frames a benchmark for agents optimizing computational cost, not just answer accuracy, relevant to anyone building agents for heavy numerical workloads.

sa6caf48446.title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN
sa6caf48446.description: arXiv:2611.16088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Subsurface schematisation supports geotechnical decisions but remains challenging because sparse site-investigation data leave substantial gaps in information about ground conditions. This study explores TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on general synthetic tabular data, for this task. Using only grid coordinates and soil behaviour type index observations from sparse cone penetration tests (CPTs), we first reconstruct two-dimensional sections without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries. We evaluate the approach on synthetic sections and at two field sites in the Netherlands, comparing it with SchemaGAN, a conditional generative adversarial network trained on synthetic geotechnical sections, and with reference interp
sa6caf48446.summary: Researchers test TabPFN, a tabular foundation model, to reconstruct 2D subsurface sections from sparse cone penetration test data without geotechnical fine-tuning.
sa6caf48446.why: It shows a general pretrained tabular model can fill sparse-data gaps in a specialized engineering domain without task-specific training.

sd61e30d5f8.title: Show Your Work in Swahili: Reinforcement Learning for Native-Language Mathematical Reasoning
sd61e30d5f8.description: arXiv:2611.16104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Fikiria, a two-stage SFT+GRPO recipe for Swahili mathematical reasoning. Its reward multiplies a format gate by a weighted sum of answer accuracy and the ChrF\texttt{++} similarity of the Swahili reasoning to an in-language reference chain of thought, so that training targets the surface fidelity of the reasoning trace and not only the final answer. We train on a 2.3k-problem Swahili dataset created by translating GSM8K with GPT-4.1 and filtering with SSA-COMET. On AfriMGSM Swahili, Fikiria-AfriqueQwen-14B reaches 79.2\%. Under the same fixed prompt and strict answer-format scoring, GPT-4o reaches 68.0\%, partly because it often fails the required answer format; IrokoBench reports 78.8\% for GPT-4o using a best-per-model prompt,
sd61e30d5f8.summary: Fikiria, a two-stage SFT plus GRPO recipe, trains models for Swahili math reasoning, rewarding reasoning-trace similarity to native-language references as well as answer accuracy.
sd61e30d5f8.why: It offers a reward design for improving non-English reasoning fidelity, useful for teams building multilingual reasoning models.

s6b519fad44.title: Trained on What Screen Readers Cannot Read: Accessibility Debt in the GUI Corpora Behind Computer-Use Agents
s6b519fad44.description: arXiv:2611.16107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computer-use agents learn to operate mobile interfaces from corpora of captured screens and accessibility trees. The same trees are what a screen reader consumes, so an agent trained on them inherits whatever labelling gaps the underlying applications carry. This paper measures one of those gaps, content-description coverage, in two Android corpora: Rico, collected in 2017, and AndroidControl, collected in 2024. Across 17,373,614 interface elements, 17.74% of the Rico elements that need a content description under our coding rule carry one, against 57.27% in AndroidControl. The difference of 39.5 percentage points holds under five alternative coding rules and when whole apps are resampled. It describes two datasets that also differ in app s
s6b519fad44.summary: A study finds content-description labelling coverage in Android GUI corpora used to train computer-use agents is low, with gaps persisting between 2017 and 2024 datasets.
s6b519fad44.why: Agents trained on poorly labelled interface data inherit accessibility gaps, so teams should audit training corpora and evaluate accessibility outcomes.

s6e1c056840.title: ADAPT: Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing for Pull Requests
s6e1c056840.description: arXiv:2611.16114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern software development relies on pull requests (PRs) that introduce small, targeted code changes. Once merged, these changes should be protected by focused tests that exercise the behavior the PR introduces, yet developers often submit PRs without such tests, leaving the new behavior unguarded against future regressions. Most test generation techniques target entire software units and optimize objectives such as code coverage rather than the behavior a change introduces, and prior diff-aware approaches have had limited success in capturing it. We propose ADAPT (Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing), a regression test generation approach that uses an autonomous coding agent to produce change-focused tests for PRs. Given a PR, the agent anal
s6e1c056840.summary: ADAPT is an agentic approach that generates focused tests for pull request code changes, targeting the behavior a diff introduces rather than whole units or coverage.
s6e1c056840.why: Diff-aware test generation could help teams guard new PR behavior against regressions without relying on developers to write tests.

s3acbbdee6e.title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety
s3acbbdee6e.description: arXiv:2611.16123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a tool-using LLM agent team violates policy, aggregate outcomes do not reveal whether an upstream message changed the executor's action. We introduce SwarmSafe-Delta, a paired executable protocol that freezes upstream computation, varies real, hidden, and format-matched placebo delivery, and scores a single committed action against deterministic benign and risky policy states under preassigned budgets. Across four models and constructed optional tasks, real delivery at $N=4$ produces 21.4% risky-world violations, versus 5.0% with placebo and 1.0% with hidden delivery (paired differences +16.4 and +20.3 percentage points). Real delivery also improves benign task success, illustrating that suppressing communication sacrifices utility. In
s3acbbdee6e.summary: SwarmSafe-Delta is a paired protocol that isolates how upstream messages affect an LLM agent team's policy-violating actions, comparing real delivery against placebo messages.
s3acbbdee6e.why: It gives teams a method to measure whether inter-agent messages alone cause unsafe actions, informing multi-agent safety design.

se25494dbc0.title: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction
se25494dbc0.description: arXiv:2611.16172v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a critical semiconductor manufacturing process where material removal rate (MRR) is a key metric for process monitoring and advanced process control (APC). Virtual metrology enables MRR estimation from process time series signals, supporting run-to-run(R2R) control and process optimization while reducing reliance on physical metrology. Existing approaches typically rely on simplified linear assumptions or require handcrafted feature engineering. In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining(GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, followed by superv
se25494dbc0.summary: Researchers propose a self-supervised attention-based model for virtual metrology, estimating chemical mechanical planarization material removal rate from process time series.
se25494dbc0.why: It reduces reliance on physical metrology and handcrafted features in semiconductor process control, relevant to industrial ML deployments.

sf1afdd74ed.title: JudgeMix: Judge-Guided Mixed-Rollout Data Synthesis for LLM Agents
sf1afdd74ed.description: arXiv:2611.16174v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on expert trajectories is a standard paradigm for training LLM agents. However, it suffers from a well-known training-inference distribution mismatch, calling for target-aware data synthesis strategies that ground the training data in the target model's native state distribution. To bridge this gap, emerging approaches incorporate the expert either to guide mixed rollouts alongside the target model, or to provide dense step-wise supervision. Nonetheless, existing methods apply expert assistance blind to the target model's inherent behavior: they either disrupt the rollout using sub-optimal random intervention heuristics, or they enforce indiscriminate uniform supervision that unnecessarily overwrites the model's
sf1afdd74ed.summary: JudgeMix proposes judge-guided mixed-rollout data synthesis to train LLM agents, using expert assistance aware of the target model's state during rollouts.
sf1afdd74ed.why: It targets the training-inference distribution mismatch in SFT for agents, a practical concern for teams fine-tuning agent models.

s5b84a3b705.title: Same-State Pairs Make One JEPA Proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis Vacuous
s5b84a3b705.description: arXiv:2611.16182v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), the JEPA proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) assumes that every observation determines the world state and that a spectral gap makes minimizers unique up to rotation. Under the hard-whitening population objective, same-state positive pairs make the induced world kernel the identity: every centered whitened state function is a global minimizer, and, when $d_z-1\ge 2k$, two minimizers can have best-rotation squared residual $2k$. The uniqueness claim is conditional; for $k<d_z-1$ its idealized same-state limit is vacuous. One of the paper's four quantitative results survives: a gap-free lower bound. Its bound vanishes only at perfect scene-explained fraction; it bounds ali
s5b84a3b705.summary: A paper argues that same-state positive pairs make the JEPA proof of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis vacuous, undermining its uniqueness claim.
s5b84a3b705.why: It challenges a theoretical justification for representation convergence in JEPA-style models, relevant mainly to researchers evaluating those foundations.

sb910ac292a.title: Data-Efficient LLM Safety Alignment Guided by Interpretable Features
sb910ac292a.description: arXiv:2611.16183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing large language models typically rely on massive fine-tuning datasets for safety alignment, which results in higher costs for safety alignment and often leads to the problem of over-refusal. We propose Less is Safer (LIS), a compact yet highly effective dataset for safety alignment, constructed through interpretable feature-guided selection and adversarial synthesis. Specifically, we leverage Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) activations to efficiently select prompts that cover diverse and interpretable safety features. Then, we employ a multi-agent adversarial synthesis framework to generate harmless prompts that nevertheless elicit unnecessary refusals. LIS contains only 2.4K samples, yet outperforms much larger datasets, e.g., TRIDENT-Cor
sb910ac292a.summary: Less is Safer (LIS) is a compact safety alignment dataset built with sparse autoencoder feature-guided selection and adversarial synthesis, aiming to reduce over-refusal.
sb910ac292a.why: A small, interpretable safety dataset could lower alignment costs and over-refusal, a practical trade-off for teams tuning deployed models.

s0d12b99ed7.title: When can an interpretability claim be trusted? Stability and certification of feature dimensionality, ridge leverage and the feature recovery rate
s0d12b99ed7.description: arXiv:2611.16190v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interpretability tools increasingly support safety claims, such as that a sparse dictionary has recovered most of a model's features. Such claims rest on measurements with arbitrary thresholds, and small changes to the model weights, a different training seed or a different threshold can reverse them. We study two widely used measurements in toy models and synthetic dictionaries with known ground truth: the feature dimensionality of Elhage et al. and the feature recovery rate (FRR) with a cosine threshold. We characterize exactly where feature dimensionality is discontinuous and replace it with a regularized (ridge) version with sharp stability bounds: the ridge leverage score changes by at most $3\sqrt{3}/(8\sqrt{\lambda})$ times the opera
s0d12b99ed7.summary: The paper studies when interpretability claims, such as sparse dictionaries recovering most features, are reliable under small changes in weights, seeds, or thresholds.
s0d12b99ed7.why: Safety claims built on interpretability metrics can be fragile to thresholds and seeds, so teams should validate them before relying on them.

s2350e5d835.title: Guided Generation of Linux Kernel Semantic Patches with Small Local Language Models
s2350e5d835.description: arXiv:2611.16215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a Linux kernel API changes, hundreds of drivers are converted by hand over months, and the earlier conversions are reviewed examples for the later ones. We ask whether small open language models running on a laptop can turn such examples into Coccinelle semantic patches, the rules kernel maintainers already use for tree-wide changes. We adapt guided code generation to this task: the training examples are decomposed by script into a tree of change variants, the model writes one small rule per variant under feedback from applying it to the examples, deterministic components repair SmPL syntax and generalise driver-specific names, rules are composed greedily, and a compile critic repairs or rejects a rule whose output does not build. We e
s2350e5d835.summary: Researchers test whether small open language models on a laptop can generate Coccinelle semantic patches from examples of Linux kernel API conversions.
s2350e5d835.why: Small local models producing kernel refactoring rules could speed tree-wide API migrations, which engineers maintaining large codebases would find useful.

sd1d5743b5e.title: Indic-Task Gains and Regressions after Reinforcement Learning
sd1d5743b5e.description: arXiv:2611.16228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We run reinforcement learning (RL) with GRPO across four environments, starting from a supervised fine-tuned 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model covering English and eight Indic languages. We compare the model before and after RL across 34 benchmarks in one evaluation campaign. MATH improves by 36.07 points, and most Indic benchmarks also improve. Yet XQuAD-Indic F1 falls 19.32 points as English answers rise from 8.7% to 91.7%; IndicQA falls 8.64, while English XQuAD gains 11.71 F1. A second RL run from the same supervised initialization adds an Indic environment together with language and repetition rewards. Compared with the released model, it improves both passage-answering and instruction-following benchmarks, along with preserving MATH pe
sd1d5743b5e.summary: GRPO reinforcement learning on a 30B mixture-of-experts model improves MATH by 36.07 points but causes regressions on several Indic-language benchmarks, such as XQuAD-Indic F1 falling 19.32 points.
sd1d5743b5e.why: RL gains can come with cross-lingual regressions as answers shift to English, so teams must evaluate across languages, not just aggregate benchmarks.

sd1afacf3f5.title: Label-Efficient Document-Grounded Factuality Detection via Cross-Paraphrastic Invariance Learning
sd1afacf3f5.description: arXiv:2611.16264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate fluent claims that are unsupported by a given source document, motivating accurate and efficient document-grounded factuality detection. Existing LLM-based evaluators often require repeated inference and incur high computational cost, whereas compact factuality detectors are efficient at inference time but commonly rely on large labeled or synthetically generated corpora. We propose CPIL (Cross-Paraphrastic Invariance Learning), a two-stage Siamese framework that converts a small labeled set into relational supervision without acquiring additional factuality labels. CPIL constructs positive pairs from distinct label-preserving paraphrastic views of the same document-claim instance and negative pairs
sd1afacf3f5.summary: CPIL, a two-stage Siamese framework, trains compact document-grounded factuality detectors from a small labeled set using cross-paraphrastic invariance learning.
sd1afacf3f5.why: It offers a way to build efficient factuality checkers with limited labeled data, useful for teams running hallucination detection at scale.

sb67d815d4a.title: Rectified Looped Transformer
sb67d815d4a.description: arXiv:2611.16265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Looped Transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared block, offering a parameter-efficient approach to language modeling. However, most existing works directly reuse each loop's output as the next's input, which can lead to hidden-state scale growth and perturbation amplification as recurrence deepens. We propose Rectified Looped Transformer (RLT), which redesigns feedback between loops using an interpolation schedule inspired by flow-based modeling. At each loop, RLT forms the next input by linearly interpolating between the current state and its prediction. Such interpolation distributes state changes across loops, encouraging a smoother trajectory from the initial input to the final output. Theoretical analysis pr
sb67d815d4a.summary: Rectified Looped Transformer (RLT) redesigns feedback between loops using an interpolation schedule, aiming to prevent hidden-state scale growth in looped language models.
sb67d815d4a.why: Looped transformers offer parameter-efficient depth, and stabilizing recurrence could make them more viable for compact language model designs.

sd86af2b614.title: SMIC: Shared Multiscale Input-Reference Conditioning across Transformer Layers for Natural Language Inference
sd86af2b614.description: arXiv:2611.16270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Natural Language Inference models can be sensitive to localized lexical changes. We introduce Shared Multiscale Input-Reference Conditioning (SMIC), which constructs a single input-dependent multiscale reference and reuses it across Transformer layers. Each layer applies its own multiscale transformation to the shared reference and injects the resulting conditioning feature before the attention update. We instantiate SMIC in a token--context Transformer (TCT) and conduct from-scratch comparisons against decoder-based and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) baselines across all three ANLI rounds. TCT-SMIC attains the highest observed ten-seed mean accuracy on all three ANLI rounds. The ablations further support the contribution of SMIC. We evaluate
sd86af2b614.summary: Researchers introduce SMIC, a method that builds one multiscale reference from the input and reuses it across Transformer layers for natural language inference.
sd86af2b614.why: It offers an architectural tweak to improve NLI robustness to localized lexical changes, though gains are only described in from-scratch comparisons.

s332feabe8d.title: Eliciting and Mitigating Specification Satisficing in Coding Agents
s332feabe8d.description: arXiv:2611.16289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents often fail to meet all requirements in the task description. In some of these failures, the agent considers an implementation choice that meets a requirement, but later decides to commit to another one that does not meet the requirement for a reason it finds acceptable. We call this specification satisficing. It is challenging to identify and mitigate specification satisficing because the agent accepts such choices for its own reasons, and existing self-correction methods are biased toward them. We propose SatisFix, which guides a coding agent to report these choices and their reasons, and then check each choice against the task description. We evaluate SatisFix on DeepSWE and SWE-bench Pro with five LLMs as backbones and two
s332feabe8d.summary: Researchers define 'specification satisficing,' where coding agents accept implementations that miss requirements, and propose SatisFix to identify and mitigate it.
s332feabe8d.why: Coding agents that silently skip requirements are a reliability risk, and existing self-correction methods reportedly miss this failure mode.

sf2750eea5d.title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram
sf2750eea5d.description: arXiv:2611.16308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge of phase stability is the first requirement for materials design, and predicting the conditions under which new materials can be synthesized has become a key capability of self-driving laboratories (SDLs). For inorganic materials, notably alloys, these predictions come from thermodynamic databases built with the CALPHAD method. Building a database, however, requires expert judgment at many steps, and because these decisions are rarely recorded, others can use a database but cannot regenerate or update it. Machines can already collect the data, build a first model with machine-learned interatomic potentials and refine it against experiments. The assessment itself, the sequence of judgments that turns these parts into a reliable dat
sf2750eea5d.summary: ORCHID-SAGE is presented as a fully reproducible CALPHAD workflow that records expert decisions so thermodynamic phase diagrams can be regenerated and updated.
sf2750eea5d.why: Recording the decisions behind materials databases makes them reproducible and updatable, which matters for self-driving lab pipelines.

s7c4499abd6.title: Shared Item-Level Error Limits the Aggregation of Small Language Models in Fermi Estimation
s7c4499abd6.description: arXiv:2611.16315v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems of language models are often motivated by an averaging argument: if the agents' errors are unbiased and independent, the error of an aggregate of N answers falls as 1/sqrt(N). Fermi estimation, whose continuous answers are aggregated on the logarithmic scale, permits a direct test. We decompose the log10 error of each answer into the mean error of its model on the item, common to all its draws on the item, and a residual, and estimate both from 2.51M answers given before any communication by 15 open-weight models (3B-72B) on realFP, with replication under a single prompt pair on realFP, Science Olympiad Fermi questions and a guesstimation set. Given the item, teammates' errors are uncorrelated and teams behave as indepen
s7c4499abd6.summary: A study of 15 open-weight models on Fermi estimation finds that shared item-level error limits gains from aggregating small language model answers.
s7c4499abd6.why: Multi-agent averaging may not reduce error as much as expected, since errors are correlated across draws for the same item.

sbf348a53d8.title: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization
sbf348a53d8.description: arXiv:2611.16317v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization enables memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models through forward-only evaluations, but high-dimensional random perturbations can limit optimization efficiency. Sparse perturbations reduce the search dimension, making the selection of informative coordinates critical. We propose Wanda-Importance Sparsity-MeZO (WIS-MeZO), which uses Wanda weight--activation saliency to construct task-conditioned sparse perturbation masks while keeping the pretrained model dense. We analyze support quality through gradient energy capture and relate it to gradient estimation and convergence. Across 16 benchmarks with LLaMA and Qwen models ranging from 3B to 32B parameters, WIS-MeZO achieves higher aggregate scores tha
sbf348a53d8.summary: Researchers propose WIS-MeZO, which uses Wanda saliency to build sparse perturbation masks for memory-efficient zeroth-order fine-tuning of LLMs.
sbf348a53d8.why: Sparse, task-conditioned perturbations could cut the search dimension for forward-only LLM fine-tuning, reducing memory needs.

s2d2c809538.title: SUMNO: Spatially Unrolled Multigrid Neural Operator for Fluid Flow Surrogates
s2d2c809538.description: arXiv:2611.16341v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data-driven surrogate modeling has emerged as a powerful paradigm for accelerating computational fluid dynamics, and hierarchical U-shaped networks, which resemble the structure of classical Geometric Multigrid (GMG) methods, have become prevalent designs. Modern surrogates built on these designs achieve competitive accuracy at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers; however, accurate prediction of complex flows remains challenging, and no existing architecture leads across them. In such networks, the multigrid analogy mainly concerns the multi-resolution topology, while their components largely follow common vision practice. To address this, this study introduces SUMNO, a multigrid neural operator for fluid flow fields on regular grid
s2d2c809538.summary: SUMNO is a spatially unrolled multigrid neural operator proposed as a fluid flow surrogate that aims to improve accuracy on complex flows.
s2d2c809538.why: Faster and more accurate CFD surrogates could reduce solver costs, though the text gives few performance details.

s6fa6369518.title: DRAMA: Dissecting Attention Redundancy for Accelerating Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
s6fa6369518.description: arXiv:2611.16345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal diffusion large language models (dLLMs) generate text through iterative masked denoising with bidirectional attention, offering a compelling alternative to autoregressive vision-language modeling. However, each denoising step requires a full forward pass over long multimodal sequences in which visual tokens dominate the sequence length, and a fixed step budget further compounds this quadratic per-step cost. Existing inference acceleration approaches for multimodal dLLMs characterize attention redundancy implicitly, motivating designs from isolated attention visualizations rather than from measurement. We close this gap with DRAMA, a training-free acceleration framework grounded in a systematic dissection of attention redundancy i
s6fa6369518.summary: DRAMA analyzes attention redundancy in multimodal diffusion LLMs to accelerate inference, where visual tokens dominate long sequences and cost per step is quadratic.
s6fa6369518.why: Targeting attention redundancy in multimodal diffusion LLMs addresses a real inference cost bottleneck for vision-language serving.

s6b753130ca.title: HyBridge: Bridge-Guided Self-Supervised Hyperbolic Hypergraph Representation Learning
s6b753130ca.description: arXiv:2611.16351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hypergraphs capture groupwise relationships among multiple nodes and often exhibit tree-like structures. Although hyperbolic space is well suited for modeling such structures, simply extending existing hypergraph representation learning (HRL) methods to hyperbolic space does not consistently improve performance. In this paper, we investigate the relationship between node structural properties and hyperbolic embedding radii and find that bridge nodes tend to lie closer to the center in graphs, whereas this relationship is not consistently observed in hypergraphs. We further find that conventional bridge score estimation may fail to capture the groupwise connectivity of hypergraphs. Motivated by these findings, we propose HyBridge, a self-sup
s6b753130ca.summary: HyBridge is a self-supervised hyperbolic hypergraph representation learning method that uses bridge nodes to guide embeddings.

s3c77307cee.title: ReliaGuard: Reconstruction-Aware Watermarking for Source Attribution and Blind Edit Localization
s3c77307cee.description: arXiv:2611.16368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative image editing facilitates content creation but complicates source attribution and edit verification. Existing watermarking methods combine copyright protection with tamper localization, yet background reconstruction can weaken spatial evidence even when source identifiers remain recoverable. We propose ReliaGuard, a reconstruction-aware watermarking framework for source attribution and blind edit localization. The writer optimizes keyed feature responses in both the protected image and its variational autoencoder reconstruction under image-distortion and source-preservation constraints. Using only the received image and a secret key, the reader combines watermark responses with local image context through residual evidence refine
s3c77307cee.summary: ReliaGuard is a watermarking framework that aims to support source attribution and blind edit localization for generative image edits, even after reconstruction.
s3c77307cee.why: Watermarks that survive VAE reconstruction could help verify provenance of AI-edited images, a concern for content platforms.

s962e2a6fca.title: Recursive State-Augmented Language Models: Persistent Latent-State Adaptation of Pretrained Language Models
s962e2a6fca.description: arXiv:2611.16375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models rely on finite token contexts, limiting access to earlier interactions. We introduce Recursive State-Augmented Language Models (Recursive SALM), a framework in which a persistent latent state evolves with each observation and generates adaptations of a pretrained language model. A modular read-transition-write architecture separates observation encoding, latent dynamics, and predictor adaptation. We develop deterministic and stochastic formulations. The experiments evaluate only deterministic SALM with frozen GPT-2 small and exclude earlier evidence from its decoder context. On a four-turn hypothesis-inference task, latent-gated LoRA reaches 89.1% accuracy, comparable to 88.0% for a trained full-context LoRA baseline, with e
s962e2a6fca.summary: Recursive SALM adds a persistent latent state that evolves with observations and generates adaptations to a pretrained language model, evaluated with frozen GPT-2 small.
s962e2a6fca.why: A persistent latent state could extend effective memory beyond token context, though the evaluation described is limited.

sfdf72f673c.title: Beyond Compressing Everything: Contrastive Memory Learning for Selective Context Compression
sfdf72f673c.description: arXiv:2611.16384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) advance toward increasingly long inputs, soft context compression offers a promising approach to efficient inference by converting long inputs into compact memory slots. Under limited memory budgets, effective context compression remains challenging because task-relevant evidence varies substantially across queries, ranging from localized evidence to multiple distant spans or information dispersed throughout the full document. Instead of compressing everything indiscriminately, we propose CoMem, a query-guided selective context compression framework that learns memory representations conditioned on both the document and the query. CoMem develops Contrastive Compressor Learning to achieve query-sensitive yet c
sfdf72f673c.summary: CoMem proposes query-guided selective soft context compression, compressing only task-relevant parts of long inputs into compact memory slots.
sfdf72f673c.why: Selective compression targets the efficiency of long-context inference, a practical cost concern for LLM deployments.

s2bcbd3a585.title: TransXplainRRG: A Radiologist-Evaluated LVLM for Chest Radiograph Report Generation
s2bcbd3a585.description: arXiv:2611.16393v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advancements in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLM) enhance X-ray report generation, but often neglect clinical context, overlook workflow integration, and lack explainability, which hinders clinical adoption due to interpretability and reliability concerns. This paper addresses the dual challenges of performance and expert explainability in automated X-ray report generation for clinical AI applications. Our proposed approach, TransXplainRRG, utilises an off-the-shelf Swin Transformer model along with a transformer-based text encoder that incorporates patient medical history to generate a radiology report. Further, we explore an expert-guided `inside-out' approach and extract only abnormal findings for radiology report refinement. Th
s2bcbd3a585.summary: TransXplainRRG is a vision-language model for chest X-ray report generation, evaluated by radiologists and designed with explainability in mind.
s2bcbd3a585.why: Clinical report generation with explainability and radiologist evaluation is relevant to healthcare AI teams weighing adoption.

s622ce92a99.title: PhysCapBench: A Cross-Domain Benchmark for Physically Grounded Video Captioning
s622ce92a99.description: arXiv:2611.16424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physical AI aims to learn transferable physical knowledge from real-world experience to understand, predict, and act in the physical world. Internet videos and embodied demonstrations provide complementary observations of motion, interaction, and state evolution. A foundational data challenge is to measure and preserve this physical information as training supervision. In video-language pretraining, captions express observed processes in language, yet a semantically correct description can omit the interactions and transitions that define those processes. Rich physical experience in video does not automatically translate into sufficient language supervision. This gap calls for a yardstick to assess annotation quality, compare captioning str
s622ce92a99.summary: PhysCapBench is a cross-domain benchmark for physically grounded video captioning, testing whether captions capture interactions and state transitions.
s622ce92a99.why: Benchmarks for physical grounding in video captions can help evaluate training data quality for physical AI systems.

seec0636856.title: RMIT-ADM+S at TREC RAG 2026: Research Agents, Retriever Ablations, and Open-Weight Replication
seec0636856.description: arXiv:2611.16425v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the RMIT-ADM+S team's participation in the TREC 2026 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) track using the ClimbMix corpus. We submitted seven research-agent runs using proprietary OpenAI and open-weight models, exploring different retrieval strategies, writer models, and agent workflows. Pre-submission ablations identified writer selection and adjacent-chunk expansion as the main factors affecting answer quality. In the official NIST evaluation, six of seven runs exceeded the track median across all three rubric/nugget collections. Our best-performing run, brief-hybrid, achieved the highest all-item coverage among our submissions and tied the track maximum (0.892) for Batch-1 vital coverage. Human side-by-side preferences differ
seec0636856.summary: The RMIT-ADM+S team describes seven research-agent runs for TREC 2026 RAG, finding writer selection and adjacent-chunk expansion most affect answer quality.
seec0636856.why: Ablations identify writer model choice and chunk expansion as key levers for RAG answer quality.

s50ea03a1fd.title: SoScale: Second-Order Scale Search for FP4 Quantization
s50ea03a1fd.description: arXiv:2611.16426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-bit quantization reduces the memory footprint and inference cost of large language models (LLMs), yet accurate FP4 quantization remains challenging. Practical formats such as MXFP4, NVFP4, and HiF4 pair a 4-bit floating-point payload with block-wise or hierarchical scale codes, making accuracy highly sensitive to how each local distribution is scaled. Default maximum-absolute-value scaling preserves dynamic range, but can spend scarce FP4 levels on rarely occupied outlier regions and leave dense tensor values poorly resolved. Existing scale-search methods minimize local element-wise reconstruction error, optimizing tensor fidelity rather than layer-output fidelity. We propose SoScale, a second-order weight scale-code search method for h
s50ea03a1fd.summary: SoScale proposes a second-order scale search method for FP4 quantization of LLMs, targeting formats like MXFP4, NVFP4, and HiF4.
s50ea03a1fd.why: Better FP4 scale selection could improve accuracy of low-bit LLM inference, reducing memory and serving cost.

s04f8ffb8a2.title: DesignTaste: Benchmarking AI-Generator Visual Design Against Award-Wining Works
s04f8ffb8a2.description: arXiv:2611.16442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-image benchmarks commonly assess text-image alignment or overall preference. Whether models can produce good designs when a brief leaves the appearance open remains less well understood. We introduce DesignTaste, a visual design benchmark that compares generated images with award-winning works. From these works and their publicly available context, we derive 403 design briefs: 100 poster tasks from 100 Beste Plakate 2025 and 303 tasks spanning 20 categories from ADC 2026. Six leading commercial text-to-image models each generate an image from the same brief. A single model judge scores each output and the corresponding award-winning work independently on five evaluation dimensions. On each dataset, only ArtArk achieves a higher mean
s04f8ffb8a2.summary: Researchers introduced DesignTaste, a benchmark of 403 design briefs comparing text-to-image outputs against award-winning posters and design works.
s04f8ffb8a2.why: It tests whether generators produce good design when briefs leave appearance open, a gap beyond alignment and preference scores.

s252c79da1e.title: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough
s252c79da1e.description: arXiv:2611.16473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Until recently, the biggest obstacles to natural spoken interaction with social robots were speech recognition errors and turn-taking failures. Advances in speech recognition have enabled much better spoken interaction, but turn-taking failures and other misunderstandings continue to be far too prevalent. This short paper looks back at earlier methods for improving speech recognition and turn-taking in interaction with social robots, and then looks at what can be done today, arguing that multimodal bidirectional streaming is needed to reduce the frequency of turn-taking failures.
s252c79da1e.summary: A short paper argues that social robots still suffer from turn-taking failures and misunderstandings, and proposes multimodal bidirectional streaming to reduce them.
s252c79da1e.why: Turn-taking and misunderstanding remain practical barriers for spoken interfaces, even as speech recognition has improved.

s74fc34c8ad.title: Where in the Input Does a One-Pass Decision Encoder Look?
s74fc34c8ad.description: arXiv:2611.16477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Laya is a small model that answers a multiple-choice question about a text in one pass: the question, the options (each with a name and a description) and the text form one sequence of at most 512 tokens, the window, in the English release. A longer text is silently cut at the end, and we measure what that costs. Test documents place a held-out row's text, the evidence, at a chosen token offset among distractor text; 177 items, five tasks, three checkpoints (released, short-row fine-tune, long-document fine-tune), four window sizes and 93,275 scored requests. When the evidence lies beyond the window, accuracy falls to 26.4% for the released checkpoint (27.2% for both fine-tunes), near the 27.0% of guessing and below the 35.6% of always givi
s74fc34c8ad.summary: Researchers study Laya, a small one-pass multiple-choice model, measuring how performance degrades when evidence sits later in a 512-token window.
s74fc34c8ad.why: It quantifies the cost of silent truncation for long documents in small models with fixed context windows.

s17a5a27783.title: PISim: A Unified Photonic Inference Simulator for Hardware-Aware Cross-Layer Design-Space Exploration
s17a5a27783.description: arXiv:2611.16522v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Photonic neural accelerators offer ultra-low latency linear algebra, yet their usable numerical precision, sustainable throughput, and application accuracy remain tightly bounded by surrounding electro-optical interfaces and physical non-idealities. Pre-fabrication design-space exploration (DSE) requires a cross-layer electronic design automation (EDA) framework capable of evaluating disparate optical topologies under identical neural workloads and physical assumptions. We present \textbf{PISim}, a unified Photonic Inference Simulator that couples pretrained deep neural network execution with physics-based models of six accelerator architecture families, six electro-optic modulator technologies, four optical source organizations, and direct
s17a5a27783.summary: PISim is a unified photonic inference simulator for cross-layer design-space exploration of photonic neural accelerators, covering electro-optical interfaces and physical non-idealities.
s17a5a27783.why: Hardware teams can evaluate photonic accelerator designs against neural workloads before fabrication, reducing costly iteration.

sa2dbb778fd.title: RESYNC: Residual Latent-State Synchronization for Deadline-Bound Streaming Inference
sa2dbb778fd.description: arXiv:2611.16523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting every observation in a high-rate stream requires a model to finish before the next arrival. A large model may offer better predictions but miss that deadline. We propose RESYNC: the large model runs asynchronously, while a fast path updates its latest exact but stale latent state using the observations received since that state was computed and applies its unchanged prediction head. The updater learns from the frozen model's representations without task labels. Across one real and two synthetic streams and five architecture families, RESYNC beats the best compact or distilled alternative with a paired 95% interval above zero in all twelve dataset--architecture pairs with a material teacher advantage at anchor ages of 4--12 observ
sa2dbb778fd.summary: RESYNC runs a large model asynchronously while a fast path updates its stale latent state, aiming to meet deadlines in high-rate streaming inference.
sa2dbb778fd.why: It offers a way to keep predictions fresh on streams where a large model would otherwise miss arrival deadlines.

sae4337041c.title: A Joint LLM and Optimization Agent Solution for Drone Scheduling in Victim Search Missions
sae4337041c.description: arXiv:2611.16524v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Victim search in wilderness areas is time-critical. Drones enable rapid area search, but scheduling them is challenging because victims may continue moving, detection results are uncertain, and effective decisions must combine structured mission information with unstructured contextual clues and domain knowledge. To address this, we propose an agent-aided drone scheduling system. The system employs an agent at the ground control station (GCS) to coordinate multiple drones over successive search cycles. In each cycle, the agent applies a scheduling policy that combines a large language model (LLM) for reasoning about where to search with an optimizer for determining how to dispatch the drones under energy constraints. Simulation results show
sae4337041c.summary: Researchers propose an agent-aided system in which a ground-control agent combines an LLM with an optimizer to schedule multiple drones in victim search missions.
sae4337041c.why: It shows an LLM agent coordinating an optimization layer for real-time scheduling under uncertainty.

s60e155c105.title: ZONOS3-Mini Technical Report
s60e155c105.description: arXiv:2611.16525v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: ZONOS3-Mini is an ultra-compact, ultra-fast, zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model. The model can run in real time on a laptop or smartphone. For its latency and size, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and cloning fidelity. To achieve this we propose a latent MoE backbone with only 886M parameters (100M active per token) and a new audio codec, Zyphra Audio Codec 1 (ZAC-1), which represents 44.1 kHz audio at a 15 Hz frame rate. On the new ZTTS2-Eval benchmark, ZONOS3-Mini reaches a 6.71% macro-average WER over 55 language sets (35 clean and 20 in the wild), which is competitive with larger and slower state-of-the-art models. We release the model weights, inference, and training code.
s60e155c105.summary: Zyphra released ZONOS3-Mini, an 886M-parameter zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model with a new audio codec, claiming real-time operation on laptops and smartphones.
s60e155c105.why: A compact, on-device voice-cloning model with reported multilingual accuracy lowers the bar for local speech applications.

sb02c4b68c3.title: When Chekhov's Gun Fires Anyway: Over-Realization in Text-to-Image Models
sb02c4b68c3.description: arXiv:2611.16630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In text-to-image generation, a target that the prompt mentions often appears in the generated image in a way the prompt does not call for. We call this failure over-realization. Mental-spaces theory points to the situations where it can happen: under a negation, inside what a character believes or imagines, as the vehicle of a figurative comparison, or behind a viewpoint that hides the target. Prior work has studied only negation in depth, and the conventional alignment and preference metrics do not penalize the failure. We build OverReal to measure it: OverReal-Gen, 698 prompts covering the four situations, on which we measure each generator's over-realization rate; and OverReal-Det, 2,841 generated images human-labeled for whether and how
sb02c4b68c3.summary: Researchers define over-realization, where text-to-image models render prompted targets in contexts the prompt rules out, and introduce the OverReal benchmark.
sb02c4b68c3.why: Standard alignment metrics miss this failure, so teams relying on them may ship image generators that violate negations or beliefs.

s8fe06f111b.title: Dataset Distillation via Drifting
s8fe06f111b.description: arXiv:2611.16642v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The task of dataset distillation concerns the learning of a small set of synthetic samples that can serve as an effective replacement for a large real dataset when used for downstream tasks. While many solutions have been proposed since the problem's inception, most of them primarily seek to optimize the distilled data with respect to a classifier. In this work, we propose a new distillation method that learns a set of samples such that they directly approximate the per-class data distribution. Specifically, we "drift" our distilled data in the latent space of a feature extractor such that they move both toward the real data and away from each other without using a classification objective. We find that our drifted data cover the real distr
s8fe06f111b.summary: A new dataset distillation method learns synthetic samples that directly approximate per-class data distributions rather than optimizing for a classifier.
s8fe06f111b.why: Distilled datasets that match data distributions could make training on small synthetic sets more reusable across downstream tasks.

sb48a6c0339.title: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
sb48a6c0339.description: arXiv:2611.16661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient batch execution of agent tasks is critical to LLM training and development workflows, including benchmark evaluation, synthetic-data generation, and RL rollouts. Since these tasks alternate between LLM inference and environment interaction, we present coordinated optimizations to reduce batch makespan, the time required to complete all tasks in a batch. For hybrid LLMs, a workload-based resource model guides GPU-memory allocation between key-value (KV) cache and recurrent state and provides a reference sample concurrency to exploit parallelism while limiting recomputation. Trajectory-aware routing and scheduling promote cache reuse while balancing worker load. Under constrained environment capacity, we decouple sample admission fr
sb48a6c0339.summary: Researchers present coordinated optimizations that reduce batch makespan for LLM agent workloads, including GPU memory allocation between KV cache and recurrent state for hybrid models.
sb48a6c0339.why: Batch agent evaluation and RL rollouts are costly; inference and environment coordination can cut completion time and GPU spend.

s7c04bfa567.title: MuSeToM: Multi-Sensory Evaluation of Belief Revision with Textual Cues Across Six Senses
s7c04bfa567.description: arXiv:2611.16662v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Theory of Mind (ToM), the ability to infer mental states in others, is pivotal for human social cognition. Existing evaluations of ToM in large language models (LLMs) mainly focus on static belief attribution and false-belief reasoning, leaving a critical aspect of social reasoning underexplored: can LLMs decide whether perceptual evidence is sufficient to justify another person's belief revision? To address this gap, we present MuSeToM, a human-validated, text-based benchmark for evaluating epistemic belief revision in ToM reasoning. MuSeToM contains 2,415 instances adapted from BigToM and OpenToM, with textual cues spanning six sensory categories, and tests whether models can determine when a protagonist should revise a belief and infer t
s7c04bfa567.summary: MuSeToM is a human-validated text benchmark testing whether LLMs can judge if perceptual evidence justifies another person's belief revision across six senses.
s7c04bfa567.why: It probes a social reasoning gap beyond static false-belief tests, relevant to agents reasoning about others' knowledge.

s9fbcf4075f.title: Edge-Gradient Augmentation under Reinforcement Learning for Temporal Graph
s9fbcf4075f.description: arXiv:2611.16678v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Temporal link prediction is critical for understand- ing dynamic interactions in evolving networks, informing appli- cations ranging from social network analysis to recommendation systems. Existing methods typically rely on raw temporal graph data, often neglecting explicit edge-change information that can significantly improve predictive performance. To address this gap, we propose edge-gradient reinforced learning (EG-RL), a framework that explicitly encodes edge-gradient events (edge births and deaths) through dedicated node and link encoding modules. EG-RL uses a policy-driven reinforcement-learning mechanism to dynamically select and augment the most infor- mative edge snapshots, guided by critic-based feedback to opti- mize prediction
s9fbcf4075f.summary: EG-RL is a reinforcement learning framework for temporal link prediction that explicitly encodes edge births and deaths as edge-gradient events.
s9fbcf4075f.why: Explicit edge-change signals may improve link prediction in evolving graphs used for recommendation and social analysis.

sd62214bc4b.title: MobileProbe: Adaptive Security Evaluation of Mobile Agents via Trajectory-Aware Injection
sd62214bc4b.description: arXiv:2611.16693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mobile GUI agents read the screen of a phone and operate apps on a user's behalf to complete multi-step tasks such as online shopping or messaging. Because the agent acts on whatever the screen shows, an attacker can embed malicious instructions into ordinary UI content and redirect its actions. We refer to this threat as environmental injection attack (EIA). Existing benchmarks measure this risk by pinning hand-crafted payloads to a fixed step of a fixed task. This approach faces two limitations. First, each payload is bound to one task in one app and does not transfer without manual redesign. Second, agents given the same task may follow different routes, so an agent that never reaches the injected page is recorded as safe without being t
sd62214bc4b.summary: MobileProbe is an adaptive security evaluation for mobile GUI agents that injects malicious instructions into screen content along agent trajectories, targeting environmental injection attacks.
sd62214bc4b.why: Mobile agents act on whatever the screen shows, so injection-resistance testing matters for anyone shipping agent automation.

s89f03e11e4.title: MusicRWKV: A Multimodal RWKV Framework for Music Representation Learning
s89f03e11e4.description: arXiv:2611.16718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent music foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in music representation learning, yet most existing approaches rely on Transformer architectures whose quadratic attention complexity introduces substantial computational and memory overhead when modeling long-duration music recordings. In this work, we propose MusicRWKV, a multimodal music representation learning framework built upon the RWKV architecture. MusicRWKV jointly models waveform, spectrogram, and metadata information within a unified self-supervised learning framework. To improve efficiency for long musical sequences, we introduce an invertible compression module that reduces sequence length while preserving reconstruction capability. A FiLM-based conditioning stra
s89f03e11e4.summary: MusicRWKV is a multimodal music representation framework built on RWKV that jointly models waveform, spectrogram, and metadata with self-supervised learning.
s89f03e11e4.why: RWKV's linear-complexity design offers an alternative to quadratic attention for long music recordings.

seec68b44ec.title: From Data to Wisdom: Rethinking AI Through an Epistemic Lens
seec68b44ec.description: arXiv:2611.16726v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proposes the Data-to-Wisdom Epistemic Architecture for AI (EAAI), a conceptual framework treating Data, Information, Knowledge, Understanding and Wisdom as five distinct but recursively interacting epistemic functions: observation, contextual interpretation, modeling and prediction, critical evaluation and informed judgment. Two observations motivate it: sequential readings of the Knowledge Pyramid obscure how these functions interact, and a targeted review of ten Bayesian reference books finds that prior distributions are defined mathematically while "prior information" and "prior knowledge" are not consistently distinguished as epistemic categories. A Bayesian interpretation relates the likelihood, prior and posterior distribut
seec68b44ec.summary: The paper proposes the Data-to-Wisdom Epistemic Architecture, a conceptual framework treating data, information, knowledge, understanding and wisdom as interacting epistemic functions.

s09e30861aa.title: From Foundation VLM to Versatile Driving VLM: A Triplet Incremental Training Approach
s09e30861aa.description: arXiv:2611.16727v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adapting general Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to Autonomous Driving (AD) is thought to require heavy 3D spatial priors or intrusive architectural overhauls to compensate for a lack of spatial grounding. In this work, we present a counterintuitive pilot study: off-the-shelf general VLMs already exhibit remarkable adaptability across diverse driving tasks, while precise metric depth remains the primary missing link, a bottleneck readily addressable via onboard sensors and depth foundation models. To this end, we introduce the Triplet Incremental Training Framework, a non-intrusive paradigm that seamlessly instills 3D geometric awareness into a general VLM backbone while fully preserving its open-world capabilities. Driven by automatically co
s09e30861aa.summary: A pilot study finds off-the-shelf general vision-language models adapt well to diverse driving tasks, with metric depth as the main gap, and introduces a Triplet Incremental Training approach.
s09e30861aa.why: It suggests driving VLMs may not need heavy 3D priors or architectural overhauls, with depth sensors or depth models closing the main gap.

s3966540c41.title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
s3966540c41.description: arXiv:2611.16728v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generalist manipulation policies can benefit from the complementary experience of humans, real robots, and simulated agents. However, differences in morphology, sensing, and control interfaces make it difficult to learn effectively from their combined demonstrations. We introduce EgoX, an egocentric cross-embodiment learning framework that organizes heterogeneous demonstrations through semantically corresponding observation and action modalities. EgoX pretrains a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming (MXT+) on this mixture and fine-tunes it on target-embodiment demonstrations. Within each embodiment, MXT+ assigns a dedicated tokenizer to each observation modality and a dedicated expert to each action modality, wi
s3966540c41.summary: EgoX is a framework for learning manipulation policies from combined human, real robot, and simulated demonstrations using a Modularized Cross-Embodiment Transformer with Embodiment Dreaming.
s3966540c41.why: It offers a way to pool heterogeneous demonstration data across morphologies and sensors, which could reduce data collection costs for robot policies.

sadfd7cf196.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
sadfd7cf196.description: arXiv:2611.16748v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framewor
sadfd7cf196.summary: PhysLoop is a harness that uses LLM physics knowledge to guide self-improving video generation models toward more physically consistent training videos.
sadfd7cf196.why: It proposes a way to generate physics-aware training data for video models without costly manual supervision, though the text gives limited detail on results.

see925d9f48.title: ORCA:Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment for Multi-View Clustering
see925d9f48.description: arXiv:2611.16749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep multi-view clustering often suffers from redundant information accumulation during fusion and indiscriminate alignment across representation levels. We propose Orthogonal Residual Consensus Alignment (ORCA) to address these challenges. Its semantic incremental recurrent fusion module extracts cross-view orthogonal residuals as non-redundant increments and adaptively weights recurrent states through divergence-guided gating. Its consensus-calibrated hierarchical contrastive alignment module uses the global consensus to weight contrastive alignment of view-level, pairwise, and recurrent representations. Together, these modules balance view-specific structure with cross-view consistency. Experiments on five benchmarks against fifteen comp
see925d9f48.summary: ORCA is a deep multi-view clustering method that uses orthogonal residual fusion and consensus-calibrated contrastive alignment to reduce redundancy and improve alignment.

s2f8fa3f613.title: AgriSense: Vision-Language Decision Support and Robotic Intervention in a Virtual Greenhouse Copy title
s2f8fa3f613.description: arXiv:2611.16752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autonomous greenhouse management increasingly requires robotic systems that integrate perception, navigation, environmental regulation, and plant-level intervention. This paper presents AgriSense, a framework combining an Isaac Sim virtual greenhouse, a quadruped mobile manipulator, RGB and LiDAR-inertial sensing, environmental control, and supervised vision-language decision support. Frozen DINOv2 and BERT encoders, together with structured environmental inputs, support joint prediction of twelve environmental references, a target zone, and an intervention flag. Checkpoint replay reproduces 41/43 zone decisions. Across five seeds on a source-grouped test set, the full, image-removed, and language-removed configurations each achieve 43/44 c
s2f8fa3f613.summary: AgriSense combines an Isaac Sim virtual greenhouse, a quadruped mobile manipulator, and vision-language decision support for autonomous greenhouse management.
s2f8fa3f613.why: It shows an integrated simulation-to-robot pipeline pairing frozen encoders with environmental inputs for agricultural decisions, though the text gives few performance details.

s52f734c7de.title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
s52f734c7de.description: arXiv:2611.16767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road. While recent benchmarks have begun assessing these models on driving scenes, they mainly target routine traffic conditions and general comprehension tasks based on existing driving datasets and therefore fail to evaluate model performance on the rarest and most safety-critical driving events, also known as "corner cases". To provide a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs on precisely these scenarios, we introduce DashBench, a benchmark testing 25 Video LLMs on 1,709 carefully curated driving videos spanning not only collision-relat
s52f734c7de.summary: A new benchmark evaluates Video LLMs on rare, safety-critical autonomous driving corner cases rather than routine traffic scenes.
s52f734c7de.why: Routine-scene benchmarks overstate readiness; teams deploying video LLMs in driving need tests focused on rare, safety-critical events.

sa8e284ad44.title: DPA: Decentralized Primal Averaging with Quasi-Global Momentum for Highly Heterogeneous Data
sa8e284ad44.description: arXiv:2611.16871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decentralized training of deep learning models keeps training data local and supports on-device learning over networks. In realistic scenarios, heterogeneity across agents' local data poses an optimization challenge and can severely degrade test accuracy, especially on sparse communication graphs. Building on recent advances in centralized primal averaging, we propose Decentralized Primal Averaging (DPA), a decentralized learning algorithm that combines primal averaging with a local quasi-global momentum buffer. DPA maintains three coupled sequences for optimization, gradient evaluation, and output averaging, while using consecutive mixed iterates to construct a network-aware momentum direction without transmitting an auxiliary tracking var
sa8e284ad44.summary: DPA is a decentralized learning algorithm combining primal averaging with a local quasi-global momentum buffer to handle highly heterogeneous data on sparse communication graphs.
sa8e284ad44.why: It targets accuracy loss in decentralized training on heterogeneous, on-device data, a practical constraint for federated-style deployments.

sfa2d422630.title: Context Graph: Explainable Multi-Agent Decision Chains in AI-RAN
sfa2d422630.description: arXiv:2611.16879v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-RAN distributes network control across multiple autonomous agents, namely xApps and rApps operating over shared radio resources. When an alert or degradation appears, operators currently lack a structured way to trace which decision caused it, what context triggered that decision, and how other agents interacted. Existing explainability tools focus on single-model feature attribution or linear event logging, neither of which captures cross-agent decision chains. We propose the Context Graph, a heterogeneous directed graph that organizes policies, measurements, decisions, and alerts into a queryable explanation layer. Its foundational primitive is the Decision-Event node acting as a causal junction, where incoming edges capture triggering
sfa2d422630.summary: The Context Graph is a heterogeneous directed graph proposed to trace cross-agent decision chains among xApps and rApps in AI-RAN networks.
sfa2d422630.why: Operators of multi-agent radio networks need traceable decision chains to diagnose which agent caused a degradation.

s25ce1e5259.title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
s25ce1e5259.description: arXiv:2611.16881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) produce highly accurate contact maps from single-sequence inputs. People often take this accuracy as proof that these models implicitly learn invariant coevolutionary statistics, extracting the same signals as classical alignment-based methods like Potts. In this work, we introduce a diagnostic framework around a global bijective relabeling of the amino-acid alphabet. This transformation permutes residue letters while leaving all alignment-level information, column entropies, and pairwise edit distances unchanged. Pseudolikelihood Potts models and inverse-covariance estimators remain invariant under this transformation, but pLMs fail the test. Across multiple architectures (ESM-2, MSA Transformer, AMPLIFY) and
s25ce1e5259.summary: A diagnostic study shows protein language models' contact predictions fail to hold under a bijective relabeling of amino-acid letters, questioning that they learn invariant coevolutionary statistics.
s25ce1e5259.why: It challenges the assumption that high accuracy from protein language models reflects robust underlying biological signal.

sef4c6ed80e.title: LLM-Assisted Verification in Dafny
sef4c6ed80e.description: arXiv:2611.16886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Formal verification of complex algorithms requires expertise in program specification, invariant construction, mathematical proof, and the management of automated theorem provers. Although large language models (LLMs) can generate program code and proof fragments, reliably developing complete machine-checked verifications remains challenging: it requires an iterative process of constructing and validating specifications and invariants, building proofs, diagnosing solver failures, and optimizing verification performance. This paper presents a systematic ten-step workflow for LLM-assisted verification of scientific algorithms using the Dafny verification system. The workflow integrates algorithm formalization, contract development, empirical
sef4c6ed80e.summary: A paper presents a system that uses LLMs to assist with formal verification in Dafny, covering specifications, invariants, proofs, and solver diagnosis.
