sef4c6ed80e.why: LLM-assisted formal verification could lower the expertise barrier for machine-checked correctness, though reliability remains a stated challenge.

s07d2091ec7.title: Look It Up: Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Codebook Search
s07d2091ec7.description: arXiv:2611.16890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Attributing short LLM-generated texts to a specific source remains challenging for existing multi-bit watermarking methods, which often require long generations or costly decoding to recover payloads reliably. We propose a codebook-based watermarking scheme that maps an $n$-bit payload to a longer $u$-bit codeword and embeds it during generation through token-level logit biasing. During extraction, the received bit sequence is matched to the nearest codeword in a precomputed secret codebook using Hamming or Levenshtein distance. Experiments show that our method achieves near-perfect recovery for 16-24 bit payloads on 200-token generations and strong performance on 127-token generations for base models. Results are weaker on some instruction
s07d2091ec7.summary: A codebook-based multi-bit watermarking scheme embeds payloads into LLM text via logit biasing and recovers them by nearest-codeword search.
s07d2091ec7.why: It aims to attribute short LLM outputs to sources without long generations, relevant to provenance and misuse tracking.

s0dda1fef1f.title: STEALTH: Steganographic Text Encoding Agnostic to Low-Level Tensor Hardware
s0dda1fef1f.description: arXiv:2611.16928v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Provably secure linguistic steganography hides a message inside text sampled from a language model, so that without the key, a stegotext is computationally indistinguishable from an honest model sample. Nearly every such scheme assumes the receiver can recompute the sender's token probabilities exactly bit for bit. We show this assumption is fragile: across three model families, bit-exact schemes decode almost none of our messages once the receiver's floating-point precision, quantization, or GPU architecture differs from the sender's, or even when the receiver merely scores a text in parallel versus one token at a time, with the same model, precision, and hardware held fixed. We present STEALTH, a scheme built for exactly this setting. The
s0dda1fef1f.summary: STEALTH shows provably secure linguistic steganography schemes often fail to decode when receiver precision, quantization, or GPU hardware differs from the sender's.
s0dda1fef1f.why: Engineers relying on bit-exact probability recomputation across hardware should expect steganographic and watermark decoding to break under numerical differences.

sfa6281f33d.title: SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection
sfa6281f33d.description: arXiv:2611.16929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The easy access to Large Language Models (LLMs) has made AI-generated texts on the web increasingly ubiquitous, making AI-text detection a crucial task. Prompts greatly influence the generation process, but existing detectors focus solely on the generated texts --- supervised methods learn from labeled texts only, and zero-shot methods rely on the text's probability distributions --- ignoring the underlying generation process, which limits their robustness in open-world scenarios. We introduce SPADE: Soft Prompts for Ai-text DEtection, a novel framework for detecting AI-generated text that transfers better across datasets. Specifically, we measure the prompt's influence and use it as a discriminative signal. We characterize the prompt's inf
sfa6281f33d.summary: SPADE introduces soft prompts to detect AI-generated text by modeling the generation process, rather than relying only on the text or its probabilities.
sfa6281f33d.why: Detectors that account for prompts may be more robust in open-world settings, though the text gives little on benchmark results.

s5fff94d321.title: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
s5fff94d321.description: arXiv:2611.16933v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Full-duplex spoken dialogue models learn turn-taking, overlaps and backchannels from conversations recorded with one channel per speaker, but most available conversational audio is a single mono mix. We present Kezek, a model that turns a mono recording of exactly two people into one track per person with the original length and timing; overlaps and short replies ("yeah", "mm-hm") stay on the track of the person who said them. Kezek decides who speaks when and who is who once for the whole recording (stage 1: a two-voice activity model guided by a speaker fingerprint trained to be insensitive to phase), and a conditioned time-domain separator only carries out that decision (stage 2), with outputs that always sum to the input. Standard separ
s5fff94d321.summary: Kezek splits mono recordings of two-person conversations into separate per-speaker tracks, preserving timing and overlaps, to create full-duplex dialogue training data.
s5fff94d321.why: It offers a way to turn abundant single-channel conversation audio into training data for full-duplex spoken dialogue models.

scd9d1a105b.title: Claude’s Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful

s99d40623cf.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
s99d40623cf.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots your initialized environment and restores it for each new session, so session start no longer grows with image size. This post explains how V2 starts a session, how to measure session start time, and four patterns to keep work off the first request.
s99d40623cf.summary: AWS explains how Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots initialized environments so session startup no longer scales with image size, and offers four patterns for faster startup.
s99d40623cf.why: Snapshot-based restore decouples session start time from container image size, which affects latency planning for agent deployments.

s94d8e8d365.title: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard
s94d8e8d365.description: Coding agents work in tasks, and the number that matters is cost per solved task, not price per token. In this post, you use the AWS CDK to deploy LiteLLM with the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing plugin on Amazon Bedrock, then measure cost per solved task for a routed model group against single-model baselines.
s94d8e8d365.summary: AWS shows how to deploy LiteLLM with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing on Amazon Bedrock and measure cost per solved coding-agent task against single-model baselines.
s94d8e8d365.why: Cost per solved task, not price per token, is the metric to track when routing coding-agent requests across models.
